issues.title: Refactor test-integration.sh to fixture-driven pytest discovery (eliminate manual test wiring)
issues.body:
## Problem

`scripts/test-integration.sh` is a 665-line bash script that explicitly enumerates ~20 `pytest tests/integration/test_*.py` invocations, one per file. Adding a new integration test file requires editing the script. Forgetting to wire a file means the test silently never runs.

This is not a hypothetical risk -- it just bit us:

- `tests/integration/test_skill_install.py` was never wired into the script. Two existing tests (`test_reinstall_same_skill_is_idempotent`, and the new `test_reinstall_does_not_leak_apm_pin_to_deploy_targets` from PR #1153) silently rotted until I noticed and patched it in PR #1153 (commit `941c6942`).
- No CI workflow runs the full integration script. `.github/workflows/ci-integration.yml` only invokes `test_runtime_smoke.py`; the other ~19 files run only on manual release-validation execution. Most "integration coverage" runs on the honor system.

## Real constraints (what's legitimate)

The script does several things that genuinely need orchestration:

- Builds a PyInstaller binary (or reuses CI artifact at `./dist/$BINARY_NAME/apm`)
- Symlinks the binary into `$PATH` so tests exercise the **shipped binary**, not in-process `python -m apm_cli`
- Sets up runtimes (copilot/codex/llm) by invoking `apm runtime setup`
- Resolves GitHub tokens via `github-token-helper.sh`

These are real concerns. **Per-file pytest enumeration is not.**

## What's wrong (per Python testing world-class standards)

1. **Manual wiring is the bug we just hit.** Pytest's whole value-prop is auto-discovery (`pytest <dir>` finds and runs everything matching `test_*.py`). The bash script defeats that.
2. **Bash is the wrong layer for test selection, reporting, and exit codes.** The 20 `if pytest ... ; then log_success ; else log_error ; exit 1 ; fi` blocks reimplement what pytest does natively, and worse: a single test file failure aborts the whole run via `set -e`, masking subsequent failures.
3. **No marker-based gating.** Different files need different env (`ADO_APM_PAT`, `GITHUB_APM_PAT`, `APM_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1`, runtime presence). Today this is encoded as conditional bash branches; it should be `@pytest.mark.requires_ado_pat` etc., selectable via `pytest -m`.
4. **The "built binary" constraint doesn't justify bash sprawl.** It's a `session`-scoped fixture, not a loop.

## Proposed pattern

```python
# tests/integration/conftest.py
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def apm_binary():
    # build once OR read APM_BINARY_PATH from env (CI), prepend to PATH
    ...
```

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
    "requires_apm_binary",
    "requires_github_apm_pat",
    "requires_ado_pat",
    "requires_runtime_codex",
    "requires_runtime_copilot",
    "requires_runtime_llm",
]
```

```python
# Per test file (replaces today's pytestmark skipif chains):
pytestmark = [pytest.mark.requires_apm_binary, pytest.mark.requires_github_apm_pat]
```

`scripts/test-integration.sh` shrinks to ~50 lines: detect platform, build/locate binary, set up runtimes, export tokens, then **one** invocation:

```bash
pytest tests/integration/ -v --tb=short \
  $( [[ -z "${ADO_APM_PAT:-}" ]] && echo '-m "not requires_ado_pat"' )
```

Pytest handles discovery, selection, reporting, exit codes. Bash handles env setup. Each layer does what it's good at.

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/test-integration.sh` no longer enumerates individual `pytest test_*.py` calls; it invokes `pytest tests/integration/` with marker selection.
- A new test file dropped into `tests/integration/` with the right markers automatically runs without script edits.
- All currently-wired integration tests still run (no regressions).
- Conditional gating (ADO PAT, GitHub PAT, runtime presence) preserved via markers + skipif fixtures, not bash branches.
- CI integration workflow (`.github/workflows/ci-integration.yml`) optionally extended to run the full marker-filtered suite (currently only runs smoke).

## Out of scope

- Migrating tests off the built binary to in-process invocation (that's a separate, larger discussion).
- Adding new test coverage (this is a pure refactor).
- Changing `github-token-helper.sh` or runtime-setup commands.

## References

- PR #1153 (where the wiring gap was discovered and patched in commit `941c6942`)
- `scripts/test-integration.sh:336-664` (the enumerated pytest blocks)

issues.title: Audit unmarked integration tests + swap test-integration.sh to pytest discovery (PR2 of #1166)
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1167 (PR1 of #1166). PR1 landed marker infrastructure in `tests/integration/conftest.py`. This issue tracks the remaining execution-side work: replacing `scripts/test-integration.sh`'s 386-line `run_e2e_tests()` (26 explicit per-file pytest invocations) with a single `pytest tests/integration/` discovery call.

## Why this is split out

The script swap was attempted as part of #1167 and reverted. A test-coverage probe (`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_APM_PAT -u ADO_APM_PAT pytest tests/integration/`) collected 559 tests across 64 files but produced **88 failures across 12 files** — none of them caused by the marker refactor itself. The bash script silently invoked only 26 files; the other 38 have either no markers or surface real pre-existing bugs. Shipping the swap immediately would mix marker-gap noise with real-bug noise on the very first CI run, which would train maintainers to ignore integration results — exactly the failure mode that #1166 is trying to fix.

## Inventory of files needing work

**41 integration test files have no `pytestmark` and no `requires_*` marker.** Of those, the following 12 produce failures when run without tokens (full list in the test-coverage probe):

Network / token gated (need `requires_github_token` or similar marker):
- `tests/integration/test_skill_bundle_live.py` (18 failures)
- `tests/integration/test_marketplace_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_azure_skills_marketplace.py` (likely `requires_ado_pat`)
- `tests/integration/test_drift_check_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_drift_check.py`
- `tests/integration/test_link_rewrite_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_transitive_chain_e2e.py` (3 failures)
- `tests/integration/test_intra_package_cleanup.py`

Likely real bugs surfaced (need triage, not markers):
- `tests/integration/test_virtual_package_orphan_detection.py` — `test_azure_devops_virtual_collection_not_flagged_as_orphan` returns the wrong package name shape (expected `company/my-azurecollection/copilot-instructions/collections/csharp-ddd-cleanarchitecture`, got `company/my-azurecollection/copilot-instructions-csharp-ddd-cleanarchitecture`). The bash script never invoked this file — the bug has been silent in CI.
- `tests/integration/test_local_install.py` — fixtures don't create `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and the post-#1165 target detection rejects the install.
- `tests/integration/test_local_content_audit.py`
- `tests/integration/test_policy_install_e2e.py`
- `tests/integration/test_selective_install_mcp.py`

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every `tests/integration/test_*.py` file either carries an appropriate `requires_*` marker (declared in `tests/integration/conftest.py`) or is documented in this issue as a real bug to fix separately.
2. Real bugs (the second list above) are filed as their own issues and either fixed or marked `xfail` with a tracking link before the script swap lands.
3. `scripts/test-integration.sh::run_e2e_tests()` is replaced with the architect-recommended discovery call:
   ```bash
   export APM_E2E_TESTS=1
   export APM_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1
   pytest tests/integration/ -v -s --tb=short --ignore=tests/integration/marketplace
   ```
4. CI release validation (`build-release.yml`) passes on a token-equipped run.
5. A second probe (token-stripped) returns 0 failures — only skips driven by markers.

## Reference design

Architect-recommended approach D: full discovery + explicit `--ignore` for legacy `marketplace/`, no `KNOWN_EXCLUDED` deselect list. The script was reduced from 739 to 354 lines in the PR1 attempt; that diff is preserved in the worktree at `1c08e15f^` for reuse once gates 1-2 above are met.

## DevX nits to fold in

- Pre-run banner: `echo "Running integration tests ($(find tests/integration -name 'test_*.py' | wc -l) files, ignoring marketplace)..."` before the pytest invocation (devx-ux-expert nit).
- Drop the legacy 22-line success summary in `main()` listing "HERO SCENARIO 1/2/3..." — pytest's own summary line is the correct signal once the script orchestrates a single invocation (devx-ux-expert nit).

## Out of scope

- CI workflow changes beyond removing now-dead branches in `build-release.yml`.
- Windows `.ps1` parity.
- `tests/integration/marketplace/` (legacy fixtures kept on the old gate).

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install --target agent-skills` installs to `.agents/<skill>` instead of `.agents/skills/<skill>` when `.agents/` does not exist
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When running `apm install --target agent-skills` in a project where the `.agents/` directory does not yet exist, skills are installed to `.agents/<skill-name>/` instead of the expected `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/`. The `skills/` subdirectory level is dropped entirely.

## To Reproduce

1. Start from a clean directory with **no** `.agents/` folder present.
2. Create a minimal `apm.yml`:
   ```yaml
   name: my-project
   version: 1.0.0
   description: Test project
   author: test
   dependencies:
      apm:
       - blader/humanizer
      mcp: []
   scripts: {}
   ```
3. Run:
   ```
   uv tool run --from git+https://github.com/microsoft/apm.git apm install --target agent-skills
   ```
4. Inspect the created directory structure.

## Expected behavior

Skills should be installed under `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/`, consistent with the `agent-skills` target convention and with behavior when `.agents/` already exists.

```
.agents/
└── skills/
    └── <skill-name>/
        └── SKILL.md
```

## Actual behavior

Skills are installed directly under `.agents/<skill-name>/`, skipping the `skills/` subdirectory:

```
.agents/
└── <skill-name>/
    └── SKILL.md
```

## Root cause hypothesis

When the `.agents/` directory is absent, APM likely creates it on the fly but does not correctly resolve the full target path `.agents/skills/`. The `skills/` segment is lost during directory creation, suggesting the path construction logic may be splitting or truncating the target path incorrectly in the "first-time init" code path.

## Environment

- **OS**: Linux (WSL 2 / Ubuntu)
- **Python Version**: see `uv` managed environment
- **APM Version**: 0.12.3
- **Install method**: `uv tool run --from git+https://github.com/microsoft/apm.git`

## Workaround

Manually create the `.agents/skills/` directory before running `apm install`:

```bash
mkdir -p .agents/skills
apm install --target agent-skills
```

issues.title: v0.12.3: audit-replay rewrites in-package asset links against scratch dir, producing false drift
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm audit --ci` reports false drift on agent/instruction files that contain relative links to repo-root files (e.g. ``[`MANIFESTO.md`](../../MANIFESTO.md)``). On-disk SHA matches the lockfile SHA exactly, and `apm install --force` is a no-op -- yet drift is reported.

Main branch of microsoft/apm is currently red on the APM Self-Check gate because of this.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd microsoft/apm
uv run apm audit --ci
# [!] Drift detected: 6 file(s)
#   - .github/agents/apm-ceo.agent.md
#   - .github/agents/auth-expert.agent.md
#   - .github/agents/devx-ux-expert.agent.md
#   - .github/agents/oss-growth-hacker.agent.md
#   - .github/agents/supply-chain-security-expert.agent.md
#   - .github/instructions/doc-sync.instructions.md
```

All six files contain `[..](../../<repo-root-file>.md)` style links.

## Root cause

Replay calls `integrate_package_primitives(package_info, scratch_root, ...)` with `project_root = scratch_root` (`src/apm_cli/install/drift.py:466`). The link resolver's in-package asset rewrite at `src/apm_cli/compilation/link_resolver.py:503` then computes `os.path.relpath(candidate, ctx.target_location)` where:

- `candidate` = `<actual-repo>/MANIFESTO.md` (resolved against the real source package_root from `init_link_resolver`)
- `ctx.target_location` = `<scratch>/.github/agents/`

...yielding `../../../../../../../../Users/.../awd-cli/MANIFESTO.md` instead of `../../MANIFESTO.md`. That diverges from what real install writes to disk, so audit reports drift.

Diff captured by suppressing the scratch-dir cleanup (`shutil.rmtree` no-op):
```
< - [`MANIFESTO.md`](../../MANIFESTO.md)
> - [`MANIFESTO.md`](../../../../../../../../Users/danielmeppiel/Repos/awd-cli/MANIFESTO.md)
```

## Fix sketch

The asset-link rewriter must compute relative paths in the **logical** (project-relative) deploy layout, not the scratch layout. Options:

1. Pass a `logical_target_location` alongside the physical scratch path through to `LinkResolutionContext`, computed as `project_root / target_path.relative_to(scratch_root)`.
2. Rewrite via project-relative paths and translate to scratch only at filesystem write time.
3. Disable `enable_asset_rewrite` in the replay code path (loses replay fidelity for self-packages).

## Impact

Blocks the APM Self-Check CI gate for any repo that (a) is on v0.12.3, (b) installs a self-package, (c) has primitives containing `../<repo-root-file>` style links. Currently breaking microsoft/apm `main` and PR #1181.

issues.title: shared/apm.md: drop `|| 'all'` fallback on `target` (gh-aw substitution incompatible with GHA-idiom fallbacks)
issues.body:
## Summary

PR #1184 introduced the pattern `target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }}` in `shared/apm.md`. The `|| 'all'` fallback **defeats gh-aw's compile-time substitution** of `${{ github.aw.import-inputs.* }}`, so consumer-supplied `with: target: copilot` is silently ignored — the lock.yml keeps the unresolved expression and the runtime env var ends up empty (which apm then treats as `all`, triggering `copilot-cowork` install attempts that fail with `requires --global`).

## Reproduction

Consumer workflow:

```yaml
imports:
  - path: shared/apm.md
    with:
      packages: ["org/repo/plugins/foo#v1.0.0"]
      target: copilot   # ← ignored
```

After `gh aw compile` (v0.71.5 and v0.72.0 both reproduce):

```yaml
# lock.yml
- name: APM Install
  uses: microsoft/apm-action@v1.7.2
  with:
    packages: '["org/repo/plugins/foo#v1.0.0"]'           # ← substituted (array, bare expression)
    target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }} # ← NOT substituted
```

## Root cause

gh-aw's substitution regex ([`pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go:922` @ v0.72.0](https://github.com/githubnext/gh-aw/blob/v0.72.0/pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go)):

```go
var importInputsExprRegex = regexp.MustCompile(
    `\$\{\{\s*github\.aw\.import-inputs\.([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?)\s*\}\}`)
```

Matches **only bare** `${{ github.aw.import-inputs.X }}`. The `|| 'all'` inside the brackets makes the regex not match → no substitution → unresolved expression survives into lock.yml → empty env at runtime.

This explains the asymmetry seen in the wild: `AW_APM_PACKAGES: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.packages }}` (bare) gets substituted; `target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }}` (with fallback) does not.

## Why `|| 'all'` is redundant anyway

gh-aw's [`applyImportSchemaDefaultsFromFrontmatter`](https://github.com/githubnext/gh-aw/blob/v0.72.0/pkg/parser/import_field_extractor.go#L875) already injects schema-declared defaults into the inputs map **before** substitution. With the schema PR #1184 already added:

```yaml
import-schema:
  target:
    type: string
    default: all
```

…and `target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target }}` (no fallback), the behavior is exactly what `|| 'all'` was meant to express:

| Consumer | After substitution |
|---|---|
| `with: target: copilot` | `target: copilot` |
| `with:` (target omitted) | `target: all` (from schema default) |

## Proposed fix

One-line change in `shared/apm.md`:

```diff
-target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target || 'all' }}
+target: ${{ github.aw.import-inputs.target }}
```

Schema default `all` is already declared by PR #1184, no other change needed. Verified locally against gh-aw v0.72.0: lock.yml then carries the literal substituted value (`target: copilot` when consumer provides it; `target: all` when omitted).

## Evidence

- Smoke run with `|| 'all'` (current shared/apm.md): apm install fails because cowork install needs `--global` — [hackathon-white-pig-8/zava-storefront run 25495022790](https://github.com/hackathon-white-pig-8/zava-storefront/actions/runs/25495022790)
- Smoke run with vendor-patched literal `target: copilot` (proves substitution path is the only blocker): [run 25495232796](https://github.com/hackathon-white-pig-8/zava-storefront/actions/runs/25495232796) — green end-to-end (apm install 11s, agent 7m11s, full pipeline succeeds)
- Local repro that the elegant fix (drop `|| 'all'`) compiles to literal `target: copilot`: confirmed against gh-aw v0.72.0

## Optional parallel fix in gh-aw

Make `importInputsExprRegex` tolerant of GHA-idiom `|| <fallback>` so consumers can keep using the familiar pattern. Happy to file that on `githubnext/gh-aw` separately — but the apm-side fix is sufficient and aligns with intent (schema defaults exist for exactly this purpose; the `||` belt-and-suspenders just made the suspenders cut the belt).

## Bonus: cowork-in-`all` malfunction (separate but related)

While debugging, surfaced what looks like a second upstream bug in apm: when `target=all` is passed, apm attempts to install `copilot-cowork` and fails with `'copilot-cowork' target requires --global`. But [`src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py:202`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py) explicitly documents that `EXPERIMENTAL_TARGETS` (incl. `copilot-cowork`) is "NOT included in the `parse_target_arg('all')` expansion" — and indeed `normalize_target_list("all")` returns `{vscode, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini}`, no cowork. So cowork is being enumerated by some other code path. Worth a separate issue — happy to file with the same evidence if useful.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-05-07
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-07
**APM Version**: 0.12.4 (9d4e2ba)
**Commands Inspected**: 57 (top-level + all subcommands and sub-subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` omits `windsurf` from accepted values
- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` help text does not list `windsurf` as a valid value, even though `windsurf` is fully supported by the underlying `TargetParamType`. The `apm install --target` help correctly includes `windsurf`. This inconsistency will cause users to miss that `windsurf` is a valid target for `apm deps update`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help` shows: `Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, agent-skills, all.`
  - `apm install --help` shows: `Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all.`
  - Source confirms `windsurf` IS valid: `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/cli.py` line 700-704 uses `TargetParamType()` but has a hand-written help string that omits windsurf.
  - The docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` line 1097) also list `windsurf` as valid for `apm deps update`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help string in `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/cli.py` to add `windsurf` after `gemini`: `"Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all."`

---

#### `apm cache clean` has two redundant flags doing the same thing
- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: Both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes` are documented as "Skip confirmation prompt". Having two flags with different names for the exact same behavior is confusing and inconsistent with the rest of the CLI, which uses `-y/--yes` as the convention for skip-confirmation (e.g., `apm deps clean`, `apm marketplace remove`, `apm runtime remove`).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
  ```
  Source (`src/apm_cli/commands/cache.py` lines 58-74): both flags are checked with `if not force and not yes:`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f/--force` from `apm cache clean` to unify on `-y/--yes` for confirmation-skipping, matching the pattern used by all other commands. Alternatively, keep `--force` as a hidden alias if backward compatibility is required.

---

#### `apm mcp install` options appear as disconnected epilog text rather than proper CLI options
- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: `apm mcp install` uses `ignore_unknown_options` and `allow_extra_args` to forward arguments to `apm install --mcp`. Its supported flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) are shown as free-form epilog text, not as registered Click options. Users cannot discover individual flag descriptions via `--help`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL    Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE    Environment variable (repeatable)...
  ```
  The epilog is rendered as a block of unformatted text after the Options section.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) register the key options explicitly on `mcp install` so they appear properly in `--help`, or (b) rewrite the epilog to be clearly formatted with line breaks and indentation so the hint text is readable. Option (b) is lower effort and preserves the passthrough design. Example: split each option onto its own line in the epilog string.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm deps tree` docs omit the `--global` flag
- **Command**: `apm deps tree`
- **Problem**: The CLI reference docs at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` (around line 1000-1026) document `apm deps tree` with no Options section. The actual CLI has a `-g, --global` flag.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps tree --help
  Options:
    -g, --global  Show user-scope dependency tree (~/.apm/)
    --help        Show this message and exit.
  ```
  The docs only show a code block `apm deps tree` with no options listed.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add an Options section to the `apm deps tree` documentation listing `-g, --global`.

---

#### `apm update` documentation example output uses emoji, violating the ASCII-only encoding rule
- **Command**: `apm update`
- **Problem**: The docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` around line 829) show a sample update notification that includes the emoji `warning sign + variation selector`. The project encoding rules mandate all CLI output and docs stay within printable ASCII (U+0020-U+007E). The correct convention per the codebase is `[!]`.
- **Evidence**: The sample output block in the docs reads:
  ```
  [warning emoji]  A new version of APM is available: 0.7.0 (current: 0.6.3)
  Run apm update to upgrade
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the warning emoji with `[!]` in the example output block:
  ```
  [!] A new version of APM is available: 0.7.0 (current: 0.6.3)
  Run apm update to upgrade
  ```

---

#### `apm compile` auto-detection table uses deprecated target alias `vscode`
- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The auto-detection table in the docs lists `vscode` as a detected target name (condition: "`.github/` exists only"). However `vscode` is a deprecated alias for `copilot`. Users reading the table may expect to see `vscode` as output from `apm targets` but the CLI now uses `copilot` as the canonical name.
- **Evidence**: The table shows:
  ```
  | `.github/` exists only | `vscode` | AGENTS.md + .github/ |
  ```
  But `apm targets` outputs `copilot` for the same condition. The docs themselves note "`vscode`, `agents` -- Deprecated aliases for `copilot`" elsewhere in the same file.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the auto-detection table to use `copilot` instead of `vscode` in the Target column.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm run`, `apm preview`, `apm list` -- Consistent help text, no crashes, error messages are clear
- `apm deps list`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps clean` -- Correct flags, clear documentation
- `apm mcp list`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show` -- Consistent with docs
- `apm config set`, `apm config get`, `apm config unset` -- Error handling is clean; missing args produce helpful messages
- `apm compile` -- Rich help text, flags consistent with docs
- `apm runtime setup`, `apm runtime list`, `apm runtime remove`, `apm runtime status` -- Complete and accurate
- `apm audit` -- Comprehensive flag set, well documented
- `apm pack`, `apm unpack` -- Accurate help, deprecation notice present on unpack
- `apm marketplace` (all subcommands including authoring commands) -- Authoring/consumer split is clear, all subcommands present
- `apm experimental list/enable/disable/reset` -- Consistent flags, `--json` output option works
- `apm policy status`, `apm cache info`, `apm cache prune`, `apm outdated`, `apm prune` -- Accurate and consistent
- `apm targets`, `apm view`, `apm search` -- Work as documented
- Error handling: Invalid flags, missing required arguments -- All produce clean Click error messages with usage hints, no stack traces observed

issues.title: [BUG] YAML field `target` is not honored
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

If you set the `target` field in the configuration is not honored. The type of the field is string ot list<string> in the [documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/manifest-schema/#36-target), but the reality is that it is a string of a comma-separated string

This configuration works

```yaml
version: 0.1.0
description: test
author: foo
license: Apache-2.0
type: hybrid
target: copilot
compilation:
  strategy: single-file
  exclude:
  - docs/**
dependencies:
  apm: 
    - github/awesome-copilot
  mcp: []
scripts: {}
```

This configuration works too

```yaml
version: 0.1.0
description: test
author: foo
license: Apache-2.0
type: hybrid
target: copilot,claude
compilation:
  strategy: single-file
  exclude:
  - docs/**
dependencies:
  apm: 
    - github/awesome-copilot
  mcp: []
scripts: {}
```

These two configurations fail with the same error

```
[x] [x] Unknown target '['copilot''

Valid targets: agent-skills, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, opencode, windsurf

Fix with one of:

  apm targets                            # see all supported harnesses
  apm install <pkg> --target agent-skills
  apm install <pkg> --dry-run

Or declare in apm.yml:

  targets:
    - agent-skills
```

```yaml
version: 0.1.0
description: test
author: foo
license: Apache-2.0
type: hybrid
target: ['copilot', 'claude']
compilation:
  strategy: single-file
  exclude:
  - docs/**
dependencies:
  apm: 
    - github/awesome-copilot
  mcp: []
scripts: {}
```

```yaml
version: 0.1.0
description: test
author: foo
license: Apache-2.0
type: hybrid
target: 
  - 'copilot'
  - 'claude'
compilation:
  strategy: single-file
  exclude:
  - docs/**
dependencies:
  apm: 
    - github/awesome-copilot
  mcp: []
scripts: {}
```

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Configure `target` field with `claude` and `copilot` in the apm.yml file 
2. run `target install`
3. See error

**Expected behavior**

Only the selected `target` must be created without failures

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.13.11
 - APM Version: 0.12.3

**Logs**
If applicable, add any error logs or screenshots.

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

issues.title: [Feature] GitLab host support for marketplace and install
issues.body:
## Problem

GitLab does not implement GitHub's Contents API (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/...`). Today, APM uses generic FQDN logic that assumes `/api/v3` endpoints with GitHub-compatible URL shapes, which breaks:

1. **Marketplace fetch** - `marketplace.json` cannot be retrieved from GitLab-hosted repositories
2. **File reads during install** - Single file downloads (e.g., `SKILL.md`) fail for GitLab-hosted packages
3. **Git operations** - GitLab uses different authentication conventions than GitHub for HTTPS git-over-PAT
4. **Host classification** - GitLab hosts are misclassified as "generic", causing token misrouting (GitHub tokens sent to GitLab hosts)

### Current behavior
- `apm install gitlab.com/group/project` fails with API errors or authentication failures
- GitLab PATs supplied via `GITLAB_TOKEN` are not recognized; APM attempts to use `GITHUB_TOKEN` instead
- Nested GitLab groups (e.g., `group/subgroup/repo`) are not handled correctly

## Proposed Solution

Add first-class GitLab host support with explicit host classification, GitLab REST API v4 integration, and PAT-primary HTTPS git transport.

### Key capabilities

| Capability | Implementation |
|------------|----------------|
| **Host detection** | Recognize `gitlab.com`, `GITLAB_HOST` env var, and `APM_GITLAB_HOSTS` list |
| **API integration** | Use GitLab Files API v4 for marketplace and file reads |
| **Token chain** | Support `GITLAB_APM_PAT` → `GITLAB_TOKEN` resolution (isolated from GitHub tokens) |
| **Git transport** | PAT-primary HTTPS with GitLab-compatible auth (not GitHub `x-access-token` convention) |
| **Shorthand resolution** | Probe repo boundaries left-to-right for nested group paths |

### Host classification order
```
github.com → kind="github"
*.ghe.com → kind="ghe_cloud"
Azure DevOps FQDNs → kind="ado"
GITHUB_HOST match → kind="ghes" (GHES takes precedence)
GitLab detection → kind="gitlab"
Generic FQDN → kind="generic"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apm install gitlab.com/group/project` succeeds using only `GITLAB_APM_PAT` or `GITLAB_TOKEN`
- [ ] GitLab SaaS (`gitlab.com`) is auto-detected without configuration
- [ ] Self-managed GitLab hosts work via `GITLAB_HOST` or `APM_GITLAB_HOSTS`
- [ ] `marketplace.json` fetch uses GitLab Files API v4 when source is GitLab-hosted
- [ ] Git operations (clone, fetch, ls-remote) succeed via PAT-primary HTTPS without external credential helpers
- [ ] `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_APM_PAT` are NOT sent to GitLab hosts
- [ ] Token-bearing URLs and errors are redacted in logs and diagnostics
- [ ] Nested group paths (e.g., `group/subgroup/repo`) resolve correctly
- [ ] Direct shorthand installs probe repo boundaries left-to-right for earliest qualifying match
- [ ] `apm deps list` shows `gitlab` as Source for GitLab-class dependencies
- [ ] All existing GitHub.com, GHES, Azure DevOps behavior remains unchanged (non-regression)
- [ ] Full pytest suite passes (`uv run pytest -q`)

## Out of Scope

- SSH as primary transport (remains optional fallback)
- GitLab CI-specific token handling (use `GITLAB_APM_PAT` in CI)
- GitLab Issue/MR integration
- GitLab-specific marketplace features beyond file fetch

## Suggested Labels

`type/feature`, `area/auth`, `area/marketplace`, `area/install`

## References

- Spec: `apm-gitlab-host-support.spec.md` (stable)
- Related work: Token precedence fix for GitLab hosts

issues.title: RFC: peer_dependencies semantics for cross-cutting substrate plugins
issues.body:
## Problem

APM's transitive resolver uses **first-wins** flattening (see `src/apm_cli/deps/apm_resolver.py:478`). For ordinary tool deps that's fine — the conflict is logged as a warning, the build proceeds, and the consumer can either accept the resolved ref or pin explicitly.

For **cross-cutting substrate plugins** that act as a *floor* (e.g. a `secure-baseline` shipping security instructions + a security reviewer persona that every consumer must inherit), first-wins is dangerous: a phase-kit plugin upgrade that bumps its transitive ref of the substrate would silently shift the floor without any signal in the consumer's PR diff.

Today the workaround in our marketplace (`DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config`) is:

1. Phase kits declare `dependencies.apm: []` — they do **not** redeclare the substrate as a transitive dep.
2. Consumers pin the substrate **explicitly** in their own `apm.yml`.
3. A reusable CI workflow (`apm-baseline-check.yml`) fails the build if the substrate is missing from the lockfile, or if the resolved graph contains multiple distinct refs of it.

That works, but it pushes a discipline (carry-the-pin, add-the-CI-gate) onto every consumer team. It would be cleaner if the substrate plugin itself could **declare** the expectation, and APM could **error at install time** when the consumer hasn't satisfied it — same shape as npm `peerDependencies`.

## Proposal

Add a `peer_dependencies` (or `peerDependencies`) field to plugin manifests. Semantics modelled on npm:

```yaml
# secure-baseline/apm.yml
peer_dependencies:
  apm: []   # this is the substrate; it has no peers
```

```yaml
# code-kit/apm.yml — declares the floor it expects, but does NOT pull it transitively
peer_dependencies:
  apm:
    - DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config/plugins/secure-baseline:^5.0.0
```

```yaml
# zava-storefront/apm.yml — consumer satisfies the peer
dependencies:
  apm:
    - DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config/plugins/secure-baseline#v5.0.1
    - DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config/plugins/code-kit#v5.0.1
```

`apm install` MUST:

- Detect peer expectations from every transitively-included plugin.
- Verify each peer is **directly pinned** by the consumer (not transitively satisfied through a third plugin).
- Error if any peer is missing, mis-versioned, or pinned multiple times at incompatible refs.
- Print actionable remediation in the error: "Add `<plugin>#<ref>` to your `apm.yml` `dependencies.apm` block."

Optional: a `peer_dependencies_meta.optional: true` flag for soft expectations (warn, don't fail).

## Why this matters

- **Security floors** (secure-coding instructions, security reviewer persona, license-policy instructions) need the consumer's signature on the pin so audit trails are unambiguous.
- **Compliance instructions** (e.g. PCI-DSS, HIPAA scaffolds) need the same property — silent transitive resolution for a regulated control would be a finding.
- **Compounding org-wide grep proofs** ("show me every repo that pins the secure floor") fail when the pin can be implicit/transitive.

## Out of scope

- Range / semver semantics for the peer ref. Could mirror `dependencies.apm` exactly (git-ref strings) for now and leave semver as a separate RFC.
- Auto-fix in `apm install` to write the missing peer pin. This RFC is detect-and-error only; auto-fix is risky for security artifacts.

## Filed by

`zava-agent-config` marketplace team, off the back of the v5.0.1 → v6.0.0 work. Reference: [`CATALOG.md > Consumption patterns`](https://github.com/DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config/blob/main/CATALOG.md) (the practical workaround we ship today).

issues.title: [bug] policy inheritance: child without unmanaged_files block silently downgrades parent's action: deny
issues.body:
## Summary

When a child policy declares `extends: org` but does NOT redeclare an `unmanaged_files:` block, the merged policy's `unmanaged_files.action` is silently downgraded to the model's default (`ignore`) instead of inheriting the parent's `deny`.

The `_escalate(_UNMANAGED_ACTION_LEVELS, parent.action, child.action)` call at `src/apm_cli/policy/inheritance.py:198` correctly takes the max, but the `child.unmanaged_files` for a child that omits the block is not "no opinion" — it's `UnmanagedFilesPolicy(action='ignore', directories=())`. So `max('deny', 'ignore') == 'deny'` should hold but the resulting merged check reports as disabled.

## Repro

`org/.github/apm-policy.yml`:

```yaml
name: org
version: "1.0.0"
enforcement: block
unmanaged_files:
  action: deny
  directories:
    - .github/instructions
    - .github/agents
    - .github/hooks
```

`repo/apm-policy.yml`:

```yaml
name: child
version: "1.0.0"
extends: org
enforcement: block
dependencies:
  deny:
    - "**/some-pattern"
# (no unmanaged_files block)
```

Add an unmanaged file (e.g. `.github/hooks/sneaky.hook.md`) and run:

```bash
apm audit --ci --policy ./apm-policy.yml
```

**Expected:** `unmanaged-files` check fails with action `deny` inherited from org.

**Actual:** `[+] unmanaged-files | Unmanaged files check disabled (action: ignore)` and the audit passes.

## Workaround

Redeclare the `unmanaged_files` block in every override that should preserve the parent's posture:

```yaml
extends: org
unmanaged_files:
  action: deny
  directories:
    - .github/agents
    - .github/instructions
    - .github/hooks
```

This loses the value proposition of `extends:` (single source of truth at the org root) — the override has to mirror the parent's directory list verbatim, which is exactly what the inheritance feature is supposed to avoid.

## Suggested fix

Two routes:

1. Make the model field on `UnmanagedFilesPolicy` distinguish "default" from "explicitly set". A child that did NOT declare `unmanaged_files:` should be treated as transparent in `_merge_unmanaged_files`, returning `parent` unchanged. (Mirrors how `_intersect_allow` treats `None` as "no opinion".)
2. Or: at parse time, propagate parent values into any child block fields the child did not explicitly set, before invoking the merge.

The first is cleaner because it matches the rest of the inheritance.py contract.

## Affected versions

Reproduced with `apm` v0.x (current main). Same logic at `src/apm_cli/policy/inheritance.py:194-200`.

## Impact

Org-wide governance posture silently weakens whenever a team adds a repo override for an unrelated policy area (e.g. extra dependency deny patterns). Hard to detect — `apm audit --policy org` shows the right floor, but `apm audit --policy ./apm-policy.yml` (which the consumer typically runs in CI for layered enforcement) silently ignores the floor for `unmanaged_files`.

issues.title: [bug] apm install integrates files in .github/instructions/ that are not produced by an installed plugin
issues.body:
## Summary

When a file is dropped directly into `.github/instructions/` (not produced by any installed plugin), `apm install` appears to integrate it as if it were a managed primitive. The subsequent `unmanaged-files` policy check then reports zero unmanaged files, because everything in the monitored directory is treated as managed.

## Repro

Starting from a project with installed plugins:

```bash
cat > .github/instructions/hand-rolled.instructions.md <<'INSTR'
---
applyTo: "**"
description: "Hand-rolled, not from any plugin"
---
hello
INSTR
apm install
```

Install logs include a line like `instructions/: ..., hand-rolled.instructions.md`. The file is now treated as integrated.

Then:

```bash
apm audit --ci --policy <some-policy-with-unmanaged_files-deny>
```

`unmanaged-files` reports clean. The hand-rolled file evades the governance check that the policy is meant to enforce.

## Expected

`apm install` should only deploy files that originate from declared plugin manifests. Files that pre-exist in monitored governance directories without provenance should be:

- left untouched (not "integrated" into the managed set), and
- visible to `unmanaged-files` audit when the policy declares `action: deny`.

## Workaround

For the demo we used in this report we routed the unmanaged file to `.github/hooks/` instead, which apm install does NOT touch. That correctly trips the audit, but it also reveals the asymmetry: the same content rule applies to all three monitored directories per policy spec, but only one of them is actually enforceable today.

## Impact

A consumer can side-step org policy `unmanaged_files: action: deny` by simply placing instruction files at the right path before installing — apm install will adopt them silently and policy will treat them as managed.

## Related

Filed alongside #1198 (extends: silently downgrades unmanaged_files).

issues.title: apm audit drift: skip-with-info on cache miss instead of failing
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm audit drift` (and `apm audit --ci`) treats a cache miss during install-replay as a check FAILURE rather than a skip.

## Repro

```bash
# Fresh checkout, no cache populated
apm audit --ci --policy ./apm-policy.yml
# => drift check fails with: 'drift replay aborted: cache miss for ...'
# => exit code 1, even though all other checks pass
```

## Why this matters

Consumers wiring `apm audit` into CI commonly want to audit the **as-committed** file state without running `apm install` first (because `apm install` re-deploys upstream files and overwrites any local edits — defeating drift detection on tamper PRs). The natural pattern is:

1. `actions/checkout`
2. install apm CLI
3. `apm audit --ci` against committed files

Today this requires `--no-drift` because the drift check aborts on the cache it can't see. That's a sharp edge — users have to discover the flag the hard way.

## Suggested fix

Treat cache miss as **skip-with-info**, not failure. Print a clear message: `drift skipped: install cache not populated (run 'apm install' first or pass --no-drift)`. Other checks continue.

`content-integrity` already covers the most important threat (any deployed managed file edited post-install) using lockfile `deployed_file_hashes` — and works without cache. Drift's "replay install and diff" is stricter (catches deletions/additions too) but should be opt-in for CI flows that don't pre-install.

## Workaround

Pass `--no-drift` to both `apm audit` invocations. Documented at https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/drift-detection/ but the failure mode is non-obvious from the error message.

## Context

Discovered while wiring an enterprise demo where the audit gate runs against PR contents (no install) so deployed-file tamper is visible. Setup-only + --no-drift + content-integrity is the working combination today.

issues.title: extends: org also fails to layer dependencies.require from parent (same root as #1198)
issues.body:
## Summary

Same root cause as #1198 (`unmanaged_files` not layered through `extends: org`). The `dependencies.require` field is also dropped when a repo `apm-policy.yml` declares `extends: org` and the org floor declares `dependencies.require`.

## Repro

```yaml
# Org floor (e.g. org/.github/apm-policy.yml)
version: 1
dependencies:
  require:
    - secure-baseline
```

```yaml
# Repo override (e.g. some-app/apm-policy.yml)
version: 1
extends: org
# (does NOT redeclare dependencies.require)
```

Run `apm audit --ci --policy ./apm-policy.yml` in the repo with `secure-baseline` removed from `apm.yml`. Expected: `required-packages` check fails with `secure-baseline missing from manifest`. Actual: check passes with `No required packages configured` — the org's required list never made it into the layered policy.

## Workaround (proven)

Redeclare in the repo override:

```yaml
version: 1
extends: org
dependencies:
  require:
    - secure-baseline   # workaround: extends: org doesn't layer this
```

## Why this matters

Defeats the **"required floor"** governance pattern that the policy reference (https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/policy-reference/) is documented to support. Org wants to mandate `secure-baseline` everywhere; `extends: org` is the documented mechanism; today it silently downgrades the floor.

## Likely fix location

Same place as #1198 — the inheritance-merge code path that handles `extends:`. Looks like an additive/union merge is missing for `dependencies.require` (and possibly `dependencies.deny`, untested).

## Context

Discovered while wiring a 5-beat enterprise demo. Repro is reproducible end-to-end on a public org. Same workaround as #1198 unblocks; would prefer a fix so policy authors don't have to remember to redeclare two separate fields per override file.

issues.title: apm-action: 'apm install' before audit overwrites in-PR file tamper (drift detection blind)
issues.body:
## Summary

`microsoft/apm-action`'s default behavior runs `apm install` before any audit invocation. When a PR tampers with a deployed managed file (e.g. edits `.github/instructions/secure-coding-base.instructions.md` to weaken a security rule), `apm install` re-deploys the upstream version BEFORE the audit runs, silently overwriting the tamper. Audit then sees the pristine file and passes — even though the PR ships malicious content.

## Repro

1. Repo wires `microsoft/apm-action@v1` with default settings.
2. PR edits one line of a deployed instruction file under `.github/instructions/` or `.github/hooks/`.
3. Action runs: `apm install` overwrites the tampered file from the upstream plugin source.
4. `apm audit` runs against the now-pristine file. PASSES.
5. PR merges. Tampered content is in `main`'s history but not in the deployed tree — until someone runs `apm install` locally and the PR's edits are silently lost.

Either outcome (merge of bad intent into history; or silent loss of the edit) is broken.

## Suggested fix

Two options, both better than today:

**A. Add `audit-only` mode (recommended).** Expose an action input that runs the apm CLI install (so audit can use it) but does NOT re-deploy files. Audit sees the as-committed file state, drift / content-integrity catch the tamper.

**B. Default behavior change.** `apm install` in CI should be a no-op when `apm.lock.yaml` is present and the deployed file hashes match what's in the lockfile. Tamper is a hash mismatch; re-deploying silently overwriting it is the bug.

## Workaround (proven)

Wire your own reusable workflow that uses `microsoft/apm-action` with `setup-only: true` (apm CLI on PATH, no install/deploy), then runs `apm audit --ci --no-drift` directly. `content-integrity` check then sees the tamper via lockfile hash drift and fails the gate. Working example: `DevExpGbb/zava-agent-config/.github/workflows/apm-audit.yml@v5.1.2`.

## Why this matters

Drift detection is the WHOLE POINT of `deployed_file_hashes` in the lockfile (https://microsoft.github.io/apm/guides/drift-detection/). The default action behavior makes that detection structurally impossible in CI. Most consumers will use the action by default and assume it audits what's committed. It does not.

## Context

Discovered while building a 5-beat governance demo for an enterprise pilot. Beat 5 specifically demos a malicious instruction-file edit; surfacing it required moving off the action's default invocation.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Update revision-pins for external dependencies
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, one can pin to a `#revision` in `apm.yml` `.dependencies.apm[]`.

If one does this, `apm outdated` [^1] no longer offers updates for those revision-pinned dependencies. This causes toil when updating, raising the risk of more seldom updates and consequently raising the risk of there being a wider gap if an update must be integrated to patch a vulnerability, say - just like other dependency management.

Elaborating on how come revision-pinning is preferable -  <https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/c395761df6afe1a69e476bc60a013a94bcbc153f/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies> - but, broadly; pins do not drift (leading to surprise build failures if upstream releases), and revision-pins are not mutable like tags are (same, plus supply-chain risk were upstream's secrets compromised).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like `apm update` to have a mode whereby it will interrogate the upstreams and offer the revision for the latest release, where a package has been revision-pinned. 

It would be extra nice to mirror the dependabot feature that its `github-actions` ecosystem has, where it will update the revision-pin and then update a post-fix line-comment with the release tag that revision represents.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**Additional context**
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#using-third-party-actions "Pin actions to a full-length commit SHA"
- https://docs.cloud.google.com/software-supply-chain-security/docs/dependencies#pin

issues.title: [BUG] Custom MCP registry lookup fails — SimpleRegistryClient uses /v0/ API, official MCP Registry spec is /v0.1/
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

APM's `SimpleRegistryClient` uses the `/v0/` API prefix and a `/v0/servers/search` endpoint that do not exist in the [official MCP Registry API specification](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/generic-registry-api.md). This causes `apm install --mcp` with `--registry` to fail against any registry implementing the official spec.

The official [Generic Registry API](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/generic-registry-api.md) defines all endpoints under `/v0.1/`:

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /v0.1/servers` | List all servers (with pagination) |
| `GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions` | List all versions of a server |
| `GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions/{version}` | Get specific version (use `latest`) |

APM's `SimpleRegistryClient` (`src/apm_cli/registry/client.py`) instead calls:

| Method | Endpoint called | Issue |
|--------|----------------|-------|
| `list_servers()` | `GET /v0/servers` | Wrong prefix (`/v0/` vs `/v0.1/`) |
| `search_servers()` | `GET /v0/servers/search?q=...` | Endpoint does not exist in the spec |
| `get_server_info()` | `GET /v0/servers/{id}` | Spec uses `/{serverName}/versions/{version}` |

The [Official Registry API](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/official-registry-api.md) uses a `search` **query parameter** on `GET /v0.1/servers?search=...`, not a separate `/search` endpoint.

**To Reproduce**

1. Deploy an MCP registry implementing the [official spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) (e.g. `https://my-registry.example.com`)
2. Publish a server (e.g. `my-org/my-server`)
3. Verify it exists: `curl "https://my-registry.example.com/v0.1/servers?name=my-org/my-server"` → server found
4. Run: `apm install --mcp my-org/my-server --registry https://my-registry.example.com`
5. See error:
```
[>] Looking up 1 MCP server in registry...
[x] Server(s) not found in registry: my-org/my-server
```

**Expected behavior**

APM should use the `/v0.1/` API prefix and spec-compliant endpoints to resolve servers from any registry implementing the official MCP Registry API. Suggested changes:

1. Use `/v0.1/` prefix instead of `/v0/`
2. Replace `GET /v0/servers/search?q=...` with `GET /v0.1/servers?search=...`
3. Use `GET /v0.1/servers/{serverName}/versions/latest` for individual server lookup
4. URL-encode server names in paths (e.g. `my-org%2Fmy-server`)

**Environment:**
- OS: macOS 14.7.3 (23H417)
- APM Version: 0.12.4 (6aceef7)

**Additional context**

- [Generic Registry API Spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/generic-registry-api.md)
- [Official Registry API Spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/official-registry-api.md)

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-05-08
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-05-08
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.12.4 (73f0e9c)
**Commands Inspected**: 38

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 5 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### M1: `apm install --runtime` omits `windsurf` from valid values
- **Command**: `apm install --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI help text for `--runtime` does not list `windsurf` as a valid runtime, but the documentation explicitly includes it.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  --runtime TEXT  Target specific runtime only (copilot, codex, vscode, cursor, opencode, gemini, claude)
  ```
- **Evidence (docs line 91)**:
  ```
  --runtime TEXT - Target specific runtime only (copilot, codex, vscode, cursor, opencode, gemini, claude,windsurf)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `windsurf` to the `--runtime` help text in the CLI source, or remove it from the docs if windsurf is not a supported runtime target.

---

#### M2: `apm deps tree --global` option is undocumented
- **Command**: `apm deps tree --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI exposes a `-g, --global` flag on `apm deps tree`, but the documentation has no Options section for this command and does not mention the flag.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  Options:
    -g, --global  Show user-scope dependency tree (~/.apm/)
    --help        Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Evidence (docs, lines 999-1008)**: The `apm deps tree` section shows only an example with no options documented.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the `--global` option to the `apm deps tree` section in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md`.

---

#### M3: `apm deps update --target` CLI help omits `windsurf`
- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI help for `apm deps update --target` lists 8 targets but omits `windsurf`, while the documentation includes it.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                       copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                       gemini, agent-skills, all.
  ```
- **Evidence (docs line 1097)**:
  ```
  Valid values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, vscode, agents (deprecated), all.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `windsurf` to the `--target` values list in the `apm deps update` help text.

---

#### M4: `apm pack --target` docs list deprecated `vscode` and omit `agent-skills`
- **Command**: `apm pack --help`
- **Problem**: The documentation lists `vscode` (a deprecated alias) as a valid `--target` value for `apm pack`, and omits `agent-skills` which is valid per the CLI. The bundle target filtering table in the docs also uses the deprecated `vscode` label.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                       copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini,
                       windsurf, agent-skills, all.
  ```
- **Evidence (docs line 674)**:
  ```
  -t, --target [copilot|vscode|claude|cursor|codex|opencode|gemini|windsurf|all]
  ```
- **Evidence (docs bundle table, ~line 725)**:
  ```
  | vscode | .github/ |
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace `vscode` with `copilot` in the docs target list and bundle table. Add `agent-skills` to the `apm pack --target` documented values.

---

#### M5: `apm mcp install --help` uses non-standard help format
- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: Unlike all other commands which list options as structured Click options, `apm mcp install` only shows `--help` as a formal option. The actual supported flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) appear as free-form text in the epilog, not as proper CLI options. This breaks consistency and prevents `--help` from being machine-parseable for this command.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --mcp --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Register the forwarded flags as proper Click options on the `apm mcp install` command, or at minimum improve the epilog formatting so it renders as a clean multi-line section.

---

### Low Severity

#### L1: `apm init` missing `--target` and `--verbose` options in documentation
- **Command**: `apm init --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI exposes `--target TARGET` and `-v, --verbose` on `apm init`, but both are absent from the documentation.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  Options:
    -y, --yes        Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults
    --plugin         Initialize as plugin author (creates plugin.json + apm.yml)
    --marketplace    Seed apm.yml with a 'marketplace:' authoring block
    --target TARGET  Comma-separated target list (skip prompt, write directly)
    -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
    --help           Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Evidence (docs, lines 37-39)**: Only `-y/--yes`, `--plugin`, and `--marketplace` are listed.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `--target TARGET` and `-v, --verbose` to the `apm init` Options section in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli-commands.md`.

---

issues.title: [FEATURE] Allow per-instruction placement override (e.g., `placement:` frontmatter) to opt out of auto-distribution
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`apm compile`'s placement optimizer auto-decides whether an instruction with `applyTo:` is placed at the LCA subdirectory (Single Point) or distributed to root `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, based on a Distribution score derived from how many directories the `applyTo:` glob matches.

For instructions whose `applyTo:` covers a deep subtree (many matching directories → "High Distribution"), the optimizer always picks root. There is currently no way to override this per-instruction.

Concrete example — a monorepo with two app subtrees of asymmetric depth:

```
apps/
├── foo/      (1 small package, ~10 source dirs)
└── bar/      (multi-package SPA, ~70 source dirs)
```

```yaml
# .apm/instructions/foo.instructions.md
---
applyTo: "apps/foo/**"
---
```

```yaml
# .apm/instructions/bar.instructions.md
---
applyTo: "apps/bar/**"
---
```

`apm compile -v --dry-run` (APM 0.12.4) reports:

```
Optimizing placements...

  Pattern              Source        Co…   Placement            Metrics
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  apps/foo/**          foo.instr…    10…   apps/foo/AGENTS.md   rel: 100%
  apps/bar/**          bar.instr…    72…   ./AGENTS.md          rel: 0%

Mathematical Optimization Analysis
                       Three-Tier Coverage-First Strategy

  Pattern              Source        Distri…   Strategy        Coverage
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  apps/foo/**          foo.instr…   0.135     Single Point    Perfect
                                    (Low)
  apps/bar/**          bar.instr…   1.647     Distributed     Universal
                                    (High)
```

`apps/bar/**` ends up in `./AGENTS.md` (root) rather than `apps/bar/AGENTS.md`, even though semantically the rules are local to `apps/bar/`. The user has no way to express "yes, I know it's high-distribution; I still want it at the LCA subdirectory". This works against Claude Code's [memory documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), which recommends subdirectory `CLAUDE.md` files for **lazy-loaded** path-scoped context (root `CLAUDE.md` is recommended to stay under 200 lines for adherence). The same `apply-locally` intent applies to other targets — Cursor's `globs`, Copilot's `applyTo` — so a per-instruction opt-out helps multi-target setups in general.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A frontmatter `placement:` field with three modes. Default behavior unchanged (auto-placement); `placement:` is opt-in:

```yaml
---
applyTo: "apps/bar/**"
placement: "apps/bar"        # explicit path
---
```

```yaml
---
applyTo: "apps/bar/**"
placement: "subdirectory"    # force LCA placement regardless of Distribution tier
---
```

```yaml
---
applyTo: "apps/bar/**"
placement: "root"            # explicit root (matches today's High-Distribution outcome)
---
```

Implementation sketch: short-circuit the Three-Tier Strategy in `src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py` (around line 117) when `placement:` is present, before the auto-decision runs. The frontmatter parser in `src/apm_cli/integration/instruction_integrator.py` would just need to thread the field through.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Post-process script.** Read the generated root `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, split out `## Files matching apps/bar/**` sections, and rewrite them into `apps/bar/AGENTS.md` / `apps/bar/CLAUDE.md`. Works (idempotent if implemented carefully) but every APM user with this layout has to rediscover the issue and design the same script.
- **Splitting the wide `applyTo:` into many narrower patterns** (one per immediate sub-package) so each falls into the Low Distribution tier. Loses semantic intent ("these rules apply to the whole `apps/bar/**` subtree") and inflates the number of instruction files.
- **Manually placing the instruction file inside `apps/bar/.apm/instructions/`** to nudge the optimizer. Still subject to the same Distribution heuristic at compile time.

**Additional context**

- **Related (distinct scope):** #891 "Allow customizing skill integration target directory". Overlapping motivation but a different code path: that issue is about the **skill integration target dir** (handled in `src/apm_cli/install/`), this one is about **`applyTo:` instruction placement** (handled in `src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py`). Different frontmatter fields and configuration surfaces, so probably worth tracking separately.
- Happy to chat about the API shape if there's interest.

issues.title: [BUG] Claude .mcp.json drops env for self-defined stdio MCP servers
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a self-defined stdio MCP server declares `env` in `apm.yml`, APM generates Claude Code `.mcp.json` with an empty `env: {}` object.

The environment variables are present in the `apm.yml` MCP declaration, but they are not preserved in the Claude runtime config.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a project with this `apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: apm-claude-env-repro
version: 1.0.0
target:
  - claude
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp:
    - name: env-demo
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: npx
      args:
        - -y
        - example-mcp
      env:
        DEMO_ENV: demo-value
includes: auto
scripts: {}
```

2. Ensure Claude project config directory exists:

```bash
mkdir -p .claude
```

3. Run:

```bash
apm install --target claude --no-policy
```

4. Inspect the generated file:

```bash
cat .mcp.json
```

5. Observe that `env` is generated as `{}`.

**Expected behavior**

The generated `.mcp.json` should preserve the declared stdio environment variables:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "env-demo": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "env": {
        "DEMO_ENV": "demo-value"
      },
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "example-mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS 26.4.1
 - Python Version: 3.9.6
 - APM Version: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.12.4 (6aceef7)
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**

Actual generated `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "env-demo": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "env": {},
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "example-mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

`apm install` output reports success:

```text
Successfully configured MCP server 'env-demo' for Claude Code
[*] Installed 1 MCP server
```

**Additional context**

I searched existing MCP config / env related issues and found related adapter issues, but not this exact Claude Code stdio `env` drop.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Add IntelliJ / JetBrains as an MCP target
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

APM's promise is that "one file describes every agent's context; one command reproduces it everywhere" — but developers using JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA) with are cannot use the MCP config.

GitHub Copilot for JetBrains reads MCP server configuration from a user-scope config file. The path are:

| Platform | Path |
|----------|------|
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\github-copilot\intellij\mcp.json` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/github-copilot/intellij/mcp.json` *(unverified — follows standard macOS app-data conventions)* |
| Linux | `~/.local/share/github-copilot/intellij/mcp.json` *(unverified — follows data dir conventions)* |

The config uses a `"servers"` top-level key (not `"mcpServers"`), matching the format documented in the [official GitHub Copilot MCP docs for JetBrains](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/provide-context/use-mcp-in-your-ide/extend-copilot-chat-with-mcp?tool=jetbrains):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "memory": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory"]
    }
  }
}
```

`apm install --mcp` currently wires MCP servers into VS Code, Copilot CLI, Codex, Claude, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, and Windsurf — but not JetBrains IDEs. This forces JetBrains users to manually duplicate MCP configuration into the Copilot-for-IntelliJ config file after every `apm install`, which is error-prone and breaks reproducibility.

The [IDE & Tool Integration — Roadmap](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/integrations/ide-tool-integration/#roadmap) already lists this as planned:

> **JetBrains IDE support:** Native integration with IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, and other JetBrains IDEs

Only **MCP configuration** is missing. All other Copilot primitives (instructions, prompts, agents, skills) already work in JetBrains IDEs through the `.github/` directory that the existing `copilot` target deploys.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add `intellij` as a new MCP runtime target so that `apm install` (and `apm install --mcp`) also writes MCP server entries to the JetBrains-specific Copilot MCP config path.

Expected behavior:

- `apm install` auto-detects whether the JetBrains Copilot config directory exists and wires MCP servers into it alongside the other detected clients.
- `apm install --runtime intellij` explicitly targets IntelliJ only.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Manual copy:** Manually duplicate `.vscode/mcp.json` content into the JetBrains Copilot path after every `apm install`. Error-prone, not reproducible, defeats APM's purpose.
- **Symlink:** Symlink the IntelliJ config to `.vscode/mcp.json`. Fragile across OSes and requires admin elevation on Windows.

issues.title: Add live e2e for Artifactory VCS proxy install
issues.body:
## Gap

`src/apm_cli/deps/artifactory_orchestrator.py` (Adapter + Facade, ~330 lines) has comprehensive **unit** coverage (`tests/unit/deps/test_artifactory_orchestrator.py`, 16 tests) plus 8 other unit-level Artifactory test files, but **zero integration/e2e tests**. No test in the suite ever performs an actual `apm install` against a real Artifactory VCS-proxy endpoint.

This is a pre-existing gap surfaced (not introduced) by the modularization landed in #1223.

## Risk

The orchestrator handles 4 routing branches (explicit FQDN dep, transparent GitHub proxy, registry-only enforcement, ADO-skip) and an HTTP archive download + tarball extraction + APM validation pipeline. Silent drift in any of these would only surface in a customer's CI when their proxy starts returning unexpected payloads or auth shapes.

## Suggested approach

1. Stand up a lightweight HTTP fixture that mimics an Artifactory VCS proxy archive endpoint (serves a static `.tar.gz` of a real APM package) and run an `apm install` flow against it under `tests/integration/`. No live network, deterministic.
2. (Lower-priority) Add an opt-in `@pytest.mark.live_artifactory` test that hits a real proxy when `PROXY_REGISTRY_URL` + `PROXY_REGISTRY_TOKEN` are set in the environment, skipped in default CI.

Option 1 first; option 2 as a separate follow-up.

## Acceptance

- A new test under `tests/integration/test_artifactory_*_e2e.py` that drives `apm install` end-to-end through `ArtifactoryOrchestrator.download_package` against a fixture server.
- Asserts: package files extracted to install path, lockfile entry written with correct `source` URL, validation passed.

issues.title: Add live e2e smoke install for gitlab.com (generic git host)
issues.body:
## Gap

Generic (non-GitHub, non-ADO) git hosts -- GitLab, Gitea, Gogs, Bitbucket -- are routed through `GenericGitBackend` in `src/apm_cli/deps/host_backends.py`. Coverage today:

- Unit: `tests/unit/deps/test_host_backends.py::TestGenericGitBackend` (URL builders).
- Parse/canonicalize: `tests/integration/test_generic_git_url_install.py` exercises generic URL shapes (string and object form, HTTPS/SSH, `gitlab.com/acme/standards` shape) but does NOT perform a live install against a real gitlab.com repo.

No CI job verifies that `apm install gitlab.com/<org>/<repo>` actually clones, validates, and stamps a real public package.

## Risk

Our code path delegates to git for non-GitHub/ADO hosts (no proprietary API). If `git ls-remote` semantics or URL builders silently drift, every GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket consumer breaks with no test failing. This is a thin but high-blast-radius surface.

## Suggested approach

Add an opt-in `@pytest.mark.live_generic` test that:

1. Reads a known stable public APM-shaped repo from gitlab.com (we can publish a tiny fixture at `gitlab.com/microsoft-apm-fixtures/smoke-pkg` or pick an existing public APM package).
2. Runs `apm install gitlab.com/<that-repo>` end-to-end.
3. Asserts: clone succeeded, package validated, lockfile entry has `host: gitlab.com` and a resolved commit SHA.

Skip by default; gate on a new CI job (nightly or weekly) so a flaky upstream doesn't block PRs.

## Out of scope

Gitea/Gogs/Bitbucket smoke installs (separate follow-ups if appetite). gitlab.com is the dominant non-GitHub host and the highest-leverage signal.

issues.title: feat: make `apm update` respect air-gapped environment variables
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to #660, which made `install.sh` configurable for air-gapped / GHE environments via `GITHUB_URL`, `REPO`, and `VERSION` env vars.

## Problem

The `apm update` command (and the underlying version-checker) does not honour those same environment variables:

1. **Version check** -- the latest-version lookup always targets the public GitHub API, ignoring `GITHUB_URL` and `REPO`. In an air-gapped network this call will time out or fail.
2. **Installer download** -- the update command fetches the install script from a hardcoded public URL. Even though the downloaded `install.sh` itself now supports the env vars, the download step has no way to reach the script when the public internet is unavailable.

## Expected behaviour

`apm update` should respect the same `GITHUB_URL`, `REPO`, and `VERSION` env vars that `install.sh` supports, so that:

- The version check queries the correct API host.
- The installer script is fetched from the correct mirror / internal host.
- Setting `VERSION` skips the API call entirely (matching `install.sh` behaviour).

## Additional notes

- The `--check` flag should also work against the configured host.
- The version-checker utility used by the update-available notification on every CLI invocation has the same issue and should be fixed together.

A no-op (no operation) occurs when an agentic workflow runs successfully but determines that no action is required. For example:

- A monitoring workflow that finds everything is healthy

These are successful outcomes, not failures, and help provide transparency into workflow behavior.

issues.title: Support persisting CLI flags via `apm config` (e.g. `allow-protocol-fallback`, `ssh`)
issues.body:
### Problem

Several `apm install` behaviours are controlled by environment variables (e.g. `APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK=1`) or CLI flags (`--ssh`, `--allow-protocol-fallback`). These cannot be persisted via `apm config` — today the only valid config keys are `auto-integrate`, `temp-dir`, and `copilot-cowork-skills-dir`.

This creates friction for users who rely on SSH-based authentication to GitHub rather than PAT tokens. Every `apm install` invocation requires either:

1. Passing `--allow-protocol-fallback` or `--ssh` on every command, or
2. Setting `APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK=1` in a shell profile (`.zshrc`, `.bashrc`, etc.)

Neither option is ideal:

- **Windows users** (PowerShell, cmd) have a very different mechanism for persisting environment variables, making cross-platform instructions inconsistent.
- **Users who prefer not to modify rc files** have no persistent configuration path at all.
- **Teams sharing APM setups** cannot standardise transport preferences without documenting shell-specific workarounds per OS.

### Example scenario

A contributor authenticates to GitHub via SSH keys (no PAT configured). When they run:

```bash
apm install my-package@my-marketplace
```

The install fails because the default HTTPS clone cannot authenticate. The workaround is:

```bash
APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK=1 apm install my-package@my-marketplace
# or
apm install --allow-protocol-fallback my-package@my-marketplace
```

This must be repeated for every install, update, or marketplace operation. There is no way to persist this preference.

### Proposed solution

Extend `apm config set` to accept keys that mirror existing environment variables and CLI flags. For example:

```bash
# Persist protocol fallback preference
apm config set allow-protocol-fallback true

# Persist SSH transport preference
apm config set ssh true
```

Once set, these would be read automatically by all `apm` commands — no environment variable or CLI flag needed.

### Suggested scope

At minimum, the following should be configurable via `apm config`:

| Config key | Env var | CLI flag |
|---|---|---|
| `allow-protocol-fallback` | `APM_ALLOW_PROTOCOL_FALLBACK` | `--allow-protocol-fallback` |
| `ssh` | _(none)_ | `--ssh` |

More broadly, any behaviour currently controlled by an environment variable should have a corresponding `apm config` key, so the configuration surface is unified and discoverable.

### Additional context

- Current valid config keys: `auto-integrate`, `temp-dir`, `copilot-cowork-skills-dir`
- Precedence suggestion: CLI flag > env var > `apm config` > default
