issues.title: Epic: Strengthen install-time supply-chain integrity and policy clarity
issues.body:
## Summary
APM's role is the install-and-integrity layer for agent primitives (skills, agents, instructions, MCP server configs): resolve, pin, hash, lock, verify, and record what gets installed. Agent harnesses own runtime governance -- what a running agent may do once installed. This epic groups work that makes that separation explicit and deepens APM's install-time integrity guarantees.

## Why now
Two recurring sources of confusion and risk:
1. Users are unsure what `apm-policy.yml` governs. Because it exposes allow/deny lists, it can read like a generic permission system, when its actual job is the install contract: which sources are trusted, which versions are installed, and whether artifacts are verified.
2. Agent primitives increasingly reach a developer machine through multiple paths, some outside APM. Teams need APM to (a) state its scope clearly and (b) provide stronger, verifiable integrity for everything it does install.

## Scope (children)
- [ ] #1776 - Clarify what apm-policy.yml governs (docs + positioning)
- [ ] #1778 - Make integrity guarantees legible in apm-policy.yml (two enforceable keys)
- [ ] #1777 - Deepen install-time integrity: SBOM/inventory, provenance, (deferred) signatures
- [ ] #1775 - Surface unmanaged artifacts in apm audit (drift visibility)

## Validated build sequence
Capability ships before the docs that describe it; declarable policy ships only with enforcement behind it.
- Ship 0 (now, docs-only): #1776 scoped to behavior that exists today.
- Prerequisite (gates #1778): fix `policy/inheritance.py::merge_policies`, which silently drops existing `ApmPolicy` fields (`fetch_failure`, `registry_source`, `bin_deploy`) on inheritance, and add a structural guard test so no future policy field can be dropped.
- Wave A: #1775 (extend the existing unmanaged check; add an exclude list) and #1778 (two enforceable keys: `security.integrity.require_hashes`, `security.audit.fail_on_drift`).
- Wave B: a one-line #1776 follow-up once #1775 ships; #1777 SBOM/inventory export and provenance schema.
- Deferred: #1777 signature verification, until a signing ecosystem for agent primitives exists and there is concrete demand.

## Out of scope
Runtime permission enforcement, sandboxing, or controlling what a running agent may do once installed. Those are owned by the agent harness. APM acts only at install and configuration time. Building or operating signing infrastructure is out of scope; APM consumes standard signatures where present.

## Definition of done
All four child issues closed; docs and policy consistently describe APM as the install-and-integrity layer; new integrity capabilities shipped with tests and CHANGELOG entries; every declarable policy key is backed by enforcement at the time it ships.

issues.title: Surface unmanaged artifacts in apm audit (drift visibility)
issues.body:
Part of #1774

## Problem
Agent primitives (skills, agents, MCP server configs) can land in a workspace through paths other than APM - for example, configuration that an agent harness installs by default. Those artifacts carry no APM lockfile entry. Teams currently have no single place to see what is installed in a workspace that APM did not pin.

## What to do
- EXTEND the existing unmanaged-files check (src/apm_cli/policy/policy_checks.py, `_check_unmanaged_files`). Do not build a parallel scan: a second overlapping report on the same files produces alarm fatigue and trains users to ignore `apm audit`. There must be ONE unified unmanaged-files report.
- Enrich each finding with a `reason`: "not tracked in apm.lock.yaml" (factual wording; avoid "no integrity evidence" jargon) and, where applicable, "matches deny rule".
- Classify the primitive type (skill / agent / instruction / mcp) so a user can triage. Classify lazily - only the small set of files already flagged as unmanaged, never the whole tree.
- Where an unmanaged artifact matches an apm-policy `deny` rule (dependencies.deny or mcp.deny), surface it as a conflict for a human to resolve. Report only; do not remove it or block anything at runtime. Reuse the SAME deny glob matcher the dependency/MCP denylist checks use - factor a shared helper, do not write a second matcher.
- Add an `exclude:` list to the `unmanaged_files:` policy so teams can suppress known harness-managed paths. Without this, the check fires forever on harness-managed files and becomes noise.
- Keep this strictly to observation of the local workspace (files on disk). Do not read or interpret any harness configuration or policy.

## How
- Reuse the existing drift tree-walk rather than a second rglob over the governance dirs.
- Guard against symlinks: do not follow symlinks out of the workspace during traversal (is_file / symlink guard), with a test for a symlink pointing outside the project.
- Tests: deny-conflict (dependency and mcp paths) via the shared matcher; primitive-type classification; exclude-list suppression; symlink guard; and a non-duplication test proving a file is not reported twice.

## Framing
This is DRIFT / divergence visibility, not supply-chain-attack prevention: the lockfile is hand-editable YAML, so this does not defend against a forged lockfile. It answers "what is here that APM did not put here?" honestly.

## Why
Gives teams visibility into the full install surface, and demonstrates the value of routing integrity-critical primitives through APM, where they get pinned and hashed. As registries become the source of truth for installs, "is anything here the lockfile did not put here?" becomes the core drift question.

## Notes
Builds on the existing content-integrity / drift audit. ASCII only.

issues.title: Clarify what apm-policy.yml governs (docs + positioning)
issues.body:
Part of #1774

## Problem
`apm-policy.yml` exposes allow/deny lists for dependencies and MCP configs. In practice this can read like a general-purpose permission system, so users ask what APM actually governs and whether it overlaps with controls their agent harness already provides. It does not overlap: APM governs installation and integrity (which sources are trusted, which versions install, whether artifacts are verified, what the lockfile records), while the agent harness governs runtime behavior.

## What to do
- Reframe the policy reference page (docs/src/content/docs/reference/policy-schema.md) to lead with APM's purpose in plain terms: it is the install policy for agent primitives - which sources are trusted, which versions install, and what the lockfile records and verifies.
- Add a short "What apm-policy.yml does NOT govern" section: runtime permissions, sandboxing, what a running agent may do, and harness marketplace enablement. Those are owned by the agent harness.
- Document the meaning of `deny` precisely: APM will not install a denied artifact. `deny` is an install-time decision, not a runtime block.
- Add a one-line FAQ entry: "Does my harness's managed configuration replace APM?" Answer: "No. apm-policy.yml controls what gets installed; your harness controls what runs; they do not overlap."

## Scope discipline
Document only behavior that exists in the released CLI at merge time. The audit visibility for a denied artifact that is present from another source lands with the audit work in this epic (#1775); a one-line follow-up will add that sentence here once it ships. Do not describe unbuilt behavior.

## Why
This removes the most common point of confusion and establishes a consistent vocabulary that the rest of the epic builds on. It is the cheapest, highest-leverage clarity win and can ship first.

## Notes
Docs-only; no code change expected. Keep prose pragmatic and short per the repo docs guidelines. ASCII only.

issues.title: Deepen install-time integrity: signature verification, SBOM, provenance
issues.body:
Part of #1774

## Problem
APM already produces a lockfile (apm.lock.yaml) with per-file SHA-256 hashes and a content-drift audit. For regulated and security-conscious teams, content hashing alone is not enough: they need a machine-readable bill of materials for what was installed, recorded provenance for where each artifact came from, and - once a signing ecosystem exists - a way to verify who produced an artifact.

## What to do (phased, in this order)
1. SBOM / inventory export FIRST. Serialize the existing lockfile into a standard format (CycloneDX, optionally SPDX) as a FORMAT on the existing lockfile-export concept: `apm lock export --format cyclonedx`. This is an inventory export, not a completeness or security attestation - it reports exactly what the lockfile records (source, resolved commit, hashes), and is honest that license/CVE data is not present unless sourced from each dep's manifest.
2. Provenance schema SECOND. Formalize the fields the lockfile already records per dependency (resolved_commit, resolved_ref, resolved_url, resolved_at, hashes) into a documented provenance schema. This is re-serialization of data APM already captures - no new capture, and no self-signed attestation (a self-attestation proves nothing to a third-party verifier).
3. Signature verification LAST, and deferred. Defer until a real signing ecosystem for agent primitives exists and there is concrete demand (a useful bar: ~5 community requests). When built, APM CONSUMES standard signatures (for example verifying a signed git tag via `git verify-tag`); it does NOT build or run signing infrastructure. Surface an informational `verified | unverified | none` status; do not gate installs on it until signing is real and a policy key ships together with the enforcement.

## How
- New `src/apm_cli/export/` package for SBOM/provenance serialization. Do not bolt this onto the already-large commands/audit.py.
- Read from lockfile-recorded hashes ONLY; never re-hash the filesystem at export time.
- SBOM output MUST be deterministic: sorted components and a pinned/injected timestamp so the same lockfile yields byte-identical output (golden-file test).
- Component identity: pkg:github/owner/repo@<resolved_commit> for git deps; pkg:generic/<name>@<content_hash> for local.
- For signature verification, extract a verifier behind an interface so it can be tested with a fixture signed repo and a fake verifier (pass / fail / absent), without network and without mocking the security boundary away.
- Each phase ships with tests, docs, and a CHANGELOG entry.

## Why
This is the consumer-side assurance layer APM is positioned to own at the package level: with registries emerging as the distribution layer for agent primitives, the inventory/provenance export is what compliance teams will demand, and verification (when it lands) consumes the registry's attestations rather than competing with them. It complements the runtime controls that agent harnesses provide; it does not duplicate them.

## Out of scope
Runtime enforcement of any kind. Building or operating signing infrastructure. APM verifies and records at install time; it does not control what a running agent may do.

issues.title: Make supply-chain guarantees legible in apm-policy.yml (additive integrity keys)
issues.body:
Part of #1774

## Problem
Today `apm-policy.yml` expresses governance mainly through allow/deny/require lists. Two integrity guarantees APM can enforce at install time TODAY - content-hash verification and content drift - are not first-class, declarable policy. The file under-represents what APM already enforces, which feeds the confusion about its purpose.

## Prerequisite (must land first)
`policy/inheritance.py::merge_policies` currently rebuilds `ApmPolicy` without carrying every field, so some existing fields (`fetch_failure`, `registry_source`, `bin_deploy`) are silently dropped when a policy inherits via `extends`. Any new policy field added below would hit the same trap. Before adding keys:
- Fix `merge_policies` to carry all `ApmPolicy` fields.
- Add a structural guard test asserting the set of merged fields covers every `ApmPolicy` dataclass field (exempt `name`/`version`/`extends`), so future fields cannot be silently dropped.

## What to do
Add two additive, optional keys - and ONLY keys backed by enforcement that exists today. No breaking changes: existing policies keep working unchanged, and every new key defaults to off.
- `security.integrity.require_hashes` - require lockfile content hashes for all installs. A MISSING hash is a failure (fail-closed), not a silent pass.
- `security.audit.fail_on_drift` - make `apm audit` fail when workspace content drifts from the lockfile. Sits alongside the existing `security.audit.on_install`.

Nest both under the existing `security:` namespace. Do not introduce new top-level namespaces, and do not add a top-level `audit:` key that collides with `security.audit`.

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)
Do not add declarable keys for capabilities that are not enforceable yet (signatures, provenance, SBOM export). A policy key that validates and warns but enforces nothing creates false assurance - a team could declare it, pass CI, and be verifying nothing. Those keys ship together WITH their enforcement in the integrity issue (#1777), never ahead of it.

## How (TDD)
- Extend the policy schema and parser (src/apm_cli/policy/) with the two optional keys; default off to preserve current behavior.
- Wire `require_hashes` to the existing content-hash verification path so a missing hash fails closed.
- Tests that MUST exist before the keys land:
  - Golden-file parse-equivalence: load every fixture under tests/fixtures/policy/, parse to `ApmPolicy`, canonicalize, diff against a checked-in golden - proves old policies parse identically (the "additive / non-breaking" claim).
  - Structural merge-completeness: assert fields handled in `merge_policies` == `dataclasses.fields(ApmPolicy)` minus the exempt set.
  - None-transparency on merge: a child that is silent on a new key does not override a parent that sets it.
  - Fail-closed: a lockfile entry with a missing hash fails under `require_hashes: true`.
- Add fixtures under tests/fixtures/policy/.
- Update the policy reference page in docs.
- Add a CHANGELOG entry (additive feature).

## Why
Makes APM's enforceable integrity guarantees declarable and visible in the same file teams already use, reinforcing that the policy is the install contract. With registries on the horizon, hash-pinned installs are the near-term trust anchor, so `require_hashes` is the highest-value declarable control.

issues.title: [BUG] devDependencies.mcp entries written by --dev --mcp are silently ignored by apm install
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install --dev --mcp <name>` writes the MCP server entry to `devDependencies.mcp` in `apm.yml`, `.mcp.json`, and `apm.lock.yaml`. However, a subsequent `apm install` (e.g. after a container rebuild or fresh clone) does not restore `devDependencies.mcp` entries to `.mcp.json`. The MCP server is effectively lost on re-installation.

**To Reproduce**

1. Run `apm install --dev --mcp test-server --transport stdio -- echo test`
2. Confirm `test-server` appears in `apm.yml`, `.mcp.json`, and `apm.lock.yaml`.
3. Delete `.mcp.json` entirely (simulating a fresh install environment)
4. Run `apm install`
5. Observe: `.mcp.json` is restored with `dependencies.mcp` entries only — `test-server` is missing. The `test-server` entry is also removed from `apm.lock.yaml` at this point.
6. Run `apm install --dev --mcp test-server --transport stdio -- echo test` again to attempt recovery
7. Observe: `[i] MCP server 'test-server' unchanged` — because the entry already exists in `apm.yml`, APM considers it a no-op and does not write it to `.mcp.json`

**Expected behavior**

`apm install` should process `devDependencies.mcp` entries and restore them to `.mcp.json`, just as it does for `dependencies.mcp`.

At minimum, step 6 above should not silently no-op. If the entry is declared in `apm.yml` but absent from `.mcp.json`, `apm install --dev --mcp` (or `apm install`) should write it.

**Environment**
- OS: Linux
- APM Version: 0.20.0 (43a00c2)

**Additional context**

The `devDependencies.mcp` implementation is asymmetric and incomplete in several ways:

- **Stale removal works, restore does not**: If a server is removed from `apm.yml` entirely, `apm install` correctly detects it as stale and emits `[i] Removed stale MCP server '<name>' from .mcp.json`. But the reverse — restoring a `devDependencies.mcp` entry that is missing from `.mcp.json` — never happens.

- **Silent footgun with no recovery path**: `apm install --dev --mcp` appears to work (the server is registered in `.mcp.json` immediately), but once `.mcp.json` is regenerated by `apm install`, the entry is gone and cannot be recovered. Re-running `apm install --dev --mcp <name>` silently no-ops with `[i] MCP server '<name>' unchanged` because the entry is already in `apm.yml`. The only workaround is to manually edit `.mcp.json` or move the entry to `dependencies.mcp`.

Note: `--dev` works correctly for APM packages (`devDependencies.apm`), so users reasonably expect `--dev --mcp` to behave analogously. Related: #1549 (`apm uninstall` couldn't remove `--dev` plugins), suggesting `devDependencies` handling has been historically incomplete.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Generate a skill for prompt entries when targeting Codex
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

apm supports a `prompt` primitive, which is compiled into a slash command for Claude Code. Codex has no equivalent concept, so apm currently ignores `prompt` entries when targeting Codex.

As a result, any apm package that ships functionality as a `prompt` is effectively unusable on Codex: the author's intent is silently dropped, and a Codex user has no way to invoke that behaviour.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

When targeting Codex, generate a skill for each `prompt` entry instead of ignoring it.

A skill can be invoked explicitly on Codex, so the package author's functionality stays reachable. To reduce the risk of the model running the command on its own, the generated skill `description` can state that it should be invoked only when the user explicitly asks for it (for example: `Invoke only when the user explicitly asks for it.`).

This keeps existing `prompt`-based packages working across both Claude Code and Codex without changing the package format.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Keep ignoring `prompt` on Codex (current behaviour).** Packages that rely on `prompt` remain broken for Codex users, with no signal to the author.
- **Wait for native command/prompt support in Codex.** If Codex gains an explicit command or prompt mechanism, a future apm version can map `prompt` onto it directly. Until then, generating a skill is a working stopgap, and the migration path stays open.

**Additional context**

Generating a skill is meant as a compatibility shim, not the long-term target. The skill `description` is the main lever for controlling auto-invocation, so its wording matters and may need tuning.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-15
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-15
**APM Version**: 0.20.0 (43a00c2)
**Commands Inspected**: 56 (all top-level commands and their subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `apm update --target` omits `kiro` from the listed valid values

- **Command**: `apm update --target`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag help text lists only `claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, codex, opencode, gemini`, but `kiro` is a supported target used by other commands (`apm install`, `apm compile`). The documentation at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md` correctly includes `kiro`. This is a documentation drift between the CLI help and the reference docs.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm update --help
    -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for (e.g. claude,
                         copilot, cursor, windsurf, codex, opencode,
                         gemini). Comma-separated for multiple: ...
  ```
  vs `apm install --help` (which is complete):
  ```
  Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all.
  ```
  vs docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md`, line 46):
  ```
  Accepts a single value (claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, kiro, codex, opencode, gemini)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help text for `apm update` to list all valid values including `kiro` and `agent-skills`, matching the format used by `apm install` and `apm compile`.

---

#### 2. `apm deps update --target` omits `kiro` from both the value list and the `all` expansion

- **Command**: `apm deps update --target`
- **Problem**: The `--target` help text does not include `kiro` in its list of valid targets, and the `all` expansion is described as `copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf` (7 targets), while `apm install --target all` expands to `copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro` (8 targets). The `kiro` target is fully supported by the install pipeline.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps update --help
    -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                         copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                         gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all. ...
                         'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf
                         (excludes agent-skills)
  ```
  vs `apm install --help`:
  ```
  'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `kiro` to the list of accepted values in the `--target` flag description for `apm deps update`, and update the `all` expansion description to include `kiro`.

---

#### 3. Stale deprecation deadline in `apm init --plugin` runtime warning

- **Command**: `apm init --plugin`
- **Problem**: When invoked at runtime, `apm init --plugin` prints a deprecation warning saying the flag "will be removed in v0.16". The current CLI version is 0.20.0, meaning the removal deadline has already passed by four releases. This confuses users who see a flag still present well past its stated removal date.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm init --plugin
  [!] 'apm init --plugin' is deprecated. Run: apm plugin init
      Legacy flag will be removed in v0.16.
  ```
  Current version:
  ```
  $ apm --version
  Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.20.0 (43a00c2)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either remove the flag (it is past the stated deadline), or update the warning to a version-neutral statement such as "This flag will be removed in a future release."

---

#### 4. `apm cache clean` has two flags with identical descriptions performing the same action

- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: The command exposes both `-f/--force` and `-y/--yes`, both documented identically as "Skip confirmation prompt". This is confusing for two reasons: (1) having two flags with the exact same help text and behavior is redundant, and (2) `--force` is used throughout the APM CLI to mean "overwrite locally-authored files on collision" (see `apm install --force`, `apm update --force`), which is a different semantic from "skip confirmation prompt". Using `--force` to skip a prompt is inconsistent with its meaning elsewhere.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
  ```
  Compare with `apm install --force`:
  ```
  --force  Overwrite locally-authored files on collision and deploy despite
           critical security findings
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f/--force` from `apm cache clean` and keep only `-y/--yes` for confirmation skipping, consistent with `apm deps clean --yes` and `apm update --yes`. This aligns `--force` semantics across the CLI.

---

### Low Severity

#### 5. `apm mcp install --help` displays options in non-standard format

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: Unlike all other APM subcommands, `apm mcp install` does not list its accepted options in the standard Click `Options:` block. Instead, it appends a freeform "Common options" paragraph at the bottom of the help text without proper flag formatting. Users cannot discover available flags without reading `apm install --help` separately.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Format the forwarded options as proper help entries with consistent spacing, or list the most-used forwarded options using standard Click option declarations. The freeform paragraph is hard to read and breaks the consistent `--option  Description` format users expect from all other commands.

---

#### 6. `--verbose` flag description wording is inconsistent across commands

- **Command**: Multiple commands
- **Problem**: The `-v/--verbose` flag description varies in phrasing. While some variation is appropriate, the descriptions show inconsistent style across commands.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm init:         Show detailed output
  apm install:      Show detailed installation information
  apm update:       Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics
  apm uninstall:    Show detailed removal information
  apm audit:        Show all findings including harmless ones
  apm mcp search:   Show detailed output
  apm run:          Show detailed output
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Adopt a consistent short template for commands where verbose simply increases output detail (e.g., "Show detailed output"), and reserve longer descriptions only where verbose genuinely changes the output semantics.

---

#### 7. `apm targets --help` usage line implies a required subcommand but the command is self-executing

- **Command**: `apm targets`
- **Problem**: The help usage line reads `Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, which suggests a subcommand is expected (standard Click group pattern). However, `apm targets` runs successfully without a subcommand and displays the target resolution table. Users may assume a subcommand is required.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm targets --help
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project...
  ```
  Yet `apm targets` (no subcommand) runs and prints the table correctly.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either convert `apm targets` from a Click group to a regular command (since it has no active subcommands), or clarify in the help text that `apm targets` can be invoked directly without a subcommand.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **`apm init`** -- deprecation warnings for `--plugin` and `--marketplace` present in help text; target flag documented correctly
- **`apm install`** -- extensive flag set documented accurately; all targets including `kiro` and `agent-skills` listed; clear error messages
- **`apm uninstall`** -- clean and concise
- **`apm compile`** -- all targets including `kiro` listed; flags documented accurately
- **`apm run`** / **`apm preview`** -- consistent flags and descriptions
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/why/clean`** -- subcommand table in docs matches CLI
- **`apm mcp list/search/show`** -- help text accurate and consistent
- **`apm config / get / set`** -- well-documented; bare `apm config` invocation shows table as documented
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`** -- flags accurate
- **`apm cache info/prune`** -- clean
- **`apm audit`** -- extensive flag set documented accurately
- **`apm doctor`** -- concise and accurate
- **`apm experimental enable/disable/list/reset`** -- consistent across subcommands
- **`apm find`**, **`apm lock`**, **`apm outdated`**, **`apm pack`**, **`apm prune`**, **`apm publish`**, **`apm search`**, **`apm self-update`**, **`apm unpack`**, **`apm view`** -- all clean
- **Error handling** -- all tested invalid invocations produce clean error messages (no stack traces):
  - `apm install --nonexistent-flag` -> "No such option" + usage hint
  - `apm deps info` (missing PACKAGE) -> "Missing argument 'PACKAGE'" + usage hint
  - `apm config set` (missing KEY) -> "Missing argument 'KEY'" + usage hint
  - `apm config list` -> "No such command 'list'" + usage hint

issues.title: Evaluate a `devin` target alias for windsurf (post Devin Desktop rebrand)
issues.body:
## Context

Windsurf (the editor APM targets via `--target windsurf`) has been rebranded by Cognition as **Devin Desktop**. Devin's documentation now uses the shared `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout and cites the agentskills.io standard.

This is a deliberate follow-up split off from #1520. #1520 converges only the **skills** primitive onto `.agents/skills/` and intentionally keeps the target name `windsurf` to stay surgical.

## What to evaluate here

1. **Alias vs rename.** Add a `devin` alias that resolves to the existing `windsurf` `TargetProfile`, rather than renaming — `--target windsurf` appears in users' `apm.yml` today, so a hard rename is breaking.
2. **Config-surface drift.** Confirm whether Devin Desktop moves any of the non-skills paths that windsurf currently uses:
   - `.windsurf/rules/`, `.windsurf/workflows/`, hooks
   - the `.codeium/windsurf/` user-scope dir
   - MCP config location
   As of the #1520 work, only the skills path was confirmed-moved by Devin's docs; the rest were unconfirmed and left as-is.
3. **Docs.** Once the alias lands, update the targets matrix and authoring docs to mention the Devin Desktop name.

## Why deferred

Devin Desktop's full config surface is new and not yet stable. Aliasing should wait until the rules/workflows/mcp locations are confirmed, so we don't ship an alias that immediately needs revision.

Refs: #1520. Devin skills docs: https://docs.devin.ai/product-guides/skills

issues.title: fix(ci): spec-conformance Mode B gate fails open on unresolvable merge-base
issues.body:
## Summary

The OpenAPM "Spec conformance gate" (Mode B silent-extension detector) can **fail open** -- it silently passes a PR that adds uncited substantive code under a normative critical path, instead of firing. A governance gate that passes without evaluating is a supply-chain-integrity hole.

## Root cause

Two compounding factors:

1. `.github/workflows/spec-conformance.yml` checks out with `actions/checkout@v4` and **no `fetch-depth: 0`**. The default checkout is shallow, so `origin/main` history may not be present.
2. `tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh` tries to deepen on demand (`git fetch --depth=50`, then `--unshallow`), but when it still cannot resolve the merge-base it does:

   ```sh
   if [ -z "${MB:-}" ]; then
     echo "[!] mode_b: cannot resolve merge-base against $BASE; skipping"
     exit 0
   fi
   ```

   `exit 0` means **skip == pass**. Whether the gate actually evaluates a given PR becomes luck of the checkout.

## Evidence

- PR #1794 (declarable integrity keys) got a real evaluation -> Mode B fired (red), correctly: net-new substantive lines under `policy/` + `install/` with no spec citation.
- PR #1793 (surface unmanaged artifacts) initially showed the gate **green** while its log contained `[!] mode_b: cannot resolve merge-base against origin/main; skipping` -- a non-evaluation, not a real pass. On a later head it resolved the base and correctly fired. Same diff class, opposite gate outcome, purely from checkout depth.

## Impact

A future PR that adds uncited enforcement under a critical path can merge clean if its checkout happens to be shallow and the merge-base is unresolvable. The gate is supposed to be the backstop that forces either a spec citation or an explicit `apm-spec-waiver:` trailer; fail-open removes that guarantee non-deterministically.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `fetch-depth: 0` to the checkout step in `spec-conformance.yml` so the merge-base is deterministically resolvable in CI (root-cause fix -- makes the skip branch unreachable in CI).
2. Defense in depth: when running under CI (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`), make the unresolvable-merge-base branch **fail closed** (`exit 1` with a clear diagnostic) instead of `exit 0`. Preserve the local-dev skip (`exit 0`) so `bash tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh` on a shallow local clone stays ergonomic.
3. Update `tests/spec_conformance/test_mode_b_detector.py` to lock the new CI-fail-closed invariant.

## Notes

- This is decoupled from #1794/#1793: both are being resolved by authoring spec citations, which clears Mode B via its spec-concurrent short-circuit regardless of this fix. This issue is about closing the gate hole for all future PRs.
- Report-only framing: this is a CI-integrity correctness fix, not a behaviour change to the spec or the CLI.

Part of the install/integrity governance hardening tracked under #1774.

issues.title: Tighten MCP `extra` passthrough to an explicit `extra:` block (fail-closed authoring contract, with deprecation)
issues.body:
## Context

Split off from the trust-boundary review of PR #1765 (#1670). That PR adds MCP "extra" key passthrough and lands the **modeled-field-name denylist** (the actual exploit closure: keys named like `command`/`url`/`type`/`env`/`headers` can never be injected into an adapter config path). It intentionally **keeps** today's ergonomics: bare top-level unknown keys (e.g. `oauth:`) still pass through, at parity with the existing trust already given to `command`/`url`/`env`.

This follow-up tracks the stronger **fail-closed posture** the supply-chain lens recommended but which we deferred because it is a **breaking authoring-contract change**.

## The change to design

Require MCP server extras to live under an explicit `extra:` block and **drop + warn** on bare unknown top-level keys, instead of preserving them.

- Today (and in all three current doc examples) extras are written as bare top-level keys:
  ```yaml
  mcp:
    some-server:
      oauth: { ... }
  ```
- Target contract:
  ```yaml
  mcp:
    some-server:
      extra:
        oauth: { ... }
  ```

## Why this is `needs-design` / `breaking-change`

- It changes a **documented** authoring surface -- bare `oauth:` stops being honored. Existing `apm.yml` files break silently unless we stage it.
- Needs a **deprecation path**: ship one release that warns on bare unknown keys ("move under `extra:`; bare passthrough will be removed in a future release") while still honoring them, then flip to drop-and-warn in a later release.
- Needs the **3 doc examples rewritten** and a migration note.

## Why deferred (not done in #1765)

The denylist already closes the concrete injection edge and is non-breaking, so it shipped now. Flipping the authoring contract is a separate posture decision that deserves its own ratification and a deprecation window, rather than riding inside a passthrough fix.

## Also consider (from the same review, lower priority)

- Per-harness scoping of broadcast extras (clientId/callbackPort currently broadcast to all targets).
- A secret-shaped-value scan on extras (warn names only, never values -- current behavior).
- `to_dict` collision debug-warn.

Refs #1670, PR #1765.

issues.title: Sweep lockfile cross-target skill maps onto `.agents/skills/` for converged targets (windsurf/cursor/opencode)
issues.body:
## Context

When five targets converged their skills onto the shared `.agents/skills/` deploy path (via `deploy_root=".agents"` on the skills `PrimitiveMapping`), the **pack-time** cross-target remap in `src/apm_cli/.../lockfile_enrichment.py` (`_CROSS_TARGET_MAPS`) was only updated for **codex**. The other converged targets still remap `.github/skills/` -> `.<client>/skills/`:

- `cursor` -> `.cursor/skills/`
- `opencode` -> `.opencode/skills/`
- `windsurf` -> `.windsurf/skills/` (as of #1520, windsurf's *deploy* path moved to `.agents/skills/` but its cross-map was intentionally left untouched to keep that PR bounded)

So there is a **pack-vs-deploy drift**: these targets deploy skills to `.agents/skills/` at install time, but the lockfile enrichment rewrites paths to the per-client dir at pack time. Only codex is internally consistent.

## What to evaluate

Sweep `_CROSS_TARGET_MAPS` so all converged targets (windsurf, cursor, opencode -- and audit gemini) map skills to `.agents/skills/`, matching codex and their actual deploy path. Update the affected enrichment tests.

## Why `needs-design` (not a blind find/replace)

Existing `apm.lock.yaml` files in the wild may already reference the old per-client paths. Decide whether this needs a lockfile-version bump, a back-compat read path, or a re-pack note. Confirm the `--legacy-skill-paths` escape hatch interacts correctly (legacy mode should keep the per-client cross-map).

## Out of scope

Functional skill loading is unaffected today -- both runtimes scan `.agents/skills/`, and this is a pack-time path-string concern, not a deploy break. This issue is about removing the latent inconsistency, not fixing a user-visible bug.

Refs #1520.

issues.title: MCP extra passthrough: tighten to explicit `extra:`-only (fail-closed) with deprecation path
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to #1670 / PR #1765, which added a harness-specific **`extra` passthrough** to `MCPDependency` so keys like Claude Code's remote-MCP `oauth` block (`clientId` / `callbackPort`) survive `apm.yml` -> generated `.mcp.json` rendering instead of being silently dropped.

PR #1765 ships the **bare-key** ergonomics: any unknown top-level key on a self-defined MCP dependency is auto-captured into `extra` (matching the documented `oauth:` examples). It also adds a **modeled-field-name denylist** (a passthrough value can never shadow/redirect `name`/`transport`/`command`/`url`/`headers`/`env`/... or the Codex `http_headers` alias) so the concrete injection edge is closed.

## The deferred tightening

The supply-chain-security review lens flagged that **auto-capturing bare unknown keys is fail-open**: a transitive dependency package's `apm.yml` is parsed straight through `from_dict`, and the prior contract *dropped* unknown keys (fail-closed) whereas the new contract *preserves* them. The denylist closes the high-severity shadow/redirect edge, but the residual posture question remains: should passthrough require an **explicit `extra:` block** and **drop bare unknown keys with a warning** (fail-closed), so only keys the author deliberately nests under `extra:` flow through?

This was deliberately **sequenced out of #1765** by maintainer decision (Option B + denylist) because it is a **user-facing authoring-contract change** (the documented examples use bare top-level `oauth:`), i.e. a breaking change that needs a deprecation path rather than a silent flip.

## Proposed scope (this issue)

1. Introduce explicit `extra:` as the **only** sanctioned passthrough surface.
2. **Deprecation window**: keep capturing bare unknown keys, but emit a deprecation warning instructing authors to nest them under `extra:`. After the window, drop bare unknown keys (restore fail-closed drop-and-warn).
3. Rewrite the three doc examples (`install-mcp-servers.md`, `reference/manifest-schema.md`, `apm-usage/dependencies.md`) to nest `oauth:` under `extra:`.
4. Update `test_mcp_from_dict_unknown_keys.py` expectations accordingly.

## Also captured here (deferred from #1765, non-blocking)

- **Per-harness scoping**: `extra: { copilot: {...}, codex: {...} }` so a Claude-specific block is not broadcast to every target.
- **Secret-shaped-value scan**: warn when an `extra` *value* looks like a token/secret being written to a world-readable config.
- **`to_dict` collision debug-warn**: emit a debug log when an `extra` key shadows a known field during re-serialization.

## Why not now

Per the PR #1765 maintainer decision, #1765 keeps bare-key ergonomics + denylist (closes the concrete trust-boundary edge) and defers this fail-closed contract tightening here so the posture change is explicit, deprecation-gated, and reviewable on its own.

/cc the #1670 thread.

issues.title: Let authors target native context files (root or nested CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md), not just .claude/rules
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

A package author cannot choose where compiled guidance lands on the destination axis: the harness's native context file (`CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, root or nested in a subdirectory) versus a path-scoped rule file (`.claude/rules/`). Every `instructions` primitive compiles to a rule file. For Claude that is `.claude/rules/<name>.md`, with `applyTo:` translated to `paths:`, and the instructions section is then deduplicated out of `CLAUDE.md`. So for Claude, instruction content can only ever become a path-scoped rule.

These placements behave differently, and both native forms are useful:

- `.claude/rules/<name>.md` with `paths:` is path-scoped and lazily loaded. Claude pulls it in only when it touches a matching file.
- A root `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` is always-on. It stays in context on every turn, and Claude re-injects it after `/compact`.
- A nested `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (placed in a subdirectory) is the agent-native directory-scoping mechanism. Every major agent loads it when working anywhere in that subtree, and it survives the same way the root file does. This is directory scoping, distinct from the glob and extension scoping of a `paths:` rule.

Three use cases are blocked:

1. **Root, always-on.** Short cross-cutting rules an agent benefits from on every turn (tool-selection conventions, repo-wide layout, "use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations"). `applyTo: "**/*"` does not help: it still compiles to a rule file and is still deduplicated out of the root file.
2. **Nested, directory-scoped.** Guidance that should hold across a whole subtree (a service or package directory) and load whenever the agent works anywhere under it. The agent-native nested context file fits this exactly, but APM never targets it for Claude. The content is forced into a `paths:`-globbed rule instead.
3. **Troubleshooting and diagnostic sessions, no file editing.** A support-engineer agent diagnosing live infrastructure (database health, operator state, cluster logs) never opens a source file, so a `paths:`-globbed rule in `.claude/rules/` never fires and the skill trigger it carries is never seen. The guidance and its skill triggers must be always-on in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` to be reachable at all. APM can ship the troubleshooting skills, but it cannot place their triggers where a non-editing session will load them. See [IldarMinaev/engineer-workspace](https://github.com/IldarMinaev/engineer-workspace), which deploys PostgreSQL, Patroni, and Kubernetes diagnostic skills through APM for read-only support work of this kind.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A primitive distinct from `instructions`, provisionally `agentsmd` (or `context-file`), whose contract is "this content belongs in the harness's native context file," with an author-declared destination directory.

- The author declares a preferred folder (for example `dir: "."` for the root file, or `dir: "services/payments"` for a nested one), and APM writes the content into that directory's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`.
- On Claude the content lands in the chosen `CLAUDE.md` and is exempt from the `.claude/rules/` deduplication. It is meant to live in the context file, so the dedup pass must leave it there.
- On harnesses that already fold instructions into a context file (`AGENTS.md` for Codex and OpenCode, `GEMINI.md`), the primitive maps onto the existing context-file path; nested directories use that harness's nested-`AGENTS.md` convention.
- The difference from `instructions` is the destination (a native context file, root or nested), not the scoping strategy. `--single-agents` collapses nested files into the root, as it does today.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **`apm compile --no-dedup` / `--force-instructions`.** This keeps the instructions section in `CLAUDE.md`, but it is a consumer-side, all-or-nothing flag rather than a per-primitive author declaration, and it duplicates content into both `.claude/rules/` and the context file. That is the opposite of choosing a single destination.
- **`applyTo:` distributed placement.** APM already places nested `AGENTS.md` for fold-into-root targets via `applyTo:`, but for Claude the matching content is deduplicated out of the nested `CLAUDE.md` and only the rule file survives. The nested-context-file path is reachable for Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode, but not for Claude. That is exactly the gap.
- **Spec Kit constitution.** The constitution block is always written to the top of `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, so it covers always-on root content. But it is a single project-level block tied to `memory/constitution.md`, not a reusable primitive an upstream package can ship through `apm dependencies`, and it has no nested form.
- **Path-scoped rules alone.** Glob scoping is correct for "true when editing X." It is the wrong tool for always-on rules and for whole-subtree rules, and it is not re-injected after `/compact` the way a context file is.

**Additional context**

The motivating case is a large monorepo consuming platform conventions through `apm dependencies`. A few cross-cutting rules belong always-on in the root file, per-service conventions belong in that service's nested `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`, and stack-specific how-tos stay in path-scoped rules and skills. Today only the last is expressible for Claude.

Path scoping also assumes the agent reaches a matching file. Read-only sessions such as incident triage, infrastructure diagnostics, and support work break that assumption: there is no file event to trigger a `paths:` rule, so any guidance gated behind one stays unreachable. That guidance has to live in the always-on context file.

Relevant current behaviour:

- the Claude-Code deduplication that omits the instructions section from `CLAUDE.md` (`apm compile --target claude`, docs `producer/compile.md`, closes #1138 / #1146);
- distributed placement driven by `applyTo:` (`concepts/primitives-and-targets.md`, "Where compiled context files land");
- the compatibility matrix where `instructions / claude = native` resolves to `.claude/rules/<name>.md`.

issues.title: perf(marketplace): optional ADO REST metadata client (/_apis/git/repositories/) to avoid clone-based fetch
issues.body:
## Context

Split out from #1010 as a deferred performance optimization.

ADO-hosted marketplace sources currently fetch metadata (`apm.yml`, description, version) through the **generic-git path** (`_fetch_git` in `src/apm_cli/marketplace/client.py`), which resolves files via a git checkout/clone rather than a host REST API. This is **correct and works today** — GitHub and GitLab simply have dedicated REST fetchers (`_fetch_github`, `_fetch_gitlab`) that avoid a clone for single-file metadata reads.

## Ask

Add an optional ADO REST metadata fetcher using the Azure DevOps Git API (`GET https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_apis/git/repositories/{repo}/items?...`) so ADO marketplace metadata reads skip the subprocess-git clone, matching the GitHub/GitLab fast path. Route it through the existing `_FETCHERS` dispatch and reuse `AuthResolver` ADO auth (`ADO_APM_PAT` / `az` bearer).

## Why this is deferred (not blocking)

- The generic-git path already fetches ADO marketplace metadata correctly. This is **latency/efficiency only**, not a correctness or capability gap.
- No demand evidence: this is a maintainer-identified optimization, not a user-reported pain.
- ADO marketplace authoring/consumption is otherwise first-class at HEAD (sourceBase composition, host classification, auth routing, install e2e all shipped and tested).

## Acceptance

- [ ] ADO single-file metadata reads use the REST items API instead of a clone, behind the existing fetcher dispatch.
- [ ] Falls back to the generic-git path on REST failure / offline (no regression).
- [ ] Auth via `AuthResolver` ADO context; token never logged.
- [ ] Unit + integration coverage parity with the GitLab REST fetcher.

Labels: theme/portability, area/marketplace, type/performance, status/accepted (deferred, no milestone).

issues.title: [BUG] marketplace add --ref: registered ref not propagated to relative plugin source resolution
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a marketplace is registered with `apm marketplace add owner/repo --ref <branch>`, and its `marketplace.json` uses relative string sources (e.g. `\"./plugins/my-plugin\"`), `apm install my-plugin@my-marketplace` downloads the plugin from the repository's **default branch** rather than the registered `--ref` branch.

The ref is correctly persisted in `~/.apm/marketplaces.json` and correctly used to fetch `marketplace.json` (`client.py` passes `source.ref` to `fetch_or_cache`). However, in `resolver.py`, `resolve_marketplace_plugin` calls `_resolve_relative_source(source_str, source.owner, source.repo)` **without passing `source.ref`**. The canonical string (`owner/repo/plugins/my-plugin`) has no `#ref` suffix, so the downloader resolves against the default branch.

**To Reproduce**

1. Publish a repo with a `marketplace.json` on a non-default branch listing a plugin via a relative source. That plugin subdirectory does **not** exist on `main`:

   ```json
   {
     "name": "my-marketplace",
     "plugins": [{ "name": "my-plugin", "source": "./plugins/my-plugin" }]
   }
   ```

2. Register the marketplace pinned to that branch:

   ```
   apm marketplace add owner/catalog-repo --ref feat/my-feature --name my-marketplace
   ```

3. Install the plugin:

   ```
   apm install my-plugin@my-marketplace --target claude
   ```

4. Install resolves against the **default branch** (`main`), not `feat/my-feature`. Because the subdirectory only exists on `feat/my-feature`, the install fails:

   ```
   Error: Subdirectory not found: plugins/my-plugin
   ```

**Expected behavior**

`apm install my-plugin@my-marketplace` should install the plugin from `feat/my-feature` — the ref the marketplace was registered with.

**Root cause**

In `src/apm_cli/marketplace/resolver.py`, `resolve_marketplace_plugin` builds the canonical for a relative string source by calling:

```python
canonical = resolve_plugin_source(
    plugin,
    marketplace_owner=source.owner,
    marketplace_repo=source.repo,
    plugin_root=manifest.plugin_root,
)
```

`source.ref` is not passed. `_resolve_relative_source` returns `owner/repo/plugins/my-plugin` with **no `#ref` suffix**. The only code path that appends a ref to the canonical is the `version_spec` block at the end of the function, which fires only when the user explicitly passes a ref override via `plugin@mkt#ref` notation.

For GitLab / `*.ghe.com` marketplaces, `_source_needs_explicit_git_path` returns `True` and a structured `DependencyReference` is built (with an explicit `ref` when provided), so that host class is also affected when the dict source lacks its own `ref` field and no `version_spec` is supplied.

**Workaround**

Pass the ref explicitly at install time:

```
apm install my-plugin@my-marketplace#feat/my-feature
```

The `#feat/my-feature` becomes `version_spec` and is appended to the canonical.

**Proposed fix**

In `resolve_marketplace_plugin`, after computing `canonical` for an in-marketplace relative string source (and before the `version_spec` override block), propagate `source.ref` when no ref is already present and no explicit `version_spec` overrides it:

```python
# Propagate marketplace ref for intra-repo relative sources.
# Without this, a marketplace registered with --ref feat/xxx still downloads
# plugins against the default branch instead of the registered ref.
if (
    dep_ref is None
    and not version_spec
    and isinstance(plugin.source, str)
    and "#" not in canonical
    and source.ref
    and source.ref not in ("main", "HEAD")
):
    canonical = f"{canonical}#{source.ref}"
```

The existing test `TestGitHubMarketplace.test_github_marketplace_relative_source_returns_bare_canonical` (which uses `branch="main"`) continues to pass unchanged, since the condition excludes `"main"`.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux
- APM Version: 0.18.0 (also verified against 0.20.0 main — `source.ref` is unused in `resolve_marketplace_plugin` in the current upstream)

**Additional context**

The gap is easy to miss because the first half of the install flow _looks_ correct: `apm marketplace list` shows the right ref, and the `marketplace.json` is fetched from the right branch. The failure only surfaces later when the plugin's subdirectory is absent on the default branch.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-06-16
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-16
**APM Version**: 0.20.0 (45843c3)
**Commands Inspected**: 60 (help output collected for all top-level commands, all subcommand groups, and all documented subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 6     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `apm deps update` help text shows no deprecation warning
- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`) explicitly mark `apm deps update` as deprecated in favor of `apm update`. The help text shown by the CLI gives no indication of this.
- **Evidence (CLI)**:
  ```
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    Update APM dependencies to latest refs
  ```
  No deprecation notice anywhere in the output.
- **Evidence (docs)**: The CLI reference contains a caution block: "`apm deps update` is deprecated in favor of `apm update`, which is now a strict superset..."
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a deprecation notice to the help string, e.g.: `[Deprecated] Update APM dependencies to latest refs. Use 'apm update' instead.`

---

#### 2. `apm deps update --target` omits `kiro` from values and `all` expansion
- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: `apm install --help` and `apm compile --help` both list `kiro` as a valid target and include it in the `all` expansion. `apm deps update --help` silently omits `kiro` from both.
- **Evidence (`apm deps update --help`)**:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET   Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                        copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                        gemini, windsurf, agent-skills, all. 'all' =
                        copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+codex+gemini+windsurf
                        (excludes agent-skills)
  ```
- **Evidence (`apm install --help`)** for comparison:
  ```
  Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf,
  kiro, agent-skills, all. 'all' = copilot+claude+cursor+opencode+
  codex+gemini+windsurf+kiro (excludes agent-skills)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `kiro` to the values list and `all` expansion in the `apm deps update --target` help string.

---

#### 3. `apm update --target` description omits `kiro` from examples
- **Command**: `apm update --help`
- **Problem**: The `--target` description lists example values but omits `kiro`, which is a supported target listed in `apm install` and `apm compile`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET   Agent target(s) to update for (e.g. claude,
                        copilot, cursor, windsurf, codex, opencode,
                        gemini). Comma-separated for multiple: ...
  ```
  `kiro` is absent.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `kiro` to the example list in the `--target` description: "e.g. claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, codex, opencode, gemini, kiro".

---

#### 4. `apm config` lacks a `list` subcommand, breaking the command group pattern
- **Command**: `apm config list --help`
- **Problem**: Every other major command group in APM has a `list` subcommand (`apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm marketplace list`, `apm runtime list`, `apm experimental list`). `apm config` is the only group that does not -- it provides `get` (no-arg form shows all keys), `set`, and `unset`. Running `apm config list` produces an error.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  `apm config --help` commands: `get`, `set`, `unset` -- no `list`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either add `apm config list` as an alias for `apm config get` (no args), or document in `apm config --help` that `apm config get` with no argument lists all config keys, so users understand the pattern divergence.

---

#### 5. `apm cache clean` has two flags with identical descriptions, with one having misleading semantics
- **Command**: `apm cache clean --help`
- **Problem**: The command exposes both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes`, both described identically as "Skip confirmation prompt". `--force` carries a distinct semantic in all other APM commands (overwriting files, bypassing security blocks). Having `-f, --force` mean "skip prompt" here is inconsistent and potentially confusing.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
    --help       Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Compare with `apm install --force`: "Overwrite locally-authored files on collision and deploy despite critical security findings".
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f, --force` from `apm cache clean` and keep only `-y, --yes` for "skip confirmation". This aligns with `apm deps clean`, `apm runtime remove`, and `apm marketplace remove`, which all use `-y, --yes` exclusively.

---

#### 6. Docs list `intellij` as a valid `--target` value for `apm install`, but CLI help omits it
- **Command**: `apm install --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI reference documentation (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md`) lists `intellij` in the `--target` values table. The actual CLI `--target` help text does not list `intellij`. The value is only listed under the deprecated `--runtime` flag.
- **Evidence (docs, install.md `--target` table)**:
  > Values: `copilot`, `claude`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini`, `windsurf`, `kiro`, `intellij`, `agent-skills`, `all`
- **Evidence (CLI `apm install --help`, `--target` flag)**:
  ```
  Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, windsurf,
  kiro, agent-skills, all.
  ```
  `intellij` absent. It does appear in the deprecated `--runtime TEXT` flag: "(copilot, claude, codex, cursor, gemini, intellij, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf)".
- **Suggested Fix**: Either add `intellij` to the `--target` values list in the help text (if it is a valid `--target` value), or remove it from the docs table and note it is only reachable via the deprecated `--runtime` flag.

---

### Low Severity

#### 7. `apm mcp install --help` has poorly formatted "Common options" section
- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The help output appends a raw text block labeled "Common options" at the bottom of the Options section. The flags within it are run together in a paragraph rather than being formatted as individual, aligned CLI options like every other command.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-

- **Suggested Fix**: Format the "Common options" as a proper epilog/footer note, or list individual options with their standard alignment. If the intent is to show they are forwarded, an epilog like "All `apm install --mcp` options are accepted; see `apm install --help` for the full list." would be cleaner.

---

#### 8. `apm targets --help` shows `COMMAND [ARGS]...` in usage line despite having no subcommands
- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, implying subcommands exist. None are listed. The docs note that subcommands are "reserved for future use." Users seeing the usage line may attempt commands like `apm targets list`, which fail with "No such command 'list'."

    --all   ...

  ```
  No "Commands:" section appears.
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the usage pattern to `apm targets [OPTIONS]` until subcommands are implemented, or add a note to the help text: "No subcommands are available yet; run `apm targets` directly."

- **`apm deps --help` / `apm deps list` / `apm deps tree` / `apm deps info` / `apm deps why` / `apm deps clean`**: All correct (deprecation issue on `apm deps update` flagged above).

- **`apm runtime setup` / `apm runtime list` / `apm runtime status` / `apm runtime remove`**: All correct, consistent.
- **`apm approve` / `apm deny`**: Correct.
- **`apm audit --help`**: Comprehensive, well-documented.
- **`apm cache --help` / `apm cache info` / `apm cache prune`**: Correct. (`cache clean` issue flagged above.)
- **`apm doctor` / `apm experimental` group**: Correct.
- **`apm find` / `apm list` / `apm lock` / `apm outdated`**: Correct.
- **`apm marketplace` group** (add, list, browse, update, remove): Consistent.
- **`apm pack` / `apm publish` / `apm search` / `apm self-update` / `apm view`**: Correct.
- **`apm prune` / `apm unpack` / `apm plugin init` / `apm policy status`**: Correct.
- **Error handling**: All tested commands produce clear error messages (no stack traces) for invalid arguments and missing required arguments.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every tested command and subcommand.

issues.title: [BUG]  apm pack marketplace resolution ignores {name}, pins every package to the highest global version tag
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When `apm pack` builds a `marketplace.json`, the version-range resolution ignores the `{name}` placeholder in the tag pattern. Every remote package entry that uses a semver range is resolved to the **single highest `{version}` tag across the whole repository**, regardless of the package name. As a result,all entries end up pinned to the same `ref`/`sha` instead of each resolving to its own `{name}-v{version}` tag.

In a monorepo marketplace where each package is tagged independently as `{name}-v{version}`, this makes per-package resolution unusable: the produced `marketplace.json` points every plugin at one unrelated package's tag.

A clue that the package name is not threaded into the resolver: in `--offline` mode the error names an**empty** package — `Offline mode: no cached refs for '<owner>/<repo>' (package '')`.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a marketplace `apm.yml` with two packages from the same remote repo, each pinned by a semver**range**, using a name-scoped tag pattern:

   ```yaml
   name: my-marketplace
   version: 1.0.0
   description: repro
   marketplace:
     owner:
       name: Acme
       url: https://github.com/acme/catalog
     build:
       tagPattern: "{name}-v{version}"
     versioning:
       strategy: tag_pattern
     outputs:
       claude: {}
     packages:
       - name: pkg-a
         source: acme/catalog
         subdir: packages/pkg-a
         version: "^1.0.0"
       - name: pkg-b
         source: acme/catalog
         subdir: packages/pkg-b
         version: "^1.0.0"
   ```

2. On `acme/catalog`, create per-package tags at different versions:
   - `pkg-a-v1.0.0`
   - `pkg-b-v2.0.0`

3. Run:
   ```bash
   apm pack -m claude
   ```

4. Inspect the generated `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`:
   ```bash
   jq -r '.plugins[] | "\(.name)\t\(.source.ref)"' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
   ```

   Observed output — both entries resolve to the highest global version tag (`pkg-b-v2.0.0`), name ignored:
   ```
   pkg-a    pkg-b-v2.0.0
   pkg-b    pkg-b-v2.0.0
   ```

**Expected behavior**

Each entry should resolve against its **own** `{name}-v{version}` tags only, picking the highest tag that satisfies that entry's range:

```
pkg-a    pkg-a-v1.0.0
pkg-b    pkg-b-v2.0.0
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows (MINGW64 / Git Bash); also reproduced conceptually independent of OS
 - Python Version: 3.12.10
 - APM Version: 0.20.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a

**Additional context**

Variations tested — none restore name-scoped resolution:

| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| `build.tagPattern: "{name}-v{version}"` (single dash) + semver range | All entries → highest global version tag |
| `build.tagPattern: "{name}--v{version}"` (double dash, canonical convention) + matching tags | Same collapse |
| Per-package `tag_pattern: "{name}--v{version}"` on each entry | Same collapse |
| `versioning.strategy: per_package` + per-package `tag_pattern` | Same collapse |
| Exact `version: "1.2.1"` (bare version) | Resolves by **version only** — picks the alphabetically-first tag with that version, still ignoring `{name}`. Only "works" when the version is unique to one package or that package happens to be alphabetically first. |
| `version: "pkg-a-v1.0.0"` (full tag in `version:`) | Errors: `No tag matching version 'pkg-a-v1.0.0'found ... (pattern='{name}-v{version}')` |
| **`ref: "pkg-a-v1.0.0"` (full tag in `ref:`)** | **Correct** — resolves each entry to its own tag (this is the only working path, but it forces pinning immutable refs in `apm.yml` and writes the annotated-tag-object SHA rather than the commit SHA) |

Summary: the documented semantics (manifest schema: *"the resolver lists git tags matching the `{name}--v{version}` convention, filters to those satisfying the constraint, and resolves to the highest matching tag"*) are not honored — the `{name}` component is dropped and resolution falls back to a global version match. The only correct path today is the `ref:` override, which defeats the purpose of semver-range marketplace resolution in a monorepo.

[FEATURE] Move PyPI package ownership to Microsoft organization
issues.body:
The `apm-cli` package on PyPI is currently published under Daniel Meppiel's personal account. As this project is an official Microsoft tool, the package should be transferred to a Microsoft-owned PyPI organization to reflect that stewardship, improve discoverability, and provide organizational continuity independent of any individual contributor.

## Motivation

- **Organizational ownership**: Users and enterprises evaluating the tool expect Microsoft-hosted projects to be published under a verified Microsoft identity, not a personal account.
- **Continuity**: If the current publisher's account access changes, the ability to publish releases could be interrupted. Org-level ownership distributes that responsibility.
- **Trust signal**: A PyPI org namespace (e.g. under the microsoft organization) provides a stronger provenance signal for security-conscious users and automated dependency auditing tools.

## Proposed change

1. Create or use the existing `microsoft` PyPI organization (https://pypi.org/org/microsoft/).
2. Transfer ownership of `apm-cli` to that organization, or republish under a canonical Microsoft-owned name if a transfer is not feasible.
3. Update `pyproject.toml` `authors/maintainers` to reflect the org.
4. Update install documentation and any links pointing to the current PyPI page.

## References
[PyPI organization accounts documentation](https://docs.pypi.org/organization-accounts/)
Current package: https://pypi.org/project/apm-cli/

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-17
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-17
**APM Version**: 0.20.0 (788a09a)
**Commands Inspected**: 72 (1 top-level entry, 32 commands, 39 subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 1     |
| Medium   | 5     |
| Low      | 3     |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm targets` Usage Line Claims Subcommands That Do Not Exist

- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, which tells users that subcommands are expected. However, `apm targets --help` lists **no subcommands**, and any attempted invocation with a subcommand-style argument produces a confusing error (`Error: No such command 'X'`). Users exploring the CLI will reasonably try `apm targets list`, `apm targets show`, etc. and receive no guidance.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  ...
  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output (excluded by default).
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  No `Commands:` section is shown. Running `apm targets foo` produces:
  ```
  Error: No such command 'foo'.
  ```
- **Root cause**: `targets` is implemented as a `@click.group(invoke_without_command=True)` to allow future subcommands (`apm targets add`, etc.) but none are registered yet. The Click group template bleeds into the usage string.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) remove the `COMMAND [ARGS]...` portion by switching to a plain `@click.command` until real subcommands exist, or (b) suppress the misleading `COMMAND [ARGS]...` from the usage string until subcommands are actually added.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm cache clean` Has Two Confirmation-Skip Flags With Identical Help Text

- **Command**: `apm cache clean --help`
- **Problem**: The command exposes both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes`, both described as "Skip confirmation prompt". This creates two issues: (1) duplicate functionality with different flag names, and (2) semantic inconsistency -- `--force` in every other APM command means "overwrite locally-authored files on collision" (see `apm install --help`, `apm update --help`, `apm deps update --help`). A user who has learned that `--force` means "overwrite files" will be confused when it means "skip prompt" in `apm cache clean`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
    --help       Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Compare to `apm install --force`:
  ```
    --force  Overwrite locally-authored files on collision and deploy despite critical
             security findings
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f, --force` from `apm cache clean`. Keep only `-y, --yes` (the consistent pattern: `apm deps clean -y`, `apm runtime remove -y`). The `-f` alias predates the `--yes` convention and creates a semantic collision.

#### `apm deps update` Is Deprecated in Docs But Has No Deprecation Notice in CLI Help

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The reference documentation at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md` explicitly marks `apm deps update` as deprecated in favor of `apm update`. However, the CLI help text shows no deprecation warning. Users who run `apm deps update` have no in-band signal that they should migrate to `apm update`.
- **Evidence** (`apm deps update --help` -- no deprecation visible):
  ```
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    Update APM dependencies to latest refs
  ```
  Compare to `apm install --update` which properly surfaces its deprecation:
  ```
    --update  Update dependencies to latest Git references
              (deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan,
               or 'apm update --yes' for CI)
  ```
  And `apm init --plugin` which does the same:
  ```
    --plugin  (deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a deprecation notice to the `apm deps update` command description, e.g.: `Update APM dependencies to latest refs. (Deprecated: use 'apm update' instead, which adds an interactive plan, --dry-run, and --yes.)`

#### `apm install --help` Contains a Cross-Command Note About `apm compile`

- **Command**: `apm install --help`
- **Problem**: The description of the `--target` option in `apm install --help` includes a note that belongs in `apm compile --help`, not install's help. This cross-contamination confuses users reading install documentation.
- **Evidence** (inside `apm install --help`, within the `--target` description):
  ```
  Note: '--target all' on 'apm compile' is deprecated; use 'apm compile --all' instead.
  ```
  This sentence is about `apm compile` but appears mid-paragraph in `apm install`'s `--target` option help.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove this sentence from `apm install`'s `--target` help text. The corresponding deprecation notice (about `--target all`) should be added to `apm compile --help`'s `--target` option description, where it is currently absent.

#### `apm mcp install` Options Are Presented as Prose, Not as CLI Options

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: `apm mcp install --help` shows its supported options as a block of free-form text rather than structured Click options. This is inconsistent with every other command in the CLI, and makes the options impossible to discover via shell tab-completion.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Compare to `apm mcp search --help`, which uses proper Click options:
  ```
  Options:
    --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]
    -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
    --help           Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Expose the common flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) as first-class Click options on `apm mcp install`, forwarded to the underlying `apm install --mcp` code path. This enables tab-completion and standard `--help` discoverability.

#### `apm config list` Returns an Error With No Redirect to Correct Alternatives

- **Command**: `apm config list`
- **Problem**: Users familiar with `npm config list`, `git config --list`, or `pip config list` will naturally try `apm config list`. The command fails with a generic error and does not suggest the correct alternatives (`apm config` with no subcommand, or `apm config get` with no argument).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  The correct alternatives: `apm config` (displays a table of all settings) and `apm config get` (lists all user-settable keys with effective values).
- **Suggested Fix**: Add an `apm config list` alias that forwards to `apm config get` (no argument), providing parity with the ecosystem convention and a better first-run experience.

---

### Low Severity

#### `approve` and `deny` Descriptions End With Periods; No Other Command Does

- **Command**: `apm --help` (top-level command listing)
- **Problem**: In the top-level `apm --help` command table, `approve` and `deny` are the only two commands whose one-line descriptions end with a trailing period. All other 30 commands omit the trailing period.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  approve  Approve executable primitives for installed packages.   <- period
  deny     Revoke executable approval for packages.               <- period
  audit    Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters   <- no period
  cache    Manage the local package cache                         <- no period
  compile  Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files   <- no period
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing periods from the `approve` and `deny` command descriptions to match the convention used by every other command.

#### `apm marketplace --help` Uses Unique Section Headers Not Found in Other Command Groups

- **Command**: `apm marketplace --help`
- **Problem**: `apm marketplace` is the only command group that organizes its subcommands using labelled sections ("Consumer commands:" and "Authoring commands:"). All other command groups (`apm deps`, `apm config`, `apm mcp`, `apm runtime`, etc.) use a flat "Commands:" list.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Consumer commands:
    add       Register a marketplace
    list      List registered marketplaces
    ...
  Authoring commands:
    init      Add a 'marketplace:' block to apm.yml
    ...
  ```
  Compare to `apm deps --help`:
  ```
  Commands:
    clean   Remove all APM dependencies
    info    Show detailed package information
    ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either apply the section-header pattern to other command groups with a logical consumer/author split, or flatten `apm marketplace --help` to a standard "Commands:" list. Consistency matters more than which style is chosen.

#### `apm prune` Is Destructive But Has No `--yes` Flag for CI

- **Command**: `apm prune --help`
- **Problem**: `apm prune` removes installed packages not listed in `apm.yml` (a destructive, potentially irreversible action). It supports `--dry-run` but has no `-y, --yes` flag to skip interactive confirmation in CI pipelines. This is inconsistent with `apm deps clean`, which performs a comparable destructive action and provides both `--dry-run` and `-y, --yes`.
- **Evidence** (`apm prune --help`):
  ```
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Compare to `apm deps clean --help`:
  ```
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes` (skip confirmation prompt) to `apm prune` to enable non-interactive CI use, matching the `apm deps clean` pattern.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Error handling**: All tested error cases (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no argument, `apm config set` with missing args) produce clean, actionable error messages with no stack traces.
- **`apm deps` subcommands**: `list`, `tree`, `info`, `why` -- consistent flags, no style drift, help text matches docs.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands**: `setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove` -- consistent flag naming, experimental notice present, docs match CLI.
- **`apm mcp list/search/show`**: Consistent `--limit` and `--verbose` flags across all three.
- **`apm config get/set/unset`**: All three work as documented; error messages are clear.
- **`apm experimental` subcommands**: All four (`enable`, `disable`, `list`, `reset`) have consistent help text.
- **Deprecation notices on `apm init` flags**: `--plugin` and `--marketplace` correctly show `(deprecated)` inline.
- **`apm unpack`**: Correctly marked `[Deprecated]` with migration path in the description.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works on every command and subcommand tested (72 total).
- **`--dry-run` naming**: Consistent kebab-case spelling across all commands that support it (`apm install`, `apm deps clean`, `apm prune`, `apm pack`, `apm compile`, `apm audit`, `apm publish`, `apm unpack`).
