issues.title: [FEATURE] Make missing targets a hard error instead of silently autodetecting
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

There is no way to make `apm install` / `apm compile` fail when targets are not declared explicitly. When `apm.yml` has no `targets:` field and no `--target` flag is passed, both commands fall back to autodetecting harness targets by scanning the working tree for marker directories and files (`.claude`/`CLAUDE.md`, `.codex`, `.gemini`/`GEMINI.md`, `.cursor`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.opencode`, `.windsurf`, `.kiro`). The resolution chain is `--target` flag > `apm.yml` `target:`/`targets:` > autodetect (`resolve_targets` in `src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py`, signal list in `SIGNAL_WHITELIST`).

In CI this is the wrong default. I want a build to fail loudly when a contributor forgets to commit `targets:`, not to quietly pick targets from whatever directories happen to exist on the runner. The silent fallback defeats reproducibility: a check that runs `apm install && apm compile && git diff --exit-code` to assert that committed compiled files match `apm.yml` is not stable, because the resolved set depends on uncommitted, machine-local state rather than on `apm.yml` alone.

The existing guard does not cover this case. Autodetect only fails when it finds *zero* markers — `resolve_targets` raises `NoHarnessError` (exit 2) on an empty repo. With exactly one marker present (a committed `.claude/`, or a throwaway local `.gemini/` from an unfinished prototype) it silently resolves to that target and proceeds. So the absence of a declared `targets:` field is never reported as an error as long as the working tree contains at least one harness directory. That is precisely when I most want it reported.

(For context: a non-empty `targets:` in `apm.yml` already short-circuits resolution before autodetect, so declared targets are honoured deterministically. The strict precedence chain landed in v0.12.3 (#1165); plural `targets:` lists are honoured in `install` since v0.16.1 (#1560). The gap is only the undeclared case, where the fallback is silent rather than fatal.)

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A way to require explicit targets, so that a missing declaration is a hard error rather than a trigger for autodetection.

When enabled, `apm install` and `apm compile` resolve targets from `--target` and `apm.yml` `targets:`/`target:` only. If neither is present, they exit non-zero with a clear message ("No targets declared: set `targets:` in apm.yml or pass `--target`") and never scan the working tree. The working-tree contents — committed or not — must not affect which targets are resolved.

Any of these shapes would work; I have no strong preference:

- A flag, e.g. `apm install --require-targets` / `--no-autodetect`.
- An environment variable, e.g. `APM_REQUIRE_TARGETS=1`, convenient for CI.
- An `apm.yml` setting, e.g. `autodetect: false`.
- Making "explicit only" the default and turning autodetect into an opt-in request, e.g. `--target auto`.

The goal: given a fixed `apm.yml`, the resolved targets depend only on `apm.yml` and explicit flags, and an undeclared project fails fast instead of guessing.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Parse `apm.yml` in CI and fail if `targets:` is absent.** This works, but it is a workaround: it reimplements outside the tool a guarantee the tool should provide, and it can drift from APM's own parsing rules (singular vs plural form, CSV sugar, validation).
- **Always pass `--target` in CI.** This duplicates the target list outside `apm.yml`, so the two can drift, and it does not protect local developer runs.
- **Persist resolved targets to `apm.yml` on first install.** `apm init` already writes the resolved set into `targets:` (`_resolve_init_targets` -> `config["targets"]` in `src/apm_cli/commands/init.py`); `apm install` does not. Writing them back on first use would also make later runs deterministic. It is a softer fix than failing, but it does not give CI the "fail when undeclared" behaviour I want, so I see it as complementary rather than a substitute.

**Additional context**

- Signal list and resolution: `SIGNAL_WHITELIST` and `resolve_targets` in `src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py`; `install` calls it from `_resolve_targets_by_scope` in `src/apm_cli/install/phases/targets.py`.
- The existing zero-markers guard: `NoHarnessError` (exit 2) is raised only when autodetect finds nothing, not when `targets:` is simply undeclared.
- `compile` resolves targets through a separate legacy path (`detect_target` via `_resolve_effective_target` in `src/apm_cli/commands/compile/cli.py`), which in the autodetect branch returns `"all"` on two or more detected folders rather than failing. A `--require-targets` mode should apply to both commands and resolve this divergence so they behave identically.
- The codebase already moves toward explicitness: the "No harness detected" error notes that APM previously defaulted to `copilot` and that the default is "now explicit". Requiring declared targets is the next step on that path.

issues.title: [FEATURE] override a consumed primitive's frontmatter (e.g. agent name/description) from apm.yml
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When consuming individual primitives from another repo (e.g. `github/awesome-copilot`
agents) via `dependencies.apm`, the content is materialized verbatim and the
`apm.lock.yaml` integrity check (correctly) forbids editing it. But upstream display
names are often inconsistent or carry vendor taglines — e.g.
`Prompt Builder - Brought to you by microsoft/edge-ai`, or terse slugs like
`sast-sca-security-analyzer`. I would like to normalize these artifacts
without forking or vendoring each file — which loses `apm update` and the
supply-chain gate.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow per-dependency frontmatter overrides in `apm.yml`, applied at deploy time and
recorded in `apm.lock.yaml` so they are reproducible and visible in diffs:

```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - repo: github/awesome-copilot
      path: agents/sast-sca-security-analyzer.agent.md
      ref: <sha>
      overrides:
        name: "SAST/SCA Security Analyzer"
        # description: "Reviews dependencies and code for SAST/SCA findings."
```

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-23
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-23
**APM Version**: 0.21.0 (a9a883b)
**Commands Inspected**: 49 (32 top-level + 17 subcommands, including one non-existent command)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 6 |
| Low | 4 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `apm compile --target all` deprecation note is in the wrong command's help text

- **Command**: `apm install --help`
- **Problem**: The deprecation notice for `--target all` on `apm compile` is embedded inside the `apm install --target` description, not in `apm compile --help`. Users running `apm compile --target all` will not see any deprecation warning from `apm compile --help`.
- **Evidence**: `apm install --help` `--target` section ends with:
  ```
  Note: '--target all' on 'apm compile' is deprecated; use 'apm compile
  --all' instead.
  ```
  `apm compile --help` shows `--all` as "Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all." with no deprecation note about `--target all` being deprecated.
- **Suggested Fix**: Move the deprecation note to `apm compile --target` (or `apm compile --all`) description. Remove it from `apm install --target`. Alternatively, add a runtime warning when `apm compile --target all` is invoked.

---

#### 2. `apm deps update --help` does not show deprecation notice

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The docs (`reference/cli/deps.md`) explicitly mark `apm deps update` as deprecated in favor of `apm update`. The runtime does emit a deprecation warning when invoked. However, the `--help` text contains no deprecation indicator.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help` output:
    ```
    Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

      Update APM dependencies to latest refs

    Options:
    ...
    ```
    No deprecation mentioned.
  - Runtime output: `[!] 'apm deps update' is deprecated; use 'apm update' instead.`
  - `deps.md`: contains a caution admonition explicitly calling it deprecated.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `[DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead]` to the command description string so it appears in `--help` output, not just at runtime.

---

#### 3. `apm mcp install --help` has non-standard, unformatted options block

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The help text shows only `--help` as a registered option, then appends an unformatted prose block titled "Common options" within the Options section. These options are NOT registered Click options -- they are forwarded to `apm install --mcp` at runtime. The display is inconsistent with every other command's help and misleads users about which flags are parsed at which level. Additionally, placing flags before the `NAME` positional argument yields a confusing error: "MCP name cannot start with '-'; did you forget a value for --mcp?" when Click treats unrecognized pre-positional options as the NAME argument.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Every other command (e.g., `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm compile`) uses standard Click option formatting.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either register the forwarded options as proper Click params on `apm mcp install`, or move the prose note to the command description (not the Options section) and use standard formatting (e.g., a `\b` epilog block).

---

#### 4. `apm update --target` description is truncated compared to related commands

- **Command**: `apm update --help`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag for `apm update` gives a short description with example values but does not list all supported targets (copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all) and omits the `copilot-cowork` experimental target that appears in the equivalent flags for `apm install` and `apm deps update`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm update --target`: `"Agent target(s) to update for (e.g. claude, copilot, cursor, windsurf, kiro, codex, opencode, gemini). Comma-separated for multiple: --target claude,cursor."`
  - `apm install --target`: full enumeration of all targets, `antigravity`, `agent-skills`, `all`, and `copilot-cowork` experimental note.
  - `apm deps update --target`: same full enumeration as `apm install`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Align `apm update --target` description with `apm install --target` to include the full target list and the `copilot-cowork` experimental note. Similarly, ensure `apm compile --target` also includes the `copilot-cowork` note (currently absent).

---

#### 5. `apm doctor` has no dedicated CLI reference page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` is a top-level command (`apm --help` lists it; it runs and works correctly), but it has no dedicated page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` and is absent from the reference index table in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`. It is only mentioned incidentally in guide pages.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm doctor --help` works: `"Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero if a critical check fails."`
  - `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` -- no `doctor.md`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md` CLI table has no `doctor` row.
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` and add a `doctor` entry to the reference index table (e.g., under "Inspect and audit" alongside `audit`).

---

#### 6. Reference index table omits 7 commands that have dedicated doc pages

- **Command**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`
- **Problem**: The CLI commands table in the reference index lists a subset of commands, leaving out 7 commands that each have their own dedicated reference page.
- **Evidence**: The following commands have pages under `reference/cli/` but are absent from the index table:
  - `approve` / `deny` -- covered in `approve.md`
  - `find` -- `find.md`
  - `lock` -- `lock.md`
  - `pack` -- `pack.md`
  - `plugin` -- `plugin.md`
  - `publish` -- `publish.md`
  - `self-update` -- `self-update.md`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the missing commands to the reference index table under appropriate phase categories (e.g., `approve`/`deny` under Governance; `find` under Inspect and audit; `lock` under Project setup; `pack`/`publish`/`plugin` under Author and distribute; `self-update` under Cache and config).

---

### Low Severity

#### 7. `--verbose` / `-v` flag descriptions are inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The description for the `-v, --verbose` flag varies significantly across commands with no clear pattern.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm init`: "Show detailed output"
  - `apm install`: "Show detailed installation information"
  - `apm uninstall`: "Show detailed removal information"
  - `apm update`: "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"
  - `apm compile`: "Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"
  - `apm run`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`: "Show detailed output"
  - `apm deps update`: "Show detailed update information"
- **Suggested Fix**: Adopt a consistent base pattern. Command-specific additions are fine ("Show detailed output" as base; add context where it adds value). Standardize at minimum the base wording.

---

#### 8. `apm deps list` has no `--verbose` flag while peer `deps` subcommands do

- **Command**: `apm deps list`
- **Problem**: `apm deps list --help` shows no `-v, --verbose` flag, while `apm deps update` and `apm deps why` both support `--verbose`. For a listing command, verbose output (e.g., showing source URLs or primitive counts) would be expected.
- **Evidence**: `apm deps list --help` options: `-g, --global`, `--all`, `--insecure`, `--help`. No verbose flag.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose` to `apm deps list` to show additional detail (source URL, primitive type breakdown), or document in the help text that `--insecure` adds the Origin column as the available detail level.

---

#### 9. `apm outdated --parallel-checks` uses non-standard default format and inconsistent short flag

- **Command**: `apm outdated --help`
- **Problem**: The parallel flag uses `(default: 4, 0 = sequential)` inline in the description rather than Click's standard `[default: 4]` display. The short flag `-j` is also inconsistent -- all other parallel flags (e.g., `apm install --parallel-downloads`, `apm update --parallel-downloads`) have no short flag. The flag name itself (`--parallel-checks`) differs from `--parallel-downloads` used elsewhere.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm outdated`: `-j, --parallel-checks INTEGER  Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)`
  - `apm install`: `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`
  - `apm update`: `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`
- **Suggested Fix**: Rename to `--parallel-checks` -> keep or align to `--parallel-downloads` style, remove `-j` short flag for consistency, and use Click's `default=4` parameter so the standard `[default: 4]` appears in help.

---

#### 10. `apm audit` help description is too narrow for its actual scope

- **Command**: `apm audit --help`
- **Problem**: The one-line description "Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters" understates the command's scope. `apm audit` also performs drift detection, lockfile integrity CI checks, and policy enforcement -- all shown in the extensive options list.
- **Evidence**: `apm audit --help` description vs. options including `--ci` (lockfile CI gates), `--no-drift` (install-replay drift check), `--policy` (policy enforcement), and `--external` (SARIF scanner ingestion).
- **Suggested Fix**: Expand the description to something like: "Scan for hidden Unicode characters, detect install drift, and run lockfile integrity checks for CI gates." This avoids documenting the full feature set in the one-liner while still representing the command's breadth.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- **Core install/uninstall lifecycle**: `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update` -- flags are well-described and consistent with docs.
- **`apm compile`**: Comprehensive help text with clear flag descriptions; `--all` alias is properly documented.
- **`apm deps` subcommands** (`list`, `tree`, `info`, `clean`, `why`): Help text matches docs.
- **`apm mcp` search/show/list**: Consistent format, defaults match docs (`list --limit` defaults to 20, `search --limit` defaults to 10).
- **`apm config` subcommands** (`get`, `set`, `unset`): Match docs precisely; `apm config` (bare) renders project+global config table correctly.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands** (`setup`, `list`, `status`): Clean, minimal, accurate.
- **`apm init`**: Deprecated `--plugin` and `--marketplace` flags are properly labeled with redirects.
- **`apm unpack`**: Deprecated properly labeled with `[Deprecated]` prefix and redirect message.
- **`apm run`**: Simple and consistent with docs.
- **`apm lock`**: Comprehensive options, `export` subcommand present and accessible.
- **`apm doctor`**: Functional with `--verbose` flag; runtime diagnostics work correctly.
- **Error handling**: All tested invalid inputs (`--nonexistent-flag`, missing required args) return clean error messages with usage hints -- no stack traces.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works on every tested command and subcommand.
- **`--dry-run`**: Present and consistently described on all commands where applicable (`install`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `audit`, `publish`, `unpack`).

issues.title: [aw] No-Op Runs
issues.body:
This issue tracks all no-op runs from agentic workflows in this repository. Each workflow run that completes with a no-op message (indicating no action was needed) posts a comment here.

<details>
<summary>What is a No-Op?</summary>

A no-op (no operation) occurs when an agentic workflow runs successfully but determines that no action is required. For example:
- A security scanner that finds no issues
- An update checker that finds nothing to update
- A monitoring workflow that finds everything is healthy

These are successful outcomes, not failures, and help provide transparency into workflow behavior.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How This Helps</summary>

This issue helps you:
- Track workflows that ran but determined no action was needed
- Distinguish between failures and intentional no-ops
- Monitor workflow health by seeing when workflows decide not to act

</details>

<details>
<summary>Resources</summary>

- [GitHub Agentic Workflows Documentation](https://github.com/github/gh-aw)

</details>

> [!TIP]
> To stop a workflow from posting here, set `report-as-issue: false` in its frontmatter:
> ```yaml
> safe-outputs:
>   noop:
>     report-as-issue: false
> ```

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-06-24
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-24
**APM Version**: 0.21.0 (a9a883b)
**Commands Inspected**: 32 top-level commands + all subcommands for `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`, `cache`, `marketplace`, `experimental`, `plugin`, `policy`, `lock`, `targets` = approximately 60+ help pages

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 1     |
| Medium   | 4     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### High Severity

#### `--runtime intellij` silently ignores unknown target instead of erroring
- **Command**: `apm install --runtime intellij --dry-run`
- **Problem**: The `--runtime` flag help text lists `intellij` as a valid value, but `--target intellij` (the current preferred flag) rejects it with a hard error. Using `--runtime intellij` silently succeeds but falls back to auto-detected targets rather than filtering to intellij — the user gets no warning that their specified runtime was ignored.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # --target intellij (preferred flag) correctly errors:
  $ apm install --target intellij --dry-run
  Error: [x] Unknown target 'intellij'

  # --runtime intellij (deprecated flag) silently ignores the value:
  $ apm install --runtime intellij --dry-run
  [>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
  [i] Dry run mode - showing what would be installed:
  [i] APM dependencies (2):
  [i]   - _local/apm-issue-autopilot#main -> install
  [i]   - _local/batch-bug-shepherd#main -> install

  # apm install --help lists intellij as a valid --runtime value:
  --runtime TEXT   Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex,
                   cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode,
                   vscode, windsurf)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either add validation to `--runtime` so `intellij` (and any other unknown value) produces an error with a message pointing users to `--target`, or remove `intellij` and `vscode` from the `--runtime` help text since they are not accepted by `--target`. The install.md docs describe `--runtime` as a "Legacy alias for `--target`" — the two flags should accept the same valid values.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm audit` short description omits drift detection and CI gate functionality
- **Command**: `apm --help`, `apm audit --help`
- **Problem**: The short description shown in `apm --help` and `apm audit --help` reads "Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters". This is incomplete — `apm audit` also runs drift detection (install replay to detect hand-edits) and a CI gate mode (`--ci`) for lockfile consistency checks. Users may not discover the broader functionality.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm --help shows:
  audit         Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters

  # But apm audit --help and audit.md describe two full modes:
  # 1. Content scan: hidden Unicode + drift detection (install replay)
  # 2. CI gate mode (--ci): lockfile consistency + policy checks
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the short description to something like: `Scan installed primitives for hidden Unicode, drift, and lockfile violations`

#### `apm doctor` has no CLI reference documentation page
- **Command**: `apm doctor --help`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` exists in the CLI and is mentioned in guides, but it has no dedicated reference page at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md`. All other commands have a reference page. The CI reference index lists 30 doc files but there are 32 CLI commands (the two without pages being `doctor` and `deny` — though `deny` is covered in `approve.md`).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm doctor --help
  Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]

    Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace
    config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero if a critical check
    fails.

  Options:
    -v, --verbose  Show detailed output
    --help         Show this message and exit.

  # No doctor.md exists:
  $ ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/ | grep doctor
  (no output)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` documenting the command, its checks, exit codes, and examples (e.g., `apm doctor`, `apm doctor --verbose`).

#### `vscode` is an accepted `--target` alias that is undocumented
- **Command**: `apm compile --target vscode`, `apm install --target vscode`
- **Problem**: `vscode` is accepted as a `--target` value and works (deploys to Copilot paths), but it is not listed in the `--target` help text for any command, and it does not appear in any CLI reference documentation. It is listed in `--runtime` help text for `apm install` but not in `--target`. Users cannot discover this alias from the help system.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm compile --target vscode --dry-run
  [*] Starting context compilation...
  [i] Targets: vscode  (source: --target flag)
  [i] Compiling for AGENTS.md + .github/copilot-instructions.md +
      .github/prompts/ + .github/agents/ - explicit --target flag
  [i] [dry-run] showing placement without writing files

  # But vscode does NOT appear in apm compile --help --target values:
  # Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini,
  #         antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either add `vscode` (and `intellij` if it will be supported) to the valid-values list in the `--target` help text across all commands, or document it as a recognized alias in the CLI reference docs and the targets matrix.

#### `apm mcp install --help` uses non-standard option display format
- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The help output for `apm mcp install` lists the common forwarded options as a prose paragraph in the description rather than as proper Click option entries. This makes the help text harder to read and inconsistent with every other command in the CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Usage: apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME

    Add an MCP server to apm.yml. Alias for 'apm install --mcp'.
    ...

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  All other commands show flags as structured `--flag  description` entries. This command has them as run-on prose.
- **Suggested Fix**: Format the forwarded options as proper Click option entries in the help text (even if they are forwarded), or move the prose to the description block above `Options:` where it reads more naturally as a cross-reference note.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm prune` lacks `-y/--yes` flag, inconsistent with similar cleanup commands
- **Command**: `apm prune --help`
- **Problem**: `apm prune` prompts for confirmation before removing packages but has no `--yes` / `-y` flag to skip the prompt in CI or scripted environments. The two other cleanup commands (`apm deps clean` and `apm cache clean`) both support `-y, --yes`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm prune --help
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    --help     Show this message and exit.

  $ apm deps clean --help
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt    # <-- present here
    --help     Show this message and exit.

  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt  # <-- present here
    --help       Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes` to `apm prune` to allow non-interactive use in CI pipelines, matching the pattern established by `apm deps clean` and `apm cache clean`.

#### `apm targets` usage line shows `COMMAND [ARGS]...` with no subcommands
- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, implying it is a command group with subcommands, but no subcommands are listed in the output. Running `apm targets` with no arguments does work (prints the targets table), but the usage format is confusing. The docs note this is intentional ("reserved for future use"), but a user reading only `--help` gets no explanation.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm targets --help
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project. ...

  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output (excluded
            by default).
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  # No "Commands:" section follows
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to the help description that no subcommands are currently available, or restructure `apm targets` as a regular command (not a group) until subcommands are implemented.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all consistency checks:

- `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run` — well-structured help, accurate docs
- `apm deps list/tree/info/clean/update/why` — consistent options, accurate docs, correct deprecation notices
- `apm mcp search/show/list` — consistent options and docs
- `apm config get/set/unset` — well documented (note: `apm config list` does not exist; it is not documented and the CLI correctly rejects it)
- `apm runtime setup/list/status/remove` — consistent options across CLI and docs
- `apm cache clean/info/prune` — consistent options and docs
- `apm lock`, `apm lock export` — hybrid group+command pattern works correctly
- `apm audit`, `apm approve`, `apm deny`, `apm pack`, `apm publish`, `apm outdated`, `apm prune`, `apm search`, `apm view`, `apm find`, `apm list`, `apm doctor`, `apm self-update`, `apm unpack`, `apm preview`, `apm experimental`, `apm policy`, `apm plugin` — no option crashes or tracebacks
- Error handling: All tested invalid-argument cases produce clean error messages (no stack traces)

issues.title: [FEATURE] Enhance apm.lock.yaml to Include Installed Package Name and Version Metadata
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

APM packages require a `name` and `version` in `apm.yml`, but after `apm install` consumers cannot easily determine which package versions are installed because `apm.lock.yaml` only records repository, path, commit, and hash information.

This becomes more challenging when packages have transitive dependencies. For example, installing a Spring Boot package may automatically install additional packages such as Mermaid, documentation standards, or other shared packages. While these dependencies appear in `apm.lock.yaml`, their package versions are not visible.

As a result, it is difficult to answer:

* Which version of the Spring Boot package is installed?
* Which versions of transitive dependencies were installed?
* Which repositories are using older package versions?
* What changed between two package upgrades?

### Describe the solution you'd like

Enhance `apm.lock.yaml` to include package metadata extracted from each package's `apm.yml`, such as package name and version.

Example:

```yaml
dependencies:
  - name: springboot
    version: 1.2.2
    resolved_commit: b62358...
    virtual_path: packages/springboot

  - name: mermaid
    version: 1.0.4
    resolved_commit: b62358...
    virtual_path: packages/mermaid

  - name: documentations
    version: 2.1.0
    resolved_commit: b62358...
    virtual_path: packages/documentations
```

Ideally this information should be available for both direct and transitive dependencies.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Generating a custom inventory file by parsing `apm.lock.yaml` and then reading each package's `apm.yml` to determine the package version. While this works, it requires additional scripts and custom tooling in every consuming repository.

### Additional context

Our organization maintains shared APM packages such as Spring Boot, Angular, Mermaid, and documentation standards. Developers often need to understand exactly which package versions are installed in a repository, including automatically installed dependencies.

Having package name and version information directly available in `apm.lock.yaml` would make dependency inventory, auditing, troubleshooting, and upgrade planning much easier while preserving the existing commit-based lockfile behavior.

issues.title: [BUG] local_deployed_file_hashes differ between Windows and Linux for identical content
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When I install the same APM project on Windows and on Linux, the
`local_deployed_file_hashes` recorded in `apm.lock.yaml` differ between the two platforms,
even though the source content is identical and unchanged. As a result the lockfile changes
depending on which OS ran `apm install`, producing noisy diffs / churn when the project is
installed from different machines (for example a Windows workstation versus a Linux CI
runner). The deployed files have the same content on both platforms — only their recorded
hashes differ.

**To Reproduce**

1. Use an APM project with local primitives (under `.apm/`) so that `apm install` records
   `local_deployed_file_hashes`.
2. Run `apm install` on Linux and note the `local_deployed_file_hashes` values in
   `apm.lock.yaml`.
3. Run `apm install` on Windows from the same, unchanged source.
4. Compare `apm.lock.yaml`: the `local_deployed_file_hashes` entries differ between the
   Windows run and the Linux run.

**Expected behavior**

For identical source content, `apm install` should record identical
`local_deployed_file_hashes` regardless of the operating system, so the lockfile is stable
across Windows and Linux and does not churn between machines / CI.

**Environment**

- OS: occurs across platforms — the hashes differ between Windows and Linux
- APM Version: 0.21.0

**Additional context**

The divergence looks line-ending related: the same content ends up with different line
endings depending on the OS (CRLF on Windows, LF on Linux), which changes the bytes that
get hashed. Suggested fix: write deployed files with deterministic LF line endings on every
platform, and/or normalize line endings before computing the recorded hash, so the value is
platform-independent.

issues.title: [BUG] hook_integrator merges all per-harness hook manifests into every target (codex/cursor hooks leak into .claude/settings.json)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator` does not select a single per-harness hook manifest when integrating a package's hooks. Instead, for a package that ships multiple per-harness hook manifests (`hooks.json`, `hooks-codex.json`, `hooks-cursor.json`), it merges **all** of them into **every** target, irrespective of which harness each manifest is meant for and irrespective of which targets are enabled.

The result is that a single target's hook config (e.g. `.claude/settings.json`) ends up containing:

- the foreign Codex hook command (`session-start-codex`), which is wrong for Claude, and
- the Cursor manifest's lower-case `sessionStart` event with a relative `./hooks/run-hook.cmd` path, which is invalid for both Claude and Codex.

Three distinct defects are visible in one reproduction (all in `hook_integrator`):

1. **No per-target manifest selection (primary).** `hooks-codex.json` and `hooks-cursor.json` are integrated into the `claude` target, and `hooks.json` + `hooks-cursor.json` into the `codex` target. The filename suffix that identifies the harness (`-codex`, `-cursor`) is ignored.
2. **Each manifest is processed twice.** The integrator walks both `<pkg>/hooks/` and `<pkg>/.apm/hooks/`, so every manifest is integrated from two source dirs (`12 hook(s) integrated (6 adopted)` = 3 manifests × 2 dirs × 2 targets).
3. **Hook-script path is doubled during validation.** The "script exists" check resolves `.../superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd` as `.../superpowers/hooks/hooks/run-hook.cmd` (extra `hooks/` segment) and emits a spurious `Hook script not found` warning, even though the deployed command (`.claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd`) is correct and present.

The lower-case `sessionStart` from the Cursor manifest also triggers a `hook event casing mismatch` warning against **both** the `claude` and `codex` targets, because the Cursor manifest is fed into integrators that expect PascalCase.

**To Reproduce**

`obra/superpowers` is a convenient public repro: it ships three per-harness hook manifests under both `hooks/` and `.apm/hooks/`:

| manifest | intended harness | event key | command |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hooks.json` | claude | `SessionStart` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start` |
| `hooks-codex.json` | codex | `SessionStart` | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start-codex` |
| `hooks-cursor.json` | cursor | `sessionStart` | `./hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start` |

Steps:

1. In an empty git repo:
   ```
   apm install obra/superpowers --target claude,codex
   ```
2. Inspect `.claude/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json`.

(It also reproduces with a single target, e.g. `--target claude`, and with `--skill <name>` selection — neither narrows the hooks.)

**Expected behavior**

- The `claude` target should integrate **only** `hooks.json`.
- The `codex` target should integrate **only** `hooks-codex.json`.
- `hooks-cursor.json` should be integrated only when `cursor` is a target.
- `.claude/settings.json` should contain a single `SessionStart` entry pointing at `session-start`; no `session-start-codex`, no lower-case `sessionStart`.
- No `casing mismatch` warning for `claude`/`codex` (the lower-case event belongs to the Cursor manifest only).
- No `Hook script not found` warning for a script that exists.

**Actual behavior**

`apm install obra/superpowers --target claude,codex` produces a contaminated `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "startup|resume|clear",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "\".claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd\" session-start-codex", "async": false }
        ]
      },
      {
        "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "\".claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd\" session-start", "async": false }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "sessionStart": [
      { "command": "./hooks/run-hook.cmd session-start" }
    ]
  }
}
```

The first `SessionStart` entry runs the **Codex** hook script inside Claude, and the trailing lower-case `sessionStart` is the **Cursor** manifest. `.codex/hooks.json` is symmetric: it carries the Claude `session-start` (which relies on `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, undefined under Codex) plus the same lower-case `sessionStart`.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)
- Python Version: n/a — installed via the standalone CLI binary (PyInstaller bundle, `apm_cli` 0.21.0), not a venv
- APM Version: 0.21.0 (975f8f0)
- VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a
- Harnesses / targets: `claude`, `codex`
- Affected package: `obra/superpowers` (commit `896224c4` at time of repro)

**Logs**

Relevant lines from `apm install obra/superpowers --target claude,codex` (with `APM_LOG_LEVEL=INFO`):

```
INFO apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: detected hook event: SessionStart
Hook script not found: .../apm_modules/obra/superpowers/.apm/hooks/hooks/run-hook.cmd
INFO apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: detected hook event: sessionStart
Hook events for target 'claude' may not be recognized: sessionStart. Target expects PascalCase (e.g. PreToolUse). Rename events to match the PascalCase convention, then reinstall.
WARNING apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: hook event casing mismatch (no mapping): sessionStart
...
Hook script not found: .../apm_modules/obra/superpowers/hooks/hooks/run-hook.cmd
...
WARNING apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target codex: hook event casing mismatch (no mapping): sessionStart
  |-- 12 hook(s) integrated (6 adopted) -> .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json
  |   SessionStart: runs .claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-codex.json)
  |   sessionStart: runs ./hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-cursor.json)
  |   SessionStart: runs .claude/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks.json)
  |   SessionStart: runs .codex/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-codex.json)
  |   sessionStart: runs ./hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks-cursor.json)
  |   SessionStart: runs .codex/hooks/superpowers/hooks/run-hook.cmd (hooks.json)
```

The integration summary itself shows all three manifests being applied to both targets.

**Additional context**

- No per-package knob works around this: `--target <single>` still merges the foreign manifests, and `--skill` only filters skills, not hooks. There appears to be no `--no-hooks` / hook-exclude option.
- Likely fix area: when integrating hooks for target `T`, select the manifest whose harness suffix matches `T` (`hooks.json` → claude default, `hooks-<harness>.json` → that harness), and don't fan a manifest out to non-matching targets. Also dedupe the `hooks/` vs `.apm/hooks/` source dirs, and fix the doubled `hooks/hooks/` path in the script-existence check.
- Possibly related (hook integration): #1823 ("Cursor hook integration omits required top-level `version` in `.cursor/hooks.json`").

issues.title: [FEATURE] Per-package opt-out for hooks (e.g. --no-hooks / hooks: false in apm.yml)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

A package's install is all-or-nothing across component *types*. If I depend on a package for its skills, I cannot opt out of its hooks. The current selectors don't cover this:

- `--skill NAME` (persisted as `skills:` in `apm.yml`) filters *which skills* are installed, but hooks are still deployed in full.
- `--only [apm|mcp]` selects a *dependency type*, not a component type within a package.
- `--exclude` / `--runtime` / `--target` filter by *harness*, not by component.
- `apm config auto-integrate false` is global and also disables skill integration, for every package.

So there is no way to say "install this package's skills, but not its hooks."

This bites in practice with multi-harness skill packages such as `obra/superpowers`: its SessionStart hooks are currently mis-integrated (see #1892 — manifest cross-contamination, missing dispatched scripts, broken plugin-root paths), and I simply don't want that hook auto-loading at session start anyway. Today my only recourse is to delete the generated hook entries from `.claude/settings.json` / `.codex/hooks.json` after every install — which APM overwrites on the next `apm install` / `apm update`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A per-package / per-component opt-out for hooks (and ideally other component types), expressed both as a CLI flag and as durable `apm.yml` state so it survives reinstall. For example:

- CLI: `apm install obra/superpowers --no-hooks` (repeatable / per-package), persisted into `apm.yml`.
- `apm.yml` dependency object, mirroring the existing `skills:` selector:

  ```yaml
  dependencies:
    apm:
      - git: obra/superpowers
        hooks: false        # do not integrate this package's hooks
        # or, granular:
        # components: [skills]            # allow-list
        # exclude-components: [hooks]     # deny-list
  ```

When a package's hooks are opted out, `apm install` / `apm update` should skip writing them to every target's hook config and not re-add them on subsequent runs.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Post-install manual cleanup of `.claude/settings.json` / `.codex/hooks.json` — not durable; APM regenerates the hooks on the next install/update.
- `auto-integrate: false` — too blunt; it disables all integration (skills included) for all packages.
- `--skill` selection — only narrows skills; has no effect on hooks (verified: hooks still deploy with a `skills:` filter present).
- Forking the package to strip its hook manifests — heavy and unmaintainable for a consumer.

**Additional context**

- Motivating issue: #1892 (hook integration defects on `obra/superpowers`). Even once those bugs are fixed, a consumer may legitimately not want a package's SessionStart hook to auto-load; a supported opt-out is the clean answer.
- The symmetric `skills:` selector already exists in the dependency schema, so a `hooks:` / `components:` selector would be a natural extension.
- Environment: APM 0.21.0 (975f8f0), macOS, standalone CLI binary.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-25
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-25
**APM Version**: 0.21.0 (d9fe3dd)
**Commands Inspected**: 27 (top-level + all subcommands under `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm doctor` has no CLI reference documentation page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: Every other command in the CLI has a dedicated reference page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. The `apm doctor` command exists and works, and is mentioned in guides, but has no reference page at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` -- no `doctor.md` exists
  - `apm doctor --help` returns valid output:
    ```
    Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]

      Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI,
      marketplace config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero
      if a critical check fails.

    Options:
      -v, --verbose  Show detailed output
      --help         Show this message and exit.
    ```
  - Contrast: `approve.md` covers both `apm approve` AND `apm deny`; `doctor` has no coverage at all in the reference section.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` covering synopsis, all options, exit codes, and examples. The guides content at `docs/src/content/docs/guides/operating-installed-context.md` provides a good starting point.

---

### Medium Severity

#### RST double-backtick notation rendered raw in terminal help text

- **Commands**: `apm approve`, `apm deny`
- **Problem**: The help text for both commands uses RST/Sphinx-style double-backtick markup (` ``text`` `) which renders as literal double-backtick characters in the terminal instead of formatted code. All other commands use plain text or single backticks consistently.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm approve --help
    Adds entries to ``~/.apm/approvals.yml`` (user-local, never committed to
    source control) so that hooks, MCP servers, canvas extensions, and bin/
    executables from the specified packages are deployed during ``apm install``.

  $ apm deny --help
    Removes entries from ``~/.apm/approvals.yml`` (user-local approvals store).
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace ` ``~/.apm/approvals.yml`` ` with single backticks in the `approve` and `deny` command docstrings in the source (likely `src/apm_cli/commands/approve.py`).

---

#### `apm config get` shows a misleading "bug in command routing" error for invalid key input

- **Command**: `apm config get`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config get` with an unknown key shows an error message that incorrectly implies a software bug. The user simply entered an invalid key -- it is not a bug.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config get nonexistent_key
  [x] Unknown configuration key: 'nonexistent_key'
  [i] Valid keys: auto-integrate, target, mcp-registry-url, temp-dir, allow-protocol-fallback, prefer-ssh
  [i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.
  ```
  The third line is incorrect -- this is normal user input validation, not an internal routing failure.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the "This error may indicate a bug in command routing" line from this error path, or replace it with: `[i] Run 'apm config get' with no argument to see all effective values.`

---

#### `apm mcp install --help` uses non-standard option presentation

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: Instead of defining options as standard Click options (shown in the `Options:` section), `apm mcp install` embeds option names as an unformatted paragraph inside the help text. This is visually inconsistent with all other commands.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  All forwarded options are crammed into a single paragraph with no line breaks between option entries.
- **Suggested Fix**: Move the common options list out of the option block and into the epilog/description as a clean formatted list. For example: `All options from 'apm install --mcp NAME' are accepted. Run 'apm install --help' for the full list.`

---

#### `--yes` / `-y` flag has three different descriptions across commands

- **Commands**: `apm deps clean`, `apm update`, `apm runtime remove`
- **Problem**: Three commands share a `-y, --yes` flag for skipping confirmation prompts, but each describes it differently:
  - `apm deps clean`: `Skip confirmation prompt`
  - `apm update`: `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`
  - `apm runtime remove`: `Confirm the action without prompting`
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps clean --help
    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt

  $ apm update --help
    -y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)

  $ apm runtime remove --help
    -y, --yes  Confirm the action without prompting
  ```
  The third form ("Confirm the action without prompting") is semantically different from "Skip confirmation prompt" and could confuse users.
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all three to: `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`. Update `deps clean` and `runtime remove` source to match `apm update`.

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing punctuation in one-line command descriptions

- **Commands**: `apm pack`, `apm publish`
- **Problem**: Most commands in `apm --help` have no trailing period on their one-line description, but `pack` and `publish` do.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm --help
    compile   Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files   <- no period
    config    Configure APM CLI                                       <- no period
    pack      Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.    <- has period
    publish   Publish a package to a registry.                       <- has period
    run       Run a script with parameters (experimental)            <- no period
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing periods from `pack` and `publish` one-line descriptions to match the majority convention.

---

#### Several command descriptions are truncated in `apm --help`

- **Command**: `apm --help` (main help)
- **Problem**: Five commands have one-line summaries that are too long and are cut off with `...` in the main help view.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm --help
    doctor     Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI,...
    find       Trace a materialized file back to its contributing...
    install    Install APM and MCP dependencies (supports APM packages,...
    lock       Resolve dependencies and write apm.lock.yaml without...
    uninstall  Remove APM packages, their integrated files, and apm.yml...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Shorten these one-line summaries to fit within a standard 80-character terminal. For example:
  - `doctor`: "Run environment diagnostics"
  - `install`: "Install APM packages and MCP servers"
  - `lock`: "Write apm.lock.yaml without deploying files"

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- `apm init`, `apm compile`, `apm update`, `apm uninstall`, `apm run` -- consistent help structure, correct flag descriptions, no typos
- `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps clean`, `apm deps update` -- all subcommands present and functional
- `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`, `apm mcp list` -- correct `--limit` defaults (20 for list, 10 for search), consistent `-v/--verbose` flag
- `apm config get`, `apm config set`, `apm config unset` -- consistent with documentation (no `list` subcommand in docs or CLI -- both are aligned)
- `apm runtime setup`, `apm runtime list`, `apm runtime status`, `apm runtime remove` -- all present with consistent flag descriptions
- Error handling: All commands produce clean error messages for invalid flags and missing required arguments -- no stack traces observed
- Documentation cross-reference: All CLI commands have corresponding docs coverage (`deny` is correctly combined with `approve` in `approve.md`)
- Flag consistency: `--dry-run` present across all relevant commands; `--verbose`/`-v` consistent where expected; `-g`/`--global` consistent across scoped commands

issues.title: [FEATURE] Primitives exclusion for targets
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Our team uses both Copilot as Github reviewer agents and Claude Code as coding agents. I have to target both `claude` and `copilot` in our `apm.yml` in order to generate primitives for both.
The problem resides in the fact that both `.agents/` and `.claude/` are generated for skills primitives. I don't want to bloat our repository with unnecessary files in `.agents/` because none of them are used in Claude Code context. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Here is an example of what it could look like in the `targets` section:

```yaml
targets:
  - harness: "copilot"
    primitives: ["instructions"]
  - harness: "claude"
    primitives: ["*"]
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

I've considered pruning `.agents/` folder in the apm `scripts` section after installation. Unfortunately, this also systematically breaks `apm audit --ci` in our CI workflow
Also considered : moving `instructions` from `.apm/` to `.github/`, which also removes them for `.claude/` after using `apm install`

**Additional context**

Having more flexibility on the targets setup will be highly beneficial for entreprise-level codebases, where we value control over our infrastructure. Thank you!

issues.title: Persist resolved MCP server invocations in lockfile for fully-offline `apm mcp export`
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up from #1868 (`apm mcp export --runtime <target>`, PR #1905).

`apm mcp export` regenerates runtime MCP config from resolved `apm.yml` + lockfile state. Today it is **fully offline for self-defined servers** (`registry: false`, whose full config lives in `apm.yml`), but **registry-sourced servers require MCP-registry reachability** to materialize their server invocation (command/args/env).

## Why the network call is unavoidable today

The lockfile's `mcp_configs` field (`src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py`) stores each dep's `apm.yml` declaration as a drift-detection baseline (`MCPIntegrator._detect_mcp_config_drift`). It does **not** store the resolved server invocation returned by the registry. So when `apm mcp export` writes a registry-sourced server into a runtime config file, it must call `validate_servers_exist` + `batch_fetch_server_info` against the registry to obtain the actual command to write.

This was accepted as the v1 boundary for #1868 per a two-lens advisory panel (python-architect + devx-ux-expert), which recommended documenting the boundary now and tracking fully-offline support as a separate, separately-reviewed change.

## Ask

Persist the resolved MCP server invocation (command, args, env, and any overlay-applied fields) for registry-sourced deps in the lockfile so that `apm mcp export` -- and air-gapped CI -- can regenerate registry-server config without any network round-trip.

## Design notes (light)

- Coordinate with the lockfile metadata work in #1904 (name/version per entry) to avoid schema churn / migration thrash.
- Likely a new per-server field under `mcp_configs` (or a sibling map) capturing the resolved invocation, written during `apm install`'s registry path and consumed by `_apply_mcp_configs` when present.
- Consider a `--offline` flag on `apm mcp export` that hard-errors if any requested registry server lacks a persisted invocation, so the offline guarantee is explicit and CI-enforceable.
- Treat the persisted invocation as inventory/display state, not a trust anchor (same boundary discipline as the #1904 name/version metadata).

## Context

Parent: #1868 / PR #1905. Related: #1904.

issues.title: [DESIGN] Per-package primitive routing (`targets:`) as the single placement mechanism
issues.body:
## North star

APM needs exactly **one** answer to "who controls which primitive goes to which harness, and in what shape." This issue records the converged three-layer model so future requests (and PRs) resolve against a single design instead of accreting per-type flags and new verbs.

This supersedes the per-primitive-type approach in #1898 and is the design that PR #1902 implements.

## The three layers

| Layer | Question | Mechanism | Status |
|-------|----------|-----------|--------|
| **CONSENT** | May this package's executable run at all? | `executables: {allow, deny}` keyed per-package x per-exec-type (hooks/mcp/bin/canvas), deny-wins, deny-by-default | shipped (`security/executables.py`) |
| **PLACEMENT** | Which harness(es) does this package go to? | per-package `targets:` on a dependency entry, **uniform across every primitive type in that package** | PR #1902 |
| **PORTING** | What shape per harness? | each primitive written to the harness's native format (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.agents/skills/`, ...) | shipped |
| *(intra-harness)* | Where inside a harness do instructions land? | `apm compile` (root/nested `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules` toggle) | shipped |

## Design rulings (and why)

1. **No new lifecycle verb.** `apm install` is idempotent regeneration; `apm audit` detects drift. We do not add `apm sync`, `apm mcp export`, or a `--check` flag (declines #1868 / closes PR #1905).
2. **No per-primitive-TYPE routing for inert primitives** (declines #1898). Splitting one package's skills to one harness and its instructions to another is a *fork* of that package. The supported path is per-package routing: route an instruction-only package to one harness and a skill-only package to another. The bloat #1898 describes is a harness-standards gap (Claude does not read the `.agents/skills/` convention that Copilot/Cursor/Codex/Gemini share), not an APM defect.
3. **Hooks are not special.** "hooks off" = the CONSENT trust floor (`apm deny <pkg> hooks`). "hooks to one harness" = plain per-package `targets:`. No dedicated `hooks:` lever.
4. **We port, we do not glue.** Porting a primitive into each harness's native format is faithful porting. Inventing a universal cross-harness format, or translating semantics between harnesses that disagree on a should-be-standard, is out of scope. (This is also why #1892 is a porting *bug*, not a translation layer.)

## Folds into this design

- #1898 -- per-package routing covers the legit residual; per-type filter declined.
- #1868 / PR #1905 -- export verb declined.
- #1894 -- already expressible via the deny-by-default trust floor; at most a `--no-hooks` sugar that writes the `deny`.
- #1807 -- intra-harness placement served by `apm compile`; any author-intent residual is the PORTING layer here.
- #1892 -- the porting bug PR #1902 fixes.

## Implementation

The build surface is substantially PR #1902. Re-reviewed via the apm-review-panel against this model, then driven to green. #1882 (require explicit targets) is tracked separately as opt-in governance.
