issues.title: PR #1798 lifecycle "hooks" collides with the agent-hooks primitive -- rename to "scripts" + integrate governance
issues.body:
## Summary

A 3-lens design/UX/security red team (run while shepherding #1798) found that the **lifecycle "hooks"** framework introduced by #1798 (closes #1529) collides head-on with APM's existing **agent-hooks primitive** and never enters the executable-trust governance ladder (#1873). Verdict was **unanimous: rename `hooks` -> `scripts` before merge, and route lifecycle execution through the existing `executables` policy ladder**. Migration cost is **zero** (PR is unreleased). This issue records the finding so the author (@sergio-sisternes-epam) and maintainer can act with full context.

> Correction (post-review against `origin/main` @ 6bd88ccc3): an earlier revision of this issue referred to an admin setting `allowExecutables: { hooks: false }` as a global toggle. That is schema-invalid and has been removed -- see the accurate governance model below.
>
> Correction 2: an earlier revision proposed folding lifecycle scripts into the package-keyed `executables` ladder as a 5th exec type (`EXEC_TYPE_SCRIPTS`). That conflates two different concepts -- supply-chain trust of INSTALLED package primitives vs. run-time execution of imperative lifecycle actions. Section 2 below now keeps them as SEPARATE governance surfaces.

## The collision (grounded in code)

APM already ships **"hooks"** as a first-class managed primitive -- agent tool-loop callbacks compiled into harnesses (Claude `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`, Copilot `preToolUse`, Cursor `afterFileEdit`):

- `src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py`
- `docs/src/content/docs/producer/author-primitives/hooks-and-commands.md` (its title literally says "lifecycle hooks" for AGENT hooks)
- `src/apm_cli/security/executables.py` -> `EXEC_TYPE_HOOKS = "hooks"`, one of the governed exec types
- discovery path `.apm/hooks/*.json`, envelope `{"version":1,"hooks":{...}}`, keys `type`/`bash`/`timeoutSec`

PR #1798 reuses **the same noun, the same `.apm/hooks*` path, the same JSON envelope, and the same inner keys** for package-manager lifecycle scripts (`pre-install`/`post-install`/...). Same word, opposite meaning.

## How executable governance actually works (post-#1873)

Two distinct layers, neither of which the PR touches:

1. **Org policy** (`apm-policy.yml`, `policy/schema.py::ExecutablesPolicy`): an `executables:` block with
   - `deny_all` -- kill-switch denying **every executable type for all packages** (OR-merged through inheritance);
   - `deny` / `require` / `recommend` / `enforce` -- package-canonical-string lists.
   These feed `security/executables.py::resolve_exec_decision`, a deny-wins, first-match-wins ladder keyed by `(package_key, exec_type)` with exec types `hooks` / `mcp` / `bin` / `canvas`.
2. **Consumer consent** (`apm.yml`, `allowExecutables`): **package-keyed** approvals `{ "<pkg>@<ver>": { hooks|mcp|bin|canvas: bool } }`. It is local per-package consent, NOT a global on/off switch.

## Three-lens verdict

| Lens | Verdict | Severity |
|------|---------|----------|
| primitives-architect | RENAME-REQUIRED | 9/10, conf 9.5 -- 2 BLOCKERs + 1 HIGH |
| devx-ux (pkg-mgr mental model) | RENAME-REQUIRED | 9/10, 95% |
| supply-chain-security | governance bypass confirmed | HIGH |

**BLOCKER 1 -- discovery cross-read:** identical JSON shape (`{"version":1,"hooks":{...}}`) in overlapping `.apm/hooks*` locations means a lifecycle script can be silently fed to the agent-hook compiler (or vice versa), undetectable at parse time.

**BLOCKER 2 -- governance bypass (corrected):** lifecycle script execution in `build_runner_from_context` never calls `resolve_exec_decision`, so it sits **entirely outside** the #1873 ladder. An org that sets `executables.deny_all: true` to lock down every executable primitive would still have lifecycle command scripts auto-execute on `apm install`. The org kill-switch and per-package deny/recommend do not reach lifecycle scripts at all.

**HIGH -- naming polysemy:** every doc/error/help string must forever qualify "hooks (agent)" vs "hooks (lifecycle)".

## Recommended remediation

### 1. Rename `hooks` -> `scripts` (npm/yarn/pnpm/cargo/bundler prior art; reserve "hooks" for the agent primitive)

| Current (PR #1798) | Proposed |
|---|---|
| `apm hooks` (+ test/init/validate) | `apm scripts` |
| `.apm/hooks.json` | `.apm/scripts.json` |
| `~/.apm/hooks/*.json` | `~/.apm/scripts/*.json` |
| `core/lifecycle_hooks.py` | `core/lifecycle_scripts.py` |
| `core/hook_executors.py` | `core/script_executors.py` |
| `commands/hooks.py` | `commands/scripts.py` |
| envelope `{"version":1,"hooks":{...}}` | `{"version":1,"scripts":{...}}` |
| events `pre-install` etc. | unchanged |

### 2. Govern lifecycle scripts as a SEPARATE surface (do NOT fold into the package-keyed `executables` ladder)

These are two different concepts and must not be conflated:

| | `executables` (#1873) | lifecycle scripts (#1798) |
|---|---|---|
| Question | "deploy/materialize this installed primitive?" | "run this imperative command at this PM event?" |
| Verb | deploy into harness | execute during install flow |
| Key | `(package_key, exec_type)` -- package identity intrinsic | source scope (policy/user/project); often NO package identity |
| Moment | resolve/deploy time | lifecycle event (`pre-install`...) |

Folding scripts in as a 5th `exec_type` would force **synthetic package keys** (`__project__` etc.) for things that have no package -- a fabricated identity the supply-chain lens explicitly warned against. npm models this the same way: per-dependency trust is one thing; lifecycle `scripts` are governed separately (`--ignore-scripts`).

Recommended:

- Give lifecycle scripts their **own source-scoped policy surface** (e.g. a `scripts` / `lifecycle` policy block, or a `run-scripts` toggle), keyed by source scope, NOT by package canonical string.
- Keep a **content-hash dev-local trust store** (direnv / Workspace-Trust model) as the project-source consent layer.
- Honor org `executables.deny_all` as a **one-directional safety ceiling only**: if an org has locked down all executable primitives, also suppress lifecycle scripts (denying arbitrary RCE is strictly safer). Implement by READING that flag, not by merging scripts into `resolve_exec_decision`.
- Surface the new surface in `apm policy explain` as its own section, distinct from the package executable rows.

### 3. Security gap to close regardless of naming

As written, `build_runner_from_context` fires discovered project scripts with **no consent gate** -- cloning an untrusted repo and running `apm install` executes attacker-controlled `shell=True` commands. The dev-local trust gate above (skip untrusted project scripts until explicitly trusted) is the minimum fix; a hardened branch implementing this (plus credential-denylist allowlisting for #1529's `ANALYTICS_TOKEN`, log redaction, and HTTP working-directory PII minimisation) exists locally and can be contributed once the noun/governance direction is settled.

## Links
- PR: #1798
- Origin issue: #1529 (narrow opt-in analytics; the scope this generalized)
- Governance baseline: #1873 (executable-trust ladder)

/cc maintainer -- naming + governance is a positioning decision; flagging rather than rewriting the contributor's PR unilaterally.

issues.title: [BUG] apm audit reports false "unintegrated" drift on .agents/skills/ for deps narrowed via per-dependency targets:
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a `dependencies.apm` entry uses per-dependency `targets:` to narrow a skill dependency to a subset of harnesses (e.g. `targets: [claude]`), `apm install` correctly deploys the skill only to that harness's directory (`.claude/skills/`) and **not** to the cross-tool `.agents/skills/` mirror. But `apm audit --ci` still expects `.agents/skills/<dep>/...` and reports those files as `unintegrated` drift, failing the audit even though `apm install` reports the state as up to date.

`apm install` and `apm audit` disagree on the expected file set. This appears to be a gap in the per-dependency `targets:` feature (#1902, v0.22.0): the audit drift replay does not honor per-dependency `targets:`. The `content-integrity` check itself passes — only the `drift` check is wrong.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `apm.yml` with global `targets: [claude, copilot]` and a skill dependency in object form narrowed to Claude:
   ```yaml
   targets: [claude, copilot]
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: owner/repo
         path: skills/some-skill
         targets: [claude]
   ```
2. Run `apm install` → skill lands in `.claude/skills/some-skill`, nothing in `.agents/skills/`. Re-running `apm install` reports `No changes -- install state already up to date`.
3. Run `apm audit --ci` → `Drift detected: N file(s)` with `unintegrated: .agents/skills/some-skill/...`; audit exits non-zero.

**Expected behavior**

`apm audit` should honor per-dependency `targets:` when computing the expected deployed-file set, so a dependency narrowed away from the cross-tool / Copilot targets does not produce false `unintegrated` drift for `.agents/skills/`. Audit should agree with `apm install`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11 (also reproduced in CI on Linux / `ubuntu-latest`)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.22.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a (Claude Code + Copilot targets)

**Logs**

```
[+] Replayed N package(s)
[>] Diffing scratch vs working tree...
[!] Drift detected: <count> file(s)
...
  drift details:
    - unintegrated: .agents/skills/<skill-a>/SKILL.md
    - unintegrated: .agents/skills/<skill-a>/references/<file>.md
    - unintegrated: .agents/skills/<skill-b>/SKILL.md
    ...
[x] 1 of 9 check(s) failed
```

(`content-integrity` check passes; only the `drift` check fails.)

**Additional context**

Related but distinct from closed issues #1716 (`.agents/skills/` content *escaping* the drift check) and #1411 (false *orphaned* drift for non-skill primitives with `auto_create=False`). Here it is false **`unintegrated`** drift specifically triggered by per-dependency `targets:` narrowing. Use case: routing skills to Claude only while keeping Copilot for instructions + MCP servers.

issues.title: [BUG] apm audit reports false Copilot instruction drift when .github exists but Copilot is not a target
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install` and `apm targets` honor project-level `targets:` from `apm.yml`, but
`apm audit --ci` appears to replay local instructions for Copilot when a regular `.github/`
directory exists, even if Copilot is not an active target.

In this state, `apm install` is a no-op and does not create `.github/instructions/**`, but
`apm audit --ci` fails with false `unintegrated` drift for `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`.

**To Reproduce**

Create a minimal project:

```yaml
# apm.yml
name: apm-audit-github-dir-targets-repro
version: 1.0.0
description: Minimal repro for audit target drift when .github exists.
author: Repro
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp: []
includes: auto
scripts: {}
targets:
  - claude
  - codex
  - cursor
```

```markdown
<!-- .apm/instructions/local.instructions.md -->
---
description: Local instruction target repro.
applyTo: "**/*"
---

# Local Instruction Target Repro

When editing this repository, use the local instruction.
```

Also add any normal GitHub repository file, for example:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/placeholder.yml
name: Placeholder

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  noop:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: "true"
```

Then run:

```bash
apm install --no-policy
apm targets
find .github -maxdepth 3 -type f -print
apm audit --ci --no-policy
```

`apm install --no-policy` reports:

```text
[i] Targets: claude, codex, cursor  (source: apm.yml)
[+] <project root> (local)
|-- 2 rule(s) adopted -> .claude/rules/, .cursor/rules/
|-- (files unchanged)

[i] No changes -- install state already up to date
```

`apm targets` reports Copilot as inactive:

```text
claude   active
copilot  inactive   needs .github/copilot-instructions.md
cursor   active
codex    active
```

`.github` contains only the workflow file:

```text
.github/workflows/placeholder.yml
```

But `apm audit --ci --no-policy` fails:

```text
[>] Replaying install (cache-only)...
[+] Replayed 1 package(s)
[>] Diffing scratch vs working tree...
[!] Drift detected: 1 file(s)

drift details:
  - unintegrated: .github/instructions/local.instructions.md

[x] 1 of 9 check(s) failed
```

**Expected behavior**

`apm audit --ci` should use the same target resolution as `apm install` and `apm targets`.

If `targets:` excludes Copilot and `apm targets` reports Copilot inactive, audit replay should not expect
`.github/instructions/**`, even when the repository has a normal `.github/` directory for GitHub workflows or linter
configuration.

**Actual behavior**

`apm install` does not deploy Copilot instructions and reports the project as up to date, but `apm audit --ci` expects
`.github/instructions/local.instructions.md` and fails drift detection.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux x86_64
- Python Version: Python 3.14.6
- APM Version: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.22.0 (78811e3)
- VSCode Version: n/a

**Additional context**

This is related to but distinct from:

- #1923: false drift for dependencies narrowed via per-dependency `targets:`.
- #1846: false `no-orphaned-packages` for transitive dependencies, which appears fixed in 0.22.0.

This issue is specifically about project-level `targets:` being honored by `apm install` / `apm targets`, but not by
the `apm audit --ci` drift replay when `.github/` exists for unrelated GitHub repository configuration.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Support policy enforcement on non-GitHub remotes: add --policy to apm install (and/or auto-discovery for GitLab/ADO/plain git)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

On non-GitHub remotes there's no way to apply policy at install time. apm install has no --policy flag, and policy auto-discovery only works for GitHub/GHE remotes.  
Both gaps are already documented in the Governance guide §14 ("Known gaps and limitations"). Per that section, when git remote get-url origin points to GitLab, ADO, or a plain git host, auto-discovery falls through with no policy applied, and the only documented mitigation is apm audit --ci --policy <path-or-url> in CI.  
That leaves a real hole: teams on a GitLab/ADO remote can gate at audit/merge time, but get zero enforcement at install time. For agent primitives, presence is effectively execution, a disallowed skill, steering file, or hook is active on the developer's workstation the moment it lands on disk, i.e. in the window between apm install and the eventual MR.   
Audit-at-merge catches it before it reaches main, but not before it reaches the developer's machine. Orgs wanting defense-in-depth (block at install, not just at review) currently have no supported mechanism on non-GitHub remotes, short of baking the policy into a custom install image, which doesn't generalize across teams.  


**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a --policy <path-or-url> flag to apm install, mirroring the flag apm audit already supports. It would apply the policy at install time and fail closed on violation, consistent with audit behaviour.   
This is fully explicit, requires no remote detection, and lets any host (GitLab, ADO, plain git) point install at a vendored or internally-hosted policy.  
Existing semantics should be preserved: tighten-only inheritance (enterprise → org → repo), and the existing cross-host extends: rejection (credential-leak mitigation) - a vendored same-host policy is unaffected.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Extending policy auto-discovery to non-GitHub remotes (GitLab/ADO/plain git) using the same git-host abstraction already used to resolve package dependencies, which works across these hosts today. This would remove the need to pass --policy explicitly, but it's a larger surface change. Happy to go this route instead if maintainers prefer it - the --policy flag just seemed the smaller, higher-leverage fix.  
Audit-time gating only (apm audit --ci --policy …), the currently documented mitigation. This works for blocking at merge, but consciously accepts the install-to-MR workstation window with no enforcement, which is insufficient for teams that want install-time defense-in-depth.  
Baking the policy into a custom install image. Works, but every consuming team has to build and maintain their own policy-bundling image rather than pointing install at an internal policy file, not generalisable.  

**Additional context**

Both gaps are documented as known limitations in the Governance guide §14:   https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance-guide/#14-known-gaps-and-limitations. 
This request targets the install-time half. Related §9 air-gapped guidance already recommends apm audit --ci --policy ./vendored-policy.yml as the gating workaround, so a vendored/internally-hosted policy file is an established pattern; this just extends it to the install step.   
Motivation is enterprise rollout on an internal GitLab host where install-time enforcement is wanted alongside the existing CI gate.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-26
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-26
**APM Version**: 0.22.0 (f8c4244)
**Commands Inspected**: 27

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 1 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm deps update` missing deprecation notice in CLI help
- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The CLI help text shows no deprecation notice. The docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`) explicitly warn that `apm deps update` is deprecated in favor of `apm update`, and the internal guide (`packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/commands.md`) also marks it as "Deprecated -- use `apm update` instead". Users who discover the command through `apm deps --help` have no in-CLI signal to switch to `apm update`.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI output: `Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...` / `Update APM dependencies to latest refs` -- no deprecation mention
  - Docs: `:::caution[Deprecated] \`apm deps update\` is deprecated in favor of [\`apm update\`](../update/), which is now a strict superset...`
  - Compare: `apm install --update` DOES inline its deprecation: `(deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan, or 'apm update --yes' for CI)`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a deprecation notice to the `apm deps update` description string, matching the pattern used by `apm install --update`. For example: change the command description to `"Update APM dependencies to latest refs (deprecated: use 'apm update' instead, which is a strict superset)"`.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm install --runtime` does not disclose it is a legacy alias
- **Command**: `apm install --runtime`
- **Problem**: The `--runtime` flag in CLI help describes itself as "Target specific runtime only (...)" with no indication that it is a deprecated legacy alias for `--target`. The install documentation explicitly calls it a "Legacy alias for `--target` (single value only). Still accepted; prefer `--target`." Users reading only CLI help are not guided toward `--target`.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI output: `--runtime TEXT  Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex, cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf)`
  - Docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md`): `| \`--runtime VALUE\` | unset | Legacy alias for \`--target\` (single value only). Still accepted; prefer \`--target\`. |`
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--runtime` help string to: `"(Legacy alias for --target, single value only; prefer --target) Target specific runtime ..."`.

---

#### `apm install --runtime` lists `vscode` but `--target` does not
- **Command**: `apm install --runtime` vs `apm install --target`
- **Problem**: The `--runtime` flag lists `vscode` as a valid value (`copilot, claude, codex, cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf`) but the `--target` flag does NOT list `vscode` in its values. If `vscode` is a supported target, it should appear in `--target`; if it is not, it should be removed from `--runtime`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `--runtime` valid values from CLI help: `copilot, claude, codex, cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf`
  - `--target` valid values from CLI help: `copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all`
  - `vscode` appears in `--runtime` but not in `--target`
- **Suggested Fix**: Audit whether `vscode` is a functional target. If yes, add it to the `--target` enumerated values. If no, remove it from the `--runtime` help text.

---

#### `apm compile --no-dedup` / `--no-force-instructions` confusing flag naming
- **Command**: `apm compile --help`
- **Problem**: Both flag names in the pair start with `--no-` but the action described is a positive one ("Include the instructions section"). The actual usable alias (`--force-instructions`) is only mentioned in the description prose, not in the usage line. This creates a confusing double-negative (`--no-force-instructions` means "do NOT force-include", i.e. the default state).
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI output: `--no-dedup / --no-force-instructions   Include the instructions section in CLAUDE.md even when .claude/rules/ is already populated... Alias: --force-instructions.`
  - The guide (`packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/commands.md`) correctly lists it as `--no-dedup / --force-instructions` (positive alias shown)
  - Running `apm compile --force-instructions` works, but this alias is hidden in the options table
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the Click boolean flag definition to surface `--force-instructions` as the primary positive name and `--no-force-instructions` (or `--no-dedup`) as the disable form. The usage line should show `--force-instructions / --no-force-instructions` with `--no-dedup` listed as an alias in the description.

---

#### `apm mcp install` uses non-standard options presentation
- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: The `apm mcp install` help shows only `--help` as an explicit option, then lists common forwarded options as freeform text after the options block. Users must separately consult `apm install --help` to discover flags like `--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--dry-run`, etc. The options are not machine-parseable and break the standard Click help contract.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either declare the forwarded flags as explicit Click options on `apm mcp install` (matching their definitions in `apm install`), or at minimum move the prose list outside the `Options:` section using a Click epilog so help text renders cleanly. The current layout embeds unstructured text inside the options block.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm deps info` help does not mention it is an alias for `apm view`
- **Command**: `apm deps info --help`
- **Problem**: The help text says only "Show detailed package information" with no indication that it is equivalent to `apm view PACKAGE` for installed packages. The documentation (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`) says "Equivalent to `apm view PACKAGE` for installed packages; prefer `apm view` in new scripts." Users are not guided toward the canonical `apm view` command.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI output: `Usage: apm deps info [OPTIONS] PACKAGE` / `Show detailed package information`
  - Docs: "Show detailed information about one installed package: manifest metadata, primitive inventory, and source. Equivalent to [\`apm view PACKAGE\`](../view/) for installed packages; prefer \`apm view\` in new scripts."
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `apm deps info` description to: `"Show detailed package information (alias for 'apm view PACKAGE' for installed packages; prefer 'apm view' in new scripts)"`.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- `apm --help`: Top-level help, version flag, and common workflows section are accurate and complete.
- `apm init --help`: All flags documented; deprecated flags (`--plugin`, `--marketplace`) correctly note alternatives inline.
- `apm install --help`: Comprehensive flag documentation; inline deprecation notice on `--update` is correct. `--frozen`, `--dry-run`, and `--force` semantics are accurately described.
- `apm uninstall --help`: Consistent with documentation; `--dry-run`, `-v`, `-g` flags all present.
- `apm update --help`: Complete; `-y`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`, `--parallel-downloads` all accurately described.
- `apm compile --help` (aside from `--no-dedup` naming): All other flags accurate.
- `apm run --help`: Correct; `--param` / `-p` and `--verbose` present.
- `apm deps list/tree/clean/why --help`: Flags consistent with documentation.
- `apm mcp list/search/show --help`: Default values consistent with docs (`list` default 20, `search` default 10).
- `apm config / get / set / unset`: Behavior matches documentation; `apm config` with no subcommand correctly prints a merged table.
- `apm runtime setup/list/status/remove --help`: All subcommands present and consistent with documentation.
- Error handling: All tested invalid-argument and missing-argument cases produce clean `Error:` messages, not stack traces. (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no arg), `apm config set` (no args), `apm mcp search` (no query).)
- `apm unpack --help`: Deprecation notice present and correctly points to `apm install`.

issues.title: apm install --update silently skips packages when both repo URL and tag change simultaneously
issues.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary

When a package in `apm.yml` is updated to point to a **new repository** _and_ a **new tag** simultaneously (e.g. after a monorepo reorganisation), `apm install --update` reports _"No changes — install state already up to date"_ and does **not** update the lock file or the installed files. The stale lock entry is silently carried forward.

### APM version

```
Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.21.0 (975f8f0)
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a package installed at an old location, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   # apm.yml (before)
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - private-org/old-repo/content/my-package#my-package/v1.0.0
   ```
   Lock file contains:
   ```yaml
   - repo_url: private-org/old-repo
     resolved_ref: my-package/v1.0.0
     virtual_path: content/my-package
   ```

2. Update `apm.yml` to point to the package's new canonical location (same package name, new repo + new path):
   ```yaml
   # apm.yml (after)
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/my-package#my-package/v1.1.0
   ```

3. Run:
   ```
   apm install --update --target copilot
   ```

### Actual behaviour

```
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.2s.
```

Lock file is **not** updated. Still contains the old `repo_url`, `resolved_ref`, and `virtual_path`.

### Expected behaviour

APM should detect that the declared dependency in `apm.yml` no longer matches the locked entry (different `repo_url` + different tag), re-resolve, update the lock, and install the new version.

### Verbose output (smoking gun)

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Parsed apm.yml: 1 APM deps, 0 MCP deps
Loaded apm.lock.yaml for SHA comparison (2 dependencies)
    private-org/old-repo/sdlc/agents: locked at 673c47f8
Resolved 1 direct dependencies (no transitive)
...
apm.lock.yaml unchanged -- skipping write
[i] No changes -- install state already up to date in 0.2s.
```

`apm.yml` contains **12** APM dependency entries, but `Parsed apm.yml: 1 APM deps` — only 1 is being processed for resolution. The resolver appears to skip packages already present in the lock file by matching on package name / tag stem, without validating that `repo_url` or `virtual_path` still match the declaration in `apm.yml`.

### Lock file drift (before vs after)

| Field | apm.yml (declared) | apm.lock.yaml (stale) |
|---|---|---|
| repo | `private-org/new-repo` | `private-org/old-repo` |
| tag | `my-package/v1.1.0` | `my-package/v1.0.0` |
| virtual_path | `packages/category/subcategory/my-package` | `content/my-package` |

Same pattern observed for two other packages migrated in the same operation.

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | macOS Darwin |
| APM version | 0.21.0 (975f8f0) |
| Lock file `apm_version` | 0.18.0 (generated 2026-06-15, before the edit) |
| Command | `apm install --update --target copilot` (run from `~`) |
| Cache | 8 git repos, 10 checkouts, 274.7 MB |

`apm.yml` (illustrative — all refs anonymised):
```yaml
name: global
version: 1.0.0
dependencies:
  apm:
  - private-org/old-repo/devops/pkg-a#pkg-a/v1.0.0
  - private-org/old-repo/architecture/pkg-b#pkg-b/v1.1.0
  - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/my-package#my-package/v1.1.0
  - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/pkg-c#pkg-c/v0.2.0
  - private-org/new-repo/packages/category/subcategory/pkg-d#pkg-d/v1.0.0
  - private-org/toolkit-repo/packages/toolkit#toolkit/v0.5.1
  - public-author/public-package
  - /local/path/to/package  # local dep
  mcp: []
```

### Workaround

Manually edit `apm.lock.yaml` to remove the stale entries, then re-run `apm install`. APM will re-resolve and install correctly.

Alternatively, `apm cache clean` followed by `apm install` also forces a full re-resolution.

### Impact

This affects any user who **migrates a package from one repository to another** (e.g. monorepo reorg, marketplace consolidation) while keeping the same package name/tag stem. The silent no-op is particularly dangerous because there is no warning — the user assumes the update succeeded.

### Hypothesis

The resolver's drift-detection logic appears to match lock entries by **tag stem** (e.g. `my-package`) rather than by the full `(repo_url, resolved_ref, virtual_path)` tuple. When the tag name is unchanged (same package name, version bumped OR same version in a new repo), the lock entry is considered a match and the re-resolution is skipped.

issues.title: Track KTLO/maintenance risk of `llm-github-models` (default `github/` runtime plugin)
issues.body:
## Context

`llm-github-models` is a **core runtime dependency** (`pyproject.toml`). It provides the `github/...` model strings (e.g. `github/gpt-4o-mini`) via the `llm` CLI's plugin entry-point auto-discovery. This is APM's **default, documented free-tier runtime**:

- `templates/hello-world/apm.yml` -> `llm: "llm hello-world.prompt.md -m github/gpt-4o-mini"`
- Referenced across docs: `consumer/run-scripts.md`, `reference/cli/list.md`, `reference/cli/runtime.md`, `integrations/runtime-compatibility.md`, and the GitHub Models free-tier onboarding hook.

## The concern

`llm-github-models` was flagged as a potential **KTLO ("keep the lights on") / maintenance liability** — a third-party plugin that APM's primary first-run experience depends on, but which APM does not control. If it stalls, breaks against newer `llm` releases, or is abandoned, the default `apm run` quickstart degrades.

## Current coupling (assessed)

- **Zero code coupling.** `grep` finds it referenced ONLY in `pyproject.toml` (declared dependency) + generated egg-info. No `import` anywhere in `src/`, `docs/`, `templates/`, or `packages/`. APM relies entirely on `llm`'s plugin auto-discovery at runtime.
- Compatible with the current `llm 0.31` (`llm-github-models` 0.18.0 requires `llm>=0.26`). Floor was just raised to `>=0.18.0` in #1936 for supply-chain hygiene.

## Why this is tracked separately (not fixed in #1936)

#1936 (Dependabot remediation) deliberately **kept** the plugin: removing it would break the default `-m github/gpt-4o-mini` quickstart, which is a P4 adoption-funnel / UX-is-the-floor surface — a product decision, not a security cleanup.

## Options to evaluate

1. **Keep + monitor** (status quo): pin a known-good floor, watch upstream release cadence, add a CI smoke test that exercises `github/...` resolution so breakage is caught early.
2. **Vendor-neutralize the default**: make GitHub Models opt-in and pick a more clearly maintained default, with template + docs updates. (Higher blast radius.)
3. **Reduce dependence**: document a fallback runtime path so a `llm-github-models` outage does not hard-block first-run.

## Suggested next step

Decide between (1) and (2). If (1), add a lightweight CI check that the `github/` model namespace still resolves after `llm`/plugin bumps, so KTLO drift surfaces in CI rather than in users' first run.

_Filed as follow-up to the Dependabot remediation in #1936._

issues.title: [BUG] apm install deploys skill-bundle files verbatim with CRLF, causing content-integrity hash drift in CI
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`#1913` normalizes APM-*rendered* text files to LF on every platform. But skill **bundle** files that APM copies **verbatim** from a dependency are not normalized: if the dependency's source ships CRLF, APM deploys them with CRLF and records **CRLF hashes** in `apm.lock.yaml` (`deployed_file_hashes`).

Most repos normalize committed text to LF (`core.autocrlf=true`, or a `.gitattributes` with `text=auto`). So the committed blob is LF while the lockfile hash is CRLF. On a Linux CI checkout (LF), `apm audit --ci` then reports `content-integrity` hash drift for every file of that dependency, failing the audit — even though the content is identical apart from line endings.

It passes locally on Windows (working tree is CRLF, matching the CRLF lockfile hash) and fails on Linux CI (LF) — the same platform split `#1913` set out to remove, but for copied bundle files rather than rendered ones.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Depend on a skill package whose source files use CRLF line endings:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: owner/repo
         ref: some-branch     # source ships CRLF
         targets: [claude]
   ```
2. On Windows (or any repo with `core.autocrlf=true` / `text=auto`), run `apm install`. APM deploys the skill verbatim with CRLF and records CRLF hashes in `apm.lock.yaml`.
3. Commit the deployed files — git normalizes them to LF in the blob.
4. On Linux CI: `apm audit --ci` → `content-integrity: N file(s) with hash drift`, exit 1. `apm audit` on Windows is green.

**Expected behavior**

APM should normalize deployed **text** files to LF on every platform — including skill-bundle files copied verbatim from a dependency — consistent with `#1913`, so `deployed_file_hashes` match LF-normalized git blobs and `apm audit --ci` is stable across Windows and Linux. (Binary files should be left untouched.)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11 (audit fails on Linux / `ubuntu-latest` CI)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.23.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a (Claude Code + Copilot targets)

**Logs**

```
                           [>] APM Policy Compliance

```

**Additional context**

Distinct from #1913 (rendered files) and #1923/#1930 (audit honoring per-dependency `targets:`). This one is specifically about **copied skill-bundle files** keeping their upstream CRLF. issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-29
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-29  
**APM Version**: 0.23.0 (c550b36)  
**Commands Inspected**: 81 (33 top-level + 48 subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 2     |
| Medium   | 4     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### High Severity

#### H1: `apm doctor` has no dedicated CLI reference page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: A fully-functional top-level command with no `doctor.md` in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. Referenced in multiple guides but absent from the sidebar reference.
- **Evidence**: `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/ | grep doctor` returns nothing. The command works: `apm doctor --help` shows usage with `-v, --verbose`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` covering synopsis, flags, exit codes, and examples.

#### H2: `apm deny` has no dedicated CLI reference page

- **Command**: `apm deny`
- **Problem**: A distinct top-level command documented only as a sub-section within `approve.md`. No `deny.md` exists; not listed in the reference index.
- **Evidence**: `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/ | grep deny` returns nothing. Command works: `apm deny --help` shows usage.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deny.md` (or make `approve.md` discoverable as `approve-deny`). Add `deny` to the reference index table.

---

### Medium Severity

#### M1: Reference index table omits 7 commands that have dedicated pages

- **Location**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`
- **Problem**: The CLI table lists 24 commands but the following 7 have `reference/cli/` pages not linked from the table: `approve`, `find`, `lifecycle`, `lock`, `plugin`, `publish`, `self-update`. Plus `deny` and `doctor` have no pages AND no table entries (see H1/H2).
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the 7 missing commands to the table under appropriate phase headings.

#### M2: `apm mcp install` error output leaks internal implementation

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: On bad input, error output displays `Usage: apm install [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...` and `Try 'apm install --help' for help.` instead of referencing `apm mcp install`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install bad-name --transport wrong
  Usage: apm install [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...
  Try 'apm install --help' for help.
  Error: Invalid value for '--transport': 'wrong' is not one of 'stdio', 'http', ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Override the error context in `apm mcp install` so usage line and help hint reference `apm mcp install [OPTIONS] NAME`.

#### M3: `apm cache clean` has two flags with identical descriptions

- **Command**: `apm cache clean`
- **Problem**: Both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes` show description "Skip confirmation prompt" with no indication that `--yes` is an alias. The docs (`cache.md`) correctly explains the aliasing; the CLI help does not.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm cache clean --help
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update `--yes` description to: "Alias for --force; skip the confirmation prompt (for CI scripts)."

#### M4: `--force` has inconsistent semantics across commands

- **Commands**: `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm pack` vs `apm cache clean`, `apm marketplace migrate`
- **Problem**: `--force` means "overwrite locally-authored files on collision" in install/update/pack, but means "skip confirmation prompt" in `apm cache clean` and "overwrite config block" in `apm marketplace migrate`. This inconsistency conflicts with the established convention.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm install --force`: "Overwrite locally-authored files on collision"
  - `apm cache clean -f, --force`: "Skip confirmation prompt"
  - `apm marketplace migrate -y, --force, --yes`: "Overwrite an existing 'marketplace:' block in apm.yml"
- **Suggested Fix**: Reserve `--force` for collision/overwrite semantics. For `cache clean` and `marketplace migrate`, use only `-y/--yes` for confirmation-skipping.

---

### Low Severity

#### L1: `apm prune` lacks `-v`/`--verbose` flag

- **Command**: `apm prune`
- **Problem**: `apm prune` (removes packages not in `apm.yml`) has no `--verbose` flag despite similar mutating commands (`apm install`, `apm update`, `apm uninstall`) all supporting it.
- **Evidence**: `apm prune --help` shows only `--dry-run` and `--help` as options.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose` to `apm prune`.

#### L2: Deprecation notation is inconsistent

- **Commands**: `apm init` (flags), `apm unpack`, `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: Three notations used: `(deprecated)` (init flags), `[Deprecated]` (unpack command description), `DEPRECATED:` (deps update description).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm init --plugin:       "(deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead."
  apm unpack description:  "[Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle..."
  apm deps update:         "DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead"
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize on `[Deprecated]` in command descriptions and `(deprecated)` for individual flags.

---

### Clean Areas

- All 33 top-level commands respond to `--help` without errors or tracebacks.
- Invalid flags produce clean error messages with exit code 2 (no stack traces).
- Missing required arguments produce clean `Error: Missing argument` messages.
- `--dry-run` present consistently on all mutating commands (install, uninstall, update, compile, prune, pack, audit, unpack).
- `-y, --yes` for CI-safe confirmation skipping is available on all interactive prompts.
- `--global` / `-g` is consistently available across commands supporting user-scope operations.
- `--target` / `-t` is consistently named across install, update, compile, lock, and deps update.
- Status symbols (`[+]`, `[!]`, `[x]`, `[i]`, `[*]`, `[>]`) used consistently throughout CLI output.

issues.title: [BUG] Self-defined stdio MCP env ${VAR} placeholders written verbatim instead of resolved at install time (Codex/Claude)
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When a self-defined stdio MCP server (`registry: false`, `transport: stdio`) declares a `${VAR}` placeholder in its `env` block, targets that resolve variables at install time (Codex, Claude) write the placeholder string verbatim into the target config — even when the real value is present in `os.environ`. The MCP child process then receives an unresolved string like `MY_TOKEN=${MY_TOKEN}` and fails authentication.

On the same target, HTTP server **header** values resolve correctly. The problem is limited to the self-defined stdio **env block**.

## To Reproduce

Requirements: apm v0.23.0.

1. Create a directory with the following `apm.yml`, and create `.claude/` as the Claude target signal:

```yaml
name: repro
version: 1.0.0
dependencies:
  mcp:
    - name: env-demo
      registry: false
      transport: stdio
      command: echo
      args: ["noop"]
      env:
        MY_TOKEN: "${MY_TOKEN}"
```

2. Install with the real value in the environment:

```sh
MY_TOKEN="repro-secret-not-a-real-token" apm install --target claude
```

3. Inspect the generated `.mcp.json`:

```sh
cat .mcp.json
```

Codex behaves the same (project scope writes to `.codex/config.toml`):

```sh
MY_TOKEN="repro-secret-not-a-real-token" apm install --target codex
cat .codex/config.toml
```

## Expected behavior

`docs/.../reference/manifest-schema.md` §4.2.4 "Variable References in `headers` and `env`" normatively specifies install-time `os.environ` resolution for targets without runtime interpolation:

> **Codex, Gemini, and Cursor** have no runtime interpolation, so APM resolves `${VAR}`, `${env:VAR}`, and the legacy `<VAR>` at install time using `os.environ` (or an interactive prompt when missing).

The same table's `${VAR}` row (Codex/Gemini/Cursor column) also states "Resolved at install time from env (or interactive prompt)".

Claude is not in that table, but `src/apm_cli/adapters/client/claude.py` requires the same behaviour:

```python
# Claude Desktop / Code's mcp config does NOT support runtime env-var
# substitution -- the value in ``env`` must be a literal string. This
# adapter MUST keep the legacy install-time resolution behaviour.
_supports_runtime_env_substitution: bool = False
```

So `env: { MY_TOKEN: "${MY_TOKEN}" }` should be written resolved to the real value of `os.environ["MY_TOKEN"]`.

## Actual behavior

Claude `.mcp.json` — `MY_TOKEN` is unresolved:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "env-demo": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "echo",
      "env": { "MY_TOKEN": "${MY_TOKEN}" },
      "args": ["noop"]
    }
  }
}
```

Codex `.codex/config.toml` — identical:

```toml
[mcp_servers.env-demo.env]
MY_TOKEN = "${MY_TOKEN}"
```

For contrast, on the same Claude target, writing the value into an HTTP server header as `"Authorization": "Bearer ${MY_TOKEN}"` resolves correctly (`"Bearer repro-secret-not-a-real-token"`). This difference between the stdio env block and the header narrows down the cause.

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1
- Python Version: runs on APM's bundled Python 3.12 build (Homebrew)
- APM Version: 0.23.0 (01b337f)
- Affected targets: codex, claude

## Additional context

Likely cause: for the self-defined stdio `env` block, the same `dep.env` dict is passed into the resolution pipeline as both the values to resolve and the `env_overrides` map. The lookup `env_overrides.get(name) or os.getenv(name)` then returns the placeholder string (truthy) and never reaches `os.getenv`, so `${MY_TOKEN}` "resolves" to itself. Header values are not keys in that map, so they fall through to `os.getenv` and resolve correctly — matching the contrast above. I can add a file/line walkthrough and a note on the test gap in a comment.

### Not a duplicate

- #1222 — Claude `.mcp.json` drops env for self-defined stdio MCP servers (the env block was emitted empty; that path now carries the env).
- #1266 — Codex/Gemini passed self-defined stdio env verbatim by *not routing it through the resolver*; that was fixed by wiring the env block through `_resolve_environment_variables`. This report is the next layer: the env block now reaches the resolver, but the resolver shadows `os.environ` with the placeholder dict, so the value is still not resolved (and the #1266 fix is what now routes Codex through that shadowing path).

issues.title: [BUG] apm install skips GitHub Copilot skill deployment despite copilot target being configured
issues.body:
`apm install` does not deploy installed skills to GitHub Copilot’s repository skills target, even when `copilot` is explicitly listed in `apm.yml`.

In my repo, `apm.yml` contains:

```yaml
targets:
  - copilot
  - claude
  - opencode
````

After running `apm install`, skills are deployed to:

```text
.agents/skills/
.claude/skills/
```

But they are not recorded/deployed by APM under:

```text
.github/skills/
```

I manually copied the skills into `.github/skills/`, so the folder currently exists in my working tree. The evidence of the bug is the generated `apm.lock.yaml`: it records `.github/prompts/*` and `.github/instructions/*`, but no `.github/skills/*` entries. 

**To Reproduce**

1. Use a Windows machine with PowerShell.
2. Configure `apm.yml` with Copilot enabled:

```yaml
name: my-project
version: 0.1.0
targets:
  - copilot
  - claude
  - opencode
dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: ./packages/openspec-skills
      alias: openspec-skills
```

3. Run:

```powershell
apm install
```

4. Inspect `apm.lock.yaml`.

**Expected behavior**

APM should deploy and track skills for GitHub Copilot when `copilot` is listed as a target.

Expected deployed files should include entries like:

```text
.github/skills/openspec-apply-change
.github/skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md
.github/skills/openspec-archive-change
.github/skills/openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md
.github/skills/openspec-explore
.github/skills/openspec-explore/SKILL.md
.github/skills/openspec-propose
.github/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md
```

**Actual behavior**

`apm.lock.yaml` includes skill deployment entries for:

```text
.agents/skills/*
.claude/skills/*
```

But does not include any:

```text
.github/skills/*
```

For Copilot, APM only generated/tracked:

```text
.github/prompts/*
.github/instructions/*
.github/agents/*
```

**Environment**

```text
OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise 10.0.26200 64-bit
Python Version: Python 3.14.0
APM Version: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.21.0
VSCode Version: 1.126.0
VSCode Commit: 7e7950df89d055b5a378379db9ee14290772148a
Architecture: x64
```

**Logs**

No error is emitted. `apm install` completes successfully.

Relevant `apm.lock.yaml` evidence:

```yaml
apm_version: 0.21.0
dependencies:
- repo_url: _local/openspec-skills
  package_type: apm_package
  deployed_files:
  - .agents/skills/openspec-apply-change
  - .agents/skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md
  - .agents/skills/openspec-archive-change
  - .agents/skills/openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md
  - .agents/skills/openspec-explore
  - .agents/skills/openspec-explore/SKILL.md
  - .agents/skills/openspec-propose
  - .agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md
  - .claude/skills/openspec-apply-change
  - .claude/skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md
  - .claude/skills/openspec-archive-change
  - .claude/skills/openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md
  - .claude/skills/openspec-explore
  - .claude/skills/openspec-explore/SKILL.md
  - .claude/skills/openspec-propose
  - .claude/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md
  - .github/prompts/implement-ready-issues.prompt.md
  - .github/prompts/opsx-apply.prompt.md
  - .github/prompts/opsx-archive.prompt.md
  - .github/prompts/opsx-explore.prompt.md
  - .github/prompts/opsx-propose.prompt.md
  - .github/prompts/validate-open-prs.prompt.md
```

**Additional context**

This looks like a Copilot target deployment inconsistency.

APM already maps some artifacts to Copilot paths, such as `.github/prompts`, `.github/instructions`, and `.github/agents`. But skill artifacts are skipped for `.github/skills`.

The current `.github/skills` folder in my repository was manually copied after install, not created/tracked by APM.

## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-30
**APM Version**: 0.23.1 (d1d926d)
**Commands Inspected**: 43 (23 task-required + 20 additional)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 1     |
| Medium   | 4     |
| Low      | 1     |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm doctor` has no dedicated CLI reference page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` is a fully implemented, user-facing diagnostic command with `--verbose` support, but it has no dedicated page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. Every other top-level command has a reference page; `doctor` is the only exception. The command is referenced in guides (`operating-installed-context.md`, `security.md`, `publish-to-a-marketplace.md`) and in the `approve.md` page, meaning users following those cross-links have no reference target.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm doctor --help
  Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]

    Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace
    config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero if a critical check
    fails.

  Options:
    -v, --verbose  Show detailed output
    --help         Show this message and exit.
  ```
  `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` returns no `doctor.md`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` documenting the command, its `--verbose` flag, exit codes, and the checks it runs (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace config).

---

### Medium Severity

#### Reference index table omits many existing commands

- **Command**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`
- **Problem**: The CLI commands table in the reference index is missing the following commands that all exist in the CLI and have dedicated doc pages: `approve`/`deny`, `find`, `lifecycle`, `lock`, `plugin`, `publish`, `self-update`. A user browsing the reference index will not discover these commands.
- **Evidence**:
  The table in `reference/index.md` lists phases and commands, but these commands with their existing `.md` files are absent from every row:
  - `approve.md` (covers both `apm approve` and `apm deny`)
  - `find.md`
  - `lifecycle.md`
  - `lock.md`
  - `plugin.md`
  - `publish.md`
  - `self-update.md`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the missing commands to the index table. Suggested groupings:
  - Project setup: add `lock`
  - Inspect and audit: add `find`
  - Author and distribute: add `plugin`, `publish`
  - Governance: add `approve`/`deny`, `lifecycle`
  - Utility: add `self-update`

#### README CLI Reference link uses wrong path

- **Command**: `README.md` line 9
- **Problem**: The README links to `(microsoft.github.io/redacted) for the CLI Reference, but all actual CLI reference pages live under `/reference/cli/` (e.g., `/reference/cli/install/`). The path `cli-commands` does not appear anywhere in the docs source tree.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  **[CLI Reference]((microsoft.github.io/redacted)
  ```
  Actual pages: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md`, `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md`, etc. No `cli-commands/` directory exists.
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the README link to `(microsoft.github.io/redacted) (or the index page if one exists at `/reference/cli/`).

#### `--yes` / `-y` flag description is inconsistent across commands

- **Command**: `apm update`, `apm deps clean`, `apm init`
- **Problem**: The `-y, --yes` flag has three different descriptions across commands that all use it for the same general purpose (skipping a confirmation prompt).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm update:     -y, --yes   Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)
  apm deps clean: -y, --yes   Skip confirmation prompt
  apm init:       -y, --yes   Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults
  ```
  `apm deps clean` is missing "the" and the parenthetical. `apm init` uses completely different wording.
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to a consistent pattern. For example:
  - `apm update` / `apm deps clean`: `Skip the confirmation prompt`
  - `apm init`: `Skip interactive prompts (use auto-detected defaults)`

#### `apm config get` help does not describe its list-all behavior

- **Command**: `apm config get`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config get` with no argument prints all user-settable configuration keys and their effective values, but the help text gives no hint of this behavior. Users who want to see all config values might not discover this.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config get --help
  Usage: apm config get [OPTIONS] [KEY]

    Get a configuration value

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  The description "Get a configuration value" does not mention the no-argument behavior. Compare with the docs (`reference/cli/config.md`): "With no argument, prints all user-settable keys with their effective values (defaults included)."
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the help string to: `Get a configuration value (omit KEY to list all settable keys with effective values)`.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm unpack` deprecation notice lacks a replacement callout in top-level help

- **Command**: `apm --help`, `apm unpack --help`
- **Problem**: `apm unpack` is labeled `[Deprecated]` in the top-level command listing, which is good. However, the one-line summary in `apm --help` says only "[Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle..." without stating the replacement. Users unfamiliar with the tool may not see the replacement (`apm install <bundle-path>`) unless they read `apm unpack --help`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm --help
  ...
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
  ...

  $ apm unpack --help
  ...
    [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project. Use 'apm
    install <bundle-path>' instead -- this command will be removed in a future
    release.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Minimal: append the replacement to the top-level summary line: `[Deprecated] Use 'apm install <bundle-path>' instead.`

---

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **Top-level flags**: `--version`, `--verbose` / `-v`, `--help` all work correctly on every tested command and subcommand.
- **Error handling**: Invalid options, missing required arguments, and conflicting flags all produce clear, actionable error messages (no tracebacks observed).
- **`--dry-run` flag**: Present and consistently described on all destructive commands that support it (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `prune`, `audit`, `publish`).
- **`apm deps` group**: `list`, `tree`, `info`, `clean`, `why` all have correct help text matching the documentation.
- **`apm mcp` group**: `list`, `search`, `show`, `install` all have correct help text and default values matching the documentation (list default: 20, search default: 10).
- **`apm config`**: `get`, `set`, `unset` are accurately documented. No `list` subcommand exists or is documented.
- **`apm runtime`**: `setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove` all exist and match the documentation.
- **`apm install` / `apm update`**: Complex flag sets are accurately documented with defaults.
- **Deprecation notices**: `apm deps update`, `apm init --plugin`, `apm init --marketplace`, `apm install --runtime`, `apm install --update` all clearly state they are deprecated and provide the replacement.

issues.body: **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** When finding a specific skill you want to install on GitHub, you would need to manually break-down the URL to the file, e.g. https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/main/skills/productivity/handoff/SKILL.md, into the repo URL and skill-path as two separate inputs for `apm install`. issues.title: [BUG] Copilot hook events are never renamed to camelCase
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The docs state hook files may be authored in the Claude (`PreToolUse`,
`PostToolUse`) or Copilot (`preToolUse`, `postToolUse`) shape and that "events
are renamed per target during merge." For the **copilot** target this rename
never happens: `apm install` warns about a casing mismatch and deploys the
event unrenamed.

Root cause is in
[`hook_integrator.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py):

- `_HOOK_EVENT_MAP` has entries for `claude`, `gemini`, and `kiro`, but **no
  `copilot` entry** — while `_HOOK_EVENT_EXPECTED_CASING["copilot"] =
  "camelCase"`, so `_emit_hook_event_diagnostics` flags `PostToolUse` as an
  unmappable "casing mismatch."
- The Copilot deploy path also calls the diagnostic with a hard-coded empty map
  (`_emit_hook_event_diagnostics(..., "copilot", {})`) and writes the events
  through unchanged, so it never applies a mapping even if one existed.

A fix needs both: a `copilot` mapping (`PreToolUse`→`preToolUse`,
`PostToolUse`→`postToolUse`) and for the Copilot path to apply it during merge.

**To Reproduce**
1. Use a package with a hook authored in the Claude shape
   (`{ "hooks": { "PostToolUse": [...] } }`) and `copilot` in `targets`.
2. Run `apm install`.
3. See the casing warning; `.github/hooks/<pkg>-<file>.json` keeps `PostToolUse`.

```
Hook events for target 'copilot' may not be recognized: PostToolUse. Target
expects camelCase (e.g. preToolUse). Rename events to match the camelCase
convention, then reinstall.
WARNING apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target copilot: hook event casing mismatch (no mapping): PostToolUse
```

(In the same run the `gemini` target *is* renamed correctly to `AfterTool`,
confirming the per-target rename machinery works for targets that have a mapping.)

**Expected behavior**

The Copilot target renames `PostToolUse` → `postToolUse` automatically and emits
no warning.

**Environment**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.23.1

**Logs**

See the warning block above.

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs (`make copilot-rename`).

issues.title: [BUG] `apm audit` reports phantom drift immediately after a clean install
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Right after a successful `apm install`, `apm audit --ci` reports several hook
files as `modified` and exits non-zero. Re-running `apm install` does not clear
it.

Capturing the audit's replay scratch tree and diffing it against disk shows the
only difference on each flagged file is the `_apm_source` ownership marker:

```diff
# .claude/apm-hooks.json  (audit replay  vs  what `apm install` wrote)
-      "_apm_source": "apm-bugs"
+      "_apm_source": "_local/apm-bugs"
```

`HookIntegrator._get_hook_source_marker()` returns `"_local/<name>"` for the
project's own root-local content and the bare `<name>` otherwise, gated on:

```python
def _is_root_local_package(package_info, project_root):
    return Path(package_info.install_path).resolve() == Path(project_root).resolve()
```

- At **install** time `project_root` is the real project dir and equals the
  self-package's `install_path` → `True` → marker `"_local/apm-bugs"`.
- During the **audit replay**, writes are redirected to a scratch dir, so the
  integrator's `project_root` is the scratch tmpdir while `install_path` still
  points at the real project → `False` → bare `"apm-bugs"`.

So the replay stamps a different marker than install did, and every hook entry
carrying `_apm_source` differs byte-for-byte from disk. Normalization
(`utils/normalization.py`) does not neutralize the marker, so it surfaces as
drift. (The one hook file with no `_apm_source` marker — the Copilot file, which
never gets one — is the only file that does *not* drift.)

**To Reproduce**
1. Install a package that deploys hooks to targets which persist `_apm_source`
   (claude, codex, cursor, gemini, windsurf): `apm install`.
2. Run `apm audit --ci`.
3. See drift reported on the just-installed files; exit code 1.

```
[!] Drift detected: 5 file(s)
  modified (5):
    - .claude/apm-hooks.json
    - .codex/hooks.json
    - .cursor/hooks.json
    - .gemini/settings.json
    - .windsurf/hooks.json
```

**Expected behavior**

A file just written by `apm install` is not reported as drifted by the next
`apm audit`. The replay should compute the same root-local marker install did
(compare `install_path` against the original project root, not the scratch
redirect target), or `_apm_source` should be excluded from the drift comparison.

**Environment**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.23.1

**Logs**

See the drift block above.

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs (`make audit`).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-07-01
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-01
**APM Version**: 0.23.1 (d1d926d)
**Commands Inspected**: 30 (23 from checker spec + 7 additional subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 2 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm config list` command does not exist

- **Command**: `apm config list --help`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config list --help` returns an error. The consistency checker workflow (`cli-consistency-checker.md`) lists this as a command to verify. The command does not exist and is not documented in any reference page. This is also a discoverability problem: users familiar with `npm config list` or `git config --list` will naturally try `apm config list` and hit an error.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list --help
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  The actual subcommands available are `get`, `set`, `unset`. Bare `apm config` shows configuration, and `apm config get` with no argument lists all keys.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `apm config list` as an alias for `apm config get` (with no argument), which already prints all user-settable keys. Update `cli-consistency-checker.md` to reflect the correct command, and document the alias in `docs/reference/cli/config.md`.

---

#### `--target intellij` is rejected by CLI but documented as valid

- **Command**: `apm install --target intellij`
- **Problem**: The docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md`) explicitly list `intellij` as a valid `--target` value: `Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, intellij, vscode, agent-skills, all`. However the CLI rejects it. The `--runtime` flag (described as the "legacy alias for --target") does accept `intellij` and successfully maps it to `copilot`. This creates a confusing split: the legacy flag works but the current flag does not.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm install --target intellij
  Error: [x] Unknown target 'intellij'

  $ apm install --runtime intellij   # succeeds -- maps to copilot
  [>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
  ```
  From source (`src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py` line 452):
  ```python
  RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET: dict[str, str] = {
      "vscode": "copilot",
      "agents": "copilot",
      "intellij": "copilot",
  }
  ```
  `intellij` is in `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET` but NOT in `KNOWN_TARGETS`, which is why `--target` validation rejects it.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) add `intellij` as a recognized alias in the `--target` parser (mapping to `copilot`), consistent with how `--runtime` handles it; or (b) remove `intellij` from the `--target` values listed in `docs/reference/cli/install.md` and clearly document that `intellij` is only valid with `--runtime` (legacy). Option (a) is preferred for forward compatibility.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm config --help` does not mention bare `apm config` behavior

- **Command**: `apm config --help`
- **Problem**: The help output for `apm config` lists only `get`, `set`, `unset` subcommands with no hint that bare `apm config` (no subcommand) displays a full configuration table. The docs (`docs/reference/cli/config.md`) document this prominently in the Synopsis: `apm config  # show current configuration`. New users reading `apm config --help` have no way to discover this feature.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config --help
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...

    Configure APM CLI

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value
  ```
  (No mention of the bare invocation behavior.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note in the group-level help or an Examples block, e.g.: `Run with no subcommand to display the current project and global configuration.`

---

#### `vscode` is a valid target but missing from both `--target` and `--runtime` help text

- **Command**: `apm install --target vscode` (works), `apm install --runtime vscode` (works)
- **Problem**: `vscode` is a recognized target alias (maps to `copilot`, registered in `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET`). It works correctly at runtime with `--target vscode`. However, it appears nowhere in the `--target` or `--runtime` help text. Users trying to target VS Code Copilot explicitly cannot discover this alias from help text.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm install --target vscode
  [>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
  [i] Targets: copilot  (source: --target flag)
    [+] ./packages/apm-issue-autopilot (local)
  EXIT: 0
  ```
  From `apm install --help`:
  ```
  --target TARGET  ... Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                   gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all.
  ```
  (`vscode` is absent from this list despite working.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `vscode` to the `--target` help value list with a note that it is an alias for `copilot`. Also note it in `docs/reference/cli/install.md`.

---

#### `intellij` listed in `--runtime` help but not in `--target` help despite docs claiming it as a `--target` value

- **Command**: `apm install --runtime intellij` / `apm install --target intellij`
- **Problem**: This is the second facet of the `intellij` target inconsistency. The `--runtime` flag's help text lists `intellij` as a valid value. The docs for `--target` list `intellij` as valid. But `--target intellij` fails (High finding above). This means the `--runtime` and `--target` help texts are inconsistent with each other and both are inconsistent with actual CLI behavior. (See High finding for the full breakdown.)
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm install --help | grep -A2 "runtime"
  --runtime TEXT  Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex,
                  cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode,
                  windsurf) (legacy alias for --target, single value only; ...)
  ```
  `--runtime` lists `intellij`; `--target` does not.
- **Suggested Fix**: Align `--runtime` and `--target` so they accept the same aliases. At minimum, document in `--runtime` help that `intellij` is a `--runtime`-only alias (not valid with `--target`) until the `--target` validator is updated.

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent `--verbose` / `-v` flag descriptions across commands

- **Commands**: `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`
- **Problem**: The `-v, --verbose` flag is described differently across commands with no semantic difference:
  - `apm init`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm install`: `Show detailed installation information`
  - `apm uninstall`: `Show detailed removal information`
  - `apm update`: `Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
  - `apm compile`: `Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis`
  - `apm run`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm mcp search` / `apm mcp show`: `Show detailed output`
  The context-specific descriptions for `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile` are more informative, but `init`, `run`, `mcp *` use a generic "Show detailed output" that provides no additional guidance.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either use a consistent base phrase ("Enable verbose output") for all commands, or keep per-command context but ensure every description is specific (avoid the generic "Show detailed output" for commands where the verbose behavior is well-defined).

---

#### Inconsistent `--yes` / `-y` flag descriptions across commands

- **Commands**: `apm update`, `apm deps clean`, `apm runtime remove`
- **Problem**: The `-y, --yes` flag has three different phrasings:
  - `apm update`: `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`
  - `apm deps clean`: `Skip confirmation prompt`  (missing CI/automation note)
  - `apm runtime remove`: `Confirm the action without prompting`  (inverted framing)
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm update --help   | grep "\-y"
  -y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)

  $ apm deps clean --help | grep "\-y"
  -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt

  $ apm runtime remove --help | grep "\-y"
  -y, --yes  Confirm the action without prompting
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to `Skip the confirmation prompt` (or `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`) across all commands.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- `apm --help` -- top-level command listing and structure
- `apm init --help` -- options and description correct
- `apm install --help` -- comprehensive, detailed, accurate (besides `intellij`/`vscode` note above)
- `apm uninstall --help` -- accurate
- `apm update --help` -- accurate
- `apm compile --help` -- accurate and thorough
- `apm run --help` -- accurate
- `apm deps list --help`, `apm deps tree --help`, `apm deps info --help`, `apm deps clean --help`, `apm deps why --help` -- all accurate
- `apm deps update --help` -- deprecation warning present and correct
- `apm mcp --help`, `apm mcp search --help`, `apm mcp show --help`, `apm mcp install --help`, `apm mcp list --help` -- all accurate; list/search default limits match docs
- `apm config set --help`, `apm config get --help`, `apm config unset --help` -- accurate (note: `unset` is documented but was not in the original checker spec)
- `apm runtime --help`, `apm runtime setup --help`, `apm runtime list --help`, `apm runtime status --help`, `apm runtime remove --help` -- all accurate
- `apm lock --help`, `apm lock export --help` -- accurate, README SBOM claims verified
- Error handling -- `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), `apm config set` (missing args) all produce clean error messages with no stack traces
- Exit codes -- all tested error paths return exit code 2 cleanly

issues.title: [FEATURE] Support the .config/ directory convention (pi0/config-dir) for apm.yml, apm.lock.yaml, and apm-policy.yml
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

APM currently expects its config surface — `apm.yml`, `apm.lock.yaml`, and `apm-policy.yml` — at the repository root. On a project that already has a full root (`.editorconfig`, `.gitattributes`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, framework configs, etc.), that's three more top-level files, plus the `.apm/` working directory. This repo's own root is a good example of the clutter it creates: `apm.yml`, `apm.lock.yaml`, `.apm/`, `.agents/`, `.github/`, `.vscode/`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml` all sit side by side.

[pi0/config-dir](https://github.com/pi0/config-dir) proposes a convention several tools are converging on: put per-tool configuration under `.config/<toolname>.<ext>` (or `.config/<toolname>/` when it needs to nest) instead of a bespoke root dotfile, so a project's root stays legible and tools have one predictable place to look.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Let APM resolve its config surface from `.config/` as an alternative to the project root, following the pi0/config-dir naming rules (explicit tool name, no redundant `.config`/`.conf` suffix, extension required, lowercase). Accept any of these manifest locations, in order:

```
apm.yml                     # today's root-level manifest (unchanged, no breaking change)
.config/apm.yml              # flat form
.config/apm/config.yml       # nested form — lets .config/apm/ also hold the lockfile/policy below
```

Lockfile and policy nest alongside the manifest once it's under `.config/`:

```
.config/apm/apm.lock.yaml   # lockfile    (replaces root apm.lock.yaml)
.config/apm/policy.yml      # org policy  (replaces root apm-policy.yml)
```

Resolution order: check root first (no breaking change), then `.config/apm.yml`, then `.config/apm/config.yml` — mirroring config-dir's own "allow top-level conventions the same as before" guidance and its nesting recommendation for tools whose config grows past a single file. `apm init` could offer a `--config-dir` flag to scaffold directly into `.config/apm/` for new projects.

This is adjacent to #612 (custom config file name/path via env var or `--config` flag) but distinct: #612 solves the `apm.yml` *name* collision (APM vs. other "apm" acronyms) with an escape hatch; this issue is about adopting an established, multi-tool *directory* convention as a first-class alternative location — which also declutters the lockfile and policy file, not just the manifest. The two aren't mutually exclusive; a `.config/`-based resolver could still consult `APM_CONFIG_FILE`/`--config` for the exact filename underneath it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- #612's per-file rename escape hatch — solves the naming collision but not root clutter, and doesn't cover the lockfile or policy file.
- Leaving this to each consuming project's own conventions — doesn't help since APM itself hardcodes the root lookup.

**Additional context**

- Prior art: pi0/config-dir's [`.config` dir support tracker](https://github.com/pi0/config-dir/discussions/6) lists which tools already support this.
- Related: #612 (alternate config file name/path), #1161 (docs on `.apm/<type>/` vs root convention dirs).

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile extremely slow on large monorepos — placement optimizer scales with directory count × targets (~14 min for 6 instructions)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm compile` (even `--dry-run`) takes **~821 seconds (~13.7 min)** on a large monorepo, despite the project declaring only **6 instruction primitives** (plus 6 skill deps and 3 MCP servers).

The `--verbose` timings show the cost is almost entirely the **instruction placement optimizer** ("Three-Tier Coverage-First Strategy" / "Coverage-Constrained Optimization" / "Hierarchical Coverage Analysis"), *not* file scanning or markdown link resolution:

```
Project Analysis:        4805.0 ms      # fast
Instruction Processing: 428664.2 ms      # ~7.1 min  (pass 1: AGENTS.md / copilot)
Instruction Processing: 338774.7 ms      # ~5.6 min  (pass 2: CLAUDE.md / claude)
Generation time:        458460 ms
Perf: 3 walks, 162777 files visited, 11.715s total walk time   # fast
```

~768s of the 821s is "Instruction Processing". The repo has **53,330 files across 7,496 directories** (max depth 11). Each **universal `**` instruction** (we have 4: architecture, coding-conventions, git, overview) is classified "Distributed" and runs a **hierarchical coverage verification across all 7,496 directories**:

```
Pattern   Matching Files   Placement       Coverage Result
**        7496 dirs        ./AGENTS.md      Selective -> Coverage verified
**        7496 dirs        ./AGENTS.md      Selective -> Coverage verified
**        7496 dirs        ./AGENTS.md      Selective -> Coverage verified
**        7496 dirs        ./AGENTS.md      Selective -> Coverage verified
```

This looks like roughly **O(patterns × directories)** per-directory scoring, and it is **run once per target family** (AGENTS.md for copilot + CLAUDE.md for claude ≈ doubling the cost). A universal `**` pattern trivially places at the repo root, so the per-directory coverage scan appears to be wasted work.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. In a repo with several thousand directories (here: ~7,500 dirs / ~53,000 files), declare a few instruction primitives scoped to `**` (universal) and target multiple platforms, e.g. `targets: [claude, copilot]`.
2. Run command `apm compile --dry-run --verbose`
3. Observe the total runtime (~13.7 min here) and that the "Instruction Processing" timing dominates, with each `**` pattern reporting "7496 dirs ... Coverage verified".

**Expected behavior**

Placement optimization should scale reasonably with directory count. In particular, universal `**` patterns should short-circuit to the repo root without a per-directory hierarchical coverage scan, and the directory analysis should be shared across target passes rather than recomputed per target. Compiling 6 trivial instruction files should take seconds, not ~14 minutes.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.23.1
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a

**Logs**

`apm compile --dry-run --verbose` (excerpts above). Key timings:
- `Instruction Processing: 428664.2ms` (pass 1) + `338774.7ms` (pass 2)
- `Perf: 3 walks, 162777 files visited, 11.715s total walk time`
- Total wall clock: ~821s.

**Additional context**

Suggested directions:
1. Short-circuit `**` (universal) patterns: they always place at root; skip the per-directory hierarchical coverage scan entirely.
2. Cache / share the directory analysis between the two target passes instead of recomputing it per target.
3. Expose a flag to skip the optimizer (single-root placement) on large repos, or make the coverage-scan complexity independent of total directory count.
