issues.title: [BUG] Anonymous HTTPS clone URLs drop the .git suffix, breaking hosts that require it (e.g. GitBucket)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install` fails for every dependency hosted on a git server whose
smart-HTTP endpoint is only served at the `.git` path and does not redirect
the bare path — GitBucket is the concrete case. The failure is independent of
ref type (tag / branch / none) and of full vs. shallow clone.

The root cause is an asymmetry in URL construction. APM strips the `.git`
suffix when parsing the dependency URL (`models/dependency/reference.py`),
which is fine as an internal canonical form — but when the clone URL is
rebuilt, only the **anonymous HTTPS** branch fails to re-append it
(`src/apm_cli/utils/github_host.py`, `build_https_clone_url`):

| Builder | Emits `.git`? |
|---|---|
| HTTPS with token (`build_https_clone_url`, token branch) | yes |
| **HTTPS anonymous (`build_https_clone_url`, no-token branch)** | **no** |
| Plain HTTP (`build_clone_http_url`) | yes |
| SSH (`build_ssh_url`, both SCP and `ssh://` forms) | yes |
| GitLab token form (`build_gitlab_https_clone_url`) | yes |

Because `GenericGitBackend` never embeds tokens in URLs (auth is delegated to
git credential helpers, `deps/host_backends.py`), a generic-host dependency
**always** takes the anonymous branch — so for hosts like GitBucket there is
no working HTTPS configuration at all. Writing the `.git` suffix explicitly
in `apm.yml` does not help, because the parser strips it before the builder
runs.

GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket / Gitea all accept the suffix-less form (redirect
or dual-serve), which is presumably why this has gone unnoticed.

**To Reproduce**

With any GitBucket instance (auth via git credential helper):

1. Declare a GitBucket dependency:

   ```yaml
   # apm.yml
   name: gitbucket-repro
   version: 0.0.1
   targets:
     - claude
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package.git
         ref: v0.1.0
     mcp: []
   ```

2. Run `apm install`.
3. See error (exit code 128 from git; note the missing `.git` in the cmdline).

Sanity check outside APM (same machine, same credentials):

```
$ git ls-remote https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package.git   # works
$ git ls-remote https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package       # fails
```

**Expected behavior**

The clone URL preserves (or re-appends) the `.git` suffix, matching what the
token, SSH, and plain-HTTP builders already do. The dependency installs over
plain HTTPS with credential-helper auth.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows 11
- Python Version: 3.13
- APM Version: 0.23.1 (also reproduced reading `main`)
- Host: GitBucket 4.x behind HTTPS, auth via Git Credential Manager

**Logs**

```
[>] Resolving git/owner/some-package...
[DEBUG] _clone_with_fallback: repo=git/owner/some-package, is_ado=False, is_generic=True, has_token=False, auth_scheme=basic, protocol_pref=none, allow_fallback=False
[DEBUG] transport plan: strict=True, attempts=[('https', False, 'plain HTTPS')]
[DEBUG] Attempting clone with plain HTTPS (URL sanitized)
[x] 1 package failed:
  +- git/owner/some-package -- Failed to download dependency: Failed to clone repository
     ... Last error: Cmd('git') failed due to: exit code(128)
     cmdline: git clone -v --depth=1 --branch=v0.1.0 -- https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package
```

**Additional context**

Two aggravating factors make this hard to diagnose in the field:

- GitBucket answers **401 before 404** on the suffix-less path, so git treats
  the repo as private and invokes the credential helper — users get an auth
  dialog (Git Credential Manager) for a URL that can never work, and APM's
  error text ("configure SSH keys or a git credential helper") points at
  authentication rather than the URL.
- The `insteadOf` workaround needs one entry per package repository on every
  developer machine, because a prefix rewrite is the only way to re-append a
  suffix.

Proposed fix — one line in `build_https_clone_url` (plus four test
expectations: three in `tests/unit/test_generic_git_urls.py`, one in
`tests/test_github_downloader_token_precedence.py`):

```diff
     if token:
         # Use x-access-token format which is compatible with GitHub Enterprise and GH Actions
         return f"https://x-access-token:{token}@{netloc}/{repo_ref}.git"
-    return f"https://{netloc}/{repo_ref}"
+    return f"https://{netloc}/{repo_ref}.git"
```

All supported hosts accept the `.git`-suffixed form, so this is
backward-compatible. Verified against a real GitBucket instance: stock 0.23.1
fails as above, and with this patch the same manifest installs successfully
(plain HTTPS, credential-helper auth, no `insteadOf` rewrites). Happy to open
a PR.

issues.title: [BUG] apm install --frozen reports locked private Git dependency as missing
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install --frozen` reports a private Git dependency as missing from `apm.lock.yaml`, even though the dependency is present in the lockfile and regular `apm install` resolves it successfully.

**To Reproduce**

Manifest:
```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: git@git.example.com:org/private-skills.git
      ref: 2026.06.10
```

Generated lockfile:
```
dependencies:
- repo_url: org/private-skills
  name: private-skills
  host: git.example.com
  resolved_commit: abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12
  resolved_ref: 2026.06.10
  version: 2026.6.10
  package_type: marketplace_plugin
```

```shell
$ apm install --frozen --no-policy

[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml…
- frozen: apm.lock.yaml is out of sync with apm.yml.
- org/private-skills is declared in apm.yml but missing from apm.lock.yaml
[i] Tip: run ‘apm outdated’ to see what changed, then ‘apm update’.
[!] Install interrupted after 0.0s.
```

**Expected behavior**

`apm install --frozen` should accept the lockfile because the private Git dependency is present and resolved in `apm.lock.yaml`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- APM version: `0.23.1`
- Platform: macOS arm64
- Install source: Homebrew
- Command: `apm install --frozen --no-policy`

**Additional context**

- `apm install --no-policy` succeeds and installs this dependency from cache.
- `apm outdated` also sees the dependency.
- Rewriting the manifest dependency from SSH to HTTPS did not fix the frozen validation failure.
- Regenerating `apm.lock.yaml` with APM `0.23.1` did not fix the frozen validation failure.
- `apm install --frozen --dry-run` appears to pass, but the real frozen install fails.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-07-02
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-02
**APM Version**: `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.23.1 (bf4a2b8)`
**Commands Inspected**: 51 (top-level, all subgroups: deps, mcp, config, runtime, and all standalone commands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm doctor` has no dedicated CLI reference page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: `apm doctor` is a full command visible in `apm --help` output and referenced in 9+ documentation pages (guides, enterprise docs, reference pages for other commands), but has **no dedicated reference page** in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. Every other non-deprecated command in `apm --help` has a corresponding `.md` file in that directory. `apm doctor` is absent.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm --help` output lists: `doctor  Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI,...`
  - `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` — no `doctor.md` file
  - Referenced in: `docs/guides/operating-installed-context.md` (x5 occurrences), `docs/enterprise/security.md`, `docs/producer/publish-to-a-marketplace.md`, `docs/reference/cli/policy.md`, `docs/reference/cli/approve.md`
  - `apm doctor --help` output: `Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]` with `-v, --verbose` flag
- **Suggested Fix**: Create `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` documenting the command, its `-v/--verbose` flag, exit codes (0 = all checks pass, non-zero = critical check fails), and the list of checks it runs (git, network, auth, gh CLI, marketplace config).

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm config set/get <invalid_key>` emits a misleading "report this bug" message

- **Command**: `apm config set <invalid_key>` and `apm config get <invalid_key>`
- **Problem**: When a user provides an unknown configuration key, the CLI emits `[i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.` — a message that implies a software defect. This is a normal user-input validation path, not a bug, and will generate unnecessary bug reports.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config get invalid_key
  [x] Unknown configuration key: 'invalid_key'
  [i] Valid keys: auto-integrate, target, self-update.channel,
  self-update.install-dir, mcp-registry-url, temp-dir, allow-protocol-fallback,
  prefer-ssh
  [i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.
  ```
  Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/config.py:456-458` (config set path) and `:607-609` (config get path).
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the third `[i]` line entirely. The `[x] Unknown configuration key` and `[i] Valid keys` lines are sufficient and correct. Users should not be told to report a bug when they type an unknown key.

---

#### Reference index CLI commands table omits several documented commands

- **Command**: `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`
- **Problem**: The reference index page lists CLI commands in a phase-grouped table, but the following commands have dedicated `reference/cli/*.md` pages that are not linked from the index table:
  - `approve` (and `deny`) — has `approve.md`
  - `find` — has `find.md`
  - `lock` — has `lock.md`
  - `lifecycle` — has `lifecycle.md`
  - `plugin` — has `plugin.md`
  - `publish` — has `publish.md`
  - `self-update` — has `self-update.md`
  - `doctor` — has no page (see High severity finding above)
- **Evidence**: Running `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` shows 31 files. Cross-referencing with the index table at `docs/reference/index.md` under "CLI commands" — the above commands are absent from all phase rows.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the missing commands to appropriate phase rows in the index table, for example:
  - Project setup: add `self-update`
  - Inspect and audit: add `find`, `lock`, `doctor`
  - Author and distribute: add `publish`, `plugin`
  - Governance: add `approve`/`deny`, `lifecycle`

---

#### `apm audit --dry-run` semantics conflict with `--dry-run` in every other command

- **Command**: `apm audit --dry-run`
- **Problem**: In every other APM command that supports `--dry-run` (`install`, `compile`, `pack`, `uninstall`, `prune`, `deps clean`, `unpack`), the flag means "preview what the whole command would do without making changes." In `apm audit`, `--dry-run` is a modifier of `--strip` only — it has no effect and emits a warning when used without `--strip`. The help text is technically accurate but the inconsistency creates a poor experience.
- **Evidence**:
  - Help text: `--dry-run   Preview what --strip would remove without modifying files`
  - Running `apm audit --dry-run` (without `--strip`) outputs: `[i] --dry-run only works with --strip (e.g. apm audit --strip --dry-run)`
  - Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py:887-889`: `if dry_run and not strip: logger.progress("--dry-run only works with --strip ...")`
  - Compare: `apm install --dry-run` help: `Show what would be installed without installing`
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) rename the flag to `--dry-strip` or `--preview-strip` so it does not conflict with the `--dry-run` convention used everywhere else, or (b) extend `--dry-run` to also preview the scan findings without writing anything (making it a true dry-run of the audit). If (a), update `audit.md` accordingly.

---

#### `apm targets --help` implies subcommands exist but none are listed

- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...` (Click command-group syntax), which tells users there are subcommands. However, no commands are listed in the help output. `targets.md` explains this is intentional ("no subcommands ship today"), but the help text itself gives no indication — users will look for a subcommand list that simply does not appear.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm targets --help
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

    Show resolved targets for the current project. If APM detects a target you
    don't intend (e.g. CLAUDE.md is documentation, not a Claude Code config),
    pin your targets explicitly in apm.yml.

  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output (excluded by
            default).
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  No "Commands:" section appears.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a note to the command description or options group, such as: `Note: no subcommands are available yet; invoking 'apm targets' without arguments prints the resolved-target table.`

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm mcp list` and `apm mcp search` have inconsistent default limits

- **Commands**: `apm mcp list`, `apm mcp search`
- **Problem**: Within the same `apm mcp` command group, `list` defaults to `--limit 20` and `search` defaults to `--limit 10`. There is no documented rationale for the difference.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm mcp list --help`: `--limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 20]`
  - `apm mcp search --help`: `--limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]`
- **Suggested Fix**: Align both to the same default (either 10 or 20), or document why different defaults are appropriate in the help text.

---

#### `--verbose` flag descriptions are inconsistent in detail level

- **Commands**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` / `-v` flag description varies from highly specific to completely generic across commands, with no consistency pattern.
- **Evidence**:
  - Generic "Show detailed output": `apm init`, `apm run`, `apm preview`, `apm doctor`
  - Contextual descriptions:
    - `apm install`: `Show detailed installation information`

issues.title: [BUG] `apm pack` ignores the declared `skills:` subset filter on git dependencies — bundles the entire upstream repo, or silently bundles nothing
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When an `apm.yml` dependency declares a `skills:` subset filter on a git dependency, `apm install` correctly deploys
only the named skills to harness directories (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, etc.). `apm pack` (default
`--format plugin`) does not respect the same filter: depending on local cache state, it either bundles the entire
upstream repository for that dependency, or silently omits the dependency's skills entirely.


**To Reproduce**

Manifest (`apm.yml`):

```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: mattpocock/skills
      ref: bc4cf90
      skills:
        - productivity/grill-me
        - productivity/grilling
```

Steps and results, all run against the same manifest:

1. `apm install` — correct. Only `.agents/skills/grill-me` and `.agents/skills/grilling` deployed (verified by listing
   `.agents/skills/` directly; also matches `apm.lock.yaml`'s `skill_subset` field).
2. `apm pack` (no other commands in between) — bundles the entire `mattpocock/skills` repository under
   `build/<pkg>/skills/`: every top-level category in the upstream repo (`tdd`, `teach`, `deprecated`, `zoom-out`,
   `writing-great-skills`, `handoff`, `triage`, and roughly 20 others), not just the 2 declared skills.
3. `apm install` → manually `rm -rf apm_modules` → `apm pack` — bundles **zero** skills from `mattpocock/skills`. No
   warning or error is emitted; the bundle is simply missing that dependency's content.
4. `apm install` → `apm prune` → `apm pack` — same result as step 2. `apm prune` does not remove or touch the cache for
   this dependency, since it's still referenced in `apm.yml` (just with a narrower `skills:` list).

**Expected behavior**

`apm pack` should bundle exactly the skills recorded as deployed for the active target (matching what `apm install`
already deploys and what `apm.lock.yaml`'s `skill_subset` / `deployed_files` record), regardless of whether the raw
`apm_modules/<owner>/<repo>/` cache happens to be present.

### Actual behavior

`apm pack` reads directly from the raw, unfiltered `apm_modules/<owner>/<repo>/skills/` cache directory rather than from
the filtered, already-deployed output. When that cache is missing, there is no fallback, and the bundle silently omits
the dependency instead of erroring or re-resolving it.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- `apm --version` reported `0.23.1`
- `pyhton --version` reported `3.14.6`
- macOS, zsh.

### Impact

Any package that declares a filtered `skills:` subset on a git dependency cannot produce a correct plugin bundle via
`apm pack` today. This blocks using `apm pack` as a distribution path for packages with OSS skill dependencies scoped to
a subset of a larger upstream repo.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install` removes all comments from `apm.yml`
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
We have comments in our `apm.yml` file to indicate purpose. Running `apm install <new-skill>`, `apm uninstall` or any other file that updates the skill will remove any comments from the file, regardless of placement.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install a skill with `apm install`
2. Add a `# comment` anywhere in `apm.yml`
3. Install a second skill with `apm install`
4. See comment removed

**Expected behavior**
Since comments are a native part of the yaml language, I'd expect that these comments would be left alone. It's less expected in a lock-file, but leaving comments alone (preferrably whitespace too) inside of the `apm.yml` file would be beneficial.

issues.title: Verify TLS using the system trust store by default (breaks in enterprise/proxy environments)
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm` fails TLS verification against internal Git hosts that use a corporate CA or a TLS-inspecting proxy, even when `git` and `curl` to the **same host** succeed. Defaulting to the OS trust store (or honouring the standard CA env vars) would make APM work out-of-the-box in enterprise environments.

Related to #428, but distinct: #428 was about APM's bundled OpenSSL pointing at a non-existent python.org cert path. This issue is about internal/corporate root CAs not being present in the bundled `certifi` set **at all**, which is the common enterprise failure mode.

## What happens

```
apm marketplace add https://<internal-ghe-host>/Org/repo.git --name foo

[x] Failed to register marketplace: Failed to fetch marketplace 'foo':
HTTPSConnectionPool(host='<internal-ghe-host>', port=443): Max retries exceeded with
url: /api/v3/repos/Org/repo/contents/marketplace.json?ref=main
(Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1,
'[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1010)')))
```

`git clone` of the exact same URL succeeds, which makes the failure confusing for users.

## Root cause

APM (Python + `requests`/`urllib3`) verifies against the bundled **`certifi`** CA set, which does not include internal/corporate root CAs or the certs injected by a TLS-inspecting proxy. System tools (`git`, `curl`) read the OS trust store (e.g. `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`), so they succeed against the same host — hence the inconsistent behaviour.

## Current workaround

Users must manually point Python at the system bundle in every environment:

```bash
export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
```

This is easy to miss and has to be repeated per shell/container, which is a poor first-run experience in enterprise setups.

## Requested behaviour (any of these)

1. **Preferred:** Use the OS trust store by default via the [`truststore`](https://pypi.org/project/truststore/) package (Python 3.10+), e.g. `truststore.inject_into_ssl()` at startup. This automatically picks up corporate CAs on Linux/macOS/Windows with no user configuration and is the modern recommended approach for exactly this problem.
2. Explicitly honour `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` (and document them) so the standard env vars "just work".
3. Add a config/flag such as `apm config set ca-bundle <path>` (or `--ca-bundle`) to pin a custom CA file.

Please **do not** offer a "disable verification" flag as the primary remedy — trusting the OS store is the secure fix.

## Environment

- APM CLI `0.23.1`
- Bundled Python (PyInstaller)
- Linux (dev container, Ubuntu 24.04), behind a corporate CA / TLS-inspecting proxy
- `git clone` of the same URL succeeds; `apm marketplace add` / `apm install` fail

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Fresh install of APM in an environment where only the **OS** trust store contains the corporate CA can `apm marketplace add` / `apm install` from an internal HTTPS Git host without setting any env vars.
- Behaviour documented for air-gapped / custom-CA setups.

issues.title: Producing Claude Desktop–consumable plugin artifacts (skills/agents/...)
issues.body: ### Summary We're starting to use APM to distribute an internal plugin (`jahia/cortex`) and I'd like less-technical teammates to consume some of it directly in **Claude Desktop** (the app UI), not just via the CLI. Installing globally works perfectly: ```bash apm install -g jahia/cortex ``` The skills/agents are correctly available in the CLI and in Claude Desktop's `Code` tab (I can invoke them). But in the desktop app's **Settings → Plugins **, the plugin appears with 0 skills or agents: My understanding is that `apm install` / `apm compile` *projects* primitives into the target harness directories at install time (e.g. `~/.claude/...`), which is why they resolve fine in the CLI and `Code` tab. The desktop app's plugin manager, however, seems to expect a repo that already contains the standard Claude plugin package layout discoverable at the repo/marketplace level, artifacts that the source repo doesn't commit, since APM generates them on the consumer's machine rather than shipping them pre-built. ### Question Is there a supported way — or plans — for APM to emit the standard Claude plugin artifacts at **release/repo level**, so a repo can be added directly as a plugin/marketplace in Claude Desktop without the end user running the `apm` CLI? Ultimately, I'd like non technical users to be able to integrate the plugin in Chat, Cowork and `Code` from Claude Desktop, while developers working in a repo would use APM and apm.yml to manage the plugin/repo lifecycle. ### Environment - APM: `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.23.1 (d1d926d)` - Package: `jahia/cortex` - Client: Claude Desktop

issues.title: [FEATURE] Verify TLS using the system trust store by default (breaks in enterprise/proxy environments)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`apm` fails TLS verification against internal Git hosts that use a corporate CA or a TLS-inspecting proxy, even when `git` and `curl` to the **same host** succeed. This makes the first-run experience in enterprise environments confusing and requires per-shell env-var setup.

What the user sees:

```
apm marketplace add https://<internal-ghe-host>/Org/repo.git --name foo

[x] Failed to register marketplace: Failed to fetch marketplace 'foo':
HTTPSConnectionPool(host='<internal-ghe-host>', port=443): Max retries exceeded with
url: /api/v3/repos/Org/repo/contents/marketplace.json?ref=main
(Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1,
'[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed:
unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1010)')))
```

`git clone` of the exact same URL succeeds, which is what makes this so confusing.

**Why it happens:** APM classifies GitHub/GHES/GitLab hosts and fetches `marketplace.json` (and package metadata) through the REST Contents API using **`requests`**, via a plain module-level session:

```python
# src/apm_cli/marketplace/client.py
_HTTP_SESSION = requests.Session()
```

A default `requests.Session()` verifies against the bundled **`certifi`** CA set (`certifi.where()`), which does not include internal/corporate root CAs or the certs injected by a TLS-inspecting proxy. The PyInstaller build bundles this set explicitly (`build/apm.spec`: `'certifi'  # CA certificate bundle for SSL verification in frozen binary`). Repository operations, by contrast, shell out to `git`, which reads the OS trust store (e.g. `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`) -- so `git clone` succeeds while the `requests`-based Contents API call fails against the exact same certificate chain.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Use the OS trust store by default via [`truststore`](https://pypi.org/project/truststore/) (Python 3.10+; APM already requires `>=3.10`), e.g. call `truststore.inject_into_ssl()` once at CLI startup. This automatically picks up corporate CAs on Linux/macOS/Windows with **no user configuration**, is the modern recommended approach for exactly this problem, and makes `git` and `apm` behave consistently against the same host.

Acceptance criteria:

- A fresh install of APM, in an environment where only the **OS** trust store contains the corporate CA, can `apm marketplace add` / `apm install` from an internal HTTPS Git host **without setting any env vars**.
- `git`-based and `requests`-based operations use a consistent trust source.
- Behaviour documented for air-gapped / custom-CA setups (extend the existing [`troubleshooting/ssl-issues`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/troubleshooting/ssl-issues/) page).

Please **do not** offer a "disable verification" flag as the primary remedy -- trusting the OS store is the secure fix.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var (current workaround).** This already works and is documented, and APM already prints a hint pointing at it on TLS failure. But it must be re-set per shell / per container and is easy to miss:
  ```bash
  export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
  ```
  Note a sharp edge worth fixing regardless: **`SSL_CERT_FILE` alone does not repair the APM `requests` path.** `requests` pins `certifi.where()` and only consults `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` -- it ignores `SSL_CERT_FILE`. So the fix documented for the older #428 (setting only `SSL_CERT_FILE`) does **not** help the marketplace / install code path; users additionally need `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. This split between "what the OS trusts", "what `git` uses", and "what `requests` uses" is exactly the confusion `truststore` removes.

- **A `--ca-bundle` flag / `apm config set ca-bundle <path>`.** Lets users pin a custom CA file without relying on env vars. Useful as a secondary option, but still not zero-config.

- **Disabling verification.** Rejected -- insecure, and not an acceptable default or primary remedy.

**Additional context**

Related to #428, but distinct: #428 was about APM's bundled OpenSSL pointing at a non-existent python.org cert path. This issue is about internal/corporate root CAs not being present in the bundled `certifi` set **at all**, which is the common enterprise failure mode.

Environment where this was observed:

- APM CLI `0.23.1`
- Bundled Python (PyInstaller, `--onedir`)
- Linux (dev container, Ubuntu 24.04), behind a corporate CA / TLS-inspecting proxy
- `git clone` of the same URL succeeds; `apm marketplace add` / `apm install` fail

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-07-03
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-03
**APM Version**: 0.23.1 (bf4a2b8)
**Commands Inspected**: 30 (`apm` top-level + `init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps` group x7, `mcp` group x5, `config` group x3, `runtime` group x5, plus `lock`, `lock export`, `audit`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm audit` help description is incomplete and uses incorrect terminology

- **Command**: `apm audit`
- **Problem**: The `--help` description ("Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters") is misleading on two counts: (1) it says "packages" but APM's own terminology is "primitives"; (2) it omits the two other major modes the command provides — drift detection and CI gate lockfile/policy checks. A user reading only `apm audit --help` would have no idea the command can run a CI gate (`--ci`), detect drift, or enforce policy.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI `apm audit --help` first line: `Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters`
  - Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py:1039` — `@click.command(help="Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters")`
  - Docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/audit.md`) description: `Scan installed primitives for hidden Unicode, drift, and lockfile/policy violations.`
  - Docs description of modes: "`apm audit` is the explicit security and integrity tool. It runs in two modes: **Content scan mode** (default) ... **CI gate mode** (`--ci`). Runs lockfile consistency checks plus drift ..."
  - README: `` `apm audit` rebuilds your agent context in scratch and diffs it against your working tree to catch hand-edits before they ship ``
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `help=` string in `src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py` line 1039 to match the docs: `"Scan installed primitives for hidden Unicode, drift, and policy violations"` (or a similarly complete description).

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` uses a non-standard help format

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The help output for `apm mcp install` shows "Common options" as raw plain text embedded inside the Options section, rather than as properly registered Click options. This is unlike every other command in the CLI, making it harder for users to understand which flags are actually accepted vs. just referenced.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see 'apm install --help' for full list):
      --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
      --url URL           Server URL for remote transports
      --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable)
      --header KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable)
      --registry URL      Custom registry URL
      --mcp-version VER   Pin registry entry to a specific version
      --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Compare with `apm mcp search --help` or any other subcommand, where all options are uniformly formatted as Click options.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) register the forwarded flags as proper Click options in `apm mcp install` so they appear as standard help entries, or (b) move the "Common options" note to the command description/epilog section so it doesn't appear as a broken options sub-list.

#### `apm config` breaks the command-group "list" pattern

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Every other multi-subcommand group in the CLI provides an explicit `list` subcommand (`apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm runtime list`). `apm config` instead uses the bare `apm config` (no subcommand) to display all configuration. This inconsistency breaks the predictable pattern users learn from peer commands, and running `apm config list` returns an error (`No such command 'list'`).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  ```
  $ apm deps --help | grep Commands -A5
  Commands:
    clean   ...
    info    ...
    list    List installed APM dependencies
    tree    ...
  $ apm mcp --help | grep Commands -A5
  Commands:
    install  ...
    list     List all available MCP servers
    ...
  $ apm runtime --help | grep Commands -A5
  Commands:
    list    List available and installed runtimes
    ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add an `apm config list` alias that calls the same display logic as `apm config` (no subcommand), making the pattern consistent with `apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, and `apm runtime list`.

#### `--dry-run` flag description is inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm prune`, `apm publish`, `apm audit`
- **Problem**: The `--dry-run` flag uses two different description styles: "Show what would be X without Y" (majority pattern) vs. "Preview without Z." (with trailing period, used only by `apm publish`). `apm update` and `apm compile` also deviate with "Render the update plan and exit without changing anything" and "Preview compilation without writing files" respectively — mixing description styles and capitalization conventions.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm install  --dry-run`: `Show what would be installed without installing`
  - `apm prune    --dry-run`: `Show what would be removed without removing`
  - `apm publish  --dry-run`: `Preview without uploading.`  (period; different verb)
  - `apm update   --dry-run`: `Render the update plan and exit without changing anything`
  - `apm compile  --dry-run`: `Preview compilation without writing files`
  - `apm audit    --dry-run`: `Preview what --strip would remove without modifying files`
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all `--dry-run` descriptions to the pattern `"Show what would be <verb> without <doing it>"`, e.g.: `"Preview without uploading"` → `"Show what would be published without uploading"`.

---

### Low Severity

#### Trailing period inconsistency in top-level command descriptions

- **Command**: `apm --help` Commands section
- **Problem**: 6 out of 33 top-level commands end their one-line description with a period while the remaining 27 do not. This is inconsistent punctuation within the same help page.
- **Evidence** (commands WITH trailing period):
  - `lifecycle   Inspect, test, and scaffold lifecycle scripts.`
  - `pack        Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.`
  - `publish     Publish a package to a registry.`
  - `self-update Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.`
  - `targets     Show resolved targets for the current project.`
  - `unpack      [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.`
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing periods from the 6 affected command `help=` strings to match the no-period convention used by the majority.

#### `--verbose` flag descriptions are inconsistently worded across commands

- **Commands**: All commands with `--verbose`
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag carries slightly different descriptions across commands, ranging from the generic "Show detailed output" to highly specific "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics". While some variance is acceptable (verbose mode differs per command), the inconsistency between `apm run --verbose` ("Show detailed output") and `apm update --verbose` ("Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics") makes it hard to predict what verbose mode adds.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm init     --verbose`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm install  --verbose`: `Show detailed installation information`
  - `apm uninstall--verbose`: `Show detailed removal information`
  - `apm update   --verbose`: `Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
  - `apm compile  --verbose`: `Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis`
  - `apm run      --verbose`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm mcp *    --verbose`: `Show detailed output`
- **Suggested Fix**: Use command-specific descriptions (not generic "Show detailed output") consistently, so users know what extra information each verbose mode provides. For commands where verbose adds no unique detail, "Show detailed output" is acceptable but should be verified.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Error handling**: All tested invalid inputs (`--nonexistent-flag`, missing required args) produce clean usage errors — no stack traces.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every inspected command and subcommand.
- **`apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`**: Core command help text is comprehensive and accurate.
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/clean/why`**: Consistent with documentation and expected behavior.
- **`apm mcp list/search/show`**: Descriptions and defaults match documentation (list default: 20, search default: 10).
- **`apm config get/set/unset`**: Documented and consistent.
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`**: All subcommands match documentation including `-y/--yes` on `remove`.
- **README command references**: All commands mentioned in README (`apm install`, `apm compile -t`, `apm install --skill`, `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx`, `apm audit --ci`) exist in the CLI and accept the documented flags.
- **Deprecation markers**: `apm deps update` and `apm unpack` are clearly marked as deprecated in both help text and documentation.
- **Exit codes**: Invalid flag = exit 2, missing required arg = exit 2. Consistent with Click conventions.

issues.title: [BUG] apm install replays stale locked commits and produces a different dependency graph than a fresh install
issues.body:
_It took me a while to chase this one down. It wasn't super clear from the documentation whether the original behavior (transitive devDependencies being installed) was intended behavior. If that's indeed not intended, then maybe the docs can also be improved to make it more explicit 😄 ._

_It's been a bit tricky to get a reproducible sample, as it depends on state of some internal repos. I hope it's sufficient to look into what's happening based on this report, else I can see if I can put some public repos in the right state to reproduce the issue._

---

**Describe the bug**  
`apm install` can resolve a different dependency graph depending on whether `apm.lock.yaml` already exists.

When a lockfile is present, APM replays the exact commit recorded in the lockfile for an unpinned dependency. When the lockfile is removed, APM resolves that same dependency from the current upstream default branch.

If the upstream package changed its dependency manifest between those two commits, the resulting dependency graph can differ significantly even though the consumer's `apm.yml` did not change.

In practice, this means:

- `apm install` with an existing lockfile can install extra transitive packages from an older locked commit
- `rm apm.lock.yaml && apm install` can resolve a newer upstream commit and install fewer packages

This makes the two flows observably different in ways that are surprising when the direct dependency in `apm.yml` is unpinned.

**To Reproduce**  
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an APM project with an unpinned direct dependency:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - owner/repo
   ```
2. Ensure `owner/repo` is a public package whose `apm.yml` changed between two commits such that:
   - an older commit has a transitive package under `dependencies.apm`
   - a newer commit moved that same package to `devDependencies.apm`
3. Generate and commit `apm.lock.yaml` while it still points at the older commit.
4. Run:
   ```bash
   git reset --hard
   git clean --force -dfx
   apm install -v
   git status --short
   ```
5. Observe that APM replays the locked commit and installs the transitive package from the older dependency graph.
6. Reset again and run:
   ```bash
   git reset --hard
   git clean --force -dfx
   rm apm.lock.yaml
   apm install -v
   git status --short
   ```
7. Observe that APM resolves the current upstream commit instead, and the transitive package is no longer installed because it now lives under `devDependencies`.

Representative logs from the locked run:
```text
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Using apm.lock.yaml (N locked dependencies)
    owner/repo: locked at <old-sha>
Resolved dependency tree: X direct + Y transitive deps
```

Representative logs from the fresh run:
```text
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Resolved X direct dependencies (no transitive)
Generated apm.lock.yaml with X dependencies
```

**Expected behavior**  
I expect this behavior to be made explicit and easier to reason about for unpinned dependencies.

At minimum, `apm install` should make it very clear that:

- with a lockfile, it is replaying the exact old commit from `apm.lock.yaml`
- without a lockfile, it is resolving the current upstream state

Right now, this can look like a dependency-resolution bug when in reality the dependency graph changed because the locked upstream commit and the newly resolved upstream commit differ.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.14.6
- APM Version: 0.23.1
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**  
APM source inspection shows the relevant behavior:

- lockfile replay path uses the locked commit SHA when no ref drift is detected
- transitive resolution only walks `get_apm_dependencies()` and does not walk transitive `get_dev_apm_dependencies()`

Representative user-visible logs:
```text
Using apm.lock.yaml (N locked dependencies)
    owner/repo: locked at <old-sha>
```

and:
```text
Resolved X direct dependencies (no transitive)
```

**Additional context**  
The important detail is that this is easiest to trigger when the direct dependency is **unpinned** in `apm.yml`.

With a committed lockfile:

- APM replays the older locked commit
- the older dependency manifest may still expose transitive packages under `dependencies`

Without the lockfile:

- APM resolves a newer upstream commit
- the newer dependency manifest may have moved those same packages to `devDependencies`

Since APM does not traverse transitive dev dependencies, the two installs produce different results.

This behavior appears to come from the interaction of:

1. lockfile replay of exact commits for reproducibility
2. unpinned direct dependencies
3. upstream manifest changes between commits
4. transitive traversal including only production dependencies

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile emits duplicate H1 in CLAUDE.md (extra '# Project Standards' after '# CLAUDE.md' banner); AGENTS.md has single H1
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm compile` emits **two level-1 (`#`) headings** at the top of the generated `CLAUDE.md`: the `# CLAUDE.md` banner **plus** an extra `# Project Standards` title. The Codex `AGENTS.md` produced in the same run has only a single `#` heading. This trips markdown linters (e.g. markdownlint `MD025 / single-title/single-h1`) and is inconsistent between the two output paths.

## Environment

- APM CLI: **0.23.1 (d1d926d)** (also present in 0.23.0)
- Targets: `claude`, `codex`
- OS: macOS (darwin)

## Repro

`.apm/instructions/*.instructions.md` sources contain **no** `#` (H1) headings — the highest level used is `##`:

```
$ grep -rc "^# " .apm/instructions/ | grep -v ':0'
no H1 in any source instruction
```

Run `apm compile`.

## Actual

Generated `CLAUDE.md` (two H1s):

```markdown
# CLAUDE.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI -->
<!-- Build ID: dc755bbc9a3d -->

# Project Standards        ← extra second H1, not present in any source

## Files matching `**`
## ...
```

Generated `AGENTS.md` from the **same** compile run (single H1):

```markdown
# AGENTS.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI from distributed .apm/ primitives -->
<!-- Build ID: 05510661a194 -->
<!-- APM Version: 0.23.0 -->

## Files matching `**`
## ...
```

So `# Project Standards` is injected **only** into the Claude output path. It is not derived from any source instruction, nor from `apm.yml` (whose `name:` is unrelated to the string "Project Standards") — it appears to be a hardcoded section title in the Claude compiler.

## Expected

The Claude output should have a single top-level `#` heading, consistent with the `AGENTS.md` output. Either:

1. Drop the extra `# Project Standards` title so `CLAUDE.md` starts with just the `# CLAUDE.md` banner followed by `##` sections (matches `AGENTS.md`), **or**
2. Demote `Project Standards` to `##` if a section title is intended.

Right now there is no CLI flag or `apm.yml` field to control this (`apm compile --help` exposes nothing for the banner/title), so users can't opt out — the double-H1 is unavoidable and, since `CLAUDE.md` is a gitignored generated artifact, it can't be hand-fixed without being overwritten on the next compile.

## Impact

- markdownlint `MD025` warnings on every generated `CLAUDE.md`.
- Inconsistency between the Claude and Codex output shapes for the same sources.

issues.title: [BUG] Combined hook manifests (claude-codex-hooks.json) route to one target only; claude silently gets Copilot-schema fallback hooks
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Filename-based hook routing recognizes only single-token stems. In
[`hook_file_routing.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/hook_file_routing.py),
`_hook_file_allowed_targets` matches `<token>-hooks`, `*-<token>-hooks`, or `hooks-<token>`, so a combined
manifest named `claude-codex-hooks.json` (a real authoring pattern: both `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and
`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` in DietrichGebert/ponytail point their `hooks` at this one file) matches only via
`endswith("-codex-hooks")` and routes to **codex alone** -- never claude.

The claude target then falls back to the universal `.apm/hooks/hooks.json`. That file is generated during plugin
normalization from the **first** `plugin.json` found by `find_plugin_json`
([`helpers.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/utils/helpers.py)), whose precedence puts
`.github/plugin/plugin.json` (Copilot) above `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Net effect: Copilot-schema hooks
(camelCase events, `bash`/`powershell`/`timeoutSec`, no matcher nesting) are written into `.claude/settings.json`,
where Claude Code silently ignores them, and the events that exist only in the Claude manifest (`SubagentStart`)
are dropped entirely.

A fix needs the stem matcher to recognize multi-token combined names: when every segment before `-hooks` is a
known target token, route to the union of those targets (`claude-codex-hooks` -> claude + codex).

**To Reproduce**

1. `mkdir /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro`
2. `apm install DietrichGebert/ponytail -t claude`
3. Inspect `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "sessionStart": [
      { "type": "command",
        "bash": "node \".claude/hooks/ponytail/hooks/ponytail-activate.js\"",
        "powershell": "node \".claude/hooks/ponytail/hooks/ponytail-activate.js\"",
        "timeoutSec": 5 } ],
    "userPromptSubmitted": [ { "...same shape..." : "" } ]
  }
}
```

**Expected behavior**

`claude-codex-hooks.json` is selected for both claude and codex. `.claude/settings.json` receives PascalCase
nested hooks (`SessionStart` / `SubagentStart` / `UserPromptSubmit` with `matcher`/`hooks` entries), matching what
the codex target already receives from the same file.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux
- Python Version: 3.13
- APM Version: 0.23.1 (also reproduced on main @ 13e96d16)

**Logs**

```
Hook events for target 'claude' may not be recognized: sessionStart, userPromptSubmitted. Target expects
PascalCase (e.g. PreToolUse). Rename events to match the PascalCase convention, then reinstall.
WARNING apm_cli.integration.hook_integrator target claude: hook event casing mismatch (no mapping): sessionStart, userPromptSubmitted
```

**Additional context**

Same routing subsystem as #1892 / #1902 (which introduced filename routing and its deprecation path) and the
mirror image of #1977 / #1979 on the copilot side. The recommended object-form workaround (`targets: [claude,
codex]` on the dependency) does not avoid this: it bypasses filename routing entirely and deploys **all** of the
package's hook files to claude, so the correct PascalCase hooks arrive together with the Copilot-schema entries.
The target-agnostic `find_plugin_json` precedence that produces the Copilot-shaped universal fallback is arguably
a separate design issue; happy to file it separately. PR with fix + regression tests incoming.

issues.title: [BUG] Deployed hook scripts crash at runtime: required sibling modules are not copied, and the consumer's package.json module type is applied to them
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Hook integration copies only the script files referenced directly by hook commands. In
[`hook_integrator.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py),
`_rewrite_hooks_data` extracts the script paths named in each command and the deploy path `shutil.copy2`s exactly
those files into the target tree (`.claude/hooks/<pkg>/`, `.github/hooks/scripts/<pkg>/`). Two problems follow:

1. **Sibling modules are not copied.** DietrichGebert/ponytail's entry scripts begin with
   `require('./ponytail-config')`, `require('./ponytail-instructions')`, `require('./ponytail-runtime')` -- none
   of which are referenced by a hook command, so none are deployed. Every deployed hook crashes with
   `Cannot find module './ponytail-config'`, in every project, for every target.

2. **The copies inherit the consumer project's module type.** Because the deployed scripts live inside the
   consumer's tree, Node resolves their module system from the *consumer's* `package.json`. In any project with
   `"type": "module"` (a very common modern Node setup), the package's CommonJS scripts are parsed as ESM and die
   even earlier: `ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope`. The package's own `package.json`
   (which correctly declares its module semantics) is left behind in `apm_modules/`.

The same scripts run correctly from `apm_modules/<owner>/<pkg>/hooks/`, where all siblings exist and the package's
own `package.json` governs module resolution. So the deployment step is what breaks them.

**To Reproduce**

1. `mkdir /tmp/repro && cd /tmp/repro`
2. `apm install DietrichGebert/ponytail -t copilot`
3. Run a deployed hook the way the harness would:

```
$ echo '{}' | node .github/hooks/scripts/ponytail/hooks/ponytail-activate.js
Error: Cannot find module './ponytail-config'
```

4. Add a typical consumer `package.json` (`{"type": "module"}`) and run again:

```
$ echo '{}' | node .github/hooks/scripts/ponytail/hooks/ponytail-activate.js
ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope
```

5. Contrast with the undeployed original, which works:

```
$ echo '{}' | node apm_modules/DietrichGebert/ponytail/hooks/ponytail-activate.js
PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE -- level: full   (exit 0)
```

**Expected behavior**

Deployed hook scripts are runnable: their module dependencies are present and they keep the module semantics their
package declares, regardless of the consumer project's `package.json`.

Two possible directions:

- Copy the package's entire hooks directory (not just command-referenced entries) and preserve the package's
  `package.json` module `"type"` alongside the copies, keeping the current self-contained deploy model; or
- Do not copy at all: rewrite hook commands to execute from `apm_modules/<owner>/<pkg>/...`, matching the native
  Claude Code plugin model (`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` with the whole plugin directory present). Trade-off:
  `apm_modules/` is gitignored, so deployed hooks would require `apm install` after clone.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux
- Python Version: 3.13
- APM Version: 0.23.1 (also reproduced on main @ `14a87475`)

**Logs**

```
file:///.../.claude/hooks/ponytail/hooks/ponytail-activate.js:9
const fs = require('fs');
           ^
ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope, you can use import instead
This file is being treated as an ES module because it has a '.js' file extension and
'/.../package.json' contains "type": "module". To treat it as a CommonJS script, rename it to
use the '.cjs' file extension.
```

**Additional context**

Found while validating #2021 (refs #2020): once hook manifests route correctly to the claude target, the deployed
scripts crash at session start with the errors above. The copilot target hits this today with no other bug
involved -- the repro above is stock v0.23.1. Package authors can partially defend with `.cjs` extensions (fixes
the module-type issue, not the missing siblings). Ponytail is authored to the native Claude Code plugin spec,
where the whole plugin directory is present at runtime, so its multi-file scripts are conventional rather than
unusual.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Deprecate and remove filename-based hook routing in favor of per-package `targets:`
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

APM currently has *two* mechanisms that answer "which harness(es) does a package's hooks go to":

1. **Canonical:** per-package `targets:` on a dependency entry (the single placement mechanism ratified in #1911). When present (`dep_targets_active`), it fully governs routing.
2. **Legacy fallback:** when a dependency declares no `targets:`, APM infers targets from the hook *filename* via an invented token convention (`<prefix>-<target>-hooks.json`, e.g. `claude-codex-hooks.json` -> claude + codex), implemented in `src/apm_cli/integration/hook_file_routing.py` -- a module whose own docstring reads *"Deprecated hook filename-routing helpers"* and whose core function documents *"Filename routing is a deprecated package-authoring convenience, not an authorization boundary."*

The filename path is fragile and surprising:
- It silently mis-routed combined manifests (#2020): `claude-codex-hooks.json` deployed to only one target, so the other harness silently got no hooks / a schema-mismatched fallback. That was a genuine data-loss-class bug.
- Routing on an invented naming pattern is implicit and easy to get wrong (unknown/partial tokens fall back to "universal" or last-token-wins), which is exactly the ambiguity `targets:` was introduced to eliminate.

#2021 (closes #2020) fixed the correctness bug **and** started the wind-down by emitting a deprecation warning on every filename-routed hook, pointing authors at the `targets:` object form. But there is currently **no tracked plan to actually remove the legacy path** -- so it will accrete indefinitely. This issue records that removal plan.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

A staged deprecation-to-removal of filename-based hook routing, leaving `targets:` (#1911) as the single placement mechanism for hooks, consistent with design ruling #3 ("hooks are not special"):

1. **Now (shipped in #2021):** filename-routed hooks emit a one-per-package deprecation warning that shows the equivalent `targets: [...]` and links the manifest-schema object form.
2. **Next (this issue):** documentation sweep -- mark filename routing deprecated in the package-authoring guide and manifest-schema reference; ensure every authoring example uses `targets:`; add a CHANGELOG "Deprecated" entry.
3. **One minor release later:** escalate the runtime warning (louder, and count it toward the `apm audit` drift/health surface) so silent reliance is visible before removal.
4. **Target removal release:** delete `hook_file_routing.py`'s inference (keep only the "no `targets:` -> universal" default), remove the token table, and drop the associated filename-routing tests. Packages that still rely on filename inference will need a one-line `targets:` addition (the warning already tells them exactly what to write).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Keep it forever as a convenience.** Rejected: two placement mechanisms for the same question is the accretion #1911 explicitly set out to end, and the #2020 bug shows the legacy path is a silent-failure surface.
- **Hard-remove immediately (no ramp).** Rejected: it would break existing packages that ship `*-hooks.json` without `targets:` with no migration window. The staged warn-then-remove path is friendlier to the contributor base.
- **Fold into "require explicit targets" governance (#1882).** Related but distinct: #1882 makes *missing* targets a hard error (opt-in governance for *autodetection* broadly); this issue is specifically about retiring the *filename-token* inference for hook manifests. They should land coherently but are separately scoped.

**Additional context**

- North-star design: #1911 ([DESIGN] Per-package primitive routing (`targets:`) as the single placement mechanism).
- Bug that exposed the fragility + added the deprecation warning: #2020 / #2021.
- Related governance: #1882 ([FEATURE] Make missing targets a hard error instead of silently autodetecting).
- Code to retire: `src/apm_cli/integration/hook_file_routing.py` (`_HOOK_FILE_TARGET_TOKENS`, `_hook_file_allowed_targets`, suffix-segment helpers) and its call sites in `hook_integrator.py` / `kiro_hook_integrator.py` (guarded by `dep_targets_active`).

No breaking change is proposed in this issue itself -- it tracks the plan so the removal is scheduled rather than indefinite. The actual removal release needs maintainer sign-off on timing.

issues.title: [BUG] devDependencies are invisible to orphan detection
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install` installs packages declared under `devDependencies.apm` and
records them in the lockfile (`is_dev: true`), but every consumer of the
"declared dependencies" set only looks at the production bucket, so any
installed dev dependency is seen as orphaned. This happens whether or not the
project also declares production dependencies:

- `apm prune` treats the just-installed dev dep as orphaned and **deletes it**
  from `apm_modules/` — even though its own help says it removes "packages
  *not listed in apm.yml*" (dev deps are listed), and there is no
  `--production`/`--omit=dev`-style flag that would make this intentional.
  `apm install` → `apm prune` → `apm install` oscillates forever.
- `apm audit --ci` fails the `no-orphaned-packages` check on the dev dep's
  lockfile entry and exits 1. The suggested remedy ("run 'apm install' to
  clean up") does nothing — install correctly keeps the dev dep — so the CI
  gate fails permanently.

(When the project declares *only* dev dependencies, the same prod-only view
also mislabels it as having no dependencies at all — `lockfile-exists: "No
dependencies declared -- lockfile not required"` — but the prune deletion and
orphan failure above do not depend on that.)

Single root cause: `APMPackage.get_apm_dependencies()`
([`models/apm_package.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/models/apm_package.py))
returns only `dependencies["apm"]`, and its sibling
`get_dev_apm_dependencies()` is never consulted by any of these paths:

- [`commands/prune.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/prune.py):
  `declared_deps = apm_package.get_apm_dependencies()` → dev deps missing from
  `expected_installed` → `safe_rmtree`'d as orphans.
- [`policy/ci_checks.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/policy/ci_checks.py):
  `_check_no_orphans` builds `manifest_keys` from `get_apm_dependencies()`;
  a dev dep's lockfile entry is direct (`resolved_by: null`), so it satisfies
  the orphan predicate. (`_check_lockfile_exists` gates on the equally
  prod-only `has_apm_dependencies()`, producing the "No dependencies
  declared" message in the dev-only case.)
- [`commands/_helpers.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/_helpers.py):
  `_check_orphaned_packages()` (the on-disk scan) makes the identical call.

**To Reproduce**
1. Declare a local package under `devDependencies.apm` in `apm.yml`
   (and nothing under `dependencies.apm`).
2. Run `apm install` — succeeds; package lands in `apm_modules/`, lockfile
   entry written with `is_dev: true`.
3. Run `apm audit --ci`:

```
│ [+]      │ lockfile-exists        │ No dependencies declared -- lockfile not │
│          │                        │ required                                 │
│ [x]      │ no-orphaned-packages   │ 1 orphaned package(s) in lockfile -- run │
│          │                        │ 'apm install' to clean up                │

  no-orphaned-packages details:
    - ./sub-package

[x] 1 of 5 check(s) failed
```

Exit code 1; re-running `apm install` does not clear it.

4. Run `apm prune` (or `--dry-run`):

```
[>] Analyzing installed packages vs apm.yml...
[!] Found 1 orphaned package(s):
[!]   - _local/sub-package
[i] + Removed _local/sub-package
[*] Pruned 1 orphaned package(s)
```

`apm_modules/` is now empty; the next `apm install` reinstalls the package.

**Expected behavior**

A dependency declared in `devDependencies.apm` and installed by `apm install`
is not an orphan: `apm prune` leaves it installed (npm parity: `npm prune`
keeps dev deps unless `--omit=dev` is passed), and `apm audit --ci` passes
right after a clean install.

**Environment**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.23.1

**Logs**

See the audit table and prune output above.

**Additional context**

Observed side inconsistency: after the (wrongful) prune, the `apm.lock.yaml`
entry for the removed package survives, so the lockfile and `apm_modules/`
disagree until the next install.

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs (`make audit` and
`make prune` in `dev-dependencies/`).

issues.title: Add `apm doctor tls` trust-source diagnostic + test-suite ssl-isolation fixture
issues.body:
## Context

Fast-follow from the #2005 / #2004 OS-trust-store work. Two observability/hygiene items the red team surfaced that were out of scope for the blocker fixes:

### 1. `apm doctor tls` (or `apm doctor` TLS section)

#2005 added a verbose trust-source log line (`[i] TLS: verifying against OS trust store (truststore)` / `... bundled CA (certifi fallback)` / `... explicit CA bundle in use` / `... disabled`). That is the shippable minimum, but a dedicated diagnostic would let enterprise users self-serve when TLS fails:

- Print the **active trust source** (OS store / certifi fallback / explicit bundle / disabled).
- Print the resolved precedence (`APM_DISABLE_TRUSTSTORE`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`/`CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, future `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE`, OS store, certifi).
- Optionally probe a URL and report which CA source verified it.
- Surface `APM_DISABLE_TRUSTSTORE=1` in the TLS **failure** message (currently only OS store / `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` are mentioned).

### 2. Test-suite ssl-isolation fixture

Importing `apm_cli.cli` (and now `configure_tls_trust()`) monkeypatches process-global `ssl.SSLContext`. ~110 tests import the CLI, so global SSL state can leak across tests (the #2005 verifier already needed a local `truststore.extract_from_ssl()` guard + autouse isolation in the TLS integration suites). Promote this to a shared, autouse `conftest` fixture that snapshots/restores ssl (`extract_from_ssl`) around tests, so no suite silently inherits an injected global.

## Acceptance

- `apm doctor` reports the active TLS trust source and precedence.
- A shared autouse fixture guarantees no cross-test global-ssl bleed; the per-suite guards in the TLS tests can then be removed.

issues.title: Add additive corporate-CA support: APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE (npm NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS parity)
issues.body:
## Context

Fast-follow from the #2005 / #2004 OS-trust-store work. A red-team review (enterprise-proxy + package-manager-precedent panels) flagged that APM has **no additive CA path**: `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` **replace** the trust set (and skip truststore injection entirely). Many enterprises hand developers a single corporate-root PEM but do **not** permit OS trust-store edits, so they need "OS roots **plus** this one extra CA", not "only this CA".

This is the standard npm model (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, additive) and Node's `--use-system-ca` (system + bundled + extra). APM lacks the equivalent.

## Proposal

Add an additive `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` (and optionally `APM_EXTRA_CA_DIR`) that is layered **on top of** the OS trust store rather than replacing it:

- Implement via a scoped `SSLContext` that first loads the OS/certifi defaults, then `load_verify_locations(APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE)` — OS/certifi defaults remain intact.
- Propagate to `apm run` child runtimes through the same `build_child_tls_env()` seam introduced in #2005 (export the extra bundle so Python and Node children both honor it, e.g. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for Node runtimes).
- Precedence must be documented explicitly alongside the existing `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` (replace) and `APM_DISABLE_TRUSTSTORE` (opt-out) knobs.

## Acceptance

- An enterprise PEM set via `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` is trusted **in addition to** the OS store for both `apm install` and `apm run`.
- e2e test: private-CA server trusted via `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` while public HTTPS (OS/certifi roots) still verifies.

Deferred deliberately from #2005 to avoid half-shipping (Node-only) the additive path.

issues.title: [BUG] some awesome-copilot plugin does not install SKILLs and Agents
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Installing the awesome-copilot plugin which hosted at [awesome-copilot](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot) with `apm install XXXX@awesome-copilot` does not place the plugin's SKILLs and Agents into `.claude/` and `.agents/`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run `apm install XXXX@awesome-copilot`
2. Check `.claude/` and `.agents/` after installation
3. Confirm that the plugin's SKILLs and Agents were not created in either directory

**Expected behavior**

issues.title: [FEATURE] TargetProfile: plugin-bin-contract abstraction for multi-harness bin/ deployment
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Plugin `bin/` deployment is currently hard-wired to Claude Code's skills-directory plugin contract. As new harnesses adopt executable-deployment patterns (e.g. Codex CLI, Gemini CLI), each harness will need its own bin/ placement, PATH setup, and reload mechanism. Without an abstraction, the `_deploy_plugin_bin` function will grow per-harness branches and the gate logic (deny, scope, trust-posture) will be duplicated.

This was identified as item 6 in the advisory review panel on PR #1591 (tracked in #1620).

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Introduce a `TargetProfile` (or similar) abstraction that encapsulates the per-harness bin/ deployment contract:

- **bin_dir(project_root, scope)** -- where to place executables for this harness
- **bin_path_mechanism** -- how the harness discovers deployed bins (PATH env, config entry, manifest)
- **reload_hint** -- user-facing instruction to activate new executables (e.g. `/reload-plugins`, restart)
- **requires_plugin_manifest** -- whether the harness needs `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` or equivalent
- **supported_scopes** -- which install scopes (user, project) support bin/ deployment

Each `TargetProfile` would implement the contract for its harness, and `_deploy_plugin_bin` would delegate to the active profile instead of hard-coding Claude-specific logic.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Keep the current approach and add per-harness `if` branches as needed (simpler short-term, scales poorly).
- Use a registry/dict mapping harness names to deployment functions (lighter than a full class hierarchy, but less extensible).

**Additional context**

- Parent issue: #1620 (item 6)
- The current Claude-only implementation is stable and well-tested; this is a forward-looking design issue, not a regression.
- Priority: low -- only becomes relevant when a second harness adopts bin/ deployment.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Support workspace-level (.mcp.json) and global (-g) MCP configurations for Copilot CLI
issues.body: # [FEATURE] Support workspace-level (.mcp.json) and global (-g) MCP configurations for Copilot CLI ### **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.** Currently, managing MCP servers for the GitHub Copilot CLI is limited because APM's `copilot` integration target is hard-coded to global scope. Specifically: * Running `apm integration install copilot` always writes the configuration globally to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, even when run without `-g` / `--global` inside an APM project workspace. * The APM CLI's Copilot integration does not support project-scoped installations. Since the GitHub Copilot CLI itself supports project-scoped MCP configurations loaded from `.mcp.json` or `.github/mcp.json` at the workspace root, forcing all installations to be global causes environment pollution. This leads to configuration bloat, potential tool argument conflicts between different workspaces, and prevents workspace-specific tools from being checked into version control. The official Copilot CLI documentation is not fully clear here but as on the main MCP config section it does nto vocer taht option (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/overview#add-an-mcp-server), though it is officially documented as supproted behaviour here (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference#mcp-server-loading-priority) Warning message from Copilot CLI that currently this config is not supported. Working (manually created) project-level .mcp.json config ### **Describe the solution you'd like** Extend APM's Copilot integration to support both project-local and user-global installation scopes: 1. **Install-Write Path (`CopilotClientAdapter`)**: * By default (project scope), write the configuration locally to `/.mcp.json`. * Only write to the user-global `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` when the `--global` / `-g` flag is explicitly provided. 2. **Runtime-Read Path (`CopilotRuntime`)**: * Discover and read MCP configurations following the Copilot CLI's official loading priority: 1. Current working directory `.mcp.json` 2. Current working directory `.github/mcp.json` 3. User-global fallback `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` * Ensure the parser supports the workspace-scoped `"mcpServers"` root key (used in `.mcp.json`) in addition to the global `"servers"` key. ### **Describe alternatives you've considered** * **Manually maintaining local configuration files**: Copying and pasting MCP configurations manually to `.mcp.json` when working in a specific project. This is error-prone and bypasses APM's dependency resolution, updating, and installation workflows. * **Injecting all project configurations into global config**: Keeping the current global-only behavior. This is undesirable because it exposes all workspace tools to Copilot in every directory, increasing startup overhead and causing command/context pollution. ### **Additional context** * **Official Reference**: GitHub Copilot CLI's [MCP server loading priority documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference#mcp-server-loading-priority). * **mcp.json migration**: Official docs how to migrate form VS Code format to `.mcp.json` https://gh.io/copilotcli-mcpmigrate * **Parity**: Other client adapters in APM (like Cursor and Windsurf) already support project-local scoping. Implementing this will achieve feature parity for the Copilot integration.
