issues.title: [BUG] apm install <positional URL> exits 0 when the install totally fails; manifest-declared equivalent exits 1
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm install <positional-url>` exits `0` when the requested install
**totally fails**. Pointing a positional install at an unreachable git host
deploys nothing, yet the command returns success (exit `0`). The
manifest-declared equivalent of the same unreachable dependency correctly
exits `1`. A CI pipeline or wrapper script that runs `apm install <url>` and
trusts the exit code will treat a complete install failure as success.

## Baseline and environments

- Baseline SHA: `4257698916736679478af4a9c37dc055b22b0d7a` (origin/main); HEAD
  retained the behavior.
- APM: 0.24.1 (`uv run apm`)
- Platform / arch: macOS / arm64
- Harness: target-independent (dependency-resolution layer, pre-adapter)

## Native contract

- `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md:195-201`: exit `0` means all
  requested dependencies deployed; a dependency-resolution failure or any
  reported install error exits `1`.

## Exact reproduction

```
# fresh HOME / disposable project, no manifest declaring the dep
apm install https://127.0.0.1:1/org/repo.git   # unreachable host
echo $?                                          # observed: 0
```

Control (manifest-declared equivalent): declare the same unreachable URL in
`apm.yml` and run `apm install` with no positional arg -> exits `1`.

## Expected and actual behavior

- Expected: bounded non-zero failure with clear diagnostics, unchanged
  manifest/lock, and no partial remote deployment (exit `1`).
- Actual: exit `0`, manifest/lock unchanged, no partial deploy, no timeout --
  reproduced twice from fresh state. The error is emitted to the user but the
  process still terminates successfully.

## Finder and independent confirmation

- Finder: `rasc-w2-macos` (remote-auth / supply-chain domain worker).
- Confirmer: `conf-rasc-r1-02` (distinct identity). Independently reproduced
  positional unreachable exit `0` and manifest-declared exit `1` on both
  baseline SHA and latest HEAD; confidence high.

## Falsification controls

- Clean isolated control from fresh HOME/project: manifest-declared unreachable
  dependency exits `1` (isolates the defect to the positional entry path, not
  the network failure itself).
- Repeat fresh-state run reproduced the same exit `0`.
- Reachable local-package positional install control exits `0` correctly (the
  success path is intact).

## Normalized fingerprint

`INSTALL_VALIDATION_ALL_FAILED_EXIT_ZERO`

## Historical siblings

Same triaged "silent-success" theme (`theme/portability`, `priority/high`),
distinct mechanisms and owners:

- OPEN #2116 `apm install --skill <name>` silent no-op -- a `--skill` filter
  miss on a **reachable** Claude-plugin repo. Different owner (skill-filter
  resolution), not clone failure.
- OPEN #2103 missing declared plugin components silently ignored -- a
  declared-but-missing **component path** inside a **reachable** plugin exits
  `0`. Different owner (component-path resolution).
- OPEN #1882 `[FEATURE]` make missing targets a hard error -- adjacent theme.

This finding is distinct: a **positional** install of a **totally unreachable**
git host exits `0`, while the **manifest-declared equivalent of the same
unreachable dependency exits `1`**. The novel signal is the positional-vs-
manifest entry-path asymmetry for an identical total-failure input, pinned to
`install.py:1512-1526`. It adds a confirmed, owner-scoped data point to the
existing cluster rather than duplicating it.

## Architecture diagnosis

Invariant (thematic): equivalent operations must derive their terminal signal
from a canonical result representing the full requested operation.

Canonical owner (this finding): `src/apm_cli/commands/install.py:1512-1526`.
`_ValidationOutcome.all_failed` is the canonical positional-validation fact
(defined `src/apm_cli/core/command_logger.py:27-40`, rendered as an error at
`command_logger.py:233-247`), but `command_logger` does not own process
termination. `install.py` converts `outcome.all_failed` into a **normal
return**, so Click exits `0`. The manifest-declared path instead reaches the
main install pipeline whose dependency/auth/general failures exit `1` at
`install.py:1595-1621`.

Confidence: confirmed for this single owner. Note (escalate): this finding
*rhymes* with a separate audit finding (local-path sub-package MCP source
drift, filed separately) under the same "terminal-signal parity" invariant, but
the architecture diagnosis established **no shared canonical owner** -- install
termination and audit consistency are distinct subsystems. Do **not** introduce
a cross-command terminal-signal framework to unify them; fix each at its own
owner.

## Blast matrix

- command: `install` (positional vs manifest-declared parity; partial and
  all-failed batches for regression)
- scope: project observed; global/user regression-relevant
- primitive: APM git dependency observed (unreachable positional + manifest
  source)
- target: target-independent (pre-adapter dependency layer)
- host: totally unreachable git host and localhost-refused endpoint observed
  exit `0`; reachable local package control exits `0`; auth-failure exit `1`
  regression-relevant
- platform: macOS/arm64 observed; linux + windows regression-required

## Fix constraints

Minimal remediation: make install's outcome-to-exit conversion fail nonzero
when `_ValidationOutcome.all_failed`, while preserving rollback, partial-success
policy, and the existing all-failed diagnostic. Do **not** add a cross-command
abstraction. Required regression + mutation coverage: positional unreachable
exits `1` and rolls back; manifest-declared equivalent exits `1`; mixed
valid/invalid positional batch continues with the valid package; all-invalid
batch exits `1`; already-present package stays successful; reachable-local
control exits `0`; a mutation that replaces the nonzero termination with a
normal return must fail a public CliRunner/subprocess test (not only a mocked
helper assertion). Fix/TDD/CI/mergeability ownership belongs to
`batch-bug-shepherd`, not this report.

## Principles

- P6 Reliability over magic: an emitted install error must not exit `0`.
- P4 UX is the floor: preserve diagnostics, partial-success behavior, target
  inference, and recovery hints while correcting only false terminal success.
- P5 Portability: apply equivalent failure semantics across targets, hosts, and
  operating systems.
- P3 Vendor-neutral: the fix operates on the dependency/validation model before
  any target adaptation; no harness translation layer.

## Evidence

Finder, confirmer (fresh-state repeat + manifest-declared control), and the
architecture diagnosis (cluster `arch-cluster-a-terminal-signal-parity`,
topology `escalate`) are archived by the red-team run. Full sanitized
artifacts available on request.

---
Filed by the APM red-team reliability sweep (Round 1). Confirmed by an
independent second reproduction. Handed to `batch-bug-shepherd` for triage, TDD,
review, CI, and mergeability.

issues.title: [BUG] apm audit --ci misses local-path sub-package MCP source drift (exits 0); direct MCP drift exits 1
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm audit --ci` config-consistency does **not** detect when a locally-installed
local-path sub-package changes its MCP server config after install. If a
local-path sub-package's `apm.yml` MCP `args` (or command/env/transport) drift
away from the `mcp_configs` baseline recorded in `apm.lock.yaml`, audit exits
`0` and reports "MCP configs match lockfile baseline". The equivalent **direct**
(root-declared) MCP config drift is caught and exits `1`. The audit's
drift-detection guarantee has a false-negative blind spot for transitive
local-path MCP sources.

## Baseline and environments

- Baseline SHA: `4257698916736679478af4a9c37dc055b22b0d7a` (origin/main); HEAD
  retained the behavior.
- APM: 0.24.1 (`uv run apm`)
- Platform / arch: macOS / arm64
- Harness: MCP audit fixture target copilot (config comparison is
  target-independent)

## Native contract

- `apm audit --ci` config-consistency: the current MCP config must be compared
  against the `mcp_configs` baseline in `apm.lock.yaml`; drift must fail (exit
  `1`) and name the difference.
- The #2081 fix (PR #2084, commit `6d4d8d356`) deliberately added
  `mcp_config_provenance` so lock-only transitive servers are **not** falsely
  flagged as orphans -- that exemption must be preserved.

## Exact reproduction

```
apm install --force --trust-transitive-mcp --target copilot --no-policy
apm audit --ci --no-policy --no-fail-fast -f json     # clean: exit 0

# mutate a local-path sub-package MCP config WITHOUT reinstalling
# edit packages/agent-config/apm.yml: MCP args ready -> changed
apm audit --ci --no-policy --no-fail-fast -f json     # observed: exit 0 (BUG)

# reconcile
apm install ... ; apm audit ...                        # exit 0 (lock updated)
# edit again: args changed -> changed-again
apm audit ...                                          # observed: exit 0 (BUG)
```

## Expected and actual behavior

- Expected: audit `--ci` fails (exit `1`) and names the config difference when
  the current local sub-package MCP config differs from `mcp_configs` in
  `apm.lock.yaml`; reinstall reconciles and restores a clean audit.
- Actual: on two distinct pre-reinstall source changes the lockfile `args`
  stayed old but audit exited `0` with "MCP configs match lockfile baseline".
  Reinstall updated the lock each time and the subsequent audit passed --
  confirming the drift was real and only the detection was missing.

## Finder and independent confirmation

- Finder: `ogp-w4-macos` (operations / governance / portability domain worker).
- Confirmer: `conf-ogp-r1-04` (distinct identity). Independently reproduced the
  local-path transitive drift exit `0` and the direct-MCP-drift exit `1` control
  on baseline and HEAD; confidence high.

## Falsification controls

- Clean control: unchanged local package, lock, and deployed config passed
  (exit `0`).
- Reproduction 1: local package MCP args `ready -> changed` while lock stayed
  `ready` -> audit exit `0` (miss).
- Reconciliation control: reinstall updated lock to `changed`, audit passed.
- Reproduction 2: args `changed -> changed-again` while lock stayed `changed`
  -> audit exit `0` (miss).
- Inverse control: an equivalent **direct** MCP change exits `1` with "config
  differs from lockfile baseline" -> isolates the miss to the local-path
  sub-package source-derivation path, not audit's exit mapping.

## Normalized fingerprint

`CONFIG-CONSISTENCY:local-path-transitive-mcp-source-change-ignored:exit-0`

## Historical siblings

- CLOSED #2081 (PR #2084, commit `6d4d8d356`): added `mcp_config_provenance` to
  stop false-positive orphan reports for transitive MCP servers. Its tests
  (`tests/unit/policy/test_ci_checks.py:420-468`,
  `tests/integration/test_transitive_mcp_audit_e2e.py:65-90`) cover clean-install
  false-positive prevention but **not** post-install sub-package source drift --
  this finding is the false-negative inverse in the same code region.
- CLOSED #1846 (PR #1855, commit `2d3f8d210`): established `resolved_by`
  provenance for remote dependencies declared by local-path packages.
- Open silent-success reports #2103 / #1882 share the theme, no shared owner.

This directly matches the "fix-here, miss-there" hypothesis: the #2081 fix that
added provenance to suppress false positives is exactly the region that now
lacks post-install source re-derivation, producing a false negative.

## Architecture diagnosis

Invariant (thematic): equivalent operations must derive their terminal signal
from a canonical result representing the full requested operation.

Canonical owner (this finding): `src/apm_cli/policy/ci_checks.py:229-283`
(`_check_config_consistency`). It derives `current_configs` only from
`manifest.get_all_mcp_dependencies()` (`ci_checks.py:237-239`), which
`APMPackage` implements as root production + root dev MCP entries only
(`src/apm_cli/models/apm_package.py:525-563`). The install path re-parses
installed sub-package `apm.yml` files, assigns `dep.resolved_by`, and stores the
merged config + provenance (`src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_integrator.py:210-275`,
`src/apm_cli/install/mcp/integration.py:85-95,150-172`). Audit never invokes
that source derivation, so a changed local-path sub-package is represented only
by the stale lock baseline. `mcp_config_provenance` is used at
`ci_checks.py:256-265` **solely** to exempt lock-only transitive servers from
orphan reporting -- it is trusted as current instead of re-derived.

This is upstream verdict-**input** incompleteness, not a terminal-conversion
defect: `src/apm_cli/policy/models.py:44-66` and
`src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py:698` correctly aggregate `CheckResult.passed`
into `CIAuditResult.passed` and map to exit `0`/`1`.

Confidence: confirmed for this single owner. Note (escalate): this finding and a
separate install-termination finding (#2126) rhyme under one "terminal-signal
parity" invariant but have **no shared canonical owner** (established by the
red-team architecture diagnosis, topology `escalate`). Fix each at its own
owner; do not build a cross-command consistency framework.

## Blast matrix

- command: `audit --ci` (direct vs local-path sub-package MCP parity;
  remote-sub-package regression). Siblings: `update` (rewrites `mcp_configs` +
  provenance), `uninstall` (orphan verdict), `compile` (source-vs-lock).
- scope: project observed; global/user regression-relevant for MCP persistence
- primitive: MCP observed (direct + local-path sub-package drift);
  hooks/instructions transitive source-vs-lock regression-relevant
- target: copilot observed; claude/cursor/codex/windsurf/gemini/opencode
  regression-relevant (comparison must stay vendor-neutral, must not mutate
  native runtime files)
- host: reachable local package observed; remote sub-package source
  regression-relevant
- platform: macOS/arm64 observed; linux + windows regression-required

## Fix constraints

Minimal remediation: define a side-effect-free, lock-bounded current-MCP-config
resolver that re-parses local-path sub-package manifests (reusing MCP dependency
parsing + root-first deduplication from `MCPIntegrator` without invoking install
I/O), and feed that complete current view into `_check_config_consistency`;
keep `mcp_config_provenance` for ownership/orphan classification only. No
harness translation layer. Required regression + mutation coverage: mutate
sub-package `apm.yml` command/args/env/transport without reinstall -> exit `1`
naming the diff; unchanged transitive passes; direct drift still fails; #2081
clean-install non-orphan still protected; genuine unprovenanced orphan still
fails; duplicate server names keep root-first dedup; removing the transitive
source re-derivation (or substituting stored lock configs as current) must make
the drift regression fail. Fix/TDD/CI/mergeability ownership belongs to
`batch-bug-shepherd`.

## Principles

- P6 Reliability over magic: `audit --ci` must explain source-vs-lock drift
  rather than silently trusting stale lock provenance.
- P1 No invented primitive frontmatter: source re-derivation reads canonical
  upstream primitive/package declarations; provenance stays lockfile metadata,
  no APM-only fields added to deployed primitives.
- P3 Vendor-neutral by construction: operate on the MCP model before target
  adaptation; no harness-specific exception.
- P7 Community over feature count: preserve #2081/#1846 regression protection;
  defer broader abstraction.

## Evidence

Finder, confirmer (two pre-reinstall drift reproductions + reconciliation and
direct-drift inverse controls), and the architecture diagnosis (cluster
`arch-cluster-a-terminal-signal-parity`, topology `escalate`) are archived by
the red-team run. Full sanitized artifacts available on request.

---
Filed by the APM red-team reliability sweep (Round 1). Confirmed by an
independent second reproduction. Handed to `batch-bug-shepherd` for triage, TDD,
review, CI, and mergeability.

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile --clean skips orphan removal when the last primitive is removed, leaving a stale CLAUDE.md
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm compile --clean` is documented to remove orphaned APM-owned output
files, but when the **last** primitive is removed from a project it exits `1`
with `No instruction files found` **before** the cleanup phase runs, leaving a
stale APM-owned `CLAUDE.md` (and any other orphaned target output) on disk.
The `--clean` orphan-removal contract is silently skipped precisely in the
"everything was removed" case where cleanup matters most.

## Baseline and environments

- Baseline SHA: `4257698916736679478af4a9c37dc055b22b0d7a` (origin/main)
- APM: 0.24.1 (`uv run apm`)
- Platform / arch: macOS / arm64 (target-independent gate; not platform-specific)
- Harness: Claude Code, Codex (native output targets)

## Native contract

- `apm compile --help` (v0.24.1): `--clean` removes orphaned APM-owned
  generated files.
- `references/harness-contracts.md` Claude Code (lines 14-21) / Codex
  (lines 41-48): APM-owned generated context files are APM's to clean.

## Exact reproduction

```
# disposable project with one instruction primitive
uv run apm compile --target claude          # generates APM-owned CLAUDE.md
rm .apm/instructions/base.instructions.md   # remove the last primitive
uv run apm compile --target codex --clean   # expected: cleans orphan, succeeds
```

Independent confirmation reproduced with `--target codex --clean` and observed
the same early exit + retained `CLAUDE.md` across two fresh runs.

## Expected and actual behavior

- Expected: `--clean` removes the orphaned APM-owned `CLAUDE.md` and succeeds
  (exit 0) even when no primitives remain.
- Actual: exits `1` with `No instruction files found` before cleanup; the
  orphaned APM-owned `CLAUDE.md` is left stale on disk. Both fresh runs.

## Finder and independent confirmation

- Finder: `nhf-w2-macos` (native-harness domain worker).
- Confirmer: `conf-nhf-r1-02` (distinct identity). Reproduced from clean state;
  confidence high.

## Falsification controls

- Same-target idempotent `--clean` control (with a primitive retained) reached
  compilation and removed the APM-marked stale `CLAUDE.md` -> isolates the
  defect to the zero-primitives validation gate.
- Retained-source target migration reached the cleanup phase normally.

## Normalized fingerprint

`CLEAN:NO_PRIMITIVES_EARLY_EXIT:STALE_CLAUDE_MD`

## Historical siblings

- CLOSED #1729 `apm compile --clean` never removes a stale `CLAUDE.md` after
  instructions move to `.claude/rules/`.
- CLOSED #1730 `apm compile -t copilot` writes empty AGENTS.md shells.
- CLOSED #1662 `apm install` never updates existing `.claude/rules/*.md`.

This is a regression-adjacent sibling of #1729: the earlier fix handled the
"instructions moved" case, but the "all primitives removed" edge still
short-circuits before cleanup.

## Architecture diagnosis

The target-independent `_validate_project` zero-content exit (cli.py ~1130)
runs **before** `_run_compilation` (cli.py ~1150). Because the validation gate
precedes the cleanup dispatch, it suppresses the `--clean` orphan-removal path
for **every** target, not just `CLAUDE.md`. Canonical owner: compile-command
phase ordering (validate-then-clean vs clean-then-validate).

## Blast matrix

- command: `compile` (with `--clean`)
- scope: project
- primitive: instructions (any last-removed primitive)
- target: claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini (target-independent gate)
- host: n/a (local)
- platform: macOS/arm64 observed; gate is platform-independent

## Fix constraints

Minimal remediation: ensure `--clean` orphan removal runs even when zero
primitives remain (reorder so cleanup of previously-deployed APM-owned outputs
is not gated by the empty-project validation exit). Add a regression test for
"remove last primitive then `--clean`" asserting the orphan file is deleted and
exit is 0. Fix/TDD/CI ownership belongs to `batch-bug-shepherd`, not this
report.

## Principles

- Native-fidelity: APM must not leave orphaned APM-owned files in a native
  target tree it manages.
- Vendor-neutral: applies uniformly across targets; no harness translation
  layer introduced.

## Evidence

Finder (two reproductions + same-target and retained-source controls +
cleanup-verification) and independent confirmer artifacts are archived by the
red-team run. Full sanitized artifacts available on request.

---
Filed by the APM red-team reliability sweep (Round 1). Confirmed by an
independent second reproduction. Handed to `batch-bug-shepherd` for triage, TDD,
review, CI, and mergeability.

issues.title: [BUG] Global Claude install with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR outside HOME partial-deploys then exits 1
issues.body:
## Summary

A global (`--global`) Claude install fails when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` points to an
absolute path **outside** `HOME`. APM partially deploys native files and then
exits `1` because lockfile serialization cannot encode the deployed path: the
deployed command path is outside the project tree and no dynamic-root target
matches. Native Claude supports an arbitrary absolute `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so
APM should honor it rather than assume the config root lives under `HOME`.

## Baseline and environments

- Baseline SHA: `4257698916736679478af4a9c37dc055b22b0d7a` (origin/main)
- APM: 0.24.1 (`uv run apm`)
- Platform / arch: macOS / arm64
- Harness: Claude Code (global scope)

## Native contract

- Claude settings documentation (accessed 2026-07-10):
  `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings` -- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` may be an
  arbitrary absolute path (not constrained to `HOME`).
- `references/harness-contracts.md` Claude Code (lines 14-21).

## Exact reproduction

```
# disposable project with a Claude-targeted global-scope primitive
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<absolute-dir-outside-HOME> \
  uv run apm install --global <local-package> --target claude
uv run apm compile --global
```

Reproduced with two distinct outside-HOME roots; both exited `1` after a
partial deploy.

## Expected and actual behavior

- Expected: global install honors an arbitrary `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, succeeds,
  and records deployed files without requiring the config root under `HOME`.
- Actual: two arbitrary outside-HOME roots exited `1` -- deployed command path
  was outside the project tree and no dynamic-root target matched, so lockfile
  serialization failed after partial deployment. The default `~/.claude`
  control succeeded.

## Finder and independent confirmation

- Finder: `nhf-w4-macos`.
- Confirmer: `conf-nhf-r1-04` (distinct identity). Reproduced outside-HOME
  failure (exit 1, partial deploy) and under-HOME success (exit 0). Confidence
  high.

## Falsification controls

- Default `~/.claude` global install succeeded and deployed native
  command/rule/skill files -> isolates the failure to the outside-HOME config
  root, not global install generally.
- CRLF skill-copy control was byte-identical -> excludes encoding as the cause.

## Normalized fingerprint

`GLOBAL_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:LOCKFILE_DYNAMIC_ROOT_MISS`

## Historical siblings

- CLOSED #2060 claude MCP writer ignored `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, wrote to
  `~/.claude.json` instead of `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json`.

Regression-adjacent sibling: #2060 fixed the writer honoring the env var; this
finding shows the lockfile path-serialization seam still assumes the config
root is under `HOME`, so honoring an outside-HOME root now fails at
serialization.

## Architecture diagnosis

Shared HOME-relative lockfile serialization seam: target scope resolution
(`targets.py:389-418`) supports absolute outside-HOME roots, but deployed-path
encoding (`deployed_paths.py:16-48`) recognizes only project-relative or
`resolved_deploy_root` targets -- so an outside-HOME absolute deploy path has no
representable dynamic root and serialization fails. Canonical owner: deployed
-path encoding's dynamic-root registry must include the Claude config root.

## Blast matrix

- command: `install --global`, `compile --global`
- scope: global (user)
- primitive: instructions/rules, skills, commands, mcp
- target: claude (outside-HOME `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`)
- host: n/a (local)
- platform: macOS/arm64 observed; seam is platform-independent (path-relative
  logic)

## Fix constraints

Minimal remediation: register the resolved Claude config root as a dynamic root
for deployed-path encoding so outside-HOME absolute deploy paths serialize, and
avoid partial deployment on serialization failure (fail closed or complete the
lock). Add a regression test for global Claude install with an outside-HOME
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Fix/TDD/CI ownership: `batch-bug-shepherd`.

## Principles

- Native-fidelity: honor native Claude `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` semantics.
- Fail-closed: do not leave a partially-deployed global tree on serialization
  failure.

## Evidence

Finder (two outside-HOME reproductions + default-root and CRLF controls +
cleanup-verification) and independent confirmer artifacts are archived by the
red-team run. Full sanitized artifacts available on request.

---
Filed by the APM red-team reliability sweep (Round 1). Confirmed by an
independent second reproduction. Handed to `batch-bug-shepherd` for triage, TDD,
review, CI, and mergeability.

issues.title: [BUG] Generated GitHub Copilot hook JSON omits the required top-level version: 1 field
issues.body:
## Summary

When `apm` generates GitHub Copilot hook files (`.github/hooks/*.json`) from a
manifest that does not declare an explicit version, the emitted JSON omits the
required top-level `version` field, producing `{ "hooks": { ... } }` instead of
`{ "version": 1, "hooks": { ... } }`. The official GitHub Copilot hooks format
**requires** a top-level `version` of `1`, so APM-deployed Copilot hooks are
non-conformant unless the source manifest happens to carry a version.

## Baseline and environments

- Baseline SHA: `4257698916736679478af4a9c37dc055b22b0d7a` (origin/main)
- APM: 0.24.1 (`uv run apm`)
- Platform / arch: macOS / arm64
- Harness: GitHub Copilot (hook target); Claude Code used only for isolation
  control.

## Native contract

Official GitHub Copilot hooks documentation (accessed 2026-07-10), two sources:

- `https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/hooks` -- "Hook
  configuration format": *"The JSON must contain a `version` field with a value
  of `1` and a `hooks` object containing arrays of hook definitions."* The
  documented example is `{ "version": 1, "hooks": { ... } }`.
- `https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference` -- hook
  configuration files use JSON format with version `1`.

## Exact reproduction

```
# disposable project with a version-absent hook primitive
uv run apm install --target copilot,claude
uv run apm compile --target copilot,claude --force-instructions
# inspect generated .github/hooks/*.json
```

Generated Copilot hook (baseline, version-absent input):

```json
{ "hooks": { "sessionStart": [ { "type": "command", "bash": "..." } ] } }
```

Required by contract:

```json
{ "version": 1, "hooks": { "sessionStart": [ { "type": "command", "bash": "..." } ] } }
```

## Expected and actual behavior

- Expected: every generated `.github/hooks/*.json` carries top-level
  `version: 1` and native camelCase events; Claude output stays isolated.
- Actual: two fresh version-absent inputs emitted only `hooks` at top level
  (no `version`), failing native validation. A source `version=1` control
  preserved the field; Claude/Copilot target isolation held.

## Finder and independent confirmation

- Finder: `nhf-w3-macos`.
- Confirmer: `conf-nhf-r1-03` (distinct identity). Independently reproduced APM
  output AND live-fetched the official Copilot doc to verify the version
  requirement is real. Confidence high. (This candidate was explicitly
  re-checked for false-positive risk; the official contract confirms the
  requirement.)

## Falsification controls

- Source manifest with explicit `version=1` preserved the field and passed
  native validation -> the omission is specific to version-absent input.
- Claude settings retained only `SessionStart` while Copilot retained only
  `sessionStart` -> target isolation intact; not a cross-target leak.

## Normalized fingerprint

`COPILOT_HOOK:REQUIRED_VERSION_1_OMITTED`

## Historical siblings

- OPEN #2071 Kiro hook integrator emits legacy pre-1.0 hook schema.
- OPEN #2062 `apm install --target claude` writes flat hook entries (missing
  matcher/hooks nesting).
- CLOSED #2020 combined hook manifests route to one target only; claude
  silently gets Copilot-schema fallback hooks.
- Related epic #2112 (replace vendor-to-vendor translation with OpenAPM
  semantic models), #2031.

## Architecture diagnosis

`src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py` injects a top-level version default
(`top_level_defaults={"version":1}`) only for the cursor/codex merge targets
(`_MERGE_HOOK_TARGETS`). Copilot is not in that map and is emitted through a
separate copied-file path that bypasses `top_level_defaults`, so every
version-absent Copilot hook payload lacks the required field. This is one more
instance of per-harness hook-schema divergence in `hook_integrator.py` (see
sibling cluster above).

## Blast matrix

- command: `install`, `compile`
- scope: project (`.github/hooks/`), and Copilot personal `~/.copilot/hooks/`
- primitive: hooks
- target: copilot (defect); cursor/codex carry version; claude/kiro tracked
  separately
- host: n/a
- platform: platform-independent

## Fix constraints

Minimal remediation: ensure the Copilot hook emission path applies the required
top-level `version: 1` default (consistent with the native Copilot contract)
when the source manifest omits it, without a harness translation layer -- this
is honoring the native Copilot primitive contract, not translating between
harnesses. Add a regression test asserting generated Copilot hook JSON always
has top-level `version: 1`. Fix/TDD/CI ownership: `batch-bug-shepherd`.

## Principles

- Native-fidelity: emitted primitives must satisfy the official upstream
  (Copilot) schema.
- Vendor-neutral: fix stays within the native Copilot contract; no cross-vendor
  translation layer.

## Evidence

Finder (two reproductions + version-present and target-isolation controls) and
confirmer artifacts (including the live official-contract capture) are archived
by the red-team run. Full sanitized artifacts available on request.

---
Filed by the APM red-team reliability sweep (Round 1). The official Copilot
contract was live-verified during confirmation. Handed to `batch-bug-shepherd`
for triage, TDD, review, CI, and mergeability.

issues.title: [BUG] apm audit --ci misses local-path sub-package MCP declaration REMOVAL (exits 0); change-drift exits 1
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm audit --ci` config-consistency detects when a locally-installed local-path sub-package *changes* its MCP server config, but does **not** detect when that sub-package *removes* its entire `dependencies.mcp` declaration after install. When the recorded `mcp_configs` lockfile baseline has a server that the current source no longer declares, audit still reports "All checks passed" and exits `0`. The drift-detection guarantee is one-directional: it compares current-source entries against the lock baseline but ignores lock-only (removed) entries.

This is the removal sibling of #2127 (change-drift). The pending fix for #2127 (#2132) was empirically verified to fix the *change* sub-case but still miss *removal*: overlaying #2132's `ci_checks.py` on a working build leaves the post-removal audit at exit `0`.

**To Reproduce**

Baseline SHA: `26d8cee8a4079bb3d31956f1b57d343654835fc8` (origin/main).

1. Consumer `apm.yml` declares a local dependency `./packages/agent-config`.
2. `./packages/agent-config/apm.yml` declares one MCP server (`dependencies.mcp` with `name/command/args`).
3. `apm install --force --trust-transitive-mcp --target copilot --no-policy` -> exit 0; server recorded in `apm.lock.yaml` `mcp_configs`.
4. `apm audit --ci --no-policy --no-fail-fast` (baseline, source unchanged) -> exit 0 (correct).
5. Edit `./packages/agent-config/apm.yml` to delete the entire `dependencies.mcp` block.
6. `apm audit --ci --no-policy --no-fail-fast` -> **exit 0**, "All checks passed" (BUG; should be exit 1 with a source-vs-lock drift diagnostic).

**Expected behavior**

Audit must compare the complete current MCP declaration graph against the stored lock baseline symmetrically: changed, added, AND removed declarations must all affect the consistency verdict. A removed source declaration that still exists in the lock baseline is drift and must exit 1.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS
- APM Version: 0.24.1 (`26d8cee8a`)

**Root-cause (architecture)**

`src/apm_cli/policy/ci_checks.py::_check_config_consistency` derives `current_configs` only from present manifest declarations and diffs one-directionally, so lock-only (removed) servers are never compared. Recommended fix (architecture cluster `r2-symmetric-source-lock-consistency`): introduce a side-effect-free current-MCP-config view resolver plus one symmetric source-vs-lock diff (changed / source-only / lock-only) consumed by `_check_config_consistency` and install/update reconciliation. Keep `mcp_config_provenance` for ownership classification, not as a blanket removal exemption. Vendor-neutral, no primitive-schema change, no harness translation layer.

**Additional context**

Filed from an authorized first-party reliability/regression validation sweep (red-team Round 2). Independently reproduced twice by a separate confirmer (finder != confirmer), with control (unchanged source exits 0) and cleanup verification. Distinct from #2127/#2132 (change vs removal).

issues.title: [BUG] apm audit --ci and policy status --check silently accept schema-invalid manifest identity and policy keys
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

APM accepts schema-invalid native inputs at two parser boundaries instead of rejecting them:

1. **Manifest identity (`apm.yml`).** `apm audit --ci` exits `0` for manifests whose required identity fields have the wrong type or are empty:
   - `name: ""` (empty) + `version: 123` (integer, not a version string) -> exit 0
   - `name: [a, b]` (list-valued) + `version: 1.0.0` -> exit 0
   A fully valid manifest also exits 0, so the invalid manifests are silently treated as valid.

2. **Policy (`policy.yml`).** `apm policy status --check` silently ignores an unknown/typo'd top-level key and accepts wrong-typed values with `error: null` and no warning:
   - `enforcment: true` (typo of `enforcement`) is dropped; effective `enforcement` stays `warn` with no diagnostic
   - `cache: []` (wrong type) and `dependencies.allow: ""` (empty string where a list is expected) produce `error: null`, no warning

**To Reproduce**

Baseline SHA: `26d8cee8a4079bb3d31956f1b57d343654835fc8`.

Manifest:
1. In an empty project, write `apm.yml` with `name: ""` and `version: 123`.
2. `apm audit --ci --no-policy -f json` -> **exit 0** (BUG; invalid identity tolerated).
3. Repeat with `name:` as a YAML list -> **exit 0**.
4. Control: `name: valid-pkg` / `version: 1.0.0` -> exit 0.

Policy:
1. Write `policy.yml` with `version: "1.0"`, `enforcment: true`, `cache: []`, `dependencies: { allow: "" }`.
2. `apm policy status --check --policy-source policy.yml --json` -> JSON shows `error: null`, `enforcement: "warn"` (the typo'd key was silently ignored), no warning for the wrong-typed values.

**Expected behavior**

Each native input artifact must be rejected at its parser boundary when required identity fields, known keys, container shapes, or element types violate that artifact's schema. Unknown policy keys should emit the documented warning; wrong-typed/empty identity fields should fail validation with a clear diagnostic.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS
- APM Version: 0.24.1 (`26d8cee8a`)

**Root-cause (architecture)**

Architecture cluster `r2-input-schema-boundary-gaps` (recommendation: isolated fix, not a new universal schema layer). The existing artifact-specific owners are incomplete: `validate_policy` must fully validate the policy's native schema (known keys + value types), and `APMPackage.from_apm_yml` must validate manifest identity types and non-empty values. Tighten each native parser in place; do not invent shared primitive fields or couple validation to a target. If stricter acceptance is breaking, ship a changelog + migration note.

**Additional context**

Authorized first-party reliability/regression validation (red-team Round 2). Independently reproduced twice (finder != confirmer) with valid controls and cleanup verification. Related silent-success theme: #2103 (missing declared plugin components), but a distinct mechanism (schema/type tolerance vs missing path).

issues.title: [BUG] compile --help and unknown-target error omit the accepted `intellij` target (advertised != accepted)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `intellij` target is accepted by `apm compile` (it runs, exits 0, and generates output) but is omitted from that command's own help text and from its unknown-target error listing. So the set of targets APM *advertises* for compile is narrower than the set it *accepts*. `install --help` lists `intellij` (4 mentions); `compile --help` and the compile unknown-target error list it 0 times.

**To Reproduce**

Baseline SHA: `26d8cee8a4079bb3d31956f1b57d343654835fc8`.

1. `apm compile --help` -> count occurrences of `intellij` -> **0**.
2. `apm install --help` -> count occurrences of `intellij` -> 4 (present).
3. `apm compile --target bogus` (invalid) -> error lists valid targets, but the listing **omits** `intellij`.
4. `apm compile --target intellij` in a project with a compilable primitive -> **exit 0**, generates output (e.g. `AGENTS.md`). So the target is real and accepted, just undocumented at this entry point.

**Expected behavior**

The advertised target set (help text + invalid-target error listing) must equal the accepted target set for every command that takes `--target`. If `compile` accepts `intellij`, its help and error listings must include it; conversely a target that is not accepted must not be advertised.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS
- APM Version: 0.24.1 (`26d8cee8a`)

**Root-cause (architecture)**

Architecture cluster `r2-target-capability-catalog-drift` (recommendation: canonical-owner refactor). Target identity is spread across sibling constants/paths (e.g. `src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py`: `VALID_TARGET_VALUES`, `KNOWN_TARGETS`, `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET`, plus per-command help strings). Each command surface reads a different subset, so help/error/acceptance drift apart. Recommended: a single target-capability catalog that every command's acceptance, help rendering, and invalid-target error derive from, so "accepted" and "advertised" cannot diverge. Vendor-neutral, native target names only, no translation layer.

**Additional context**

Authorized first-party reliability/regression validation (red-team Round 2). Independently reproduced twice (finder != confirmer) with control and cleanup verification. Same catalog surface previously touched by #1957/#2041 (intellij validation); this finding is the help/error advertisement gap, distinct from acceptance.

issues.title: [BUG] apm update/compile leave stale deployed_files + artifacts when the target universe contracts (only install reconciles)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a project's target universe contracts (e.g. from `copilot,windsurf` down to `copilot`), `apm update` and `apm compile` both exit `0` but leave the removed target's deployed artifacts and lockfile entries behind. The `.windsurf/rules/ghost.md` file survives and two `windsurf` `deployed_files` entries remain in `apm.lock.yaml`. Only a subsequent `apm install` reconciles the removed target. So `update` and `compile` claim success while leaving the working tree and lockfile inconsistent with the declared target set.

**To Reproduce**

Baseline SHA: `26d8cee8a4079bb3d31956f1b57d343654835fc8`.

1. Project with a primitive and `targets: [copilot, windsurf]`; `apm install` -> `.windsurf/rules/<name>.md` deployed, `windsurf` entries in `apm.lock.yaml` `deployed_files`.
2. Edit config so `targets: [copilot]` only (windsurf removed).
3. `apm update --target copilot` -> **exit 0**, but `.windsurf/rules/<name>.md` still present and windsurf lock entries remain.
4. `apm compile --target copilot` -> **exit 0**, windsurf ghost + lock entries still present.
5. `apm install` -> reconciles (removes the windsurf ghost + lock entries).

**Expected behavior**

Every command that (re)materializes deployment state for a target set (`install`, `update`, `compile`) must reconcile against the previously deployed set recorded in the lockfile and remove artifacts + `deployed_files` entries for targets no longer in scope -- or explicitly document that only `install` reconciles and have `update`/`compile` refuse-or-warn on a contracted target set. Silent exit 0 while leaving ghosts is the failure.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS
- APM Version: 0.24.1 (`26d8cee8a`)

**Root-cause (architecture)**

Architecture cluster `r2-deployment-reconciliation-entrypoint-parity` (recommendation: canonical-owner refactor). The reconcile-removed-deployment logic is reachable only from the `install` path; `update` and `compile` re-emit current-target artifacts without consulting the prior `deployed_files` baseline. Recommended: promote a single deployed-state reconciliation owner (e.g. `src/apm_cli/install/manifest_reconcile.py::ReconcileDeployedState`, backed by `deployed_paths.py`) that all three entry points call after materialization. This is the deployed-files sibling of the lockfile ghost work in #2059/#2114. Vendor-neutral, no schema change.

**Additional context**

Authorized first-party reliability/regression validation (red-team Round 2). Independently reproduced twice (finder != confirmer) with control and cleanup verification.

issues.title: [BUG] Cyclic-dependency rejection leaves un-resumable apm_modules snapshot; corrected source still fails until manual rm -rf
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When `apm install` rejects a cyclic local dependency graph (exit 1), it leaves a partial `apm_modules/` snapshot on disk. After the user fixes the source to break the cycle, `apm install` **still** exits 1 -- because the stale `apm_modules/` snapshot from the failed run is treated as authoritative. The only way to recover is to manually `rm -rf apm_modules`, after which `apm install` succeeds (exit 0, lockfile written). The failed resolution is not transactional: it neither rolls back its staging directory nor treats a corrected source as a reason to rebuild.

**To Reproduce**

Baseline SHA: `26d8cee8a4079bb3d31956f1b57d343654835fc8`.

1. Two local packages A and B where A depends on B and B depends on A (2-node cycle), consumed by the root project.
2. `apm install` -> **exit 1** (cycle correctly rejected), but `apm_modules/` snapshot is left behind.
3. Edit source to break the cycle (e.g. remove B's back-dependency on A).
4. `apm install` -> **still exit 1** (stale `apm_modules/` blocks the corrected resolution).
5. `rm -rf apm_modules` then `apm install` -> exit 0, lockfile created.

**Expected behavior**

A failed dependency resolution must be transactional: either roll back the partial `apm_modules/` staging on failure, or invalidate/rebuild it when the source graph changes, so that fixing the source and re-running `install` recovers without a manual `rm -rf apm_modules`. A rejected install should not leave a snapshot that poisons the next run.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS
- APM Version: 0.24.1 (`26d8cee8a`)

**Root-cause (architecture)**

Architecture cluster `r2-resolution-staging-transactionality` (recommendation: canonical-owner refactor). Resolution writes `apm_modules/` incrementally with no rollback boundary and no source-graph fingerprint to detect staleness. Recommended: a resolution-staging session owner (e.g. `src/apm_cli/install/resolution_staging.py::ResolutionStagingSession`) that stages to a temp location and commits on success / discards on failure, and/or fingerprints the resolved source graph so a changed source forces a rebuild. Vendor-neutral, no primitive-schema change.

**Additional context**

Authorized first-party reliability/regression validation (red-team Round 2). Independently reproduced twice (finder != confirmer) with control (single non-cyclic install succeeds) and cleanup verification.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Non-interactive flags for `apm init` project metadata (name, description, version, author)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`apm init`'s interactive mode collects four metadata fields — name, version,
description, author — but its non-interactive mode can freely set none of them,
so scripted / CI / `--yes` init is stuck with auto-detected boilerplate and must
hand-edit `apm.yml` afterward.

The command
([`init`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/init.py))
declares only these value-bearing options: the `project_name` argument, `--yes`,
`--plugin`, `--marketplace`, `--target`, `--verbose`. There is no
`--description`, `--version`, or `--author`. The two paths diverge on what a user
can control:

- Interactive
  ([`_interactive_project_setup`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/init.py))
  prompts for `name`, `version`, `description`, and `author`. In the current
  directory (no positional arg) it seeds the name prompt with the directory
  basename but lets the user type any name — a custom-named project in-place.
- Non-interactive (`--yes` or non-TTY stdin) takes
  [`_get_default_config`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/_helpers.py),
  which hardcodes `version: "1.0.0"`, `description: f"APM project for {name}"`,
  and `author` from `git config user.name`. No flag feeds `config`, so the field
  the interactive user is most likely to customize — the description — is the one
  a non-interactive user cannot set at all. For name, the positional arg is the
  only input, and `_perform_init` treats it as `mkdir(project_name)` + `chdir`
  into that subdir; a bare `.`/no-arg forces the current dir's basename. Neither
  path names a project in-place.

Current behavior — every metadata field is either rejected as an unknown option
or pinned to boilerplate:

```
$ apm init myproj --yes --description "My cool project"
Error: No such option: --description

$ apm init myproj --yes
$ cat myproj/apm.yml
name: myproj
version: 1.0.0
description: APM project for myproj      # boilerplate, unsettable
author: Jane Dev                         # git user.name, unsettable
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**

`--description`, `--version`, and `--author` flags on `apm init`, so every field
the interactive prompt collects can be set without the prompt:

```
apm init myproj --yes --description "My cool project" --version 0.1.0 --author "Jane Dev"
```

writes those exact values and exits 0. Also a way to name a project in the current
directory non-interactively (e.g. a `--name` flag decoupled from the positional
arg's mkdir behavior), matching what interactive init already allows in-place.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Run `apm init` interactively, then re-run non-interactively — not viable in CI.
- Hand-edit or `sed` the generated `apm.yml` after `apm init --yes` — works but
  defeats the point of a scaffolding command and is brittle.

There is precedent in the CLI's own scaffolding surface: sibling
[`apm marketplace init`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/marketplace/init.py)
already takes `--name` and `--owner`, so "set metadata without the prompt" is an
established mode — just not on `apm init`.

**Additional context**

Observed on `apm` v0.24.0 (Linux, Python 3.14). The gap is visible from the
`apm init` flag surface alone (`apm init --help` lists no metadata flags) and the
two code paths cited above — no reproduction directory needed.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm init --target` writes a `targets:` value that `apm install` then rejects
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm init --target <list>` persists the `--target` flag's *parsed* value straight
into `apm.yml`'s `targets:` field. But the flag parser and the manifest validator
do not share a target vocabulary, so `init` can write a token that `install` then
refuses to read back — a project that is broken the moment it is scaffolded. Two
tokens leak:

- `vscode` — from alias resolution of `copilot`/`agents`/`vscode` in any
  **multi-token** `--target` (`--target claude,copilot` → `targets: [claude, vscode]`).
- `agents` — passed through verbatim from a **single-token** `--target agents`,
  a CLI-accepted (and deprecated) alias that is not manifest-canonical.

Consequence: the scaffolded `apm.yml` cannot be installed. `apm install` aborts
with `Unknown target 'vscode'` (exit 2) and the user must hand-edit a manifest
they never wrote by hand. The manifest `init` writes even advertises the bad
tokens — its header comment reads `Accepted values: vscode, agents, copilot, ...`,
though `vscode` and `agents` are exactly the two values `parse_targets_field()`
rejects.

**Root cause: target vocabulary is fragmented across the codebase**

The `init` leak is a symptom of a deeper problem: the CLI carries several
different notions of a "canonical" target, with no single source of truth.

Two disjoint canonical sets disagree on the copilot/vscode family's canonical
spelling:

- [`ALL_CANONICAL_TARGETS`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py)
  (`core/target_detection.py`) — canonical is `vscode`.
- [`CANONICAL_TARGETS`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/apm_yml.py)
  (`core/apm_yml.py`, the manifest validator) — canonical is `copilot`; `vscode`
  is not in it.

Three-plus alias maps, some inverting each other:

- `TARGET_ALIASES` (`target_detection.py`): `copilot`/`agents`/`vscode` → `vscode`.
- `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET` (`integration/targets.py`):
  `vscode`/`agents`/`intellij` → `copilot` — the **opposite** direction.
- `_VSCODE_TARGET_ALIASES` (`compilation/agents_compiler.py`): `("copilot",
  "agents")`, applied inline.
- `_CROSS_TARGET_MAPS` (`bundle/lockfile_enrichment.py`).

Plus roughly a dozen hand-rolled checks that re-derive the same mapping in situ —
`if target == "vscode"`, `"vscode" if target in ("copilot", "agents") else
target`, `"vscode" in target` — spread across `compile/cli.py`,
`mcp_integrator.py`, `hook_integrator.py`, `registry/operations.py`, and
`lockfile_enrichment.py`.

[`parse_target_field()`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/target_detection.py)
resolves aliases only for multi-token input (a documented CLI-contract
asymmetry). In-memory consumers tolerate the unresolved token;
[`init`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/commands/init.py)
is the one path that writes it to disk, where `parse_targets_field()` validates
against the *other* canonical set and aborts.

**Recommended fix**

Point-patching `init` (resolve to a manifest-canonical token before writing)
closes this repro but leaves the fragmentation that produced it. The durable fix
is a single source of truth: one canonical target set, one alias→canonical
resolver, one direction of canonicalization — with `init`, `install`, and
`compile` all routing target values through it. That also subsumes the
consumption-side bugs (#1746, #820) noted below, which are the same fragmentation
surfacing on the read side.

**To Reproduce**

1. In an empty directory containing one primitive (e.g.
   `.apm/instructions/demo.instructions.md`, so `install` gets far enough to
   validate `targets:`), run `apm init --target claude,copilot --yes`. The flag
   is echoed already renamed:

```
[i] Targets set: claude, vscode (via --target flag)
```

2. Inspect the generated `apm.yml` — `copilot` was written as `vscode`:

```yaml
targets:
- claude
- vscode
```

3. Run `apm install` — it rejects its own scaffold, exit 2:

```
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[x] Unknown target 'vscode'

Valid targets: antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, kiro,
opencode, windsurf
[!] Install interrupted after 7.0s.
```

4. Same failure via the single-token alias path: `apm init --target agents --yes`
   writes `targets: [agents]`, and `apm install` aborts with `Unknown target
   'agents'` (exit 2).

5. Control: `apm init --target copilot --yes` writes `targets: [copilot]` and
   `apm install` succeeds. The same token survives alone and is renamed in a list.

**Expected behavior**

`apm init --target <list>` writes exactly the targets the user asked for, and the
resulting `apm.yml` installs. `--target claude,copilot` yields
`targets: [claude, copilot]`, and `apm install` exits 0. Any `--target` value the
CLI accepts must produce a manifest the CLI accepts — or be rejected up front by
`apm init` rather than at the next command.

**Environment**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.14
 - APM Version: 0.24.0

**Logs**

See the captured `apm init` and `apm install` output above.

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs
(`init-target-alias-leak/` — `make control`, `make multi`, `make agents`).

#1746 (`--target claude,copilot` silently drops Copilot from the deploy) and #820
(mixed `target: opencode,claude,copilot,agents` deploys nothing) are the same
vocabulary fragmentation surfacing on the *consumption* side — the alias-resolved
value is mishandled after parsing, so it fails silently. This issue is the
*production* side: `init` persists a CLI-vocabulary token into a manifest
validated against a narrower vocabulary, so it fails loud (`Unknown target`, exit
2). A unified target vocabulary would remove the root cause of all three.

issues.title: [BUG] Uninstalling the last-writer of a shared deployed file drops lockfile ownership from the surviving package (content-integrity coverage silently lost until reinstall)
issues.body:
## Summary
When two installed packages deploy the *same* file (a shared deployed path, e.g. an identical `*.instructions.md`), APM assigns lockfile ownership of that path to a single "last-writer" package. Uninstalling that last-writer correctly leaves the file on disk (a surviving package still provides it) and re-integrates the surviving package -- but it never transfers the `deployed_files` / `deployed_file_hashes` ownership rows to the surviving package. The shared file becomes lockfile-orphaned: present on disk, but no lockfile entry claims it, so `content-integrity` (and `apm audit --ci --no-drift`) stops verifying it until the next `apm install` restores ownership.

## Impact
- After a routine uninstall, a still-required shared file silently drops out of content-integrity coverage. Under `apm audit --ci --no-drift` (the documented reduced-coverage CI mode), tampering with that file is no longer detected (exit 0) where the unique-path control correctly detects it (exit 1).
- Self-heals on the next `apm install`, so this is a bookkeeping / coverage gap rather than data loss.

## Reproduction (Round 3 reliability sweep; finder + independent confirmer both reproduced)
1. Create two local packages A and B that each contain an identical `shared.instructions.md`.
2. `apm install` (root depends on both), then `apm update` and `apm compile`.
3. `apm uninstall <B>` (the last-writer owner of the shared path).
4. Observe: A and the integrated file remain on disk, but A has no `deployed_files` row for the shared path.
5. Tamper with the shared file; `apm audit --ci --no-drift` exits `0` (a distinct-paths control exits `1`).
6. `apm install` restores ownership; audit again detects tampering.

## Root cause (canonical-owner gap)
`apm install` has a last-writer reconciler that assigns shared-path ownership; `apm uninstall` has no counterpart. In `src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/cli.py` the removal set `all_deployed_files` is computed solely from the *removed* packages' `deployed_files`, the lockfile update only deletes removed keys, and nothing re-assigns a surviving co-owner's ownership of a shared path. The "who owns this deployed path" fact is written by one entry path (install) and never reconciled by its sibling (uninstall).

## Expected
After uninstalling a shared path's last-writer, ownership (`deployed_files` + `deployed_file_hashes`) should transfer to a surviving package that still provides that path, keeping content-integrity coverage intact without requiring a reinstall.

## Strategy compliance
Native Copilot instruction Markdown throughout; the fix is lockfile bookkeeping (ownership handoff), not harness translation. Vendor-neutral.

issues.title: [BUG] Contracting the target set leaves APM-managed MCP servers stranded in the removed harness's native config
issues.body:
## Summary
When the active target set is contracted (a target that previously received MCP configuration is dropped and the project is recompiled/reinstalled), APM's MCP cleanup only visits the *currently active* targets and removes servers by identity (`stale_names`). The dropped target's native MCP config is never revisited, so APM-managed MCP server entries previously written there (in `.mcp.json` / `config.toml` / the Claude config, etc.) remain behind.

## Impact
- Removed Codex / Kiro / Windsurf (and other) targets retain APM-managed MCP entries after they are dropped from the active set; the harness keeps advertising MCP servers APM no longer manages for it.
- Native schemas are otherwise intact (JSON/TOML and Codex literal path keys are preserved) -- this is a cleanup / lifecycle gap, not a schema-format defect.

## Reproduction (Round 3 reliability sweep; finder + independent confirmer both reproduced)
1. Install a package that contributes an MCP server across a broad target set.
2. Contract to a single target (e.g. `copilot`) and reinstall twice.
3. Add `claude`, then replace it with `cursor`.
4. Observe the MCP server still present in the removed targets' native configs.
Control: removing the MCP *dependency* while the broad target set is still active cleans all entries correctly.

## Root cause (canonical-owner gap)
The MCP write path deploys to whatever targets are active at write time, but the cleanup path (`src/apm_cli/integration/mcp_integrator.py`: `_clean_json_mcp_config` / `_clean_toml_mcp_config` / `_clean_claude_config`) only iterates active targets and diffs *server identity*. There is no per-target deployment provenance recording "APM wrote server X into target Y", so when Y leaves the active set it is never revisited to purge X. Two sibling paths (write vs cleanup) act on the same fact (which targets carry an APM-managed server) without a shared owner.

## Expected
Dropping a target from the active set should purge the APM-managed MCP entries APM previously wrote into that target's native config (or the cleanup pass should consult per-target provenance rather than only the currently active targets).

## Strategy compliance
No schema translation required -- each harness's native MCP format is read/written as-is; this is lifecycle cleanup of entries APM itself owns. Vendor-neutral.

issues.title: [BUG] Semver install/update drops the ADO bearer auth scheme (uses Basic auth), so Entra-authenticated Azure DevOps dependencies fail to resolve
issues.body:
## Summary
`RefResolver` supports an `auth_scheme` (`"basic"` | `"bearer"`) so Azure DevOps dependencies authenticated with an Entra / OAuth bearer token send it via `http.extraheader` instead of embedding a Basic credential in the URL (added in PR #2121). The marketplace/builder resolution path threads it through (`RefResolver(..., auth_scheme=auth.auth_scheme)`), but the run-scoped semver resolver used by `apm install` / `apm update` does not: `src/apm_cli/install/helpers/ref_reuse.py` extracts only `auth_ctx.token` (dropping the scheme) and constructs `RefResolver(host=host, token=token)`, defaulting to `"basic"`. The per-instance `git ls-remote` tag listing for a semver-ranged ADO dependency therefore uses Basic auth and fails before clone; re-running install/update repeats the failure identically.

## Impact
- A semver-ranged Azure DevOps dependency authenticated with a bearer token cannot be resolved by `apm install` / `apm update` (fails at tag listing with a Basic-auth failure), even though the equivalent clone / marketplace path resolves correctly.
- Deterministic; clean re-runs (resume) reproduce the same failure.

## Reproduction (Round 3 reliability sweep; finder + independent confirmer both reproduced; all subprocess I/O mocked, dummy tokens only, no real hosts)
1. Configure a GitHub semver dependency followed by an ADO semver dependency using a bearer (Entra / Azure-CLI-style) auth provider with a dummy token.
2. Resolve: GitHub succeeds; the ADO `git ls-remote` uses Basic authentication and fails.
3. Repeat with a fresh HOME -- identical failure.
4. Controls: the ADO HTTPS clone path and a direct `RefResolver(auth_scheme="bearer")` both correctly use Bearer; tokens never cross hosts.

109 relevant existing tests pass at baseline.

## Root cause (canonical-owner gap)
`AuthResolver` owns the complete `AuthContext` (token + `auth_scheme`), and `install/pipeline.py` / `install/validation.py` thread `auth_scheme` through for the clone path. The semver tag-listing sibling (`install/helpers/ref_reuse.py` -> `resolve_dep_token` / `get_or_create_resolver`) consumes the same `AuthContext` but forwards only the token, dropping `auth_scheme`. `src/apm_cli/marketplace/version_resolver.py:83` constructs `RefResolver(host=host, token=token)` with the same omission and likely shares the gap.

## Expected
The semver resolver path should preserve the resolved `AuthContext.auth_scheme` end-to-end, so an ADO bearer dependency lists tags with Bearer auth exactly as the clone / marketplace path does.

## Suggested fix direction
Thread `auth_scheme` through `resolve_dep_token` (return the `AuthContext`, or a `(token, auth_scheme)` pair) and `get_or_create_resolver` into the `RefResolver(...)` constructor, keying the run-scoped resolver cache on `(host, token_fingerprint, auth_scheme)`. Audit `marketplace/version_resolver.py:83` for the same omission.

## Strategy compliance
No harness / registry translation -- the fix only preserves existing `AuthContext` metadata APM already computes. Vendor-neutral; honors the auth-protocol boundary.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm audit` reports false drift on a dependency's skill files right after install
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When an installed package ships a skill whose bundle contains an in-package
relative markdown link (a link to a sibling file that lives elsewhere in the
package, e.g. ``[pkg](../../README.md)``), `apm audit --ci` reports the deployed
skill file as `modified` immediately after a clean `apm install`, and exits
non-zero. Re-running `apm install` does not clear it.

On install, the skill integrator rewrites in-package asset links so the deployed
copy still resolves. `_resolve_in_package_asset_link`
([`compilation/link_resolver.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/compilation/link_resolver.py))
computes the relative path from the deployed skill dir to the linked file's
post-install location under `apm_modules/`. For a package installed at
`apm_modules/_local/package/`, install writes:

```
../../../apm_modules/_local/package/README.md
```

The audit-replay ([`install/drift.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/install/drift.py))
re-integrates from the lockfile into a scratch dir, calling
`integrate_package_primitives(package_info, scratch_root, ...)` so the link
resolver's `base_dir` is the scratch tmpdir, while the dependency's contents are
materialized at their real path (`_materialize_install_path` returns the real
`apm_modules/<...>` for remote deps, and the on-disk source dir for local deps).
The linked file therefore lies **outside** `base_dir`, which trips the
"replay-frame translation" branch added for #1182
([`link_resolver.py` L518–537](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/compilation/link_resolver.py#L518-L537)):

```python
target_rel = ctx.target_location.relative_to(ctx.base_dir)  # .claude/skills/demo
relpath_anchor = ctx.package_root / target_rel              # <pkg>/.claude/skills/demo
relative_path = os.path.relpath(candidate, relpath_anchor)  # ../../../README.md
```

Re-anchoring onto `package_root` is only correct for the **self-package**, where
`package_root` equals the project root — dropping to a package-relative path then
equals the install-time deploy-relative path. For **any dependency**,
`package_root` is `apm_modules/<owner>/<repo>/` (or `apm_modules/_local/<name>/`),
nested under the project, so the re-anchor strips the whole
`apm_modules/.../` segment that a real install keeps. The replay produces
`../../../README.md` while disk holds `../../../apm_modules/_local/package/README.md`;
they differ byte-for-byte and every dependency skill file carrying an in-package
link is reported as drift. The #1182 fix closed this class of false drift for the
self-package only; it is still open for installed dependencies.

**To Reproduce**
1. `cd drift-dep-skill-links`
2. `make audit` — cleans, `apm install`, then `apm audit --ci`.
3. See `modified` drift on the just-installed skill files; exit non-zero.

```
cd drift-dep-skill-links && apm install && apm audit --ci
```

**Expected behavior**

A skill file just written by `apm install` is not reported as drifted by the
next `apm audit`. A clean install followed by an audit exits 0 with no drift.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.24.1

**Logs**

`apm audit --ci` right after a clean install:

```
  drift details:
    - modified: .claude/skills/demo/README.md
    - modified: .claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md

[x] 1 of 9 check(s) failed

[!] Drift detected: 2 file(s)

  modified (2):
    - .claude/skills/demo/README.md  [./package]
    - .claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md  [./package]

  [i] Run 'apm install' to re-sync deployed files with the lockfile.
```

The only difference on each flagged file is the rewritten link (deployed on disk
vs what the audit-replay recomputes):

```diff
-- [package README](../../../apm_modules/_local/package/README.md) — package overview
+- [package README](../../../README.md) — package overview
```

**Additional context**

Same root cause reproduces with a remote dependency (e.g. installing
`juliusbrussee/caveman`, which ships seven skills whose READMEs link to sibling
`agents/` files and the package README): six of them drift after a clean
install, the seventh — the one skill with no in-package relative link — does not.

Directly follows up #1182 ("audit-replay rewrites in-package asset links against
scratch dir, producing false drift"), whose fix handled only the self-package
frame. Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs
(`make audit` in `drift-dep-skill-links/`).

issues.title: Add ADO stale-PAT 401-to-bearer retry fallback in ref resolution
issues.body:
When a stale `ADO_APM_PAT` is present alongside a valid Azure CLI bearer credential, ref resolution (`install/phases/resolve.py`, `marketplace/version_resolver.py`) does not retry with bearer after the PAT is rejected. #2150 correctly preserved the bearer *scheme*; this is the separate, pre-existing *retry-fallback* capability. Add a tested path that falls back from a rejected stale PAT to bearer without weakening scheme preservation.

---
Surfaced by the advisory review panel on #2155 and deferred as out-of-scope for that consolidation PR. Filed for tracking by the reliability campaign.

issues.title: Define canonical hook provenance without _apm_source translation metadata
issues.body:
APM-managed native hook entries carry an invented `_apm_source` marker (pre-existing on main; moved verbatim in #2155 to shed a file-length limit). Per PRINCIPLES P1 (no invented apm-* fields downstream consumers must honor), review native hook format ownership and replace the translation-style provenance marker with a vendor-neutral ownership model (e.g. ledger/sidecar).

---
Surfaced by the advisory review panel on #2155 and deferred as out-of-scope for that consolidation PR. Filed for tracking by the reliability campaign.

issues.title: Adopt legacy lockfiles predating mcp_target_servers on upgrade
issues.body:
Lockfiles created before `mcp_target_servers` ownership state existed never adopt already-configured MCP servers, so later target contraction cannot remove those APM-managed entries. Add a forward migration/adoption path that records legacy-managed servers only when runtime config exactly matches the stored baseline, with an upgrade-and-contract regression test.

issues.title: Benchmark and optimize deployment ledger mutation paths at scale
issues.body:
The additive dual-write deployment ledger adds measurable lockfile CPU/memory at large installs (~100 packages / 5000 files), plus two avoidable quadratic paths (manifest_reconcile current-set rebuild; uninstall per-path ledger scan). Correctness holds. Measure real large-package workloads, evaluate a sparse-overlay write, and hoist the quadratic scans.

issues.title: Make uninstall deployment-state persistence atomic
issues.body:
Uninstall persists dependency removal before ledger reconciliation, so an interruption can leave the lockfile internally inconsistent (records owned by a deleted dependency). Reconcile dependency removal, survivor handoff, hashes, and ledger in memory, then perform one durable lockfile write. No demonstrated regression today; this hardens the failure window.

Pre-existing debt. Move these through logger methods, adding a logger-owned error-detail method if needed.
