issues.title: Subpath guard false-positives on a GitLab subgroup legitimately named `collections`
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm pack` rejects a perfectly valid GitLab repository URL because one of the
**subgroup** names happens to match a reserved APM primitive directory name.

Our GitLab group is literally named `collections` (it holds our asset
collections). Every repo inside it is now unusable as an APM dependency:

```
https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git
```

```
Invalid APM dependency
'https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git':
A subpath cannot be embedded in a git URL.
Got: `https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git`.
Use the `path:` key instead: `git: <repo-url>` + `path: <primitive>/<name>`
(or the shorthand `org/repo/<primitive>/<name>`).
```

Here `core` **is** the repository and `collections` **is** a real GitLab
subgroup. There is no embedded subpath.

## Reproduction

`apm.yml`:

```yaml
name: probe
version: 1.0.0
description: probe
author: probe
dependencies:
  apm:
    - https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git
marketplace:
  owner:
    name: probe
    url: https://example.com
  packages: []
```

`apm pack` -> exit 1.

## Observed behaviour matrix

| URL | Result | Correct? |
|---|---|---|
| `host/ai/collections/core.git` | REJECTED | NO - false positive |
| `host/ai/collections/core` | REJECTED | NO - false positive |
| `host/collections/core.git` (primitive at index 1) | accepted | yes |
| `host/org/repo/skills/my-skill` | REJECTED | yes - genuine |
| `host/ai/collection/core.git` (singular) | accepted | yes |

## Root cause

`src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py`, `_check_no_embedded_subpath`
(~L735):

```python
for idx, seg in enumerate(segments[:-1]):
    if idx >= 2 and seg in DependencyReference._APM_PRIMITIVE_DIRS:
        raise ValueError("A subpath cannot be embedded in a git URL. ...")
```

`_APM_PRIMITIVE_DIRS` (~L195) contains `collections`.

The `idx >= 2` scoping already acknowledges this exact false-positive class.
Its comment says it exists so as not to trip on "a subgroup literally named
after a primitive at index 1 (`group/skills/repo`)".

That reasoning is right, but the threshold assumes the repo prefix is exactly
`org/repo` - a GitHub assumption. **GitLab supports arbitrarily deep subgroup
nesting**, so a subgroup named after a primitive can legitimately appear at any
index, not just index 1. Any GitLab user with 2+ levels of nesting and a
subgroup named `collections`, `agents`, `prompts`, `instructions`, `contexts`,
or `memory` hits this.

Note `_GITLAB_VIRTUAL_ROOT_SEGMENTS` (L190, used L1106) also contains
`collections`, so this name is doubly special-cased on the GitLab path.

## Why there is no workaround

The guard runs in `_parse_dependency_string` **before** any form-specific
branching, so the object form is rejected identically:

```yaml
- git: https://<gitlab>/ai/collections/core.git
```

Same error. The error text advises `git:` + `path:`, but there is no subpath to
move into `path:` - the URL is already just a repo URL. No spelling of the URL
avoids the guard. The only workaround is renaming the GitLab group, which for
an org-wide group means breaking every existing consumer.

## Suggested fix

The URL already carries an unambiguous signal that it is a complete repository
URL: the **`.git` suffix**. `_check_no_embedded_subpath` strips it and then
discards that information:

```python
if path_part.endswith(".git"):
    path_part = path_part[:-4]
```

A URL ending in `.git` terminates at the repository, so it cannot contain an
embedded subpath. Skipping the guard when the original URL ended in `.git`
would fix this class of false positive without weakening genuine detection -
users writing the malformed `org/repo/skills/name` shorthand do not append
`.git`. This mirrors the existing `_git` escape hatch already used for Azure
DevOps (~L723).

Failing that, an explicit opt-out (e.g. a manifest flag, or honouring the
absence of `path:` as intent) would unblock affected GitLab orgs.

## Environment

- apm-cli 0.26.0 (also reproduced on 0.28.0 in CI, `python:3.12` image)
- GitLab self-managed, group nesting depth 4

issues.title: [BUG] Clone failures on github.com are reported as "network error, not an auth failure" — git stderr is dropped when wrapping CalledProcessError
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`GitCache._create_bare` wraps a failed `git clone` in a `RuntimeError` using f-string interpolation of the exception:

```python
# src/apm_cli/cache/git_cache.py:436
raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to clone {_sanitize_url(url)}: {exc}") from exc
```

`CalledProcessError.__str__` renders only `Command '[...]' returned non-zero exit status 128` — it does not include `stderr`. The underlying git diagnostic is therefore lost at this boundary.

That matters because `AuthResolver.is_public_github_auth_failure()` classifies failures by **string-matching the exception text** for markers like `authentication failed` and `could not read username`. Once `stderr` is gone, the match fails, `public_github_non_auth_failure` is set, and `build_clone_failure_message` emits:

```
Could not connect to github.com (network error, not an auth failure).
Check your internet connection and proxy settings.
```

So a plain authentication failure is reported to the user as a network/proxy problem. The real cause is only visible with `APM_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`.

The same pattern is at line 426 (`partial fallback also failed`), so both wrapping sites are affected.

**To Reproduce**

The classifier inversion can be shown directly, no private repo or credentials needed:

```python
import subprocess
from apm_cli.core.auth import AuthResolver

try:
    subprocess.run(
        ['git', 'clone', '--bare',
         'https://github.com/octocat/private-placeholder-xyz.git', '/tmp/repro_bare'],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
        env={'PATH': '/usr/bin:/bin', 'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT': '0',
             'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM': '1', 'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL': '/dev/null'})
except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
    print(AuthResolver.is_public_github_auth_failure(exc))                        # True
    wrapped = RuntimeError(f'Failed to clone URL: {exc}')  # git_cache.py:436
    print(AuthResolver.is_public_github_auth_failure(wrapped))                    # False
```

Output:

```
git stderr: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
classifier on original exception : True
classifier on wrapped RuntimeError: False
```

**Expected behavior**

`stderr` should survive the wrap, so `is_public_github_auth_failure()` still classifies correctly and the user is told authentication failed rather than being sent to debug their network and proxy settings.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS 26.5.2
 - Python Version: 3.12.7
 - APM Version: 0.28.0 (also present on `main` @ `3aa0365`)
 - git: 2.49.0

**Logs**

With `APM_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`, the real diagnostic is present:

```
remote: Invalid username or token. [REDACTED] is not supported for Git operations.
fatal: Authentication failed for 'https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git/'
```

Without it, the user only sees the "network error, not an auth failure" message quoted above.

**Additional context**

Found while installing a subdirectory package from a **private** repo over HTTPS. The message sent me looking at network and proxy configuration for a while; `git clone` by hand appeared to succeed, which reinforced the wrong hypothesis — my manual clone was being served by the `osxkeychain` credential helper, which APM deliberately disables (`credential.helper=""`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`). Reproducing APM's isolated env made the real auth failure visible.

I'm happy to open a PR: pass `exc.stderr` into the wrapped message at both sites, plus a unit test asserting `is_public_github_auth_failure()` stays `True` across the wrap. `cache/` is outside `critical_paths.txt`, so no spec ritual should be needed.

That investigation also surfaced what looks like a **separate** bug: for a private repo, the root package installs fine but a subdirectory package fails, because the shared bare-cache clone runs without credentials. I'll file that separately once I've located the exact line — mentioning it here only so the two aren't conflated.

issues.title: [BUG] --skill matches nothing on subdirectory plugin refs: 'Available: (none)'
issues.body:
Subsetting skills works for repo-root plugin packages but fails for subdirectory plugin refs — the skill enumeration comes back empty, so any `--skill` value is rejected.

Repro:

```
apm install dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced --skill csharp-scripts
```

Output:

```
[x] 1 package failed:
  +- dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced -- --skill matched no declared skills in
'dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced'. Requested: csharp-scripts. Available: (none).
[x] Installation failed with 1 error(s). No install transaction changes were committed.
```

The skill definitely exists: a bare `apm install dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced` deploys `csharp-scripts` (plus `dotnet-pinvoke` and `nuget-trusted-publishing`) fine — it's the subset matching that can't see any skills. The package resolves as `package_type: marketplace_plugin` with a virtual subdirectory path.

For comparison, `apm install DuendeSoftware/duende-skills --skill ...` (a repo-root plugin) subsets correctly, so this looks specific to the subdirectory-ref intake path not feeding the enumerator that `--skill` validates against.

Expected: `--skill` filters subdirectory plugin refs the same way it does repo-root packages, persisting the `skills:` subset in apm.yml.

apm 0.27.0 on Windows 11.

*Disclosure: drafted with AI assistance; the behavior was reproduced and verified manually.*

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-08-08 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-08

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
3 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [E] Heavy Top-Level Import -- src/apm_cli/commands/update.py:62

- Current: `from git.exc import GitCommandError` at module top level; GitPython
  (a large library with many transitive imports) is loaded unconditionally
  whenever the commands package is imported, adding startup latency for every
  sub-command invocation regardless of whether `update` is being run.
- Proposed: Defer to a local import inside the one function that uses it
  (O(1) import cost paid only when `update` actually executes).
- Fix: Move `from git.exc import GitCommandError` inside the `except` clause
  or the enclosing try-block in the function body at line 176.

#### [C] Module Import Inside Innermost Loop -- src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py:1460

- Current: `import json as _json` appears inside the body of
  `for raw_event_name, entries in hooks.items()` (line 1362), which is itself
  inside `for hook_file in hook_files` (line 1333); the import lookup executes
  on every (hook_file, event) pair even though Python caches the module.
- Proposed: Hoist the import once to the enclosing function scope or module level.
- Fix: Move `import json as _json` (or replace with the already-imported `json`
  alias used elsewhere in the file) to the top of the enclosing method so the
  lookup cost is paid exactly once.

#### [C] json.dumps Dedup Key Inside Triple-Nested Loop -- src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py:1468-1470

- Current: For each (hook_file x event x entry) triple, the code builds a
  sorted-items dict and calls `json.dumps({"s": source, "c": cmp}, sort_keys=True)`
  to produce a dedup key; this allocates a full JSON string per entry -- O(entry_size)
  string work repeated for every entry in every event across every hook file.
- Proposed: Replace string serialization with a hashable tuple key built from
  sorted items, eliminating the string allocation overhead; same O(n) pass,
  lower constant factor.
- Fix: Replace the `json.dumps` dedup key with
  `(source, tuple(sorted(cmp.items())))` -- Python can hash tuples of primitives
  natively, removing the JSON encode step entirely.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (430 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [BUG] Localised git stderr breaks auth-failure classification, suppressing the token retry
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`AuthResolver.is_public_github_auth_failure` classifies a failed clone by matching English signal strings against git's stderr (`"authentication failed"`, `"could not read username"`, `"repository not found"`, ...). Git localises those diagnostics through gettext, and APM does not pin a locale for the git subprocesses it spawns itself.

On a machine whose locale is not English, git writes its authentication failure in the user's language. The classifier does not recognise it, and the consequence is not cosmetic: the verdict gates the **token retry** in `try_with_fallback` (`src/apm_cli/core/auth.py:797-802`).

```python
if (
    lazy_public_github
    and path is not None
    and not self.is_public_github_auth_failure(exc)
):
    raise
ctx = _auth_context()
if ctx.token:
    _log(f"Unauthenticated failed, retrying with token (source: {ctx.source})")
```

Since `uses_public_github_anonymous_first` makes every github.com access start anonymously, a misclassified failure means the token is **never tried**. Installing a private-repo dependency fails, and the user is pointed at the wrong cause:

```
Could not connect to github.com (network error, not an auth failure).
Check your internet connection and proxy settings.
```

while git actually said "authentication failed".

Two things make this hard to spot:

- Clones issued through GitPython are unaffected, because GitPython forces `LANGUAGE=C`/`LC_ALL=C` on every command it runs (`git/cmd.py`). Only APM's own `subprocess` calls inherit the ambient locale — and that is the path the shared bare cache uses.
- Git ships message catalogues for 19 languages today. A user whose language has no catalogue (e.g. `ja`) sees English and is unaffected — until that translation is added.

**To Reproduce**

1. Set a locale for which git ships a catalogue: `export LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8` (`de_DE.UTF-8` behaves identically).
2. Have a token available through `gh auth login`, but not exported in the environment, so it has to come from the retry path.
3. Use a cold cache: `export APM_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d)`.
4. `apm install <org>/<private-repo>/<subdir>` — a subdirectory package, which is the case that routes through the shared bare-cache clone.

Same command, same token, same repository; only the locale changes:

| `LC_ALL` | Result |
|---|---|
| `fr_FR.UTF-8` | fails — "network error, not an auth failure" |
| `de_DE.UTF-8` | fails — same |
| `C` | installs successfully |

`LC_ALL=C apm install ...` alone makes the install succeed with no code change, which isolates the locale as the cause.

The exception captured on the failing path (values redacted):

```
CalledProcessError: Command '[... 'clone', '--bare', 'https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git', ...]'
  returned non-zero exit status 128.
  stderr: "remote: Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported
           for Git operations.
           fatal : Échec d'authentification pour 'https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git/'"
```

`is_public_github_auth_failure` returns `False` for it, so `try_with_fallback` re-raises without trying the token. Instrumenting the same run under `LC_ALL=C` yields the untranslated `fatal: Authentication failed`, a `True` verdict, and a successful token retry.

**Expected behavior**

Classification of an authentication failure should not depend on the user's locale. A private-repo dependency should install regardless of the language configured on the machine, and a genuine auth failure should be reported as such instead of as a network/proxy problem.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS (`darwin`); reproducible on any non-English locale
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.28.0 (also on `main` @ `3aa0365`)
 - git: 2.51.0, shipping catalogues for 19 languages under `share/locale/`

**Additional context**

How this surfaced: a shared agent rule hosted in a subdirectory of a private repository. The repository root installed fine, the subdirectory package did not — the subdirectory is what routes through the shared bare cache, whose `subprocess` calls carry the ambient locale. The subdirectory is the trigger, not the cause. The error message sent me looking at proxy and connectivity settings for what was a credential-resolution problem.

I have a fix and will open a PR referencing this issue: normalise the message locale in `AuthResolver._build_git_env`, the single builder every git env in the auth path routes through. Widening the classifier's vocabulary with translated strings looks like the wrong direction — the catalogues change between git versions and cover a moving set of languages.

issues.title: [BUG] Plugin root skills/ overrides the plugin.json declaration: undeclared skills deploy, declared ones drop
issues.body:
A plugin's raw root `skills/` directory overrides its resolved `plugin.json` declaration, so the set APM deploys can differ from the set the manifest declares — in both directions.

Found while working on #2530; it is a distinct defect and is deliberately not fixed in #2536.

## Behavior

`_map_plugin_artifacts` resolves the manifest into `.apm/skills/`, where a declared `skills` array replaces default discovery rather than adding to it. Deployment does not read that result: it prefers a root `skills/` bundle whenever one holds at least one skill.

Three plugins, all with `skills/{a,b}` at the root:

| `plugin.json` `skills` | resolved into `.apm/skills` | actually deployed / selectable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `["./skills/a"]` | `a` | `a`, `b` — undeclared `b` leaks in |
| `["./skills/", "./extra/solo"]` | `a`, `b`, `solo` | `a`, `b` — declared `solo` dropped |
| `["./skills/a", "./skills/b"]` | `a`, `b` | `a`, `b` — agrees |

The first row is the more likely one in practice: a plugin that ships several skills but declares only the ones it wants published still gets all of them deployed, with no diagnostic.

## Reproduction

```
mkdir -p plug/.claude-plugin plug/skills/a plug/skills/b
printf '# a\n' > plug/skills/a/SKILL.md
printf '# b\n' > plug/skills/b/SKILL.md
printf '{"name":"p","version":"1.0.0","skills":["./skills/a"]}' > plug/.claude-plugin/plugin.json

mkdir -p consumer/.claude
printf 'name: c\nversion: 1.0.0\ntargets: [claude]\ndependencies:\n  apm:\n    - path: ../plug\n' > consumer/apm.yml
cd consumer && apm install
ls .claude/skills          # a and b; only a was declared
```

`apm install --skill b` is likewise accepted, because `available_skill_names` enumerates the same raw directory.

## The open question

Does declaring `skills:` in `plugin.json` opt out of default `skills/` discovery?

Normalization already answers yes — `_resolve_sources` uses the manifest value *instead of* the default. Deployment answers no. That internal disagreement is the bug; which answer is correct is a product decision.

If "declared paths are requirements" (per the Plugin collection section of the package-types reference) means the declared set is exhaustive, the fix is to let the resolved `.apm/skills/` win for `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` in `SkillIntegrator.skill_source_dir`. That would also make `"skills": []` mean "no skills" as documented, and would fail closed when a declared path is rejected for escaping the plugin root.

It is worth noting this changes what existing consumers receive: any plugin declaring a partial list would start deploying fewer skills. That is why it is filed rather than bundled into #2536.

## Notes

- `#2536` makes enumeration and deployment agree with each other, so `--skill` no longer reports a set that differs from what deploys. It does not change which of the two sources wins.
- Neither `dotnet/skills/plugins/dotnet-advanced` (declares the whole container) nor `DuendeSoftware/duende-skills` (declares all 24 individually) triggers this.
- Environment: reproduced against `main` at 3aa036554 on Windows 11.

issues.title: [BUG] Frozen Artifactory installs treat resolved commit SHAs as branch or tag names
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When installing a Git dependency through a JFrog Artifactory remote repository, an initial installation by tag succeeds and records the resolved commit SHA in `apm.lock.yaml`.

A subsequent cold installation with `apm install --frozen` uses that locked SHA for reproducibility, but APM constructs only branch- and tag-shaped archive URLs. Artifactory exposes the commit archive through the generic GitHub commit archive path, which APM never attempts.

This causes reproducible frozen installations to fail with HTTP 404 even though the requested commit is available through the configured Artifactory repository.


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Configure an Artifactory remote repository that proxies github.com.

Configure APM to use the proxy exclusively:
```bash
export PROXY_REGISTRY_URL="https://artifactory.example.com/artifactory/github-proxy"
export PROXY_REGISTRY_ONLY=1
```

Declare a dependency using a tag:
```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - owner/example-package#2.1.1
```

Run apm install to generate apm.lock.yaml. The lockfile contains both the tag and its resolved commit:
```yaml
resolved_ref: 2.1.1
resolved_commit: <40-character-sha>
resolved_tag: 2.1.1
```

Delete the local package cache:
```bash
rm -rf apm_modules
```

Run:
```bash
apm install --frozen
```

Observe a 404 response
```
Last error: HTTP 404 from
<registory_url>/<package>/zip/refs/tags/<sha>
```


**Expected behavior**
APM should download the locked commit using a generic commit archive URL supported by the proxied GitHub endpoint:
```
/archive/<sha>.zip
```
For the same repository and commit, this URL returns HTTP 200 through Artifactory.

Frozen installation should succeed without requiring a populated local cache or falling back directly to GitHub.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS, Linux
 - Python Version: 3.14.7
 - APM Version: 0.28.0

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [C] Unconditional Redundant Dict Construction Inside Loop -- src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py:1351-1358

- Current: O(|event_map| * H) -- `event_map` dict lookup and `reverse_map` dict
  construction are repeated on every iteration of `for hook_file in hook_files`
  (line 1333), even though `config.target_key` is constant for the entire loop.
  For a package with H hook files, the reverse_map (normalised event name ->
  source alias set) is rebuilt identically H times.
- Proposed: O(|event_map|) -- build `event_map` and `reverse_map` once before
  the loop; pass them in as local variables.
- Fix: Hoist lines 1351-1358 to just before `for hook_file in hook_files:` so
  the reverse alias map is constructed a single time per integration call, not
  once per hook file.

#### [B] Linear Scan in Grant Map Lookup -- src/apm_cli/security/executables.py:256-262 (low priority)

- Current: O(G) per call -- `_map_grants` iterates over all entries in
  `grant_map` for each query, performing string equality and `_strip_version`
  on every stored key. Called 4-6 times per `resolve_exec_decision`, which is
  invoked once per (package, exec_type) pair in `exec_status_for_declaration`
  (install/exec_gate.py:100). Total work scales as O(K * E * G) where K =
  candidate package keys, E = exec types (~4), G = grant map size.
- Proposed: O(1) per lookup -- pre-build a `{version_blind_name: entry}` index
  once from the grant map so name-based resolution avoids the linear scan.
- Fix: In `_map_grants`, build a `{_strip_version(k): (k, v) for k, v in
  grant_map.items()}` dict once (or accept it as a pre-built argument) and
  replace the for-loop with direct key lookups for the common exact-match and
  name-match cases.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Opt-out for anonymous-first HTTPS on github.com behind TLS-inspecting proxies with no revocation info
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`AuthResolver.uses_public_github_anonymous_first()` (introduced in #2406, 0.27.0; refined in #2422, 0.28.0) unconditionally tries HTTPS anonymously first for any exact-host `github.com` dependency, with no opt-out. The anonymous attempt runs in a from-scratch isolated Git environment (`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` + empty `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` + disabled `credential.helper`), which ignores the user's real `~/.gitconfig` (including `http.sslBackend` and any corporate TLS trust configuration).

 

On networks behind a TLS-inspecting proxy (e.g. Netskope) whose intercepting certificate chain carries **no CRL Distribution Point and no Authority Information Access (OCSP) extensions at all** (verified with `openssl x509 -text` on leaf, intermediate, and root — not just "unreachable", genuinely absent), the isolated environment's connection attempt fails with a network/TLS-classified error (schannel: `CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK`, or a hang). `is_public_github_auth_failure()` correctly does **not** classify this as an auth failure, so APM neverresolves/tries a credential — and with `--allow-protocol-fallback` it jumps straight to SSH. If SSH is also blocked (common on corporate firewalls), install fails completely with "Could not connect to github.com (network error, not an auth failure)".

 

Critically, a plain `git clone` on the same machine/network succeeds instantly, because it uses the OS git credential helper and the use

r's real `~/.gitconfig` (`http.sslBackend=schannel`, resolving against the Windows certificate store where the corporate root CA is installed) — the exact configuration the isolated environment discards.

 

This is a regression relative to 0.26.0, whose legacy `--allow-protocol-fallback` chain unconditionally tried a final "plain HTTPS" leg deferring to the OS git config/credential helper, which happened to succeed in this exact scenario.

 

**Describe the solution you'd like**

An opt-out (CLI flag and/or env var, e.g. `--auth-first` / `APM_GITHUB_AUTH_FIRST=1`) to restore auth-first / environment-inheriting behavior for exact-host `github.com`, for users who already have a working git config/credentials but are behind a network where the isolated anonymous-first environment cannot complete a TLS handshake at all.

 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Downgrading to apm <0.27.0 — works, but loses newer fixes/features.

- Declaring dependencies with explicit `ssh://` URLs to sidestep the HTTPS path — plausible, untested, and still depends on SSH connectivity (often blocked; workable via `ssh.github.com:443` but non-obvious).

- Manually restoring TLS trust for the isolated environment via `GIT_SSL_CAINFO` + forcing `http.sslbackend=openssl` (these specific env vars survive `AuthResolver`'s isolation, unlike gitconfig-based settings) — works, but required deep reverse-engineering of `auth.py` to discover; not discoverable by a typical user hitting this.

- `http.schannelCheckRevoke=false` — does **not** reliably help when the CA chain has no revocation info at all (confirmed on 2.45.1.windows.1); matches several long-standing, unresolved community reports of the same git-for-windows/schannel limitation ([SO 65636426](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65636426), [SO 45556189](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45556189)).

 

**Additional context**

- apm-cli 0.28.0, Windows, git 2.45.1.windows.1.

- Root cause chain: PR #2406 introduced anonymous-first + isolated git env; PR #2422 refined the isolation but didn't change this behavior.

- Happy to share full repro details/logs if useful.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-10
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-10
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 33 top-level + all subcommands (approx. 60 help invocations total)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm install --target` docs missing supported targets

- **Command**: `apm install --target`
- **Problem**: The `install` reference docs list targets as: `copilot`, `claude`, `grok-build`, `cursor`, `opencode`, `codex`, `gemini`, `antigravity`, `windsurf`, `kiro`, `intellij`, `vscode`, `agent-skills`, `all`. The actual CLI accepts four additional target values that are entirely absent from the docs: `agents`, `agy`, `hermes`, `openclaw`. (The docs do separately mention `vscode` and `agents` as deprecated aliases in the `compile` reference, but not in `install`.)
- **Evidence**:
  - Actual CLI: `apm install --help` shows `agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf`
  - Docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md` line 49): `copilot, claude, grok-build, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, intellij, vscode, agent-skills, all` -- `agents`, `agy`, `hermes`, and `openclaw` are absent
  - Same omission exists in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md`
- **Suggested Fix**: Add the missing targets to the `--target` table in both `install.md` and `update.md`. Annotate `agents` and `vscode` as deprecated aliases for `copilot` (as already done in `compile.md` line 73), and `agy` as an alias for `antigravity`. Document `hermes` and `openclaw` as supported targets.

---

#### `--parallel-checks` default value format inconsistent with `--parallel-downloads`

- **Command**: `apm outdated`
- **Problem**: The `--parallel-checks` flag renders its default inline in the help description string instead of using Click's `show_default=True`, producing a different visual style compared to every other parallelism flag in the CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm outdated --help`: `-j, --parallel-checks INTEGER  Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)`
  - `apm install --help`:  `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`
  - `apm update --help`:   `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`
  - Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/outdated.py` uses `help="Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)"` without `show_default=True`, unlike install/update which use `show_default=True`
- **Suggested Fix**: In `src/apm_cli/commands/outdated.py`, change the `--parallel-checks` option to use `show_default=True` and move `(0 = sequential)` into the help string, e.g.: `help="Max concurrent remote checks (0 = sequential)"` with `show_default=True`. This produces `[default: 4]` at the end, matching the other commands.

---

#### `apm compile --all` help text omits deprecation of `--target all`

- **Command**: `apm compile --all`
- **Problem**: The CLI help text for `--all` says "Equivalent to --target all" without noting that `--target all` is deprecated in favor of `--all`. A user reading the help might use `--target all` without knowing it will emit a deprecation warning. The docs do explain this correctly.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm compile --help`: `--all  Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all.`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md` line 74-75: "`--target all` also emits a deprecation warning -- prefer `--all`."
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--all` help string to: `"Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all (deprecated form; prefer --all)."` or similar wording so the inline help reflects the deprecation.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm config list` description slightly misleading

- **Command**: `apm config list`
- **Problem**: The CLI help says "List all configuration values" but the command actually prints a filtered summary of core user-settable keys (same as `apm config get` with no argument), not every possible configuration value. The docs correctly describe it as "Alias for `apm config get` with no argument."
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm config list --help`: `List all configuration values`
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/config.md`: "`apm config list` -- Alias for `apm config get` with no argument; produces the same user config summary."
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the CLI description to: "Show a summary of user-settable configuration values (alias for 'apm config get')."

---

#### `apm deps update` stale `--target` value list (deprecated command)

- **Command**: `apm deps update --target`
- **Problem**: The deprecated `apm deps update` command advertises a shorter target list (`copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all`) compared to the current equivalents (`apm update`, `apm install`), which include `hermes`, `openclaw`, `agy`, `vscode`, `agents`, `grok-build`, `grok-cloud`, `intellij`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`. Since the command is deprecated, this inconsistency is low risk, but users who haven't migrated may be confused.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm deps update --help --target`: shows only 11 values
  - `apm update --help --target`: shows 21 values
- **Suggested Fix**: Either update `deps update` to use the shared target constant, or add a note to its help text explaining the target list is not current and users should migrate to `apm update`.

---

### Clean Areas

The following areas passed all consistency checks with no issues found:

- **Command coverage**: All 33 top-level commands are fully documented with a matching reference page in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`.
- **Error handling**: All tested invalid-input cases (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no arg, `apm config set` with no args, `apm mcp search` with no arg) produce clean, non-traceback error messages with a "Try ... --help" pointer.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every command and subcommand tested.
- **`--verbose` / `-v`**: Present and consistently named across all commands that support it.
- **`--dry-run`**: Present on all commands that perform mutating operations (`install`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `uninstall`, `unpack`, `prune`, `audit`).
- **`--yes` / `-y`**: Present on `update` and `deps clean` where confirmation prompts exist.
- **`-g, --global`**: Consistently named and described across `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`, `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `outdated`, `lock`, `compile`.
- **Subcommand structure**: `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`, `cache`, `experimental`, `marketplace`, `lifecycle`, `plugin`, `policy` all expose logical subcommand groups with sensible descriptions.
- **`apm mcp` list/search defaults**: `apm mcp list --limit` defaults to 20 (matches docs); `apm mcp search --limit` defaults to 10 (matches docs).
- **`apm config unset`**: Present in CLI and correctly documented.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands**: `list`, `setup`, `status`, `remove` all present and documented.

issues.title: [BUG] apm installed project LSP servers not discoverable by claude code
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

apm installed LSP servers at the project level are not discoverable by claude code.

The same LSP definition, when installed works on copilot (vscode) and it works when manually defined in a plugin json at the project level. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create apm.yml file with LSP

Example:
```yaml
# ...
targets:
  - claude
  - copilot
dependencies:
  lsp:
    - name: basedpyright
      command: uv
      args: ["run", "basedpyright-langserver", "--stdio"]
      extensionToLanguage:
        ".py": python
        ".pyi": python
      transport: stdio
      startupTimeout: 30000
```

2. Run `apm install`. 
3. A `.lsp.json` file is created
4. Run claude code and ask it to add a syntax error to a python file and report if it received a diagnostic notification about the error.
5. It did not and no LSP tools are available

**Expected behavior**

Claude code is notified of the error and LSP tools are available.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.28.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): 1.132.0


**Additional context**

If the LSP server is configured as a plugin under .claude/skills it works, so claude code is not reading the `.lsp.json` file.

This works:

`.claude/skills/basedpyright-lsp/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
```json
{
  "name": "basedpyright-lsp",
  "description": "basedpyright language server over tools/, launched through uv",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "lspServers": {
    "basedpyright": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "basedpyright-langserver", "--stdio"],
      "extensionToLanguage": {
        ".py": "python",
        ".pyi": "python"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install -g --mcp` is rejected outright: "MCP servers are project-scoped"
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

`apm install -g --mcp NAME` always fails, despite both the docs and `apm install --help` stating that global MCP install is supported.

**Repro**

```bash
apm install -g --mcp probe --dry-run -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch
apm install -g --mcp probe --transport http --url https://example.com/mcp --dry-run
apm mcp install probe -g --target claude --dry-run -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch
```

All three produce:

```
Error: MCP servers are project-scoped; --global is not supported for MCP entries
```

Independent of transport (`stdio`, `http`), flag order, and presence/absence of `--target`.

**Expected**

Per `apm install --help`:

> `-g, --global` … MCP servers target global-capable runtimes only (Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, Kiro, Windsurf, JetBrains Copilot).

And per https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/install-mcp-servers/:

> `apm install -g --mcp NAME` routes the write to each runtime's user-scope MCP config

The CHANGELOG also implies this path is expected to work — v0.23.1 lists a fix for "`apm install -g --mcp NAME` ignoring the package `targets:` field and `--target` flag at user scope", which presupposes the command runs at all. This looks like a regression.

**Workaround**

Declaring the server under `dependencies.mcp:` in `~/.apm/apm.yml` and running `apm install -g --only mcp --target claude` works correctly and writes to `~/.claude.json`. Only the imperative flag path is broken.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install --dry-run` creates `~/.apm/apm.yml`, `config.json`, and `apm_modules/` while reporting "no changes made"
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

`--dry-run` is not read-only at user scope; it bootstraps the user-scope root before printing that nothing changed.

**Repro**

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/fakehome && mkdir -p /tmp/fakehome
HOME=/tmp/fakehome apm install microsoft/apm-sample-package#v1.0.0 -g --target claude --dry-run
find /tmp/fakehome -maxdepth 3
```

Output ends with:

```
[*] Dry run complete - no changes made
[i] Dry run completed: would install no changes in 0.3s.
```

Yet the filesystem now contains:

```
/tmp/fakehome/.apm/apm.yml
/tmp/fakehome/.apm/config.json
/tmp/fakehome/.apm/apm_modules
```

**Expected**

`--dry-run` should not write to disk, or should state which files it will create as part of the plan.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm install --dry-run` reports "No dependencies found in apm.yml" when only `dependencies.lsp` is declared
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

Dry-run does not account for LSP dependencies, so the plan output is wrong for any LSP-only manifest.

**Repro**

```bash
mkdir /tmp/lsptest && cd /tmp/lsptest && apm init --yes && touch CLAUDE.md
```

Add to `apm.yml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp: []
  lsp:
    - name: go
      command: gopls
      args: [serve]
      extensionToLanguage:
        .go: go
```

Then:

```bash
apm install --target claude --dry-run
# [i] No dependencies found in apm.yml
# [*] Dry run complete - no changes made

apm install --target claude
# [i] Configured 1 LSP server(s) in .lsp.json
```

**Expected**

Dry-run should list the LSP dependency, as it does for `apm` and `mcp` entries.

Related: `--only` accepts only `[apm|mcp]`, so there is no way to install or preview LSP dependencies in isolation.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm uninstall` MCP cleanup ignores `--target`, aborts on JSONC in the JetBrains Copilot config, and orphans MCP servers
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

Uninstalling a package installed with `--target claude` attempts to clean MCP config for *other* runtimes. If the JetBrains Copilot config contains comments — which is what GitHub's own default template ships — the parse fails, the uninstall aborts mid-way, and MCP servers are left orphaned in the configs that were already written.

**Repro**

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fh2/.config/github-copilot/intellij
cat > /tmp/fh2/.config/github-copilot/intellij/mcp.json <<'EOF'
{
    "servers": {
        // add your MCP servers configuration here.
        // support both local(stdio) and remote(SSE/Streamable HTTP) servers.
    }
}
EOF

HOME=/tmp/fh2 apm install appwrite/claude-plugin -g --target claude
HOME=/tmp/fh2 apm uninstall appwrite/claude-plugin -g
```

Result:

```
[+] Cleaned up 2 integrated commands
[+] Cleaned up 15 integrated skills
[x] Uninstall incomplete: package removal completed, but MCP cleanup failed:
JetBrains Copilot MCP config at '/tmp/fh2/.config/github-copilot/intellij/mcp.json'
is malformed JSON (Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 3 column 9 (char 27)).
Fix the file, then rerun apm install.
```

The two MCP servers the plugin declared remain in `~/.claude.json` afterwards:

```
appwrite entries remaining: ['appwrite-api', 'appwrite-docs']
```

**Three separate problems**

1. **Target scoping:** the package was installed with `--target claude`; uninstall should not touch the JetBrains Copilot config at all.
2. **JSONC tolerance:** the file above is the stock template GitHub ships for the JetBrains Copilot plugin, comments included. JetBrains accepts it. APM parses it as strict JSON and fails.
3. **Partial failure leaves orphans:** one runtime's parse error aborts cleanup for runtimes already processed, with no rollback and no list of what was left behind. The suggested remedy ("rerun `apm install`") does not remove the orphaned entries.

issues.title: [BUG] `apm compile --global` reports "no global instructions" with no discoverable authoring path
issues.body:
**Environment:** APM 0.28.0 (e041462), installed via the `microsoft/apm` Homebrew tap. macOS (darwin 25.5.0), arm64.

---


**Summary**

The CHANGELOG for 0.28.0 states:

> `apm compile -g / --global` compiles global (`apply_to`-less) instructions into user-scope root context files

I could not find any location where a user-scope global instruction is picked up. Every target reports `skipped (no global instructions)`.

**Repro**

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fh2/.apm/.apm/instructions /tmp/fh2/.apm/instructions
printf 'Always prefer boring solutions.\n' > /tmp/fh2/.apm/.apm/instructions/probe.instructions.md
printf 'Always prefer boring solutions.\n' > /tmp/fh2/.apm/instructions/probe.instructions.md
HOME=/tmp/fh2 apm compile --global -v
```

```
claude: skipped (no global instructions)
...
[i] No user-scope root context files changed.
```

Also tried, all with the same result: both locations with an `applyTo: "**"` frontmatter block, and with a package installed globally that ships an `instructions` primitive (its rule deployed to `~/.claude/rules/` at install, but contributed nothing to compile).

**Ask**

Either this is broken, or the authoring location is undocumented. https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/install-packages/ says targets needing a root context file "require explicit `apm compile --global`" but does not say where global instructions live. A line in the docs with the expected path would resolve it if this is user error.

**Minor:** `--global` is mutually exclusive with both `--target` and `--no-dedup`/`--force-instructions`, which is not obvious from the help text.

issues.title: apm pack: --dry-run reports plugin.json will be written, but non-force run silently skips it
issues.body:
## Summary

`apm pack --dry-run` reports it will regenerate `plugin.json`, but a real run without `--force` silently skips it — so the dry-run preview doesn't match actual behavior. Separately, neither `--check-versions` nor `--check-clean` detects this drift.

## Version

APM CLI 0.27.0

## Repro

```bash
# apm.yml has version: 1.0.8; existing .claude-plugin/plugin.json also has "version": "1.0.8"
sed -i '' 's/version: 1.0.8/version: 1.0.9/' apm.yml

apm pack --dry-run
# [i] Would write plugin manifest to .../.claude-plugin/plugin.json
# implies plugin.json will be updated to 1.0.9

apm pack
# [!] .../.claude-plugin/plugin.json already exists; skipping plugin.json generation. Re-run with --force to overwrite it.
# exits 0

grep version .claude-plugin/plugin.json
# "version": "1.0.8"   <-- unchanged, now silently out of sync with apm.yml
```

## Expected

Either:
- `--dry-run` output should say the manifest write will be **skipped** (matching real, non-`--force` behavior), not "would write"; or
- `apm pack` (no `--force`) should warn or fail when the existing `plugin.json`'s version disagrees with `apm.yml`, instead of only logging a `[!]` and exiting 0.

## Also checked: existing release gates don't catch this

```bash
apm pack --check-versions --dry-run
# [*] Version alignment OK [strategy=lockstep, expected=1.0.9]   <-- only checks apm.yml against the versioning strategy, not plugin.json

apm pack --check-clean --dry-run
# [*] Marketplace working tree clean [outputs=claude, codex]     <-- only diffs marketplace.json, not plugin.json
```

Neither existing gate would catch a `plugin.json` stuck on a stale version. We ended up writing a repo-local script (`check_plugin_metadata.py`) to assert `plugin.json` matches `apm.yml` in CI, because `apm pack`/`--check-versions`/`--check-clean` don't cover it.

## Impact

Consumers installing via `apm install owner/repo@vX.Y.Z` read `plugin.json` for the version — a stale manifest ships a wrong version string with no error anywhere in the producer's pipeline.

## Performance Scan - 2026-08-11

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [A] Quadratic inheritance traversal in compile stats -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:374-380

- Current: O(D * depth * I) -- `get_optimization_stats` calls `analyze_context_inheritance`
  for every directory in `_directory_cache` (D directories); each call iterates the
  inheritance chain (up to D levels deep) and then all instructions in each level (I).
  Results are not cached. Effective complexity: O(D^2 * I) for deep trees.
- Proposed: O(D * I) -- memoize `analyze_context_inheritance` results per compile pass,
  keyed by `working_directory`. The placement_map is constant within one `get_optimization_stats`
  call, so a plain dict cache avoids redundant traversals.
- Fix: Add a local `_inheritance_analysis_cache: dict[Path, InheritanceAnalysis]` to the
  optimizer instance (or as a local dict in `get_optimization_stats`) and return the cached
  result if the key is already present before running the nested loop.

#### [C] Unconditional full cache scan on first store -- src/apm_cli/cache/http_cache.py:73,241-245,343

- Current: `_tracked_size` is initialized to `None` at `__init__`. The fast-path guard in
  `_enforce_size_cap` (line 343) is `if self._tracked_size is not None and ...`; on the
  first `store()` call the condition is False, so a full `scandir` over every cache shard
  runs unconditionally regardless of actual cache size. For a registry client that stores
  multiple responses in one session (e.g., `apm install` fetching N registry API responses),
  only the first `store()` pays the cost, but that cost is O(cache entries) even for a
  near-empty or brand-new cache.
- Proposed: O(1) skip for empty/new cache -- initialize `_tracked_size = 0` in `__init__`
  so the fast-path fires immediately for an empty cache. A single controlled scan at startup
  (via a separate `_warm_tracked_size` method) could populate the real value before the
  first store, amortizing the cost to one scan per process lifetime rather than per-instance.
- Fix: Replace `self._tracked_size: int | None = None` with `self._tracked_size: int = 0`
  in `__init__` and add an optional `_warm_tracked_size()` helper that does the real scandir
  once and stores the result; call it lazily from the first `get()` or from `__init__` if
  the cache dir is non-empty. (Low priority -- affects one scandir per CLI invocation, not
  per package.)

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (430 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [BUG] `"skills": ["./"]` in plugin.json crashes install with "maximum recursion depth exceeded"
issues.body:
A `plugin.json` declaring `"skills": ["./"]` — the documented Claude Code way to say "this plugin's single skill is at the plugin root" — makes `apm install` fail with `maximum recursion depth exceeded`. The plugin never installs.

The declaration is legal on the Claude Code side. The [plugins reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference) documents it directly: when a skill path points at a directory holding `SKILL.md` — "for example `"skills": ["./"]` pointing to the plugin root" — the frontmatter `name` determines the skill's invocation name. So this is a shape APM will meet in the wild on any marketplace that ships single-skill plugins.

## Reproduction

Minimal, no network:

```bash
mkdir -p plug/.claude-plugin consumer
printf -- '---\nname: hello\ndescription: Minimal solo skill.\n---\n\n# hello\n' > plug/SKILL.md
printf '{"name":"p","version":"1.0.0","skills":["./"]}' > plug/.claude-plugin/plugin.json

cd consumer && apm install ../plug --target claude
```

Output:

```text
[>] Resolving ../plug...
[i] Targets: claude  (source: --target flag)
  [+] ../plug (local)
[i] Removed apm.yml created by the failed install.
[x] Failed to install APM dependencies: Failed to resolve APM dependencies:
maximum recursion depth exceeded
[i] Run with --verbose for detailed diagnostics
[x] Install failed after 1.9s.
```

`--verbose` adds no diagnostic beyond the same one-line message.

Also reproduces from a public marketplace over the network, via the `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` intake path:

```bash
apm marketplace add DgxSparkLabs/marketplace-template
apm install skill-example-single@dgxsparklabs-template-marketplace --target claude
```

```text
  [x] 1 package failed:
    +- marketplace-template-skill-example-single -- Failed to download dependency
       DgxSparkLabs/marketplace-template: Subdirectory is not a valid APM package or
       Claude Skill: Failed to process Claude plugin: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

That repository is mine and I am changing the layout that triggers it, so the local repro above is the durable one.

## Mechanism

`_map_plugin_artifacts` stages declared components into `.apm/`, which lives **inside** the plugin directory. When the declared entry resolves to the plugin root itself, source and destination-parent are the same directory, and `shutil.copytree` walks into the tree it is writing:

```text
plug/                              <- copy FROM here (because "./")
├── SKILL.md
├── .claude-plugin/
└── .apm/skills/
    └── plug/                      <- copy TO here, inside the source
        └── .apm/skills/plug/
            └── .apm/skills/plug/  <- until the stack is exhausted
```

`src/apm_cli/deps/plugin_parser.py` (main @ `3aa0365`), the list branch:

```python
is_custom_list = isinstance(manifest.get("skills"), list)
if is_custom_list and skill_dirs:
    target_skills.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for d in skill_dirs:
        nested = target_skills / d.name
        if _is_same_path(d, nested):     # <- catches src == dst only
            continue
        shutil.copytree(d, nested, ignore=ignore_non_content, dirs_exist_ok=True)
```

`_is_same_path` compares resolved equality. Here `d` is the plugin root and `nested` is `<plugin root>/.apm/skills/<name>` — a **descendant**, not an equal — so the guard does not fire. The comment above the helper anticipates only the equal case ("Copying onto self raises `shutil.SameFileError`").

Frames, captured by calling the entry point directly:

```text
RecursionError; total frames: 1001
  src/apm_cli/deps/plugin_parser.py:267 in synthesize_apm_yml_from_plugin
  src/apm_cli/deps/plugin_parser.py:793 in _map_plugin_artifacts
  ... shutil.copytree recursing into its own destination
```

## Scope

Confirmed by differential testing — three plugins differing only in the declaration and file placement:

| `plugin.json` `skills` | Layout | Result |
| ---------------------- | ------ | ------ |
| `["./"]` | root `SKILL.md` | **`maximum recursion depth exceeded`** |
| *(key absent)* | root `SKILL.md` | Installs. Deploys under the **plugin directory name**, ignoring frontmatter `name` |
| `["./skills/"]` | `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Installs correctly as `<name>` |

So the trigger is the declared `"./"` entry specifically, not root-`SKILL.md` layouts in general.

Not affected, checked explicitly:

- The source plugin directory is not polluted — APM works on a copy, and `plug/` still contains exactly its two original directories afterwards.
- No oversized tree is left in `~/.apm`.
- Rollback is otherwise clean; only empty `apm_modules/` and `.claude/` directories remain in the consumer.

## Suggested fix

Make the guard a **containment** check rather than an equality check, so a destination nested inside its own source is never used as a `copytree` target. Two placements, whichever fits the design:

1. In the loop — when `nested` would land inside `d`, stage to a temporary directory outside the plugin root and move the result into place.
2. At classification — treat a declared entry that resolves to the plugin root as the "this entry *is* one skill" case and stage it under its resolved skill name from a copy taken before `.apm/` exists.

Either way, the name used should be the frontmatter `name`, since that is what Claude Code uses for a root-`SKILL.md` plugin and what a consumer will type.

## Relationship to open work

- **#2537** — declared-vs-discovered skill sets disagreeing. Same file, later stage: that bug is about which skills win, this one crashes before any set is produced.
- **#2530 / #2536** — `--skill` enumeration on subdirectory refs. From #2536's description, declared entries are classified so that "one carrying its own `SKILL.md` keeps its name" — which reads like the same branch that recurses here, so I do not expect #2536 to fix this. Worth a check by whoever owns that PR; if it does fix it, this can close as a duplicate with a regression test.
- **#760** (`harden(plugin): enforce plugin-root containment for manifest paths`) — established that declared paths must stay inside the plugin root. `"./"` satisfies that check and then breaks on the copy, so the containment work has a gap on the write side.

A regression test asserting `"skills": ["./"]` installs would cover all three.

## Environment

- `apm` built from `main` at `3aa0365`, reported as `0.28.0 (3aa0365)`; also reproduced with `apm-cli` 0.28.0 from PyPI.
- Windows 11, Python 3.14.
- Reproduced with both a local path dependency and a remote `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` marketplace.

*Disclosure: drafted with AI assistance; every command shown was executed against the versions named above and its output captured verbatim.*

issues.title: [BUG] `apm uninstall -g` leaves Copilot hook files in `~/.copilot/hooks/`
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Uninstalling a user-scope package (`apm install -g` → `apm uninstall -g`) removes
every other primitive it deployed but leaves its Copilot hook files behind in
`~/.copilot/hooks/`. The orphaned file is live wiring: Copilot CLI keeps firing a
hook belonging to a package that is gone from `apm.yml`, `apm_modules/`, and the
lockfile. Reinstalling never clears it either — the path is simply never a
deletion candidate.

Copilot is the only harness affected, and only at user scope. Uninstall's
file-level removal routes each lockfile `deployed_files` path into a per-primitive
bucket via
[`BaseIntegrator.partition_managed_files`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/base_integrator.py),
which walks a segment trie built from every non-`skills`/`hooks` primitive prefix
and falls back to the `skills`/`hooks` prefix tuples only when the trie yields no
match:

```python
if last_bucket is not None:
    buckets[last_bucket].add(p)
    continue
# Fall back to cross-target buckets
if p.startswith(skill_tuple):
    buckets["skills"].add(p)
elif p.startswith(hook_tuple):
    buckets["hooks"].add(p)
```

At user scope the Copilot target's
[`user_primitive_overrides`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py)
maps instructions to `PrimitiveMapping("", ".md", "copilot_user_instructions")` —
an empty `subdir`, so its prefix is the bare target root `.copilot/`. That prefix
becomes a catch-all trie node: `.copilot/hooks/<pkg>-<hook>.json` matches at the
first segment, `last_bucket` is set to `instructions_copilot`, and the `continue`
skips the hook fallback. The hook path is handed to
[`InstructionIntegrator.sync_for_target`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/integration/instruction_integrator.py),
whose `copilot_user_instructions` guard narrows the prefix to
`.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` and discards it. No integrator ever deletes the
file, and `HookIntegrator.sync_integration` never sees it in `managed_files`.

Nothing shadows `.copilot/prompts/` or `.copilot/agents/` — they own deeper trie
nodes and win by longest prefix. Hooks lose because they are routed by the
fallback tuples rather than by the trie. At project scope Copilot hooks land in
`.github/hooks/`, outside the `.copilot/` root, so the shadowing never applies and
removal works. The other harnesses escape for a different reason: their hooks are
merged into a shared config (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, …) and
cleaned by `_apm_source` marker rather than by `managed_files`.

The symptom resembles #2245 / #2250, but those cover the merged-hook JSON path;
this is the per-file deployment path and a different root cause. Same target and
scope as #2232, also a different cause.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `cd uninstall-copilot-user-hook-orphan`
2. `make user` — installs a package holding one hook and one prompt to user scope
   (`--target copilot`) under an isolated fake `$HOME`, then uninstalls it
3. See the prompt is removed and reported (`Cleaned up 1 integrated prompts`),
   while `.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json` survives and no hook cleanup is
   reported at all
4. `make matrix` — repeats install + uninstall at user scope for every hook-capable
   harness; only `copilot` reports an orphan
5. `make project` — installs the same package at project scope across all those
   harnesses; every hook is removed

**Expected behavior**

`apm uninstall -g` removes the hook files it deployed to `~/.copilot/hooks/`, the
same way it removes the package's prompts, and the same way project-scope
uninstall removes Copilot hooks from `.github/hooks/`. After uninstall no
harness still fires a hook from the removed package.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (Arch Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.28.0 (e041462)

**Logs**

`make user` — prompt cleaned, hook orphaned:

```
  [+] ./hookpkg (local)
  |-- 1 prompts integrated -> .copilot/prompts/
  |-- 1 hook(s) integrated -> .copilot/hooks/
  |   postToolUse: runs echo hookpkg-ran (notify.json)

[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 1.9s.
--- deployed under ~/.copilot/ ---
./.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json
./.copilot/prompts/greet.prompt.md

[i] Uninstalling from user scope (~/.apm/)
[>] Uninstalling 1 package(s)...
[+] _local/hookpkg - found in apm.yml
[i] Removed _local/hookpkg from dependencies.apm in apm.yml
[i] Removed _local/hookpkg from apm_modules/
[+] Cleaned up 1 integrated prompts
[*] Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml, Removed 1 package(s) from apm_modules/
--- after uninstall (prompt gone, hook orphaned) ---
./.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json
```

`make matrix` — user scope, every hook-capable harness:

```
claude: clean
codex: clean
copilot: ORPHANED ./.copilot/hooks/hookpkg-notify.json
cursor: clean
gemini: clean
windsurf: clean
```

`make project` — same package, project scope, all six harnesses:

```
[+] Cleaned up 1 integrated prompts
[+] Cleaned up 4 integrated commands
[+] Cleaned up 6 integrated hooks
[*] Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml, Removed 1 package(s) from apm_modules/
--- after uninstall (no file still carries the hook command) ---
```

**Additional context**

Minimal reproduction: https://github.com/sproott/apm-bugs
(`make user` / `make matrix` / `make project` in
`uninstall-copilot-user-hook-orphan/`).

issues.title: [BUG] Sub-directory AGENTS.md is overwritten whole, ignoring managed_section and foreign Git roots
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`_prepare_distributed_file()` treats every sub-directory `AGENTS.md` as APM-owned and overwrites it whole. Two layouts break under that assumption:

- **A.** A pre-existing `AGENTS.md` in a sub-directory loses its hand-authored content, even with `compilation.agents_md.mode: managed_section` set and correct `<!-- apm:start -->` / `<!-- apm:end -->` markers in the file. The root `AGENTS.md` in the same repository, same run, keeps its content.
- **B.** When the placement directory is the root of a nested independent Git repository, compile modifies a tracked file in a repository it was never pointed at. The nested repo is left with an uncommitted modification.

`AGENTS.md` is a general convention, so a sub-directory copy may predate APM or belong to another repository. #1764 fixed this for the root only. The delete path already knows about Git boundaries after #2436; the write path does not.

Affects `codex`, `copilot` and `cursor`. `claude` is unaffected, since it keeps instruction output at the root and in `.claude/rules/`.

**To Reproduce**

Case A, markers ignored below the root:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/apm-a/.apm/instructions /tmp/apm-a/apps/x && cd /tmp/apm-a

cat > apm.yml <<'YAML'
name: repro-a
version: 0.0.1
description: Repro.
compilation:
  agents_md:
    mode: managed_section
YAML

cat > .apm/instructions/s.instructions.md <<'MD'
---
description: Scoped instruction.
applyTo: '**/*.ts'
---
- Generated rule.
MD

touch apps/x/a.ts

for f in AGENTS.md apps/x/AGENTS.md; do cat > "$f" <<'MD'
# Context

SENTINEL: hand-authored, outside the managed block.

<!-- apm:start -->
<!-- apm:end -->
MD
done

apm compile --local-only --target copilot
grep -c SENTINEL AGENTS.md         # 1
grep -c SENTINEL apps/x/AGENTS.md  # 0
```

Case B, write into a nested independent Git repository:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/apm-b/.apm/instructions && cd /tmp/apm-b && git init -q .

cat > apm.yml <<'YAML'
name: repro-b
version: 0.0.1
description: Repro.
YAML

cat > .apm/instructions/s.instructions.md <<'MD'
---
description: Scoped instruction.
applyTo: '**/*.ts'
---
- Generated rule.
MD

mkdir child && cd child && git init -q .
printf '# Child context\nSENTINEL: owned by this repository.\n' > AGENTS.md
git add AGENTS.md && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm "context"
touch svc.ts && cd ..

apm compile --local-only --target copilot
# Placement: child/AGENTS.md
grep -c SENTINEL child/AGENTS.md   # 0
git -C child status --short        # M AGENTS.md
```

Placement lands on the deepest directory the matches share, so Case B needs the matching files to sit only inside the nested repository. Add a second matching file outside it and placement moves up to the root, where neither case reproduces.

**Expected behavior**

Case A: honour `managed_section` at any depth, or refuse to write a file that has markers and content APM did not generate.

Case B: do not write below a Git root other than the one containing the active `apm.yml`. Report the skipped placement instead. `distributed_compiler.py` already skips foreign Git roots when removing orphans; the write path can use the same check.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS 26.5.2 (arm64)
- APM Version: 0.28.0 (e041462), standalone binary
- Targets: reproduced on `copilot`, `codex`, `cursor`. Not reproduced on `claude`

**Root cause**

`src/apm_cli/compilation/agents_compiler.py:1677-1683`:

```python
# Honour managed_section mode for the root AGENTS.md (issue #1764).
# Sub-directory files are fully APM-generated and always overwritten.
is_root = agents_path.parent.resolve() == self.base_dir.resolve()
if is_root and config.agents_md_mode == "managed_section":
    return self._prepare_output_content_with_config(
        str(agents_path), final_content, config
    )
return final_content
```

The `is_root` guard is what #1764's fix added, and the comment states the assumption behind it. Case A is that assumption meeting a file APM did not create. `_write_distributed_file()` then passes the content straight to `CompiledOutputWriter().write()`, so nothing downstream compares it against what is already on disk.

For Case B, placement comes from `_create_placements()` in `distributed_compiler.py`, which derives `agents_path` from the directory map with no ownership check. `agents_compiler.py` contains no reference to `.git` at all, while `distributed_compiler.py` has the skip-list added for #2436.

**Suggested fix**

1. Drop `is_root` from the `managed_section` condition, so a marked file is reconciled at any depth.
2. For a file with no markers that APM did not generate, either write markers around the generated block or skip it and report the path. Overwriting it is the one option that loses data.
3. Resolve the Git root of each placement directory and skip any that differs from the working root's, reusing the boundary check from the orphan sweep.

**Additional context**

We hit this from a workspace that coordinates several independent Git repositories under one APM working root, where an instruction scoped to one stack matches files in exactly one repository. Related: #1764 (root-only fix), #2436 (same boundary on the delete path), #1730 (sub-directory placement), #1220 (per-instruction placement opt-out, closed as not planned).

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-08-11
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-11
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 25

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 2     |
| Low      | 2     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` shows a stale target values list

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag help text for the deprecated `apm deps update` command lists a significantly shorter set of accepted target values than the current `apm update` command. Missing from `deps update` help: `agents`, `agy`, `vscode`, `grok-build`, `grok-cloud`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`. Additionally, the docs for `apm deps update` explicitly list `grok-build` as valid, but the CLI help does not include it.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps update --help (stale list)
  -t, --target TARGET  Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                       gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all.

  # apm update --help (current list)
  -t, --target TARGET  Values: agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity,
                       claude, codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, hermes,
                       intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```
  The docs at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md` list `grok-build` as valid for `apm deps update`, but the CLI help omits it.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help string in the `apm deps update` command source to include the full current target list (matching `apm update`), or at minimum add `grok-build` to match the docs and add a note that experimental targets such as `copilot-app` and `grok-cloud` are also accepted when their flags are enabled.

---

#### `apm compile --all` help text does not mention that `--target all` is deprecated

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The `--all` flag description in `apm compile --help` says it is "Equivalent to `--target all`" without noting that `--target all` is the deprecated form. Both `apm install --help` and the docs explicitly state that `--target all` is deprecated for `apm compile` and `--all` should be preferred, but the `--all` flag's own description gives no such guidance.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm compile --help
  --all  Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all.

  # apm install --help (note embedded in --target description)
  For 'apm compile', use '--all'; '--target all' is deprecated.

  # docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md
  | `--all` | ... Equivalent to `--target all` and mutually exclusive with
               `--target`. Preferred form. |
  `--target all` also emits a deprecation warning -- prefer `--all`.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--all` flag help text in `apm compile` to say: "Compile for all canonical targets. Preferred form; `--target all` is deprecated and emits a warning."

---

### Low Severity

#### `-v, --verbose` descriptions are stylistically inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`, `apm deps update`, `apm mcp search`
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag description text varies noticeably across commands. Some use a short generic description, others are highly specific.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm init:        "Show detailed output"
  apm install:     "Show detailed installation information"
  apm uninstall:   "Show detailed removal information"
  apm update:      "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"
  apm compile:     "Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"
  apm run:         "Show detailed output"
  apm deps update: "Show detailed update information"
  apm mcp search:  "Show detailed output"
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Use a consistent base phrase such as "Enable verbose output" or "Show detailed output" across all commands, appending command-specific context only where genuinely useful (e.g., "Show detailed output (source attribution and optimizer analysis)" for compile).

---

#### `apm install` short description references "LSP dependencies" without a corresponding LSP command surface

- **Command**: `apm install`
- **Problem**: The one-line description of `apm install` says "Install APM, MCP, and LSP dependencies" but there is no `apm lsp` command or similar dedicated LSP management surface. The term "LSP" is a valid internal feature but is unexpected in a top-level description without further context for new users.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm install --help (first two lines)
  Usage: apm install [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    Install APM, MCP, and LSP dependencies (supports APM packages, Claude
    skills (SKILL.md), and plugin collections (plugin.json); ...)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Simplify the short description to "Install APM packages and MCP servers" (or similar), and move LSP details into the options or a notes section of the longer help. Alternatively, add a brief parenthetical like "(LSP handled via --target)" to clarify scope.

---

### Clean Areas

- All 25 `--help` invocations returned clean, well-structured output with no stack traces.
- Invalid argument handling is consistent and user-friendly: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (no arg), and `apm config set` (no args) all produce clear `Error:` messages with a `Try '... --help' for help.` hint rather than tracebacks.

issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-12

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [E] Heavy Top-Level Import -- src/apm_cli/commands/update.py:62-68

- Current: O(startup) -- `from git.exc import GitCommandError` and `from ..deps.github_downloader import GitHubPackageDownloader` are loaded at module level; since cli.py eagerly imports all command modules, gitpython and the full download machinery load on every `apm` invocation regardless of which sub-command is run (e.g. `apm list`, `apm doctor`).
- Proposed: O(0) at startup -- import cost deferred to invocation time by moving these imports inside the `update` callback function body.
- Fix: Move `from git.exc import GitCommandError`, `from ..deps.github_downloader import GitHubPackageDownloader`, and the `revision_pins` imports inside the `update()` function body so they are only imported when `apm update` is actually invoked.

#### [B] Double Linear Scan on List -- src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py:1155-1156, 1322-1323, 1397-1398, 1503-1504

- Current: O(2n) per occurrence -- the pattern `if "_git" in parts: git_idx = parts.index("_git")` performs two sequential O(n) list scans (one membership check, one index lookup) where a single scan suffices. Appears four times across parse methods; called once per dependency string parsed at install/update time.
- Proposed: O(n) with a single scan -- use `try: git_idx = parts.index("_git") ... except ValueError: pass` or precompute the index once.
- Fix: Replace each `if "_git" in parts: idx = parts.index("_git")` pair with `try: idx = parts.index("_git"); parts = parts[:idx] + parts[idx+1:] except ValueError: pass` to eliminate the redundant membership scan.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (430 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

Notes:
- Pattern A: No confirmed O(n^2) loops found; context_optimizer.py uses pattern/result caching; security/executables.py uses frozenset for O(1) membership tests.
- Pattern C: http_cache.py already implements fast-path skip before full directory scan in _enforce_size_cap().
- Pattern D: os.getenv calls in registry/operations.py loop over different variable names per iteration (not the same key fetched twice).
- Pattern F: install/phases/download.py already uses ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel downloads; sequential subprocess loops in validation.py are fallback probes (later iterations depend on prior failures).

issues.title: Add Kimi Code CLI as a compile/install target
issues.body:
## Feature request

Add **Kimi Code CLI** (Moonshot AI's agentic coding CLI, `kimi`) as a supported target for `apm compile` / `apm install`, alongside the existing claude, codex, cursor, gemini, copilot, opencode, windsurf, and kiro targets.

## Motivation

Kimi Code is a growing agent runtime with an open, file-based configuration model that maps very cleanly onto APM's primitives (instructions, agents, skills). Teams running multi-runtime setups currently have to hand-deploy APM packages to Kimi, which defeats the single-source-of-truth workflow APM provides for other runtimes.

## Proposed target mapping

Kimi Code's discovery paths (from the [official docs](https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code-cli/customization/agents.html)):

| APM primitive | Kimi Code destination (user/global) | Project level |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions (`AGENTS.md`) | `~/.kimi-code/AGENTS.md` (moves with `KIMI_CODE_HOME`) | project `AGENTS.md` / `.kimi-code/AGENTS.md` |
| Skills | `~/.kimi-code/skills/` | `.kimi-code/skills/` |
| Agents (sub-agent profiles) | `~/.kimi-code/agents/` | `.kimi-code/agents/` |

Notes that make this low-effort:

- **Shared cross-client paths already exist**: Kimi also reads `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.agents/agents/` — the same shared `~/.agents/` convention APM already uses for the codex skills deploy, so skills may need no new deploy logic at all.
- **Agent file format is markdown + YAML frontmatter** (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `whenToUse`, ...), and Kimi explicitly tolerates Claude Code-style agent files (comma-separated `tools`, unknown fields ignored, filename fallback for `name`). So existing `.agent.md` sources likely compile to Kimi profiles with little or no transformation.
- **Target detection marker**: presence of a `.kimi-code/` directory (consistent with how cursor/windsurf/kiro targets are detected).

## References

- Agents/sub-agents: https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code-cli/customization/agents.html
- Skills: https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code-cli/customization/skills.html
- Configuration (`KIMI_CODE_HOME`, `extra_agent_dirs`, `extra_skill_dirs`): https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code-cli/configuration/config-files.html
