issues.title: [FEATURE] Extend opt-in source attribution to AGENTS.md (#1341 follow-up: distributed compiler still hardcodes version comment and footer)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

#1341 asked to make the cosmetic compile comments opt-in in generated `CLAUDE.md` **and** `AGENTS.md`. The implementing PR #1584 flipped `compilation.source_attribution` to default `false` and gated those comments in `claude_formatter.py` (plus `copilot-instructions.md`), but the distributed `AGENTS.md` path was never covered.

On v0.28.0 the `APM Version` comment and the trailing footer are still emitted unconditionally there, so projects compiling for AGENTS.md-reading targets (`codex`, `opencode`, `gemini`, ...) keep paying that token cost in every session with no way to opt out.

Reproduced on apm 0.28.0 (`e041462`):

```yaml
# apm.yml
name: bannertest
version: 1.0.0
targets:
  - codex
compilation:
  source_attribution: false   # also the default since #1584
```

```console
$ apm compile --target codex
$ cat AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI from distributed .apm/ primitives -->
<!-- Build ID: f4429da3a4a0 -->
<!-- APM Version: 0.28.0 -->

## Files matching `**`

Demo rule body.

---
*This file was generated by APM CLI. Do not edit manually.*
*To regenerate: `apm compile`*
```

The same project compiled with `--target claude` honours the default correctly and emits only the load-bearing lines:

```console
$ apm compile --target claude
$ cat CLAUDE.md
# CLAUDE.md
<!-- Generated by APM CLI -->
<!-- Build ID: 9c31e7202c55 -->

## Project Standards
...
```

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Gate the two cosmetic blocks in `DistributedAgentsCompiler._generate_agents_content` on `source_attribution`, exactly as the Claude path already does:

- `src/apm_cli/compilation/distributed_compiler.py:655` -- `<!-- APM Version: ... -->`
- `src/apm_cli/compilation/distributed_compiler.py:680-682` -- the `---` / `*This file was generated by APM CLI. Do not edit manually.*` / `*To regenerate: apm compile*` footer

Reference implementation: `src/apm_cli/compilation/claude_formatter.py:299-300` and `:338-343`.

The flag value already reaches this code path, so the change looks self-contained: `agents_compiler.py:571` passes `source_attribution` into `distributed_config`, and `distributed_compiler.py:180` reads it into `placement.source_attribution`, where it currently only drives the `<!-- Sources: -->` line and the per-instruction source comments.

**Load-bearing lines that should stay unconditional**

Mirroring the Claude path, these two should keep being emitted regardless of the flag:

- `AGENTS_MD_GENERATED_MARKER` (`distributed_compiler.py:653`) -- `_find_orphaned_agents_files` only ever deletes files bearing it (`_file_has_apm_marker`, `distributed_compiler.py:783-796`), so dropping it would make `apm compile --clean` silently stop cleaning orphaned `AGENTS.md`.
- `BUILD_ID_PLACEHOLDER` (`distributed_compiler.py:654`) -- normalized away by drift detection (`utils/normalization.py:22`).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Setting `compilation.source_attribution: false` in `apm.yml` -- verified to have no effect on this path (it is already the default).
- No CLI flag, `apm config` key, or environment variable covers it; `apm compile --help` on 0.28.0 exposes nothing equivalent.
- Post-processing `AGENTS.md` after compile -- clobbered by the next `apm compile` (verified), and stripping the header marker breaks `--clean` as described above.

**Additional context**

apm 0.28.0 (`e041462`), macOS arm64. All line numbers above are against tag `v0.28.0`.

issues.title: [BUG] Hook rewriting silently skips `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/path` — a quote between the variable and the separator defeats the matcher (residual gap from #1310)
issues.body:
## Summary

`_rewrite_command_for_target` only recognises a plugin-root reference when a path separator follows the closing brace **immediately**. A hook command that closes the quote first —

```json
"command": "python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/hooks/probe.py"
```

— is not matched, so the script is never copied, the command is never rewritten, and **no warning is emitted**. `apm install` exits 0 and reports success. The raw `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` lands in `~/.claude/settings.json`, where Claude Code refuses it, producing the exact error from #1310 on every matching tool call:

> `PreToolUse:Bash hook error` — Failed to run: Hook command references `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` but the hook is not associated with a plugin. This variable is only available in hooks defined in a plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` file, not in settings.json files.

#1310 is closed and its fix works for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/path`. This is the residual case that fix does not cover. `"${VAR}"/path` is valid, idiomatic shell — it quotes the part that can contain spaces — so plugin authors write it and get a silently dead hook.

## Root cause

`apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py:652` (v0.28.0):

```python
plugin_root_pattern = (
    r"\$\{(?:CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT|CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT|KIRO_PLUGIN_ROOT|PLUGIN_ROOT)\}"
    r"([\\/][^\s\"']+)"
)
for match in re.finditer(plugin_root_pattern, command):
    ...
    if source_file.exists() and source_file.is_file():
        ...copy + rewrite...
    else:
        _rich_warning(f"Hook script not found: {source_file}")
```

The group requires `[\\/]` right after `\}`. With a `"` there, `finditer` yields nothing.

Note that the "file not found" warning lives **inside the loop body**, so a command the pattern cannot match produces no diagnostic at all. The failure is completely silent — which is why this can sit undetected indefinitely.

## Reproduction

Self-contained, no external marketplace. Two plugins identical except for one quote position.

```
probe/
  .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
  plugins/probe-broken/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
  plugins/probe-broken/hooks/hooks.json
  plugins/probe-broken/hooks/probe.py
  plugins/probe-fixed/...          # same, different hooks.json
```

`plugins/probe-broken/hooks/hooks.json`:
```json
{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[
  {"type":"command","command":"python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/hooks/probe.py"}]}]}}
```

`plugins/probe-fixed/hooks/hooks.json` — identical but for the closing quote:
```json
{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"Bash","hooks":[
  {"type":"command","command":"python3 \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/probe.py\""}]}]}}
```

```console
$ git -C probe init -b main && git -C probe add -A && git -C probe commit -m probe
$ apm marketplace add ./probe --name probe
$ apm install probe-broken@probe probe-fixed@probe -g -t claude
[*] Installed 2 APM dependencies in 0.1s.        # exit 0, no warnings
```

**Actual** — `~/.claude/settings.json`:

```
python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/probe.py                 <- unrewritten, hook is dead
python3 "$HOME/.claude/hooks/probe-fixed/hooks/probe.py"       <- correct
```

Only `probe-fixed`'s script is copied under `~/.claude/hooks/`. `probe-broken` deploys nothing and says nothing.

**Expected** — either both rewritten, or at minimum a warning that a plugin-root reference was found and not resolved.

## Suggested fix, and a trap in the obvious version

Naively widening the group to accept an optional quote (`\}["']?([\\/]...)`) produces a **broken command**: `full_var` then spans `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/probe.py`, and substituting the resolved path leaves the *opening* quote dangling —

```
python3 "/abs/path/hooks/probe.py      # unbalanced
```

A minimal safe fix is to normalise the quote pair before the existing matcher runs — rewrite `"${VAR}"/rest` to `"${VAR}/rest"` — which turns the unsupported spelling into the spelling that is already handled and already tested. Same for `'`.

Independently, moving the "not found" warning so that *any* unresolved plugin-root reference is reported would have surfaced this at install time rather than at every subsequent tool call.

## Environment

- apm 0.28.0 (78e05bb56f), Homebrew, Python 3.14
- macOS (arm64)
- user scope (`-g`), target `claude`

Related: #1310 (same symptom, fixed for the unquoted spelling), #1894 (per-package hook opt-out — would provide the missing workaround).

issues.title: apm audit always reports drift on .claude/settings.json if the project has its own hooks
issues.body:
**Version:** apm 0.26.0 (`64a7fb5`)

If my project already has hooks in `.claude/settings.json` and I install a plugin
that also has hooks, `apm audit --ci` fails from then on. It reports
`.claude/settings.json` as modified every single time.

`apm install` isn't the problem -- it merges fine and doesn't touch anything of
mine. It's the drift check: it compares the whole file against a replay of just
the packages, and that replay can't contain my hooks, so the file always looks
modified.

The error message says to run `apm install` to re-sync, but that doesn't help --
it re-merges correctly and the drift comes straight back.

## Repro

```bash
mkdir repro && cd repro
cat > apm.yml <<'EOF'
name: repro
version: 0.1.0
description: drift repro
author: x
targets:
  - claude
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: DietrichGebert/ponytail
      ref: ^4.9.0
      targets: [claude]
  mcp: []
includes: auto
scripts: {}
EOF

# my own hook, nothing to do with APM
mkdir -p .claude
echo '{"hooks":{"PreToolUse":[{"matcher":"","hooks":[{"type":"command","command":".claude/hooks/mine.sh"}]}]}}' \
  > .claude/settings.json

apm install --target claude
apm audit --ci --no-policy
```

What I get:

```
│          │ drift  │ drift detected: 1 file(s): .claude/settings.json │
  drift details:
    - modified: .claude/settings.json
[x] 1 of 10 check(s) failed
```

Delete `.claude/settings.json`, run the exact same thing again, and it's
`All 10 check(s) passed`. That's the only difference. Any plugin with hooks does
this -- ponytail is just one that's public and easy to point at.

## A couple of things I noticed

`.claude/settings.json` doesn't appear anywhere in `apm.lock.yaml` -- not in
`deployed_files`, not under `deployments`, no hash. So a file with no ledger entry
is still getting reported as drifted.

Which sort of makes sense, because it isn't really a deployed file. APM edits it
in place and shares it with me. Diffing a shared file against a package-only
replay is always going to flag it.

I checked that install really is fine: I gave it a settings file with
`permissions`, `statusLine`, a `PreToolUse` entry and a `SessionStart` entry, and
all four came through untouched with the plugin's hooks added alongside.

## Why it matters

If your project has any hooks of its own -- a formatter, a secret scanner, a
pre-tool-use guard -- you can't install a plugin with hooks and keep
`apm audit --ci` passing. Since that's the documented CI gate, you end up having
to pick one or the other.

There's no way to take just the skills either. `--skill <name>` cuts down which
skills get deployed but the hooks still install.

## Possible fix

APM already writes `.claude/apm-hooks.json`, and every entry in it is tagged with
`_apm_source: "<package>"`. That looks like enough to diff only APM's own entries
and leave the rest of the file alone.

Other options if that doesn't fit:

- Store a hash of just the injected part in the lockfile and compare against that.
- Or mark merge targets as their own thing in the ledger and skip whole-file drift
  on them, so the check stops failing in a way nobody can act on.

Happy to test a patch against the repro if that helps.

issues.title: Add Kilo Code as a compile/install target
issues.body:
## Feature request

Add **Kilo Code** as a supported target for `apm compile` / `apm install`, alongside `claude`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `grok-build`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `windsurf`, and `kiro`.

- **Target slug:** `kilo`
- **Deploy root (project):** `.kilo/`
- **Detection signal:** `.kilo/` directory (distinct from existing `kiro` target's `.kiro/`)

## Target mapping

Sources: [skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills), [subagents](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents), [custom-modes](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-modes), [AGENTS.md](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/agents-md), [custom-instructions](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-instructions), [MCP](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code).

| Primitive | Global (user) | Project |
|---|---|---|
| Instructions (`AGENTS.md`) | `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` (root and distributed subdirectories) |
| Skills (`SKILL.md` trees) | `~/.agents/skills/` (shared) | `.agents/skills/` (shared) |
| Agents | `~/.config/kilo/agents/*.md` | `.kilo/agents/*.md` |
| Prompts / Commands | `~/.config/kilo/commands/*.md` | `.kilo/commands/*.md` |
| MCP Servers | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` | `.kilo/kilo.jsonc` |

- **Instructions:** Kilo reads root + per-directory `AGENTS.md` ([agents-md](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/agents-md)). `apm compile` → `AGENTS.md` (`agents` family, distributed by default per `applyTo:` globs); `apm compile -g` → `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md` ([custom-instructions](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-instructions)).
- **Skills:** Standard Agent Skills format — folder + `SKILL.md` with `name`, `description` frontmatter. Reuses the shared `.agents/skills/` path (following `opencode` / `codex` conventions) as Kilo scans `.agents/skills/` by default ([skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills)).
- **Agents:** Markdown + YAML frontmatter; body is system prompt; filename (minus `.md`) = agent name ([custom-modes](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-modes)).
- **Prompts / Commands:** Markdown workflow files located in `.kilo/commands/*.md` ([workflows](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager-workflows)).
- **MCP Servers:** Configured under the top-level `"mcp"` key in `kilo.jsonc` ([using-in-kilo-code](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code)).

### Notes on user-scope paths (`.config` used only where no alternative exists)

- **Global skills:** Follows `opencode` / `codex` convention and targets `~/.agents/skills/` ([skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills)).
- **Global agents, commands, and instructions:** Currently have no Home-relative documented location — all live in `~/.config/kilo/` ([subagents](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents), [custom-instructions](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-instructions)).

## Key facts

1. **Skills reuse `.agents/skills/`:** Kilo automatically scans `EXTERNAL_DIRS = [".claude", ".agents"]` → `~/.agents/skills/` (global) and `.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md` up the project tree ([skills](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/skills)). APM's existing `.agents/skills/` deploy is picked up without requiring duplicate deployments to `.kilo/skills/`.
2. **Agents require native deployment:** Agent files are discovered from `.kilo/agents/` (project) and `~/.config/kilo/agents/` (global) ([subagents](https://kilo.ai/docs/customize/custom-subagents)).
3. **MCP integration:** `apm install --mcp` writes server configurations to `.kilo/kilo.jsonc` (bootstrapping the file if it does not exist) or `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` at global scope.

## Registration

- Add `kilo` to `apm.yml` `targets:` validation, `apm targets` table, and `--target` / `--all` catalog (non-explicit ⇒ included in `all`).
- Targets matrix: project root `.kilo/`; `instructions` via `AGENTS.md`; `agents` → `.kilo/agents/*.md`; `prompts` → `.kilo/commands/*.md`; `skills` → reused `.agents/skills/`; `mcp` → `.kilo/kilo.jsonc`.
- User-scope compile → `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md`.
- Tests mirroring `opencode` / `kiro` target tests.

## Config / env surface

- Config: global `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` (Windows `C:\Users\<user>\.config\kilo\kilo.jsonc`), project `./.kilo/kilo.jsonc` or `./kilo.jsonc` ([settings](https://kilo.ai/docs/getting-started/settings), [CLI](https://kilo.ai/docs/cli)).
- Extra skill dirs: `skills.paths` / `skills.urls` in `kilo.jsonc`.
- Env overrides: `KILO_CONFIG`, `KILO_CONFIG_DIR`, `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT`, `KILO_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS` ([CLI](https://kilo.ai/docs/cli), [architecture](https://kilo.ai/docs/contributing/architecture/cli-runtime)).

## Testing

- `.kilo/` activates `kilo`; no collision with `.kiro/`.
- `apm compile -t kilo` → `AGENTS.md` (root and distributed); `apm compile -g` → `~/.config/kilo/AGENTS.md`.
- `apm install -t kilo` → `.kilo/agents/*.md`, `.kilo/commands/*.md`, and skills via `.agents/skills/`.
- `apm install --mcp <name> -t kilo` → writes to `.kilo/kilo.jsonc` (bootstrapped if absent).
- `apm targets --json` lists `kilo`.
- Manual verification: `kilo` CLI picks up skills, subagents, commands, and MCP servers.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-20
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-20
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (8993dcc)
**Commands Inspected**: 29

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### README `--transport http` comment claims HTTPS
- **Command**: `apm install --mcp`
- **Problem**: The README example uses `--transport http` with the comment `# connects over HTTPS`. The `http` value is the MCP transport *protocol type* (not the URL scheme). The comment conflates the MCP transport name `http` with the HTTPS URL scheme, which could mislead users into thinking `--transport http` guarantees TLS. The actual security of the connection depends on the URL in the registry entry, not the transport type name.
- **Evidence** (README.md line):
  ```
  apm install --mcp io.github.github/github-mcp-server --transport http   # connects over HTTPS
  ```
  CLI help for `--transport`:
  ```
  --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
                  MCP transport (stdio, http, sse, streamable-http). Inferred
                  from --url or post-- command when omitted (requires --mcp).
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Change the comment to clarify that HTTPS comes from the registry entry URL, not the transport name. For example:
  ```
  apm install --mcp io.github.github/github-mcp-server --transport http   # registry entry resolves to an HTTPS URL
  ```
  Or omit the comment entirely since it is inferred by the registry.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm runtime remove --yes` uses awkward description
- **Command**: `apm runtime remove`
- **Problem**: The `-y, --yes` flag description says "Confirm the action without prompting", which is contradictory: "confirm" implies an acknowledgment, but "without prompting" means the user never sees the confirmation. Every other command with this flag uses "Skip confirmation prompt" or "Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)".
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm runtime remove --help
  -y, --yes  Confirm the action without prompting

  # apm deps clean --help
  -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt

  # apm update --help
  -y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Change `apm runtime remove` description to `Skip confirmation prompt` to match the pattern used by `apm deps clean` and `apm update`.

---

#### `apm deps why --help` examples run together on one line
- **Command**: `apm deps why`
- **Problem**: The help text examples are concatenated on a single line with no visual separation, making them hard to read in a terminal.
- **Evidence** (`apm deps why --help` description field):
  ```
  Explain why a package is installed by walking the lockfile back to one or
  more direct dependencies that pulled it in.

  Examples:   apm deps why shared-utils   apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils
  --json   apm deps why shared-utils --global
  ```
  The three example commands are all on one line separated by spaces rather than being on separate lines.
- **Suggested Fix**: Place each example on its own line in the help string (use `\n` separators or a proper `Examples:` Click epilog block), e.g.:
  ```
  Examples:
    apm deps why shared-utils
    apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils --json
    apm deps why shared-utils --global
  ```

---

#### `--verbose` flag descriptions are inconsistent across commands
- **Commands**: multiple
- **Problem**: The per-command `-v, --verbose` flag has slightly different descriptions across commands.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm mcp search / mcp show / mcp list:  "Show detailed output"
  apm install:                            "Show detailed installation information"
  apm uninstall:                          "Show detailed removal information"
  apm update:                             "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"
  apm compile:                            "Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"
  apm deps update:                        "Show detailed update information"
  apm init:                               "Show detailed output"
  apm run:                                "Show detailed output"
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Low priority -- the variations are contextually appropriate. Consider aligning the generic cases to one canonical phrasing such as `Show detailed output` for commands where the verbose behavior is not substantially different from that default.

---

### Clean Areas

- **All 29 commands responded to `--help`** without crash or traceback.
- **Error handling** is consistent: invalid flags and missing required arguments all produce clean `Usage:` + `Error:` messages with no stack traces.
- **`apm mcp` subcommand count** matches documentation exactly (list, search, show, install).
- **`apm runtime` subcommand count** matches documentation exactly (setup, list, status, remove).
- **`apm deps` subcommand count** matches documentation exactly (list, tree, info, why, update, clean).
- **`apm config` subcommand count** matches documentation exactly (get, list, set, unset).
- **No undocumented CLI commands** and **no documented commands missing from CLI** -- full symmetry between `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` and the live CLI.
- **`--dry-run` flag** is present and consistently named across all commands that support it.
- **`-g, --global` flag** is consistently named and described across deps, install, uninstall, update, compile, config, and runtime commands.
- **`apm mcp list` default `--limit`** (20) and **`apm mcp search` default `--limit`** (10) both match their documentation.
- **`apm deps update` deprecation** is consistently flagged in both CLI help text and documentation.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-08-21 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-21

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [C] Unconditional Expensive Operation -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:874-875

- Current: O(F x P) filesystem syscalls -- `file_path.resolve()` and
  `self.base_dir.resolve()` are called inside `_file_matches_pattern` for
  every (file, `**`-pattern) pair. `self.base_dir` is already a resolved path
  (set at construction, line 144), so `self.base_dir.resolve()` is a redundant
  syscall on every call. `file_path.resolve()` repeats for every file that
  reaches the `**` branch, even though file paths are constructed once during
  `_analyze_project_structure`.
- Proposed: O(1) base-dir resolve (use `self.base_dir` directly) + O(F) total
  file-path resolves (pre-compute once during `_analyze_project_structure`).
- Fix: Store resolved file paths in `_files_by_directory` during
  `_analyze_project_structure` and replace `self.base_dir.resolve()` with
  `self.base_dir` at line 875; `_file_matches_pattern` then needs no syscalls
  on the `**` branch.

#### [C] Unconditional Expensive Operation -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:1406

- Current: O(D x depth x I) `Path.resolve()` syscalls -- `_is_instruction_relevant`
  calls `working_directory.resolve()` (line 1406) for every non-global instruction.
  Its sole caller, `analyze_context_inheritance`, passes the same `working_directory`
  for all inner-loop iterations (lines 341-349), so the resolve is repeated
  O(depth x I) times per directory, and `_calculate_optimization_stats` calls
  `analyze_context_inheritance` for every directory D in the project, giving
  O(D x depth x I) redundant resolves during the stats phase.
- Proposed: O(D) `resolve()` calls total for the stats pass.
- Fix: Compute `resolved_working_dir = working_directory.resolve()` once at the
  top of `analyze_context_inheritance` and pass the pre-resolved path into
  `_is_instruction_relevant` (add a `resolved_working_dir` parameter or hoist
  the resolve into the caller).

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (430 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-08-21
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-21
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (8993dcc)
**Commands Inspected**: 52 (33 top-level + 19 subcommands across `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 0     |
| Medium   | 4     |
| Low      | 3     |

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `--verbose` flag description is inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` / `-v` flag uses different descriptions across commands with no consistent pattern.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm init:        -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
  apm install:     -v, --verbose    Show detailed installation information
  apm uninstall:   -v, --verbose    Show detailed removal information
  apm update:      -v, --verbose    Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics
  apm compile:     -v, --verbose    Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis
  apm run:         -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
  apm mcp search:  -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
  apm mcp show:    -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
  apm mcp list:    -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
  apm deps update: -v, --verbose    Show detailed update information
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Establish a standard template: either a generic `Show detailed output` for all commands (acceptable when the command name already provides context), or a consistent pattern like `Show detailed <COMMAND> output` (e.g., `Show detailed install output`, `Show detailed update output`). Either pick a uniform short form or a uniform expanded form — mixing the two is confusing.

---

#### 2. `--yes` / `-y` flag description is inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: `apm init`, `apm update`, `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The `--yes` flag uses three different description wordings.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm init:       -y, --yes   Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults
  apm update:     -y, --yes   Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)
  apm deps clean: -y, --yes   Skip confirmation prompt
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to one form, e.g., `Skip the confirmation prompt`. The context-specific wording in `apm init` could be kept since it does more than skip a prompt, but `apm update` vs `apm deps clean` should be identical.

---

#### 3. `compile --help` omits the deprecation of `--target all`

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: The docs state `--target all also emits a deprecation warning -- prefer --all`, but the CLI `--help` text for `--all` only says `Equivalent to --target all` without mentioning that `--target all` is deprecated in favor of `--all`. Users reading only the help text will not know that `--target all` is the deprecated form.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI `--help` output: `--all    Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to --target all.`
  - Docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md` line 74-75): `--target all also emits a deprecation warning -- prefer --all.`
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--all` flag description in CLI help to: `Compile for all canonical targets. Preferred form; '--target all' is deprecated and emits a warning.`

---

#### 4. `mcp search --limit` default in docs does not match `mcp list --limit` default

- **Commands**: `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp list`
- **Problem**: The docs `mcp.md` header synopsis groups both commands under `--limit N` with no default stated, which is fine. However, the defaults differ between the two commands and this asymmetry is not called out anywhere in the docs or help text.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm mcp search --help:  --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]
  apm mcp list --help:    --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 20]
  ```
  - Docs for `mcp search`: `--limit N  Number of results to show. Default: 10.` (matches CLI)
  - Docs for `mcp list`: `--limit N  Number of results to show. Default: 20.` (matches CLI)
  - The asymmetry (10 vs 20) is undocumented and surprising to users who expect the two sibling commands to share the same default.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either align the defaults (both `10` or both `20`), or add a note to the `mcp list` docs and help text explaining why the default is higher (e.g., paginated browsing vs targeted search).

---

### Low Severity

#### 5. `--dry-run` descriptions are inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: Minor wording differences across the dry-run descriptions, mixing "Show what would..." vs "Preview...".
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  apm install:    --dry-run   Show what would be installed without installing
  apm uninstall:  --dry-run   Preview removal plan (pre-uninstall scripts still run)
  apm update:     --dry-run   Render the update plan and exit without changing anything
  apm compile:    --dry-run   Preview compilation without writing files (shows placement decisions)
  apm deps clean: --dry-run   Show what would be removed without removing
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize the opening verb. Either all use `Show what would...` or all use `Preview...`. The parenthetical detail in `uninstall` (pre-uninstall scripts still run) and `compile` (shows placement decisions) is useful and can be retained.

---

#### 6. `config` has an `unset` subcommand not mentioned in task docs

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Not a bug — `apm config unset` exists in both the CLI and the reference documentation and works correctly. However, the `apm config --help` output lists `unset` as a subcommand, while several internal workflow references only enumerate `get`, `set`, `list`. This is a minor discoverability gap.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config --help
  Commands:
    get    Get a configuration value
    list   List all configuration values
    set    Set a configuration value
    unset  Unset a configuration value
  ```
  The `config.md` docs do correctly document `apm config unset KEY`. No fix needed in the product itself.
- **Suggested Fix**: No code change needed. Confirm internal workflow checklists include `unset`.

---

#### 7. `apm install` description is unusually long and parenthetical

- **Command**: `apm install`
- **Problem**: The one-line description in `--help` is significantly longer and more complex than other commands, combining multiple concerns into a single sentence.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Install APM, MCP, and LSP dependencies (supports APM packages, Claude skills
  (SKILL.md), and plugin collections (plugin.json); auto-creates apm.yml; use
  --allow-insecure for (redacted) packages)
  ```
  Compare with peers:
  ```
  apm uninstall: Remove packages using manifest entries or direct locked keys from 'apm deps list'
  apm update:    Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
  apm compile:   Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Shorten to `Install APM packages, MCP servers, and LSP dependencies` and move the parenthetical details (SKILL.md, plugin.json, --allow-insecure hint) to the extended help text or examples section.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- **Command/docs parity**: All 33 top-level CLI commands have a corresponding doc page in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`, and vice versa. No phantom or orphaned entries.
- **Exit behavior**: Invalid flags and missing required arguments produce clean `Error:` messages with usage hints and exit code `2` — no stack traces.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works on every inspected command and subcommand.
- **`-g` / `--global` flag**: Consistently named and described across `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`, `deps clean`.
- **`--dry-run` presence**: Present on all mutating commands where expected (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`).
- **Deprecated commands**: `apm deps update` and `apm unpack` clearly self-identify as deprecated in their descriptions with actionable migration instructions.
- **`apm mcp install`**: Correctly documented as an alias with forwarded flags listed inline.
- **`apm runtime`**: All four subcommands (`setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove`) are present in CLI and documented.
- **`apm deps why`**: Present in CLI and documented in `deps.md`.
- **Target value lists**: Consistent across `install`, `update`, `compile`, `deps update`.
- **`--target` / `--runtime` deprecation note**: Clearly explained in `install --help`.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-08-22 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-22

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
3 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [E] Heavy Top-Level Imports on Every CLI Invocation -- src/apm_cli/cli.py:27-56

- Current: O(n_imports) startup cost for ALL sub-commands. cli.py eagerly imports
  every command module at startup, including `commands/install.py` with 41 top-level
  imports (artifactory_resolver, gitlab_resolver, insecure_policy, package_resolution,
  package_selection, validation, transaction, and more). Every `apm list`, `apm config`,
  or `apm run` invocation pays the full install-machinery import cost.
- Proposed: O(1) startup for commands that do not use install machinery, by deferring
  command module imports until the sub-command is actually invoked.
- Fix: Replace the eager `from apm_cli.commands.install import install` pattern in
  cli.py with Click lazy-loading (e.g., a LazyGroup or a factory that defers each
  command module import inside a `@cli.command()` callback), so sub-command modules
  are only imported when selected.

#### [A] Double-Pass Partition of Remote Refs -- src/apm_cli/deps/git_remote_ops.py:107-108

- Current: O(2n) -- `sort_remote_refs` iterates the `refs` list twice: once to collect
  tags, once to collect branches. Called on every git remote discovery operation.
- Proposed: O(n) -- single-pass partition into tags and branches in one loop.
- Fix: Replace the two list comprehensions with a single loop that appends to
  `tags` or `branches` based on `ref_type`, removing the second pass entirely.

#### [B] O(n*m) Prefix Scan on Deployed Files -- src/apm_cli/bundle/lockfile_enrichment.py:150

- Current: O(n*m) -- `[f for f in deployed_files if any(f.startswith(p) for p in prefixes)]`
  evaluates up to m prefix checks per file, where n = len(deployed_files) and
  m = len(prefixes). For a large bundle with many targets this degrades linearly
  with the prefix count.
- Proposed: O(n * k) where k is average prefix length, using sorted prefixes and
  bisect to skip non-matching ranges, or accept O(n*m) if m is always small (2-4
  elements for current target set).
- Fix: Document the target-set size contract in the function docstring so a future
  contributor knows m is bounded; if the target count grows, switch to a trie or
  sorted-prefix binary search to keep the scan sub-linear. Low priority while m <= 4.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (430 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [BUG] uninstall orphans tracked files when removed package target differs from surviving manifest targets
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a global manifest already persists one target, a later package can be installed to another target with `--target`. APM deploys that package correctly, but `apm uninstall --global` resolves cleanup targets only from the surviving manifest after removing the package.

If the removed package's deployment target is absent from that surviving target set, its files are not visited. Uninstall still exits successfully and deletes the package's manifest, module, lockfile, and deployment-ledger entries. The files become untracked orphans with no warning and cannot be cleaned by rerunning uninstall because the package is no longer declared.

I reproduced this with a surviving `agent-skills` package and a removed OpenCode agent. The issue is not OpenCode-specific in the observed logic; OpenCode makes the mismatch easy to demonstrate because its user-scope agent path is distinct from `.agents/skills/`.

**To Reproduce**

Create two minimal local packages under an isolated home:

```bash
ROOT="$(mktemp -d)"
export HOME="$ROOT/home"
mkdir -p "$HOME" "$ROOT/work"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/survivor/.apm/skills/survivor"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/removed/.apm/agents"

cat > "$ROOT/survivor/apm.yml" <<'EOF'
name: survivor
version: "1.0.0"
description: Keeps agent-skills as the persisted global target.
author: repro
license: MIT
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp: []
includes:
  - .apm/skills/
scripts: {}
EOF

cat > "$ROOT/survivor/.apm/skills/survivor/SKILL.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: survivor
description: Remains installed during the reproduction.
---

# Survivor
EOF

cat > "$ROOT/removed/apm.yml" <<'EOF'
name: removed
version: "1.0.0"
description: Deploys one agent to a different global target.
author: repro
license: MIT
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp: []
includes:
  - .apm/agents/
scripts: {}
EOF

cat > "$ROOT/removed/.apm/agents/orphan.agent.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: orphan-agent
description: Must be removed when its package is uninstalled.
---

This agent should not survive package removal.
EOF

cd "$ROOT/work"
apm install "$ROOT/survivor" --target agent-skills --global
apm install "$ROOT/removed" --target opencode --global
```

At this point `~/.apm/apm.yml` still declares only:

```yaml
targets:
  - agent-skills
```

The second install correctly created `~/.config/opencode/agents/orphan.md`, and the removed dependency's lock entry and deployment ledger recorded that path.

Uninstall the second package:

```bash
apm uninstall "$ROOT/removed" --global --verbose
```

The command exits successfully:

```text
[i] Uninstalling from user scope (~/.apm/)
[>] Uninstalling 1 package(s)...
[+] _local/removed - found in apm.yml
[i] Removed _local/removed from dependencies.apm in apm.yml
[*] Updated ~/.apm/apm.yml (removed 1 package(s))
[i] Removed _local/removed from apm_modules/
    Path: _local/removed
[*] Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml, Removed 1 package(s) from apm_modules/
```

Afterward:

```bash
test -f "$HOME/.config/opencode/agents/orphan.md"  # still succeeds
```

The survivor skill remains as expected. The removed package is absent from `apm.yml`, `apm.lock.yaml`, and `apm_modules`, and the lockfile no longer mentions `.config/opencode/agents/orphan.md`.

**Expected behavior**

Uninstall should remove every tracked file owned only by the removed package, including files deployed to a target that is not present in the post-removal manifest target set. If cleanup cannot be completed, uninstall should retain recoverable ownership state and return a non-zero result rather than reporting success.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: CachyOS Linux, x86_64
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.28.0 (`e041462`)
- VSCode Version: not relevant

**Logs**

The complete relevant uninstall log is included in the reproduction above. No cleanup warning is emitted and no integrated-agent cleanup count is reported.

**Additional context**

In current `src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py`, `_sync_integrations_after_uninstall()` resolves one `_resolved_targets` set from the post-removal `apm_package.canonical_targets`. `all_deployed_files` is partitioned across known target prefixes, but Phase 1 file cleanup iterates only `_resolved_targets`. Removed-dependency deployment-ledger targets do not augment that loop. Phase 2 survivor reintegration appropriately uses the surviving target set, but Phase 1 cleanup needs the removed deployment target provenance as well.

A fix could separate the Phase 1 cleanup target set, derived from tracked removed-package deployments, from the Phase 2 survivor target set, derived from the surviving manifest. This report concerns per-file tracked cleanup. It is related to target-scope issues such as #2250 and the orphan symptom in #2558, but has a different reproduction and root cause.

issues.title: [BUG] apm lock export --timestamp accepts invalid values without error
issues.body:
### Bug Summary

The `--timestamp` option in `apm lock export` lacks validation for ISO 8601 formatting. Consequently, arbitrary or malformed string values are accepted without error and embedded directly into the generated CycloneDX/SPDX Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) metadata. This causes silent generation of non-compliant SBOM artifacts that fail downstream schema verification.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Execute `apm lock export` with an invalid timestamp string:
   ```bash
   apm lock export --timestamp "not-a-date"
   ```
2. Observe that the command executes successfully (exit code 0) without any validation warnings or errors.

Other malformed inputs that bypass validation:
```bash
apm lock export --timestamp "   "
apm lock export --timestamp "99999-99-99"
apm lock export --timestamp "2024-13-45T99:99:99Z"
apm lock export --timestamp "hello world"
```

### Expected Behavior

The CLI should validate the timestamp against the ISO 8601 specification before generating the export artifact and fail gracefully on invalid input:

```
Error: Invalid value for '--timestamp': 'not-a-date' is not a valid ISO 8601 datetime (e.g. 2024-06-01T00:00:00+00:00).
```

### Environment

 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.0
 - APM Version: 0.28.0

### Command Output / Evidence

Output excerpt from `apm lock export --timestamp "not-a-date"`:

```json
"metadata": {
  "timestamp": "not-a-date"
}
```

The command terminates with exit status 0 despite generating an invalid ISO 8601 timestamp in the specification metadata.

### Technical Details & Root Cause

The CLI documentation explicitly defines the expected format:
> *"Pin the SBOM timestamp (ISO 8601, e.g. 2024-06-01T00:00:00+00:00) for reproducible output."*

However, in `src/apm_cli/commands/lock.py`, the helper `_resolve_export_timestamp` returns user input verbatim without checking specification compliance:

```python
def _resolve_export_timestamp(explicit: str | None, ...) -> str:
    if explicit:
        return explicit  # Bypasses ISO 8601 validation
```

Validating the string via `datetime.fromisoformat()` prior to serialization will prevent silent output corruption.

issues.title: [BUG] load_frontmatter misinterprets middle horizontal rules (---) as YAML frontmatter
issues.body:
**Description of the Bug**

In `src/apm_cli/utils/yaml_io.py`, `load_frontmatter()` misinterprets Markdown section dividers (`---`) in documentation files as YAML frontmatter boundaries.

When a `.md`, `.instructions.md`, or `.agent.md` file contains two or more `---` horizontal rules in its text body (without a Line 1 frontmatter header), APM attempts to parse the document body between the dividers as YAML metadata. This causes PyYAML to raise a `yaml.scanner.ScannerError`, causing APM to log a warning and silently discard the instruction file during `apm install`.

**High Severity User Impact**

- **Ecosystem-Wide Failure (Affects ALL Packages):** This bug affects **ANY package** across the APM ecosystem whose Markdown documentation uses `---` section dividers between text or code sections.
- **Data Loss During `apm install`:** In official dependencies like `github/awesome-copilot` (declared on Line 30 of `microsoft/apm`'s `apm.yml`), **209 out of 1,758 Markdown files (11.9%)** fail to parse and are **completely dropped during installation**.
- **Incomplete AI Context:** Users run `apm install` expecting full package delivery, but 1 out of every 9 instruction files is silently omitted from their AI editor (VS Code Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code).

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a Markdown instruction file in any package with no top frontmatter that includes two `---` horizontal rules separating sections with code blocks.
2. Run `apm install` on the package containing this file.
3. Observe the warning: `Warning: Failed to parse dependency primitive...: while scanning for the next token found character '`'`
4. Note that the instruction file is discarded and not deployed to `.github/instructions/`.

**Expected behavior**

APM should verify that a Markdown file begins with `---` on **Line 1** before splitting frontmatter. If Line 1 does not start with `---`, `load_frontmatter()` should treat the file as having no frontmatter and preserve the full content intact.

**Environment**
- OS: macOS / Linux / Windows
- Python: 3.12.0
- APM Version: 0.28.0

**Additional Context**

Adding `text.lstrip().startswith("---")` in `load_frontmatter()` before splitting guarantees frontmatter is only parsed when explicitly present at the start of the file, resolving all 209 file parsing failures in `github/awesome-copilot` and preventing dropped instructions across all packages.

issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-23

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [B] Linear scan inside nested loop -- security/executables.py:267-288 and 747-755

- Current: O(K * E * C * G) -- `_map_grants` iterates all entries of each grant_map
  dict (O(G)) including calling `_strip_version(stored_key)` per entry. Called C=4-6
  times per `resolve_exec_decision`, which is itself called inside a nested loop:
  `for key in candidate_keys: for exec_type in ALL_EXEC_TYPES` (lines 747-755) and
  a second nested loop at lines 779-782. K=candidate_keys, E=exec_types (~4),
  G=grant_map size.
- Proposed: O(K * E) after O(G) pre-build -- build a
  `{stripped_key: {exec_type: bool}}` index from each grant_map (user_allow,
  user_deny, project_allow, project_deny) once before the outer loop.
- Fix: In `_map_grants`, add an optional pre-built normalized-key index parameter;
  before the outer `for key in candidate_keys` loop, call a helper that produces
  `dict[str, dict[str, bool]]` keyed by `_strip_version(stored_key)` for each
  grant_map, then replace the linear scan with an O(1) dict lookup.

#### [B] O(n*m) prefix scan on deployed files -- bundle/lockfile_enrichment.py:151

- Current: O(n * m) -- `[f for f in deployed_files if any(f.startswith(p) for p
  in prefixes)]` iterates all deployed files (n) and for each file checks all
  target prefixes (m) until a match is found. Called during `apm pack` and bundle
  export operations.
- Proposed: O(n * log(m)) or amortised O(n) -- sort `prefixes` once and use
  `bisect` to find the longest candidate prefix per file, or group files by
  common prefix using a trie-like dict keyed on the first path segment.
- Fix: Sort `prefixes` by length descending once before the comprehension and
  break early; for large deployments, build a `{first_segment: [prefixes]}` dict
  to skip non-matching prefixes in O(1) per file. Low-priority: m is typically
  10-20 entries, so the fix matters mainly for deployments with hundreds of files.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (445 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [FEATURE] Preserve full Kiro custom-agent config when compiling to the kiro target
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'm always frustrated when I try to distribute a real Kiro custom (sub-)agent through APM and almost all of its configuration is silently thrown away.

APM's Kiro agent integrator emits only three frontmatter keys — `description`, `model`, and `tools` — and drops everything else the agent declared. A Kiro custom agent supports far more: `resources` (`file://` and `skill://` — how an agent attaches its own skills and reference files), `mcpServers` (inline MCP servers scoped to the agent), `allowedTools` and `excludedTools`, `permissions` (capability-scoped allow/ask/deny rules), `toolsSettings` (including `toolsSettings.subagent` for sub-agent gating), `toolAliases`, `hooks`, `includeMcpJson`, `includePowers`, `welcomeMessage`, and `keyboardShortcut`. Also `prompt`, which in Markdown form is carried by the file body — so instructions do survive — but a declared `prompt: file://…` in frontmatter does not.

None of the rest survive `apm install` to the `kiro` target, so the agent that lands in `.kiro/agents/` is a shell of what was authored: no tool boundary beyond the coarse `tools` list, no attached skills, no scoped MCP servers.

One further sharp edge makes this worse than "some fields are dropped":

**Fail-closed on a stale tool allow-list.** The integrator validates `tools:` against a hard-coded set and refuses to deploy the *entire* agent if any value falls outside it. That set is out of date relative to current Kiro: it rejects real, current tool identifiers — `grep` (alias of `grep_search`), `glob` (alias of `file_search`), `code`, `use_aws` (alias of `aws`), `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `introspect`, `tool_search`. It also conflates category tags with tool names: `web` and `context` are *tags* that expand to tool sets (`web` → `web_fetch` + `web_search`; `context` → `disclose_context` + `introspect` + `knowledge`), not tool identifiers — so the allow-list is validating two different vocabularies against one flat set. The practical result is that a valid agent using, say, `web_fetch` is *silently not deployed* — with only a diagnostic.

The net effect: **APM cannot today distribute a usable, fully-configured Kiro sub-agent.** This blocks the single most valuable packaging use case we have — shipping focused sub-agents (information-gatherer, code-reviewer, developer) *with their tool boundary, attached skills, and MCP servers* as one versioned unit.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Widen APM's Kiro agent support so a custom agent survives packaging intact:

1. **Pass through the full Kiro custom-agent field set** when compiling to the `kiro` target, rather than reducing to three keys. At minimum: `prompt`, `resources`, `mcpServers`, `allowedTools`, `excludedTools`, `permissions`, `toolsSettings`, `toolAliases`, `hooks`, `includeMcpJson`, `includePowers`, `welcomeMessage`, `keyboardShortcut` — in addition to the existing `description`, `model`, `tools`. Unknown/forward-compat keys should be preserved (pass-through), not dropped, so APM doesn't gate on a field list it has to chase.

   Note that `resources` is not a plain `string[]`: alongside `file://` and `skill://` URIs it accepts an object form (`{"type": "knowledgeBase", "source": …, "name": …, "indexType": …, "autoUpdate": …}`). Any passthrough implementation needs to preserve non-string entries and nested structures verbatim rather than assuming scalars.

2. **Fix (or remove) the tool allow-list.** Either update it to the current Kiro tool vocabulary — and model tags and tool names as distinct concepts, since `tools:` legitimately accepts tool names, category tags, `@server`/`@server/tool`, `@builtin`, `@mcp`, and `*` — or stop hard-validating tool identifiers against a baked-in set and pass them through, letting the harness be the authority. If validation stays, it must **warn and deploy**, not fail-closed and silently drop the whole agent.

3. **(Lower priority, not a blocker) Optional JSON agent output.** Current Kiro reads both `.kiro/agents/<name>.json` and `.kiro/agents/<name>.md` (YAML frontmatter for config, body as the system prompt), with identical field support and mixed formats allowed in one workspace — so APM's existing Markdown emit is correct, and arguably the better default since it carries the prompt as the body. A JSON emit path would still be useful for authors targeting Kiro CLI 2.x, where Markdown agents are not supported, and for agents whose config is easier to express as structured data. Treat this as an option, not a fix.

The goal: `apm install` produces a Kiro agent that is byte-for-byte usable — its tool boundary, attached skills (`resources: skill://…`), and MCP servers all intact — so a package can ship an agent + its dependencies as one governed, versioned, multi-target unit.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Hand-author the agent file outside APM** (commit `.kiro/agents/<name>.{md,json}` in the consuming repo, ship only skills+MCP via APM). Works today and is our current interim, but it forks the agent definition out of the package — it isn't versioned or governed with the rest of the bundle, defeating the point of a single distributable unit.
- **Package the agent as an Agent Plugin (`--format agent-plugin`).** Not possible: the Agent Plugins spec's component types are skills and MCP servers (Kiro additionally layers a vendor `dev.kiro/` directory for steering extensions), and agents and hooks are excluded. A Kiro **Power** — an installed Agent Plugin, for the current `plugin.json` format — is a payload an agent *consumes*, not an agent definition. So the portable-plugin path structurally cannot carry an agent.
- **Adopt/extend an in-house installer** (a verbatim copy-into-`.kiro/` tool) that preserves agent config by not transforming it. This does preserve fidelity, but it's Kiro-only, fails *open* (no validation — ships broken artifacts silently), and means owning a whole installer to work around one fixable passthrough gap in APM. We'd rather fix APM.
- **Wait for the Agent Plugins spec to add agents/hooks.** The spec's own design notes say these "remain too client-specific… until their formats converge" — no committed timeline. Not a near-term option.

**Additional context**

We want to distribute focused sub-agents (each with instructions, a tool boundary, attached skills, and scoped MCP servers — optionally hooks) as versioned packages across Kiro and, later, other harnesses. APM is otherwise exactly right for this (multi-target, pinned, governed, fail-closed validation); the Kiro agent passthrough is the one blocker.

The strongest argument for **pass-through-and-preserve over a curated field list** is that Kiro's own agent-config surface is still moving, and in places the documentation disagrees with itself. Two current examples:

- **`toolsSettings`** — the [agent configuration reference](https://kiro.dev/docs/custom-agents/configuration-reference.md) calls it deprecated but still supported for MCP tool-specific settings and for `toolsSettings.subagent` (`availableAgents` / `trustedAgents`), while the CLI 3.0 and 2.x-reference pages state it was *removed* in V3. Sub-agent gating is precisely our use case, and it currently sits on the disputed field.
- **Inline agent `hooks`** — the CLI and IDE field tables describe `hooks` as CLI-only ("IDE ignores agents containing this field"), the configuration reference's own Hooks section says both surfaces accept the format, and the [hooks migration guide](https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3/hooks-migration.md) labels the embedded-in-agent form "old format — do not use in 3.0," directing hooks to standalone `.kiro/hooks/*.json` with a versioned schema and PascalCase triggers.

There are also real, if narrower, cross-surface differences — `hooks` and `includePowers` are surface-specific, and the IDE 1.0 field table types `resources` as `string[]`, which doesn't accommodate the documented object form. An integrator that curates a field list has to track all of this and will lag it. One that preserves what the author wrote does not, and stays correct across CLI/IDE and across versions.

*(Kiro capability claims above are documentation-grounded against kiro.dev CLI v3 / IDE 1.0 at time of writing, not empirically re-verified against a pinned binary. Version-specific behaviour is worth confirming against whichever Kiro version APM decides to target.)*

---

*Second pass — indication of what may need to change in the APM codebase* (paths relative to the repo; verified against current `main`):

- **`src/apm_cli/integration/agent_integrator.py` — the core of the fix.**
  - `KIRO_AGENT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (a `frozenset`, ~line 31, comment "Fail closed: any value not in this set blocks deployment"): update to the current Kiro tool set — distinguishing tool identifiers from category tags and the `@server` / `@builtin` / `@mcp` / `*` selector forms — or drop the hard gate in favour of pass-through-with-warning.
  - `_preflight_render_kiro_agent(...)` (~line 520+): today it parses frontmatter, validates `tools` (returning `(None, False)` → skip the whole agent on any unknown tool), then rebuilds an **allow-listed** frontmatter in `out_fm_ordered` emitting **only** `description`, `model`, `tools` (~lines 607–615). This is the exact reduction point — it must be widened to carry the additional fields (or, better, switched to preserve the source frontmatter minus any genuinely incompatible keys), and the fail-closed branch changed to warn-and-continue. Preservation needs to be structure-preserving: `mcpServers`, `permissions.rules`, `toolsSettings`, and object-form `resources` entries are nested, not scalar.
  - `_write_kiro_agent(...)` / the `kiro_agent` branch in `integrate_agents_for_target(...)`: currently renders Markdown, which is valid for current Kiro — the change here is to widen the emitted frontmatter, not to replace the format. An optional JSON emit path (per solution #3) would slot in alongside it.

- **`src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py` — the target mapping.** The Kiro profile maps `"agents": PrimitiveMapping("agents", ".md", "kiro_agent")` (~line 607). This mapping is correct as-is for current Kiro; it only needs touching if optional JSON output lands, which would likely mean a new/parameterised mapping (and possibly a surface or version flag).

- **`src/apm_cli/primitives/models.py` — the data model.** The `Chatmode` dataclass (agents are parsed as chatmodes) currently has only `name, file_path, description, apply_to, content, author, version, source, handoffs`. There is **no field to carry** `resources`, `mcpServers`, `permissions`, `allowedTools`, `toolsSettings`, etc. Note the Kiro integrator re-reads *raw* frontmatter directly (so it isn't strictly bound by the model), but a clean fix probably adds a structured `agent_config` / passthrough dict to the model.

- **`src/apm_cli/primitives/parser.py` — `_parse_chatmode(...)` (~line 113).** It only extracts `description`, `applyTo`, `author`, `version`, `handoffs` from `metadata`; all other agent frontmatter keys are discarded at parse time. To preserve them end-to-end (not just in the Kiro integrator), capture the remaining frontmatter here.

- **Tests / fixtures.** Kiro agent integrator tests asserting the three-field output and the fail-closed tool behaviour will need updating. Add round-trip fixtures proving `resources` (both URI and object forms), `mcpServers`, `permissions`, and unknown/forward-compat keys survive to `.kiro/agents/*.md` with nested structure intact, plus a case asserting an agent using `web_fetch` (or another currently-rejected tool) deploys rather than being skipped.

- **Scope guard.** This is intentionally about **legacy per-primitive projection to the `kiro` target** (`apm install`), not the Agent Plugins (`--format agent-plugin`) path — agents remain out of scope for the portable plugin format by spec, and PR #2654's fail-closed plugin boundary should be left untouched.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-08-24 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-24

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [C] Redundant Path.resolve() on constant base_dir in _file_matches_pattern -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:875

- Current: O(n) redundant filesystem syscalls per instruction pattern -- `self.base_dir.resolve()` is called once per project file inside the inner file-match loop, even though `self.base_dir` is already resolved at construction time (line 144: `self.base_dir = Path(base_dir).resolve()`).
- Proposed: O(1) per pattern -- replace the redundant `.resolve()` call with a direct reference to `self.base_dir`, which is already an absolute resolved path.
- Fix: Change `resolved_file.relative_to(self.base_dir.resolve())` to `resolved_file.relative_to(self.base_dir)` at line 875; `self.base_dir` is already resolved and safe to use directly.

#### [C] Redundant Path.resolve() in _calculate_hierarchical_coverage nested loop -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:1248-1263

- Current: O(n*m) filesystem syscalls -- called from `_optimize_single_coverage_placement` (line 1021) as `for candidate in candidates` (n iterations), and inside `_calculate_hierarchical_coverage` each target (m) calls `_is_hierarchically_covered`, which calls `target_dir.resolve()` and `placement_dir.resolve()`. Each unique path is resolved n or m extra times instead of once.
- Proposed: O(n+m) resolutions -- pre-resolve all target and placement paths once before the outer loop and pass the resolved paths through.
- Fix: Before the `for candidate in candidates` loop, build `resolved_targets = {t: t.resolve() for t in matching_directories}`; update `_is_hierarchically_covered` to accept pre-resolved paths, eliminating redundant `resolve()` calls across n*m iterations.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (449 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [BUG] UTF-8 BOM on an instruction file silently drops its frontmatter: applyTo scope lost, metadata leaked into compiled output, exit 0
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A UTF-8 BOM on an instruction file silently drops its frontmatter. `apm compile` exits 0, the declared `applyTo` scope is lost so the rule is applied globally, and the raw frontmatter block is emitted verbatim into the compiled context file.

`load_frontmatter` reads with `encoding="utf-8"` (`src/apm_cli/utils/yaml_io.py:492`), not `utf-8-sig`, so the BOM survives as a literal `﻿` before the line-1 `---` and the fence no longer matches.

The BOM then propagates into the generated `CLAUDE.md`, where APM's own audit flags it: `CLAUDE.md contains 1 hidden character(s)`.

This is a Windows-shaped trigger. PowerShell 5.1's `Out-File -Encoding utf8` and `>` both write a BOM, as does Notepad, so a package authored on Windows can carry one without the author ever seeing it.

**To Reproduce**

Two instruction files, identical except for the BOM:

```python
fm = '---\ndescription: Scoped rule\napplyTo: "**/*.py"\n---\n# Style\nUse type hints.\n'
Path('.apm/instructions/nobom.instructions.md').write_bytes(fm.encode('utf-8'))
Path('.apm/instructions/withbom.instructions.md').write_bytes(fm.encode('utf-8-sig'))
```

```console
$ apm compile --target claude
[!]   .apm/instructions/withbom.instructions.md: No 'applyTo' pattern specified
-- instruction will apply globally
[!]   CLAUDE.md contains 1 hidden character(s) -- run 'apm audit --file ...' to inspect
$ echo $?
0
```

Generated `CLAUDE.md` puts the BOM'd file under `### Global Instructions` with its metadata as body text:

```
### Global Instructions

﻿---
description: Scoped rule
applyTo: "**/*.py"
---
# Style
```

while the identical no-BOM file lands correctly under `### Files matching **/*.py`.

**Expected behavior**

Decode with `utf-8-sig` so a leading BOM is consumed, or fail loudly rather than silently downgrading a scoped rule to global.

**Environment**

- OS: Windows 11 Home 26200
- Python: 3.13.13
- APM: 0.28.0, verified on `main` at `88cf78a`

**Additional context**

Not a regression from #2666, which touches this function: I ran the same case on `main` (`88cf78a`) and on that PR's head (`d27ed4e`) and both lose the frontmatter identically. #372 handled a BOM in `strip_dangerous` only; this is the loader path.

Related failure profile to #2663 and #2624: exit 0 with a quietly wrong result.

I used an AI assistant to prepare this report. I ran the reproduction, the exit code, and the two-ref comparison myself on the machine described above.

issues.title: [BUG] Admin-tier lifecycle policy dir hardcodes C:\ProgramData, so it silently loads nothing when Windows is not on C:
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`_get_policy_scripts_dir()` hardcodes the `C:` drive for the admin policy tier:

```python
# src/apm_cli/core/lifecycle_scripts.py:346-351
def _get_policy_scripts_dir() -> Path:
    """Return the platform-specific policy scripts directory."""
    system = platform.system()
    if system == "Windows":
        return Path(r"C:\ProgramData\APM\policy.d")
    return Path("/etc/apm/policy.d")
```

Windows does not define ProgramData as a constant. It is stored in the registry as an
*unexpanded* string and expanded at runtime:

```
> (Get-Item 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList').GetValue(
      'ProgramData', $null, 'DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames')
%SystemDrive%\ProgramData
```

So on a machine whose `%SystemDrive%` is not `C:`, apm reads the admin tier from a
directory that is not that machine's ProgramData. The failure is silent:
`_load_scripts_from_dir()` returns `[]` for a missing directory (line 373), with no
warning. Admin-tier lifecycle policy contributes zero scripts and the tier documented as
the trust anchor quietly does nothing.

The user tier in the same module already resolves from the environment
(`_get_user_apm_yml()` honours `APM_HOME`), so the two tiers disagree about whether
location is configurable.

**Expected behavior**

Resolve the directory from the environment rather than a literal, e.g.
`Path(os.environ.get("ProgramData", r"C:\ProgramData")) / "APM" / "policy.d"`.

**To Reproduce**

I could not reproduce end-user impact here: this machine's `%SystemDrive%` is `C:`, so the
hardcoded path happens to be correct. What I did verify by running it is that the function
ignores the environment entirely, while the user tier beside it does not:

```python
import os
from apm_cli.core import lifecycle_scripts as ls

print(ls._get_policy_scripts_dir())   # C:\ProgramData\APM\policy.d
os.environ["ProgramData"] = r"D:\ProgramData"
print(ls._get_policy_scripts_dir())   # C:\ProgramData\APM\policy.d   <- unchanged
os.environ["APM_HOME"] = r"D:\apm-home"
print(ls._get_user_apm_yml())         # D:\apm-home\apm.yml           <- follows env
```

**Environment**

- OS: Windows 11 Home
- Python Version: 3.13.13
- APM Version: 0.28.0 (`lifecycle_scripts.py` byte-identical to `main` @ `88cf78a`)

**Additional context**

No test references ProgramData, so the literal does not read as a deliberately pinned
choice. One judgement call belongs to you rather than to me: on a non-`C:` system that
already has scripts in `C:\ProgramData\APM\policy.d`, switching to the environment would
stop reading them. That is why this is an issue and not a patch.

Written with AI assistance. On this machine I ran the probe above and the registry query,
and read `_get_policy_scripts_dir` and `_load_scripts_from_dir` in full; I have not tested
on an install whose SystemDrive is not `C:`, and have not claimed otherwise above.
