issues.title: [FEATURE] Deploy an Agent Plugin's skills/ to non-Copilot targets
issues.body:
## Summary A package that intentionally selects the Agent Plugins v1.0.0 layout reaches Copilot only. Its `skills/` are never deployed to `claude`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`, `opencode` or `windsurf`, even though the identical `skills/` tree deploys to all of them when the package selects the APM layout instead. I would like selecting the portable format to cost nothing in target coverage. ## Current behaviour Measured against `main` at `cfee65d`, built from source. Two packages with an identical `skills/` tree of six skills and an identical root `plugin.json` carrying the Agent Plugins `$schema`. They differ only in whether `.apm/` is present, which per [`reference/package-types.md`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/reference/package-types.md) is what makes an `apm.yml` eligible: | Variant | `package_type` | `--target claude` | |---|---|---| | `apm.yml` metadata-only, `plugin.json`, `skills/` | `agent_plugin` | 0 skills deployed, warning below | | same plus `.apm/skills` | `skill_bundle` | 6 skills deployed to `.claude/skills/` | ``` [!] Agent Plugins v1.0.0 packages install natively only for the 'copilot' target; selected target(s): claude. Re-run with --target copilot. ``` With `--target copilot` the plugin is registered via the `apm` marketplace and writes `.github/copilot/settings.local.json`, but no skills are copied. That is registration rather than deployment, so a package that also wants to serve a Claude Code or Cursor user has nothing to offer them. ```mermaid flowchart LR S["identical skills/ tree
6 skills"] --> F{"format selected"} F -->|"APM layout
eligible apm.yml + .apm/"| A["skill_bundle"] F -->|"portable layout
plugin.json only"| B["agent_plugin"] A --> A1["claude, cursor, codex,
gemini, opencode, windsurf
6 skills deployed"] B --> B1["copilot: registered,
no skills copied"] B --> B2["every other target:
0 skills"] style A1 fill:#e0ffe0 style B2 fill:#ffe0e0 ``` ## Reproduction ```bash mkdir -p plug/skills/demo consumer printf -- '---\nname: demo\ndescription: Demo skill.\n---\n\n# demo\n' > plug/skills/demo/SKILL.md printf 'name: demo-plugin\nversion: 0.1.0\n' > plug/apm.yml # metadata-only, selects plugin layout cat > plug/plugin.json <<'JSON' { "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json", "name": "demo-plugin", "version": "0.1.0" } JSON cd consumer && apm install --target claude ../plug ls .claude/skills | wc -l # 0 # now make the apm.yml eligible; nothing else changes mkdir -p ../plug/.apm && ln -s ../skills ../plug/.apm/skills apm install --target claude ../plug ls .claude/skills | wc -l # 1 ``` ## Why this matters I maintain a package whose skills live in `.agents/skills/`, which is where APM itself deploys skills for Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, Antigravity and Windsurf. Adopting Agent Plugins looked like the better design: one vendor-neutral manifest any conforming client can read, instead of an entry point specific to a single package manager. Since #2797 I can have both, by keeping an eligible `apm.yml` beside `plugin.json`, and that is what I plan to do. But it means the portable manifest is decoration: the APM-specific files are still what make the package installable for most of APM's own targets. A package that ships only the portable manifest, which is the entire point of a vendor-neutral spec, is the one that works least well here. ## The ask When a package selects the Agent Plugins layout, discover `skills/` per the spec's [fixed component locations](https://agent-plugins.org/specification#61-fixed-locations) and deploy each skill through the existing skill integration path, exactly as for a `skill_bundle`. Keep native registration as the Copilot-specific behaviour on top. Target coverage would then follow from the content rather than from which manifest the author chose. If the current restriction is a staging step after #2703 and #2705 rather than a permanent boundary, saying so in the warning text or in `package-types.md` would already help authors decide whether to adopt now or wait. ## Secondary observation, happy to split it out Adoption is harder than it needs to be for a repository whose skills already live somewhere else, and the reason is a chain of three constraints: 1. The manifest schema is [closed](https://agent-plugins.org/specification#52-manifest-object): "the only permitted top-level fields are `$schema`, `name`, `version`, `description`, `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords`, and `extensions`". There is no field to declare where skills live. ([schema](https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json)) 2. So skills can only be at the [fixed location](https://agent-plugins.org/specification#61-fixed-locations) `skills/`, as "Subdirectories containing `SKILL.md`". 3. The spec would allow reaching them by symlink. [4.1 General requirements](https://agent-plugins.org/specification#41-general-requirements), item 3: "Symlinks, junctions, reparse points, and equivalent filesystem mechanisms MAY resolve to targets within the plugin root, but clients MUST reject package paths that resolve outside it." But on `main`, [`agent_plugins/loader.py:455`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/agent_plugins/loader.py#L455) rejects a symlinked `skills/` outright with `skills.location.invalid` ("Agent Plugins skills must be a regular root directory"), and [`:498`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/agent_plugins/loader.py#L498) skips skill directories that are symlinks. The result is that a repository with skills in `.agents/skills/` cannot expose them as `skills/` through an in-root symlink, even though the spec permits it. It has to physically relocate the files and symlink in the other direction. Accepting in-root symlinks would make adoption a one-line addition for those repositories. ## Related * #2703 and #2705 delivered native Copilot registration. This asks for the complementary deployment path for the other targets. * #2797 and #2735 settled precedence when `apm.yml` and `plugin.json` coexist, which is why the reproduction pins the distinction on `.apm/` eligibility rather than on a conflict. * #2780 concerned legacy Claude plugin admission, a different manifest format. ## Environment Built from `main` at `cfee65d` via `uv run apm`, reporting `0.29.0 (cfee65d)`, macOS arm64. Behaviour differs from the released v0.29.0 binary, where the co-located layout failed outright before #2797.

issues.title: [BUG] Global install exits successfully after silently omitting a relative local transitive dependency
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
A user-scope install of an absolute local parent package silently drops that parent's existing relative local child dependency. The CLI exits 0 and reports a successful one-package install, while the child is absent from both the lockfile and native deployments.

This is an outcome/graph-completeness defect, not a request to silently relax the existing rejection of direct relative paths at user scope.

**To Reproduce**
Use a disposable fixture root and isolated HOME. All paths below labeled `/ABS/R` must be replaced with the actual absolute fixture root.

1. Create `/ABS/R/packages/parent/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: parent
version: 0.1.0
targets: [cursor]
dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: ../child
```
2. Create `/ABS/R/packages/child/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: child
version: 0.1.0
targets: [cursor]
```
3. Give each package a distinct command source: `parent/.apm/prompts/parent.prompt.md` and `child/.apm/prompts/child.prompt.md`, each with a valid description frontmatter and distinct body. For example:
```markdown
---
description: Local dependency reproduction
---
# Parent command
```
4. Create the isolated user's `~/.apm/apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: consumer
version: 0.1.0
targets: [cursor]
dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /ABS/R/packages/parent
```
5. From a separate consumer directory, run the installed CLI:
```bash
apm install --global --target cursor --no-policy --parallel-downloads 0
```
6. Inspect `~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml` and `~/.cursor/commands/`: only the parent is installed/locked/deployed.

Matched controls, each in a fresh isolated fixture:

| Scope | Parent's child reference | Exit | Locked/deployed packages |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Project | `../child` | 0 | 2 |
| User | absolute `/ABS/R/packages/child` | 0 | 2 |
| User | `../child` | 0 | 1 |

The fixture verifies that the relative reference resolves against the parent's source directory to an existing child manifest before running APM.

**Expected behavior**
A successful install must not silently omit a declared dependency. Either resolve the transitive child against its declaring local parent if that behavior is supported, or reject it with a nonzero exit and an actionable diagnostic. Whether to support anchored transitive references while retaining rejection of direct user-relative paths is an explicit contract decision.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.10, locked development dependencies
 - APM Version: 0.29.1, source commit `23e921750e5bdb25d02c7b0c71a6b97bd7b851ac`, editable installed CLI
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**
Representative observed output:
```text
[i] Installing to user scope (~/.apm/)
[>] Resolving /ABS/R/packages/parent...
[>] Resolving ../child...
[+] /ABS/R/packages/parent (local)
|-- 1 commands integrated -> .cursor/commands/
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 0.1s.
```
Exit status is 0. The child lock entry and command file are missing.

**Additional context**
Discovered while independently hardening the APMLifecycle interaction campaign after #2809 / during rework of #2813. Reproduced by both the implementation engineer and coordinating engineer. A focused unskipped regression with the three controls exists in the current, not-yet-published test-only worktree: `tests/integration/test_primitive_target_covering_array.py::test_local_transitive_command_scope_parity`.

Source evidence at the tested commit: `src/apm_cli/install/phases/resolve.py:557-570` rejects every relative local ref at USER scope before the declaring-parent source anchor at lines 580-583. This path records a callback failure but the observed overall command still succeeds. The locally available `origin/main` at `7f36da6e61fd5cebe29c16ced77fb4351823ec06` had an identical `src` tree; this is not a claim about subsequently fetched main.

Generalized properties: `outcome.status_matches_state`, dependency-graph completeness. This report does not authorize production changes or Phase 3 transaction redesign.

issues.title: [BUG] Clean grok-cloud install fails audit after replay selects a different target
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
A clean local skill installed with `--target grok-cloud` fails `apm audit --ci`: audit replays the skill into Copilot's `.agents/skills/` tree and reports that unrelated location as `unintegrated`, although the installed `.grok/skills/` file and lockfile agree.

An unrelated `.github/workflows/` file supplies a target-detection signal. Saving `apm config set target grok-cloud` does not correct audit replay. The usual durable-target workaround, `targets: [grok-cloud]` in the consumer manifest, is explicitly rejected by manifest parsing even after experimental enablement. This leaves an unresolved install/audit target-contract mismatch; it is not evidence of actual content tampering.

**To Reproduce**
Use a disposable consumer directory and isolated HOME.

1. Create a local skill package at an absolute path `/ABS/package`:
```text
package/
  apm.yml
  skills/example/SKILL.md
```
`apm.yml`:
```yaml
name: example-package
version: 0.1.0
```
`skills/example/SKILL.md`:
```markdown
---
name: example
description: Experimental target audit reproduction
---
# Clean source content
```
2. Create the consumer's `apm.yml`, substituting the actual absolute package path:
```yaml
name: consumer
version: 0.1.0
dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /ABS/package
```
3. Add an unrelated `.github/workflows/unrelated.yml` file to the consumer (for example, `name: unrelated`). Do not author a Copilot skill or request a Copilot deployment.
4. Run:
```bash
apm experimental enable grok-cloud
apm config set target grok-cloud
apm install --target grok-cloud --no-policy --parallel-downloads 0
apm audit --ci --no-policy --format json
```
5. Install exits 0, writes `.grok/skills/example/SKILL.md`, and records `grok-cloud` deployment ownership and the matching content hash. Audit exits 1 because replay expects `.agents/skills/example/SKILL.md` instead.

Additional diagnostic control: declaring `targets: [grok-cloud]` in the consumer manifest makes install exit 2 with `Unknown target 'grok-cloud'`, despite the enabled flag. That unsuccessful fixture workaround was not retained in the interaction regression.

**Expected behavior**
A clean installed target should round-trip through audit without false drift caused by an unrelated harness-directory signal. Define a consistent target-intent contract for experimental targets across install and audit, including how manifest restrictions, explicit installation targets, configured defaults, and deployment ownership interact.

Do not suppress the drift check, discard ownership assertions, or broadly ignore experimental-target findings to make the case pass.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.10, locked development dependencies
 - APM Version: 0.29.1, source commit `23e921750e5bdb25d02c7b0c71a6b97bd7b851ac`, editable installed CLI
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**
The real fixture uses a longer unique skill name; the relevant audit output is:
```json
{
  "passed": false,
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "content-integrity",
      "passed": true,
      "message": "No critical hidden Unicode or hash drift detected"
    },
    {
      "name": "drift",
      "passed": false,
      "message": "drift detected: 1 file(s): .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md",
      "details": ["unintegrated: .agents/skills/example/SKILL.md"]
    }
  ]
}
```
The actual result has ten checks: all nine non-drift checks pass, including ref consistency, deployment-ledger owners, deployed-file presence, and content integrity.

**Additional context**
Discovered while independently hardening APMLifecycle after #2809 / during rework of #2813. The unskipped, locally reproduced interaction is `tests/integration/test_primitive_target_covering_array.py::test_primitive_target_covering_array[interaction-b8852029871d9058]` in the current not-yet-published test-only worktree. The final four-shard run reproduces the failure, and the combined evidence gate correctly refuses to credit its interaction pairs.

Source boundaries at the tested commit: `install/drift.py::_read_apm_yml_target` and `run_replay` select replay targets from the manifest or detection; `core/apm_yml.py::_validate_canonical` rejects experimental capabilities in manifest target fields. `reference/cli/config.md` currently documents the configured default as an install/update setting, so simply assuming audit already promises to honor it is not a fix or a sufficient contract analysis.

Generalized properties: `routing.authorized_targets_only`, `outcome.status_matches_state`, clean install/audit consistency. Production changes and Phase 3 transaction redesign remain separately approval-gated.

issues.title: [BUG] OpenAPM local-path containment contradicts supported trusted-local sibling paths
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
OpenAPM req-mf-016 and the established CLI/shipped-guide contract disagree about trusted local dependencies outside the consuming project root.

At source revision `69f41ab7f88ac20d43728bc6d8e1e18b6a7112e3`:

- [OpenAPM req-mf-016](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/69f41ab7f88ac20d43728bc6d8e1e18b6a7112e3/docs/src/content/docs/specs/openapm-v0.1.md#L619-L627) says: "The resolver MUST refuse any local-path entry whose normalised form contains `..` segments that would escape the project root, with a diagnostic naming the offending path."
- [The shipped dependency guide](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/69f41ab7f88ac20d43728bc6d8e1e18b6a7112e3/packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/dependencies.md#L57-L68) explicitly supports local sibling layouts outside the consuming project root, anchored to the declaring local package. Remote-declared paths instead remain contained in the authenticated remote repository.
- [The local materialization owner](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/69f41ab7f88ac20d43728bc6d8e1e18b6a7112e3/src/apm_cli/install/phases/local_content.py#L184-L224) deliberately does not enforce consumer-project-root containment for trusted local packages, and explains that remote-parent expansion/rejection is the untrusted-source boundary. Locked local replay in `deps/path_anchoring.py` follows the same local-anchor contract.

The specification describes project scope as rooted at the consumer project, but user scope as independent of a project root. req-mf-016 does not explain a user-scope boundary or an exemption for trusted local declaring parents. Silently treating its MUST as nonnormative, or redefining the project root as an arbitrary common ancestor, would conceal the discrepancy.

**To Reproduce**
1. Compare the three pinned sources above.
2. Consider a consumer at `/R/consumer` that explicitly depends on local `/R/packages/parent`, whose manifest declares `path: ../child`.
3. The shipped guide and existing project-scope behavior admit `/R/packages/child`, despite it being outside the consumer root. The executed project-relative control is documented in #2815.
4. Apply req-mf-016 literally: the escaping relative entry appears forbidden. For user scope, the requirement does not supply a replacement for the consumer project root.

**Expected behavior**
A reviewed specification decision should clearly distinguish source anchoring, trusted-local admission, remote-repository containment, local-copy symlink containment, and installation scope. Normative wording, shipped guidance, implementation claims, and appropriate conformance examples should agree.

Clarify the trust boundary and user-scope interpretation explicitly. Do not weaken remote-source, symlink, materialization, or deployment containment merely to resolve this prose conflict. If the specification artifact or conformance fixtures change, they should receive the normal specification review.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: N/A for the normative discrepancy; the linked behavioral controls ran on macOS
 - Python Version: 3.12.10 for the linked behavioral controls
 - APM Version: source revision `69f41ab7f88ac20d43728bc6d8e1e18b6a7112e3`
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**
N/A. This report concerns a verified contradiction between the published requirement, shipped guide, and documented implementation boundary; the concrete CLI reproduction and controls are in #2815.

**Additional context**
Discovered by the independent #2815 fix owner during APMLifecycle Phase 2 (#2813) contract review. The maintainer explicitly chose to preserve established trusted-local sibling support for the bounded user-scope fix and track this pre-existing specification conflict separately. That ruling does not reconcile the specification or authorize an unreviewed spec change.

The #2815 fix must continue to reject direct/unanchored user-relative input and preserve remote/symlink safety. This issue is the separate specification follow-up, not permission to broaden that fix or begin Phase 3 transaction work.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Anchor user-scope hook commands to $HOME on POSIX targets so ~/.claude/settings.json stays portable across machines
issues.body:
## Summary

User-scope installs (`apm install -g`) write hook `command` entries into `~/.claude/settings.json` with the home directory expanded to a literal absolute path, e.g.

```json
"command": "node \"/Users/alice/.claude/hooks/context-mode/hooks/pretooluse.mjs\""
```

`~/.claude/settings.json` is a file many people keep in a dotfiles repo shared across machines. A literal home prefix makes the tracked file differ per host (`/Users/alice` vs `/home/alice`), so every `apm install -g` on a second machine produces a diff of the same hooks with a different prefix.

The absolute rewrite itself is right (#1310 / #1354: hook commands resolve against the cwd, not the settings file), and #1394 correctly limited it to user scope. The ask is only about *how* user-scope paths are anchored on POSIX targets.

## Proposal

For user-scope deploys on POSIX hosts, anchor the rewritten script path to `$HOME` instead of the expanded home directory:

```json
"command": "node \"$HOME/.claude/hooks/context-mode/hooks/pretooluse.mjs\""
```

Claude Code and Codex run hook commands through a shell, so `$HOME` expands at invocation time regardless of cwd, which keeps the #1310 fix intact while making the merged file host-independent. Windows targets would keep the current absolute form (`%USERPROFILE%` semantics differ and #2408 shows cwd handling is already special there).

The same applies to the `apm-hooks.json` ledger, so adoption on the next install matches the `$HOME` form.

## Evidence

Tested on apm 0.29.0 (`656f3d6`) with a scratch `HOME`:

- Rewriting the merged `settings.json` entries to `$HOME/...` by hand and reinstalling re-adds the absolute entries next to them (14 → 28 hooks).
- Rewriting both `settings.json` and `apm-hooks.json` to `$HOME/...` and reinstalling: apm adopts them (no duplicates) but rewrites them back to absolute. `apm uninstall -g <pkg>` still removes the right entries in that state.

So the change is contained in `_rewrite_command_for_target` / `_deploy_root_for_hook_rewrite` in `src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py`: when `user_scope` is set and the target is a POSIX shell-executed hook, emit `"$HOME/" + relative_to(home)` instead of `(deploy_root / target_rel).resolve()`.

## Environment

- apm 0.29.0 from commit `656f3d6e6dbade369b6fc8727a4eb7b164409b6d`
- macOS 15 (arm64) and Linux x86_64, targets `claude` and `codex`, user scope

issues.title: [BUG] User-scope hook deployment leaves out the plugin manifest: scripts reading ../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json crash (Codex Companion plugin)
issues.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2023. Hook deployment now copies the sibling modules next to a hook entry script, but a plugin whose hook scripts read files *outside* the scripts directory still crashes at runtime, because `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is rewritten to the partial copy under `~/.claude/hooks/<pkg>/` rather than to the full package tree.

Concrete case: `openai/codex-plugin-cc/plugins/codex` (Codex Companion). `hooks/hooks.json` declares

```json
"command": "node \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stop-review-gate-hook.mjs\""
```

and `scripts/lib/app-server.mjs` does

```js
const PLUGIN_MANIFEST_URL = new URL("../../.claude-plugin/plugin.json", import.meta.url);
const PLUGIN_MANIFEST = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(PLUGIN_MANIFEST_URL, "utf8"));
```

After `apm install -g` the deployed tree is `~/.claude/hooks/codex/scripts/{lib/,*.mjs,package.json}` only. Every Stop / SessionStart / SessionEnd invocation then fails:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Users/<me>/.claude/hooks/codex/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'
    at file:///Users/<me>/.claude/hooks/codex/scripts/lib/app-server.mjs:20:39
```

The same plugin installed natively through Claude Code's plugin system works, because there `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the whole plugin directory. The plugin also ships `prompts/` and `schemas/` next to `scripts/`, which the review gate reads through the broker.

## Expected

Either of:

1. Rewrite `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` (and `${PLUGIN_ROOT}`) to the package's own directory under `apm_modules/<owner>/<pkg>/…` for user-scope deploys instead of copying scripts into `~/.claude/hooks/<pkg>/`. The full tree already exists there, so every relative read works and nothing is duplicated.
2. If copying stays, copy the plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) and the package's non-primitive directories alongside the hook scripts, so the deployed root is a faithful plugin root.

## Environment

- apm 0.29.0 from commit `656f3d6e6dbade369b6fc8727a4eb7b164409b6d`
- macOS 15 arm64, target `claude`, user scope
- Workaround in use: copying `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` into `~/.claude/hooks/codex/.claude-plugin/` by hand

issues.title: [BUG] MCP server args and lock content hash recorded from the .apm-resolution-staging replacement path; the path vanishes after install
issues.body:
## Summary

A transitive package that goes through the resolution-staging "replacement" path can end up with its MCP server `args` recorded as the *staging* location, in `apm.lock.yaml`, `~/.claude.json` and `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  context-mode:
    command: node
    args:
    - /Users/<me>/.apm/apm_modules/.apm-resolution-staging/a1e585cd970240fc9c2486c04372d68a/replacements/c0524b8a…/start.mjs
```

The staging root is removed when the transaction completes, so every later MCP startup fails (`handshaking with MCP server failed: connection closed`), while `apm install -g` keeps reporting success because the lock entry is adopted as-is.

Seen with `mksglu/context-mode` pulled in transitively by a local `path:` package, user scope, `apm install -g --trust-transitive-mcp`, apm 0.29.0 at `656f3d6`.

## Where it comes from

`src/apm_cli/install/resolution_staging.py`: `prepare_replacement()` hands out an isolated path under `.apm-resolution-staging/<session>/replacements/…`, and the package is only moved to its live `apm_modules/<owner>/<repo>` location in `publish_replacement()`. If MCP integration (self-defined MCP servers in the package's `apm.yml`, `--trust-transitive-mcp` path) resolves script paths relative to the package directory *before* `publish_replacement()` runs, the recorded path is the staging one.

Secondary effect: the lock's content hash for that dependency was computed on the replacement tree. After the staging dir is gone and the operator repairs the `args` by hand, every install fails with `Content hash mismatch for mksglu/context-mode … Use 'apm install --update'`, and `--update` restructures the whole graph, which moved unrelated unpinned dependencies in my case.

## Expected

- MCP server `args` (and any deployment path) are always derived from the published live path, never from a staging path. Simplest: compute them after `publish_replacement()`, or map staging → live before writing the lock and the client configs.
- A staged replacement's content hash is written only for the published tree.
- Defensive check: refuse to write a lock or client config that contains `.apm-resolution-staging`.

## Workaround used

Replace the staging path with `~/.apm/apm_modules/mksglu/context-mode/start.mjs` in the three files, then `apm install -g --update` to accept the recomputed hash (and re-pin anything it moved).

## Environment

- apm 0.29.0 from commit `656f3d6e6dbade369b6fc8727a4eb7b164409b6d`
- macOS 15 arm64, targets `claude` + `codex`, user scope

issues.title: [BUG] agent-skills integration fixtures fail integrity checks on Windows
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The offline `agent-skills` integration fixtures hash an LF string but write it through `Path.write_text()`. On Windows this produces CRLF bytes, so the bundle integrity check rejects the fixture before the intended install assertions can run. This is a test-fixture portability problem, not a failure of the production integrity verifier.

**To Reproduce**

1. Check out `9cb174b2704c0d770110c9af7bf9ae8e24863f31` on native Windows.
2. Install the declared development dependencies with `uv sync --frozen --extra dev`.
3. Run `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_agent_skills_target.py -q`.

Observed result: 15 failed, 4 passed. For example, `test_install_agent_skills_deploys_to_agents_dir` fails on the fixture's bundle hash mismatch.

**Expected behavior**

The fixture's recorded hashes should describe its actual bytes on every platform, allowing the tests to exercise their intended target installation, convergence, migration and cleanup assertions.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: native Windows
- Python Version: 3.12.13
- APM Version: source commit `9cb174b2704c0d770110c9af7bf9ae8e24863f31`
- VSCode Version: not relevant; offline pytest reproduction

**Logs**

Representative SHA-256 values:

```text
expected LF: 21a859ee3b4842ebf32b5243849e400cb9d19802ac811daf92ce5fbf09338b88
actual CRLF: a0673773bd8e3371a0bfb52badc47c47ea23b480909ee61921817588586200a5
```

The same mismatch follows directly from hashing `skill_body.encode("utf-8")` and comparing it with the bytes written by the helper. `core.autocrlf=false` does not prevent Python's runtime newline translation.

**Additional context**

Both `_make_plugin_bundle` and `_make_multi_target_bundle` have this pattern. The uninstall fixture similarly records a hash of `SKILL_BODY` before a platform-native text write. In an isolated checkout, replacing just these three writes with `write_bytes(...encode("utf-8"))` makes this entire test file pass: 19 passed. No production verification logic is changed.

PR #1108 used the same byte-preserving repair for other local-bundle fixtures, but did not change this file. The broader repository test suite is not claimed green; separate collision-fixture and symlink-permission failures remain outside this focused report.

issues.title: [BUG] 0.29.0: an APM package hosting a marketplace manifest at its root deploys no skills - .apm/skills/ ignored, no diagnostic
issues.body:
## Summary

Since apm-cli 0.29.0, an APM package that also hosts a Claude Code marketplace manifest at its root (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) is installed with **zero skills**, silently. Its `.apm/skills/*/SKILL.md` sub-skills were deployed by 0.28.0 and every release before it; 0.29.0 deploys agents, commands and hooks from the same `.apm/` tree but drops the skills, and prints no diagnostic.

The behavior change comes with #2540 (closes #2537): a package typed `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` now takes its skill set exclusively from the resolved plugin declaration (`plugin.json` `skills` array, or a root `skills/` directory). `.claude-plugin/` at the root is enough to be typed `MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` (`detect_package_type`, "plugin.json OR .claude-plugin/ directory"), so a plain APM package whose only plugin evidence is a *marketplace* manifest - the plugin itself living in a subdirectory the manifest's `source` points at - falls into the plugin path, where its `.apm/skills/` is never consulted.

## Reproduction

Minimal package: an `apm.yml`, one sub-skill under `.apm/skills/`, and a marketplace manifest at the root whose plugin lives in `./plugin`. No root `plugin.json`, no root `skills/`.

```bash
mkdir -p mini/.apm/skills/hello mini/.claude-plugin mini/plugin
printf 'name: mini\nversion: 1.0.0\ndescription: repro\n' > mini/apm.yml
printf -- '---\nname: hello\ndescription: says hello\n---\n# hello\n' > mini/.apm/skills/hello/SKILL.md
printf '{"name":"mini-mp","owner":{"name":"me"},"plugins":[{"name":"mini","source":"./plugin","version":"1.0.0"}]}' \
  > mini/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json
printf '{"name":"mini","version":"1.0.0"}' > mini/plugin/plugin.json

mkdir consumer && cd consumer
uvx --from 'apm-cli==0.28.0' apm install --target claude ../mini   # |-- 1 skill(s) integrated -> .claude/skills/
rm -rf .claude apm.yml apm.lock.yaml apm_modules
uvx --from 'apm-cli==0.29.0' apm install --target claude ../mini   # no skill line at all; .claude/skills/ is not created
```

Observed on macOS (Darwin 25.3.0), Python 3.12 via `uvx`, 2026-09-05.

Real-world package where this was found: `using-system/oddyssey` (apm.yml + `.apm/{agents,prompts,skills,hooks}` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` pointing at `./marketplace/oddyssey`). Same commit (`6a54c2a`), user scope and project scope:

| apm-cli | `apm install --global --target claude` | `apm update --global` | project scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.28.0 | 8 skills integrated | 8 skills | 8 skills |
| 0.29.0 | 0 skills | 0 skills | 0 skills |

The lockfile written by 0.29.0 carries no `skills/` entry in `deployed_files`, so `apm audit` has nothing to flag either.

## Where it happens

`SkillIntegrator.integrate_package_skill` (0.29.0):

- `_is_plugin = package_info.package_type == MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN` is true for this package.
- `skill_source_paths(...)` -> `normalized_plugin_skill_sources(...)` reads the parser receipt `.apm/<plugin-skill-sources file>`. `_map_plugin_artifacts` only writes it from the manifest's `skills` declaration or a root `skills/` directory; neither exists here, so the result is `{}`.
- `if _is_plugin and not _source_paths:` -> `_note_plugin_declaration_deploys_no_skills(...)`, which returns early **without a message** when `declared` is `False` ("no skills by design"). The package then returns `skill_skipped=True`. The sub-skill promotion from `.apm/skills/` that served this package up to 0.28.0 is never reached.

So the two things that combine: (1) marketplace-manifest-only packages are classified as plugins, and (2) for plugins, an absent declaration is read as "no skills by design" rather than "fall back to the APM layout", with the diagnostic suppressed in exactly that case.

## Expected

One of:

- a package with an `apm.yml` and an `.apm/` tree keeps deploying its `.apm/skills/` sub-skills whatever else the repository hosts (a marketplace manifest describes *other* plugin roots, it is not this package's own declaration); or
- when the plugin path resolves to no skills and the package still has `.apm/skills/*/SKILL.md`, fall back to those; or at the very least
- print the "declares no deployable skills, so nothing under skills/ deploys" note in that case too, naming the skills that were skipped, so the author sees it. Today the install exits 0 with agents, commands and hooks deployed and the skills just missing.

## Workaround

Verified on both 0.28.0 and 0.29.0: add a root `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declaring the APM skills directory as the plugin's skills:

```json
{"name": "oddyssey", "version": "1.11.1", "skills": [".apm/skills/"]}
```

With it 0.29.0 integrates the 8 skills again (an explicit per-directory list works too). Consumers can otherwise pin `apm-cli==0.28.0`.

## References

- #2537, #2540 - the declaration-wins change this falls out of.
- 0.29.0 release notes: "fix(plugins): let the resolved declaration decide which skills deploy".

issues.title: [BUG] Unix installer executes release binaries without verifying published checksums
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
APM publishes `.sha256` sidecars for its macOS and Linux release archives, but `install.sh` downloads the archive, extracts it, and executes `apm --version` without verifying the published checksum first.

Public evidence:
- [v0.29.0 release assets](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/releases/tag/v0.29.0) include checksums for all four Unix archives.
- [Download path](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L430-L529).
- [Extraction and first execution](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L531-L552).

**To Reproduce**
1. Exercise the installer in an isolated harness with a harmless fixture archive and an intentionally mismatching checksum sidecar.
2. Make the fixture executable record invocation rather than perform installation work.
3. Observe that the current installer does not request or compare the sidecar before extracting the archive and invoking the fixture executable.

No malicious payload or privileged execution is needed for this reproduction.

**Expected behavior**
- Retrieve the checksum associated with the exact selected release and archive and verify SHA-256 before extraction or execution.
- Apply verification to both latest-version and VERSION-pinned installations, including the installer path used by self-update.
- Fail closed on missing, malformed, unavailable, or mismatching checksum data, without continuing into binary execution or silently switching to a different installation source through pip fallback.
- Work on supported macOS/Linux environments with an explicitly checked hashing tool; lack of verification capability must not silently disable verification.
- Respect configured release mirrors and no-direct-fallback policy. Keep checksum authentication scoped to the intended host; do not send GitHub credentials to mirror hosts.
- Define and document behavior for historical releases or custom mirrors without sidecars, rather than silently treating them as verified.
- Add hermetic coverage for matching/mismatching/missing checksums, pinned/latest releases, and mirror failures, asserting that no extracted binary runs on failure.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS / Linux (Unix installer).
- Python Version: N/A for the standalone installer.
- APM Version: v0.29.0 installer; same content at main revision `13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2`.
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A.

**Logs**
N/A. Source-based hardening report with a proposed harmless fixture reproduction.

**Additional context**
This is an integrity-verification gap, not evidence that any published artifact has been compromised. A checksum obtained from the same publisher is not an independent signature or provenance guarantee. Artifact signing/attestation can be considered separately; consuming the already-published checksums is the bounded change here.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Make Homebrew core the primary macOS installation path
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
APM is available in Homebrew core as `apm`, but the README and installation guide still lead with `curl -sSL https://aka.ms/apm-unix | sh` and advertise the custom tap command `brew install microsoft/apm/apm` as an alternative. This obscures the simpler package-manager-managed path and exposes new users to the standalone installer's system-directory and PATH behavior unnecessarily.

Public evidence:
- [Homebrew core formula](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/blob/main/Formula/a/apm.rb): currently packages 0.29.0 from PyPI, provides bottles, and disables self-update with guidance to use `brew upgrade apm`.
- [README installation section](https://github.com/microsoft/apm#readme).
- [Installation guide](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/getting-started/installation/).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Lead macOS onboarding with `brew install apm` for users who already have Homebrew; explain that no custom tap is required.
- Document `brew upgrade apm` as the update path for core installations. Do not recommend `apm self-update` for this distribution.
- Keep supported non-Homebrew installation choices visible, including for Linux users without Homebrew; do not require installing another package manager merely to install APM.
- Update the installation guide, quickstart, relevant CLI installation hints, and bundled APM usage guidance where applicable. Update the README subject to the repository's maintainer-approval requirement.
- Explain how existing custom-tap users can move to core without losing APM configuration or leaving conflicting executables. Establish the supported migration procedure before documenting commands; do not automatically uninstall or overwrite an existing installation.
- Describe the benefit accurately: package-manager ownership of installation and updates, not a claim that Homebrew eliminates all supply-chain risk.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keeping the tap command as the primary Homebrew recommendation adds unnecessary distribution choice for new users now that core is available. Keeping the shell one-liner first and documenting user-local overrides still puts installer-specific configuration ahead of an existing package manager.

**Additional context**
This is a documentation and onboarding change, not a proposal to remove the standalone installer or immediately retire the tap. The core formula installs the Python package in a managed environment rather than invoking APM's standalone installer. No changes to private downstream repositories are in scope.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Clarify APM's scope and remove ambiguous npm branding
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The Unix and Windows installers still identify APM as `The NPM for AI-Native Development`. This can be read as an implementation or distribution dependency rather than an analogy. APM is a Python package with standalone binary and package-manager distribution options; npm is not a prerequisite for installing the APM CLI.

The onboarding story should also explain when a dependency manager is useful without implying that every skill installation needs another CLI or that project-local, pinned, cross-harness skill installation is unique to APM.

Public evidence:
- [Unix installer banner](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L36-L41).
- [Windows installer](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.ps1).
- [Package metadata](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/pyproject.toml).
- [Homebrew core description](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/blob/main/Formula/a/apm.rb) already uses `Dependency manager for AI agent configuration`.
- [GitHub CLI's public skill-install documentation](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_skill_install) describes project/user scope, multiple agents, version pins, and source tracking. This is evidence for accurate positioning, not a request for competitor-focused shipped copy.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Replace ambiguous identity slogans on active onboarding surfaces with a literal description of APM's purpose. Keep package-manager analogies only where they are clearly presented as analogies.
- Add concise guidance for when APM earns its additional installation/setup cost: a declarative dependency set, manifest and lockfile, transitive dependencies, broader agent primitives, reproducible setup, and install-time policy.
- Acknowledge that a native skill installer can be sufficient for a skill-only workflow. Keep general-purpose shipped wording vendor-neutral and avoid unsupported exclusivity or speed claims.
- Explain that exact replay of floating dependencies requires preserving the lockfile alongside the manifest; use `--frozen` for strict replay. Do not imply that copying a floating manifest alone fixes all versions or that recording an MCP configuration pins a remote service implementation.
- Update the relevant introduction/onboarding pages and installer banners together. Any README changes require maintainer approval under repository rules.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Adding a long comparison matrix would increase maintenance and distract from onboarding. Removing every analogy is unnecessary; the important distinction is between an explanatory analogy and a claim about what the CLI depends on. Native integration or a `gh apm` wrapper would be a separate design effort, not a wording fix.

**Additional context**
This is a bounded messaging/documentation request, not a product rewrite, a new integration commitment, or a request to remove npm-based MCP launchers. It aligns with PRINCIPLES.md P1 (standard primitives usable without APM), P3 (vendor neutrality), P4 (UX), and P6 (explainable behavior).

issues.title: [BUG] Public release lookup fails when an ambient GitHub token is rejected
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Unix installer resolves `GITHUB_APM_PAT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `GH_TOKEN` and attaches the selected credential to its first release-metadata request. When a credential is rejected, the response can lack `tag_name` and installation exits with `Invalid API response received`, even when the same public APM release metadata is accessible anonymously.

This makes bootstrap of a public CLI unnecessarily depend on an ambient credential's validity or authorization. Public CLI installation and authentication for subsequently consumed private packages are separate operations.

Public evidence:
- [Token selection and metadata request](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L292-L338).
- [Retry conditions and error handling](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L340-L396).
- #1582 and #1588 explain why credential-aware lookup was introduced: anonymous rate limits on shared IPs.

**To Reproduce**
1. Use an isolated installer harness with a non-secret dummy credential in one of the supported token environment variables.
2. Stub the canonical public release-metadata request to return an authentication rejection when Authorization is present, and valid release metadata when it is absent.
3. Run the installer with no pinned VERSION and observe that the current flow does not retry the rejected public metadata request anonymously before reporting failure. Stub subsequent downloads/install operations to keep the reproduction hermetic.

**Expected behavior**
- Fetch public APM release metadata without making a rejected ambient token a prerequisite for success.
- Preserve credential-aware recovery for anonymous rate limits; do not simply revert #1588 and reintroduce the shared-IP failure.
- Bound fallback to an explicitly public bootstrap context. Preserve private repository, GHES, enterprise mirror, and no-direct-fallback semantics; do not turn authorization failures into a general policy bypass.
- Keep credentials scoped to the intended host. Never send GitHub tokens to configured mirror hosts or log token values.
- Report HTTP/auth/rate-limit/network failures accurately, with an appropriate next action, rather than conflating them with malformed metadata or a private repository.
- Assess the corresponding release lookup used by `apm self-update` and platform installers so equivalent public-bootstrap paths remain consistent. Do not rewrite package authentication as part of this fix.
- Add regression cases for accepted/rejected/missing credentials, anonymous rate limits, pinned versions, private repositories, and fail-closed mirror behavior.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS / Linux for the confirmed Unix installer path.
- Python Version: N/A for this shell metadata request.
- APM Version: v0.29.0 installer; same content at main revision `13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2`.
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A.

**Logs**
N/A. The reproduction should use synthetic HTTP responses, not real credentials or organization-specific logs.

**Additional context**
Documenting a particular token lifetime or asking users to replace their primary credential is not the fix for downloading a public release. Private dependency access must continue to require the authorization appropriate to that dependency. #2788 is a separate proposal for credential diagnostics; it does not remove this bootstrap failure.

issues.title: [BUG] Unix installer implicitly escalates privileges for default installation
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Unix installer defaults `APM_INSTALL_DIR` to `/usr/local/bin` and derives `/usr/local/lib/apm` for the bundle. When these locations are not writable, the script automatically invokes `sudo` for removal, directory creation, copying, marker creation, and symlink installation.

A routine per-user CLI installation should not implicitly transition into privileged filesystem operations. Supporting an environment-variable override does not make the default unprivileged.

Public source at the inspected revision:
- [Default install directory](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L25-L28).
- [Privileged installation operations](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L718-L758).

**To Reproduce**
1. Inspect or exercise `install.sh` in a disposable macOS/Linux environment as an ordinary user, leaving `APM_INSTALL_DIR` and `APM_LIB_DIR` unset.
2. Ensure the default system installation locations are not user-writable. In an automated harness, stub `sudo` to record and reject calls rather than elevating privileges.
3. Reach the installation phase with a valid fixture bundle. The current script attempts privileged operations automatically.

This report is grounded in the source path; no elevated installation is required to demonstrate it.

**Expected behavior**
- Fresh ordinary-user installs default to documented user-owned locations and never invoke `sudo` implicitly.
- Deliberate system-wide installation remains possible through a clearly documented opt-in or administrator-managed procedure. An unwritable destination without that intent produces an actionable nonzero failure.
- Explain PATH requirements accurately without silently rewriting shell profiles.
- Preserve existing path-safety and prior-installation guards.
- Account for existing system-wide/custom installations and `apm self-update`: do not silently create a competing second installation, remove an installation the caller cannot manage, or overwrite a package-manager-owned installation.
- Cover fresh user-local installs, unwritable custom paths, explicit system-wide intent, and existing-installation updates in regression coverage.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS / Linux (Unix installer).
- Python Version: N/A for the standalone binary path.
- APM Version: v0.29.0 installer; the same installer content was present at main revision `13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2`.
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A.

**Logs**
N/A. Source-based report; no user-specific logs are necessary.

**Additional context**
The script is not executed wholesale under `sudo`, and normal APM usage does not inherently require administrator privileges. The defect is automatic privilege escalation during bootstrap. This is distinct from the previously addressed directory-safety problem in #1690. A changed default needs a concise migration note for existing installations.

issues.title: [BUG] Uninstall reports success when package deletion fails
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm uninstall` reports success even when it fails to delete the package directory from `apm_modules/`.

The failure is logged, but the command continues and removes the package from `apm.yml` and the lockfile. This can leave the package installed on disk but no longer declared or owned by APM.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Install any package with `apm install`.
2. Prevent deletion of the package directory in `apm_modules/`, for example by holding a package file open on Windows.
3. Run `apm uninstall <package>`.
4. Observe that deletion fails, but the command still reports `Uninstall complete`.
5. Confirm that the package directory remains on disk while its manifest and lockfile entries have been removed.

**Expected behavior**

If package deletion fails, `apm uninstall` should exit with a nonzero status and must not report successful completion.

The package should remain declared and owned by APM until its removal from disk succeeds, or the command should provide an equivalent recoverable transaction state.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.14.6
- APM Version: 0.29.1
- VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**

Relevant output resembles:

```text
Failed to remove <package> from apm_modules/: <deletion error>
Updated apm.yml (removed 1 package(s))
Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml

issues.title: [BUG] Git cache pruning evicts recently used checkouts
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A successful Git cache hit does not update the checkout directory modification time, even though `apm cache prune` uses that modification time as the checkout's last-access timestamp. A checkout that is used frequently can therefore be removed as stale.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Configure a project with a Git dependency and run `apm install` once to populate the Git cache.
2. Locate the checkout under `git/checkouts_v1/<shard>/<sha>/full/` in the APM cache directory.
3. Set the modification time of the `<sha>` directory to more than 30 days ago while leaving the checkout contents valid.
4. Run `apm install` again with the same lockfile. The dependency is served successfully from the cache and the logs report a cache hit.
5. Run `apm cache prune --days 30`.
6. Observe that the recently used checkout is removed.

**Expected behavior**

A successful cache hit should refresh the checkout's last-access timestamp, or the cache should record last access using a separate durable mechanism. `apm cache prune --days 30` should not remove a checkout that was just used successfully.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.29.1
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**

No error is required to trigger the bug. The install succeeds, followed by output similar to:

```text
Pruning entries older than 30 days...
Pruned 1 checkout(s).
```

**Additional context**

The cache-hit path in `src/apm_cli/cache/git_cache.py` verifies the checkout and returns it without touching its filesystem timestamp. The prune path reads `st_mtime` from the `<sha>` directory and treats it as the access indicator. Integrity verification only reads checkout files, so it does not refresh the timestamp as a side effect.

issues.title: [BUG] HTTP cache LRU eviction ignores successful cache hits
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`HttpCache.get()` does not refresh the cached entry's modification time after a successful cache hit. Since LRU eviction uses the entry directory mtime, frequently accessed entries can be evicted as if they were unused.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Configure the HTTP cache with a small size limit.
2. Store an entry and wait briefly.
3. Read the entry successfully with `HttpCache.get()`.
4. Store newer entries until the cache size limit is exceeded.
5. Observe that the previously accessed entry may be evicted before less recently accessed entries.

**Expected behavior**

A successful cache hit should update the entry's mtime so that the entry is treated as recently used during LRU eviction.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.14.x
- APM Version: 0.29.1
- VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**

No exception is raised. The next lookup for the evicted entry becomes a cache miss and may trigger a fresh network request.

**Additional context**

`HttpCache.store()` and `HttpCache.refresh_expiry()` update the entry mtime with `os.utime()`, but `HttpCache.get()` does not.

Eviction sorts entries by mtime in ascending order and removes the oldest entries first. The existing cache tests verify that eviction occurs, but do not verify that successful cache hits protect an entry from eviction.

issues.title: [BUG] Uninstall deletes instructions from surviving transitive dependencies
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Uninstalling one parent package in a dependency diamond can delete instruction files belonging to a transitive dependency that is still required by another installed parent. The uninstall succeeds, but the surviving dependency's integrated instructions are removed.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create three local APM packages: `root-a`, `root-b`, and `shared`. Make both `root-a` and `root-b` depend on `shared`.
2. Add an instruction file such as `.apm/instructions/shared.instructions.md` to `shared`.
3. Create an application that depends on both `../root-a` and `../root-b`, then run `apm install --target copilot`.
4. Confirm that `shared` is installed and its instruction file is integrated into the application.
5. Run `apm uninstall ../root-a`.
6. Confirm that `shared` remains in `apm.lock.yaml` and under `apm_modules/`, but its integrated instruction file has been deleted.

**Expected behavior**

Uninstall should remove only files owned by the package being removed. Instruction files belonging to `shared` must remain integrated while `root-b` still depends on `shared`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.29.1
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**

No error is required to trigger the bug. The uninstall reports success, but the surviving transitive dependency's instruction file is missing afterward.

**Additional context**

During uninstall, the deployment cleanup snapshot includes paths owned by the removed packages. When the removed parent has no recorded deployed files, this snapshot is an empty set and is converted to `None`. The instruction integrator treats `None` as a legacy-cleanup request and uses the broad `*.instructions.md` pattern. The base integrator then deletes every matching instruction file, including files owned by surviving dependencies.

The existing regression scenario is covered by `tests/unit/test_uninstall_shared_diamond_dependency.py`, but its first test intentionally does not assert that the surviving transitive instruction file remains. The test comments identify this as a separate uninstall cleanup defect.

issues.title: [BUG] apm cache clean reports success when cleanup fails
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`apm cache clean` reports that the cache was cleaned successfully even when one or more cache entries cannot be deleted. Cleanup errors are suppressed, so the command exits successfully while cached content remains on disk.

**To Reproduce**

 - VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**
The command reports success without an error:

```text
[+] Cache cleaned.

issues.title: [BUG] Cache prune reports failed deletions as successful
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm cache prune` reports checkout entries as pruned even when deleting them fails.

The prune counter increments after calling `robust_rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`, which suppresses deletion errors.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an old checkout directory in the Git cache.
2. Make the checkout undeletable, for example by locking a file or denying removal permissions.
3. Run `apm cache prune --days 30`.
4. Observe that the command reports the checkout as pruned while the directory remains on disk.

A deterministic test case can mock `shutil.rmtree` to raise `PermissionError` and then call `GitCache.prune(max_age_days=30)`.

**Expected behavior**

Only successfully deleted checkout entries should be included in the pruned count.

If deletion fails, the entry should remain uncounted and the failure should be surfaced or reported as a warning.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14
 - APM Version: 0.29.1
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

**Logs**

Example incorrect output:

```text
Pruned 1 checkout(s).

issues.title: [BUG] apm prune exits zero after orphan deletion failure
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm prune` exits successfully with status code `0` when deletion of an orphaned package fails. The failure is logged, but the command does not retain a failure state. The orphaned package remains on disk.

3. Make the package directory undeletable, or simulate `safe_rmtree()` raising `OSError`.
4. Run `apm prune`.
5. Check the exit status and confirm that the orphaned package remains.

Observed output includes:

```text
Failed to remove bad-org/bad-repo: permission denied

issues.title: [BUG] Negative prune days delete the Git checkout cache
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm cache prune` accepts negative values for `--days`. A negative value creates a future cutoff time, causing all existing Git checkout cache entries to be pruned.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Populate the Git checkout cache.
2. Run `apm cache prune --days -1`.
3. Observe that all cached checkouts are removed and the command exits successfully.

**Expected behavior**

The command should reject negative values with a validation error and leave the cache unchanged.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.14
- APM Version: 0.29.1
- VSCode Version: Not relevant

**Logs**

```text
Command: apm cache prune --days -1
Result: 22 checkouts pruned
Exit code: 0

issues.title: [BUG] Global install succeeds with empty skill directories when HOME/APM_HOME uses a symlink alias
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A global install can exit successfully while deploying empty skill directories when `HOME` and `APM_HOME` use a symlink alias. The source plan authorizes canonical paths, but skill copying uses the original path spelling and excludes the authorized files.

**To Reproduce**

1. In a disposable environment, create a local APM package containing `.apm/skills/demo/SKILL.md` and `apm.yml` with a name and version.
2. Create a real temporary home and a symlink pointing to it. Set the child process's `HOME` to that symlink and `APM_HOME` to `<symlink>/.apm`.
3. Run `apm install --global <local-package> --target codex --no-policy --parallel-downloads 0`.
4. The command exits 0, but `<real-home>/.agents/skills/demo/SKILL.md` is absent. Repeat with canonical home paths: the file is deployed.

Apply only the test hunk below, leaving the implementation unchanged, then run:

```sh
uv run --extra dev pytest tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py -k reads_home_deployment_root -q
```

**Expected behavior**

Equivalent home-directory path spellings should deploy the same skill files.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS 26.6.1, Apple Silicon
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.29.1 and main at `852295c8b74ef60be0bd5e91f00ffa63152700c6`

**Logs**

```text
assert install.exit_code == 0, install.output  # passes
assert (isolated.home / ".agents" / "skills" / "demo" / "SKILL.md").is_file()
E AssertionError: assert False

FAILED test_global_install_audit_reads_home_deployment_root[True]
1 failed, 1 passed, 8 deselected
```

**Additional context**

`DeployableSourcePlan.create()` resolves `package_info.install_path`. `SkillIntegrator.integrate_package_skill()` retains its original spelling, which reaches the copy filter. `_is_safe_source_path()` performs a lexical `relative_to(source_root)` check; noncanonical candidates fail against the resolved root and are ignored.

The proposed patch canonicalizes the package root on a shallow copy of the metadata, preserving caller metadata and descendant-symlink checks. The regression fails before the fix and passes afterward. The focused security, containment, and global-audit suites pass with the patch (38 tests).

<details>
<summary>Proposed patch and regression</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py b/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py
--- a/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py
+++ b/src/apm_cli/integration/skill_integrator.py
@@ -1457,6 +1457,13 @@ class SkillIntegrator(BaseIntegrator):
         Returns:
             SkillIntegrationResult: Results of the integration operation
         """
+        # Match the canonical root used by DeployableSourcePlan without
+        # changing caller metadata or resolving links within the package.
+        from copy import copy
+
+        package_info = copy(package_info)
+        package_info.install_path = package_info.install_path.resolve()
+
         enforce_agent_plugin_deployment_boundary(package_info)
 
         # Check if package type allows skill installation (T4 routing)
diff --git a/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py b/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py
--- a/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py
+++ b/tests/integration/test_global_audit_deploy_root.py
@@ -47,12 +47,23 @@ def _tree_snapshot(
     return directories, files
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("aliased_home", [False, True])
 def test_global_install_audit_reads_home_deployment_root(
+    aliased_home: bool,
     tmp_path: Path,
     monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
 ) -> None:
     isolated = IsolatedApmEnvironment.create(tmp_path / "global-audit", base_env=os.environ)
     environment = isolated.subprocess_env()
+    if aliased_home:
+        alias = isolated.root / "home-alias"
+        try:
+            alias.symlink_to(isolated.home, target_is_directory=True)
+        except (OSError, NotImplementedError):
+            pytest.skip("directory symlinks unavailable")
+        environment["HOME"] = str(alias)
+        environment["USERPROFILE"] = str(alias)
+        environment["APM_HOME"] = str(alias / ".apm")
     environment["APM_NO_CACHE"] = "1"
     for name, value in environment.items():
         monkeypatch.setenv(name, value)
```

</details>

issues.title: [BUG] Exact version pins from `apm install pkg#X.Y.Z` make `apm outdated` always report up-to-date
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

For registry-routed dependencies, `apm install <package>#<version>` writes that version as an **exact** constraint in `apm.yml`. `apm outdated` then compares the lockfile against that constraint — not against the newest version the registry advertises — so an exact pin is always satisfied.

The result: a package locked at `1.7.0` while the registry has `1.8.0` reports `[*] All dependencies are up-to-date`.

This is the same class of gap as #1209 (SHA revision pins making `outdated` silent), but for **semver exact pins** on registry packages rather than git SHAs. #1209 was accepted and closed for the SHA path; the semver/registry path still has it.

**To Reproduce**

Against a registry that publishes both `1.7.0` and a newer `1.8.0` of the same package (reproduced on APM 0.29.1 with a JFrog Artifactory agent-packages registry; the same sequence should hold for any registry-backed package):

1. `apm experimental enable registries` and configure a default registry.
2. `apm install --no-policy '<owner>/<pkg>#1.7.0'`
3. Observe `apm.yml` contains `- <owner>/<pkg>#1.7.0` and the lockfile has `resolved_ref: 1.7.0`.
4. Confirm the registry lists a newer version (`apm view` / versions API shows `1.8.0`).
5. `apm outdated`

Output: `[*] All dependencies are up-to-date`.

Contrast — same lock at `1.7.0`, but rewrite the manifest pin to `#^1.7.0` (or `#>=1.7.0`) **without** changing the lockfile — `apm outdated` then correctly reports `1.7.0 → 1.8.0`.

A second related constraint forces wrappers and humans into that exact pin:

```text
apm install --no-policy '<owner>/<pkg>'
# version selector required: no '#<version>' found but this dep would route
# to the default registry. Add a version selector (e.g. '...#1.0.0')
```

There is no `--latest`, no default save-prefix (`^` / `>=`), and `*` / `latest` as selectors fail to download. So the only CLI form that "just install this package" can take, once you supply the required selector, writes a pin that `outdated` can never see past.

**Expected behavior**

One of:

1. **`apm outdated` / `apm update` treat an exact semver pin like a SHA pin after #1209** — report (and optionally rewrite) when the registry has a newer published version, even if the current constraint is still satisfied. This is the closest analogue to what was accepted in #1209.
2. **CLI `apm install <package>#<resolved>` records a range** (caret or `>=`) in `apm.yml` while locking the exact version in `apm.lock.yaml`, matching how npm/cargo separate declared range from lock. An explicit `=<version>` or `#=1.7.0` would remain exact.
3. **A documented default prefix** (`apm config set save-prefix '^'` or similar) so callers do not have to invent a selector shape.

(2) and (3) collide with `policy.dependencies.require_pinned_constraint` from #1491, which flags unbounded `>=` as a policy violation — so if a range is written, caret/tilde/bounded forms may be the ones that stay policy-clean. Note caret on `0.x` (`^0.7.0` → `>=0.7.0 <0.8.0`) still hides `0.8+`, which is common in early registries.

**Environment**
 - OS: macOS
 - APM Version: 0.29.1 (1b3d80a)
 - Python: 3.12

**Additional context**

Related:

- #1209 — same user-visible failure for git SHA pins; accepted as a feature, closed. This issue is the registry/semver twin.
- #1295 — requiring a selector for registry-routed deps is intentional; not asking to drop that. The missing piece is what the CLI *writes* (or what `outdated` *compares*) once a selector is supplied.
- #1491 — org policy that bans unbounded `>=`; any default range needs to stay compatible with that.
- #1962 — `apm upgrade` proposal; complementary, does not by itself fix exact-pin silence.

We maintain a thin wrapper that only exists to hide registry + short-name resolution. It currently has to invent `>=<resolved>` on the user's behalf so `apm outdated` works at all. That is compensating for this gap rather than adding domain value — happy to delete that once APM owns the pin shape or the outdated comparison.
