issues.title: [BUG] Registry-based transitive dependencies cannot be resolved
issues.body:
## Summary

I'm trying to consume APM packages published to a private Artifactory APM registry.

The root package can be found and installed from the registry, but installation fails when APM attempts to resolve transitive dependencies that are also hosted in the same registry.

Error:
```
our-apm/authoring-skills -- Failed to resolve transitive dep
our-apm/authoring-skills (via our-apm/toolkit > our-apm/authoring-skills):
registry-sourced dep is missing registry_name
(parser bug or unconfigured default registry)
```

I'm unsure whether:
* this scenario is currently unsupported,
* my configuration is incorrect,
* or there is a bug in registry-based dependency resolution.

## Repository Structure

```
toolkit-repository (git)
├─ toolkit
├─ critical-thinking
└─ authoring-skills
```

Dependencies:
```
toolkit
├─ critical-thinking
└─ authoring-skills

authoring-skills
└─ external package(s) from public registries
```

All three packages are published to the same private Artifactory APM registry.

## Package configuration

`toolkit/apm.yml`
```
dependencies:
  apm:
    - id: our-apm/authoring-skills
      version: 1.0.0
      registry: our-registry

    - id: our-apm/critical-thinking
      version: 1.0.0
      registry: our-registry
```

`Consumer project apm.yml`
```
registries:
  our-registry:
    url: https://repo.ourdomain.com/artifactory/api/agentpackages/apm-local

default: our-registry
```

## Installation attempts

#### Direct install
`apm install our-apm/toolkit#1.0.0`

#### Registry-qualified install
`apm install our-apm/toolkit@our-registry#1.0.0`

#### Declared dependency
```
dependencies:
  apm:
    - id: our-apm/toolkit
      version: 1.0.0
      registry: our-registry
```
followed by `apm install`

## Actual result

Installation fails with:
```
our-apm/authoring-skills -- Failed to resolve transitive dep
our-apm/authoring-skills (via our-apm/toolkit > our-apm/authoring-skills):
registry-sourced dep is missing registry_name
(parser bug or unconfigured default registry)

our-apm/critical-thinking -- Failed to resolve transitive dep
our-apm/critical-thinking (via our-apm/toolkit > our-apm/critical-thinking):
registry-sourced dep is missing registry_name
(parser bug or unconfigured default registry)
```

## Expected result

Since:
* the consumer project defines a default registry
* the transitive dependencies explicitly specify registry: our-registry
* all packages exist in the same registry

I would expect APM to successfully resolve and install the transitive dependencies.

## Reproduction steps
1. Create two or more APM packages.
1. Add one package as a dependency of another.
1. Publish all packages to the same private registry.
1. Configure the registry in a fresh consumer project.
1. Install the top-level package.

## Questions
1. Are registry-hosted transitive dependencies currently supported?
1. Is the registry attribute expected to work for transitive dependency resolution?
1. Is the reported error (missing registry_name) a known issue?

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows/WSL/Dev-Container
 - Python Version: None
 - APM Version: 0.30.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): 1.136.1

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile --target claude never resolves .context.md links when folding instructions into CLAUDE.md
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm compile --target claude` folds instruction bodies (global + `applyTo`-scoped) directly
into `CLAUDE.md`, but never runs them through the markdown-link resolver. Any relative link
inside an instruction body — in particular a link to a `.apm/context/*.context.md` fragment —
is emitted byte-for-byte as written in the source file, with no adjustment for the fact that
`CLAUDE.md` may live in a different directory than the source instruction (e.g. when the
instruction comes from a dependency, or from a non-root placement).

The equivalent `AGENTS.md` pipeline (`agents_compiler.py` / `distributed_compiler.py`) does not
have this problem: it explicitly calls the link resolver
(`UnifiedLinkResolver.resolve_links_for_compilation` in `distributed_compiler.py`, or
`resolve_markdown_links` in `agents_compiler.py`) before returning the generated content.
`claude_formatter.py` has no equivalent call anywhere in the file — grepping the module for
`resolve_links` / `link_resolver` returns zero matches.

Practical effect: an instruction with no `applyTo` (global, e.g. a "signpost" file whose only
job is a short pointer to a `.context.md` file with the real content) will fold correctly into
`AGENTS.md` with a correctly rewritten link, but the *same* instruction, when it ends up folded
into `CLAUDE.md`, keeps the original unadjusted relative link and the link no longer resolves
from `CLAUDE.md`'s location.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a package with one instruction and one context fragment it links to:

   ```
   my-pkg/
     apm.yml
     .apm/
       instructions/
         signpost.instructions.md
       context/
         conventions.context.md
   ```

   `apm.yml`:
   ```yaml
   name: my-pkg
   version: 0.0.1
   targets: [claude]
   dependencies:
     apm: []
   ```

   `.apm/instructions/signpost.instructions.md` (no `applyTo` — global instruction):
   ```markdown
   ---
   description: Signpost
   ---

   See [conventions](../context/conventions.context.md) for details.
   ```

   `.apm/context/conventions.context.md`:
   ```markdown
   Real content lives here.
   ```

2. Compile, forcing the instructions section into `CLAUDE.md` even though a
   `.claude/rules/` directory may already exist (`--force-instructions` is the fastest way to
   force the code path; the same missing resolution also affects the natural, non-forced path
   any time `.claude/rules/` is not yet populated, e.g. first `apm compile` run before
   `apm install`, or `apm compile --root <scratch>`):

   ```bash
   apm install --target claude
   apm compile --target claude --force-instructions
   ```

3. Inspect `CLAUDE.md`:

   ```markdown
   ## Project Standards

   ### Global Instructions

   See [conventions](../context/conventions.context.md) for details.
   ```

   The link `../context/conventions.context.md` is relative to
   `.apm/instructions/signpost.instructions.md`'s own directory (where it was authored), not to
   `CLAUDE.md`'s directory (project root). Resolved from `CLAUDE.md`'s location it points one
   directory above the project root and does not exist.

4. Compile the same package for `opencode` (or any other AGENTS.md-based target) instead:

   ```bash
   apm compile --target opencode
   ```

   `AGENTS.md` contains the *same* link, correctly rewritten to
   `.apm/context/conventions.context.md` (relative to the project root) — because
   `agents_compiler.py` / `distributed_compiler.py` do call the link resolver.

**Expected behavior**

`CLAUDE.md` should resolve the same relative links to `.context.md` / `.memory.md` fragments
that `AGENTS.md` already resolves correctly, using the same anchor (the compiled output file's
own directory), regardless of whether the instruction section is emitted via the normal path or
via `--force-instructions`.

**Environment:**
 - OS: Linux
 - Python Version: 3.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0 (commit `8c2e0d9c`, tag `v0.30.0`)

**Logs**

No error is raised; the bug is a silently-wrong output (broken relative link), not a crash.

**Additional context**

Root cause, confirmed by reading the source at `v0.30.0`:

- `src/apm_cli/compilation/claude_formatter.py` builds the `CLAUDE.md` body in
  `_generate_claude_content()` and returns `"\n".join(sections)` directly — the file contains
  zero references to `resolve_links`, `resolve_markdown_links`, `link_resolver`, or
  `UnifiedLinkResolver` anywhere.
- Contrast with `src/apm_cli/compilation/distributed_compiler.py:754`, which — for the exact
  same kind of assembled `AGENTS.md` section content — explicitly calls:
  ```python
  content = self.link_resolver.resolve_links_for_compilation(
      content=content,
      source_file=placement.agents_path.parent,
      compiled_output=placement.agents_path,
  )
  ```
  right before returning, using a `UnifiedLinkResolver` instance that had `register_contexts()`
  called on it earlier in the same compile pass.
- `src/apm_cli/compilation/agents_compiler.py` additionally calls the (simpler,
  content-inlining) `resolve_markdown_links()` helper from `link_resolver.py` in its own
  non-distributed rendering path (`generate_output()`, lines ~1467 and ~1658).
- `claude_formatter.py` has no equivalent of either call.

I verified the fix locally by adding the missing call, mirroring the `distributed_compiler.py`
pattern:

1. In `ClaudeFormatter.__init__`, construct a resolver once: `self.link_resolver =
   UnifiedLinkResolver(self.source_dir)`.
2. In `ClaudeFormatter.format_distributed`, before generating any placement content, call
   `self.link_resolver.register_contexts(primitives)`.
3. In `ClaudeFormatter._generate_claude_content`, right before `return`, replace
   `return "\n".join(sections)` with:
   ```python
   content = "\n".join(sections)
   content = self.link_resolver.resolve_links_for_compilation(
       content=content,
       source_file=placement.claude_path.parent,
       compiled_output=placement.claude_path,
   )
   return content
   ```

With this change, the reproduction above produces the correctly-resolved
`.apm/context/conventions.context.md` link in `CLAUDE.md`, identical to what `AGENTS.md`
already produces for the same source instruction. I'm happy to open a PR with this patch (plus
a regression test) if that's useful — flagging as an issue first in case there's a preferred
approach or a reason this was intentionally left out that I'm not aware of.

Separately (not part of this report, noting for completeness): I checked whether other
per-target root-context formatters have the same gap. `gemini_formatter.py` also has no
`resolve_links` call, but it turns out to be a 12-line stub that only ever emits a single
`@./AGENTS.md` import line and never assembles instruction content itself, so it isn't affected.
No other target has its own root-context formatter (`cursor` doesn't produce one; `copilot`,
`codex`, `opencode`, `windsurf`, `antigravity` all share the correctly-resolving `AGENTS.md`
pipeline).

issues.title: [BUG] Document and align APM_HOME behavior for global user state
issues.body:
## Problem

APM documents `APM_HOME` as an override for user configuration and state.

However, APM 0.29.0 uses `APM_HOME` for lifecycle state while global package commands continue to use `~/.apm`.

The documentation does not explain this difference. It does not define which files, commands, or deployment paths `APM_HOME` controls.

## Current documentation

The [environment-variable reference](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/environment-variables/#cache-and-filesystem) describes `APM_HOME` as:

> Override the APM home directory used for user config and state.

The [`apm lifecycle` reference](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/lifecycle/#environment-variables) defines these paths:

```text
$APM_HOME/apm.yml
$APM_HOME/scripts-trust.json
```

The lifecycle guide also documents the script log under:

```text
$APM_HOME/logs/scripts.log
```

In contrast, the global package-command documentation names `~/.apm` directly:

- [`apm install --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/install/#behavior) reads or creates `~/.apm/apm.yml`.
- [`apm update --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/update/) operates on dependencies under `~/.apm`.
- [`apm lock --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/lock/) writes the user-scope lockfile under `~/.apm`.
- [`apm deps --global`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/deps/) reads modules and lock state under `~/.apm`.

None of those command references explain whether `APM_HOME` changes the documented paths.

## Current implementation

The implementation follows the same split:

- [`core/lifecycle_scripts.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/lifecycle_scripts.py) reads the user lifecycle manifest from `$APM_HOME/apm.yml`.
- [`core/script_trust.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/script_trust.py) stores lifecycle trust state under `APM_HOME`.
- [`core/scope.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/core/scope.py) resolves global package metadata through `Path.home() / ".apm"`.
- [`config.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/src/apm_cli/config.py) resolves user configuration through `~/.apm/config.json`.

One APM process can therefore use two different user-manifest paths:

```text
$APM_HOME/apm.yml
~/.apm/apm.yml
```

Lifecycle processing can read the first file while global package commands read the second file.

## Why this matters

A user can set `APM_HOME` to isolate APM during a test, automation run, or temporary experiment:

```console
export APM_HOME=/tmp/apm-test
apm install --global example-org/example-package
```

Based on the [documented description of `APM_HOME`](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/environment-variables/#cache-and-filesystem), the user can reasonably expect APM-owned user state to remain under:

```text
/tmp/apm-test
```

The global install can instead read or write:

```text
~/.apm/apm.yml
~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml
~/.apm/apm_modules/
```

Depending on the target, it can also deploy files under the operating-system home.

This behavior can:

- Read the user’s real global manifest instead of the isolated manifest.
- Write package state outside the requested APM directory.
- Make an isolated test depend on existing user configuration.
- Leave test state in the user’s real home.
- Cause lifecycle processing and package installation to read different manifests.

## Documentation gap

The current documentation does not answer these questions:

1. Does `APM_HOME` control all APM-owned user metadata or only lifecycle state?
2. Does it affect global install, update, lock, dependency, and configuration commands?
3. Does it change global deployment destinations?
4. How does it interact with target-specific variables such as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`?
5. Is `APM_HOME` suitable for isolated tests and temporary global installations?
6. Which path takes precedence when multiple home variables exist?

## Requested outcome

Please define and document one supported contract for `APM_HOME`.

The implementation and documentation must agree on that contract. Several designs appear possible.

### Alternative 1: Use APM_HOME for all APM metadata

Use `APM_HOME` for APM-owned user metadata and configuration:

```text
$APM_HOME/apm.yml
$APM_HOME/apm.lock.yaml
$APM_HOME/apm_modules/
$APM_HOME/config.json
$APM_HOME/scripts-trust.json
$APM_HOME/logs/
```

Global target deployment can continue to use the operating-system home or target-specific overrides.

The documentation must state that `APM_HOME` isolates APM metadata but does not redirect target deployment.

### Alternative 2: Add a global deployment root

Keep `APM_HOME` as the metadata root and add a separate variable, such as `APM_GLOBAL_HOME`, for global deployment.

For example:

```text
APM_HOME=/tmp/apm-metadata
APM_GLOBAL_HOME=/tmp/apm-user
```

APM metadata would use `APM_HOME`. Global target files would use `APM_GLOBAL_HOME`, unless a target-specific variable has higher precedence.

This option supports isolated global installations without changing the process user’s operating-system home.

The documentation must define precedence between:

```text
target-specific override
APM_GLOBAL_HOME
operating-system home
```

### Alternative 3: Document APM_HOME as lifecycle-only

If the current split is intentional, narrow the [`APM_HOME` description](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/environment-variables/#cache-and-filesystem).

For example:

> Override the directory used for user lifecycle manifests, lifecycle trust state, and lifecycle logs.

The global command documentation must then state that dependency and configuration state always remains under `~/.apm`.

A more specific variable name or deprecation path can reduce confusion because `APM_HOME` currently implies broader scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One authoritative document defines the exact scope of `APM_HOME`.
2. Global command references state whether `APM_HOME` changes their paths.
3. Documentation lists the paths for manifests, lockfiles, modules, configuration, lifecycle state, and deployment.
4. Documentation defines precedence with target-specific home variables.
5. Documentation includes an isolation example.
6. Tests verify the selected path contract.
7. Lifecycle and global package commands do not silently select different manifests unless the documentation explicitly defines that behavior.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Support atomic exact dependency reconciliation for global installs
issues.body:
## Use case

A user is writing a script on top of APM.

The script must enforce a complete desired state for one package, such as an APM package stored in a Git repository.

The script supplies:

- The existing dependency’s canonical identity
- The desired package source and ref
- The complete desired skill subset
- The complete desired dependency-target subset
- Any missing targets that must become globally active

The script should not need to read and merge the package’s existing selection before invoking APM.

APM can read the existing declaration to locate it and produce a plan. However, existing skills and dependency targets must not affect the requested replacement values.

Without this capability, the script must parse and rewrite `~/.apm/apm.yml`. It must also reproduce APM’s identity, validation, locking, deployment, and recovery behavior.

A supported APM operation would let the script declare the desired package state while APM retains ownership of its manifest and installation transaction.

## Reproduction

I reproduced this behavior with APM 0.29.0 and an isolated home directory.

The local package contains these skills:

```text
accessibility-guide
legacy-reviewer
python-style-guide
```

The package has no producer target restriction.

A local package avoids network access while exercising the same skill-subset and dependency-target mutation path. I normalized only the temporary directory name below.

## State A

The global consumer manifest at `~/.apm/apm.yml` starts with:

```yaml
name: isolated-global-consumer
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro

dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle
      skills:
        - legacy-reviewer
        - python-style-guide
      targets:
        - claude
        - kiro
```

## Desired state B

The user wants this exact global consumer state:

```yaml
name: isolated-global-consumer
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro
  - cursor

dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle
      skills:
        - accessibility-guide
        - python-style-guide
      targets:
        - cursor
        - kiro
```

This transition must:

- Add `accessibility-guide`.
- Remove `legacy-reviewer`.
- Add `cursor` to the dependency targets.
- Remove `claude` from the dependency targets.
- Retain `kiro` in the dependency targets.
- Add `cursor` to the top-level active targets.
- Preserve all existing top-level targets, including `claude`.

The effective targets for this dependency become:

```text
[agent-skills, claude, kiro, cursor]
INTERSECT
[cursor, kiro]
=
[cursor, kiro]
```

Removing `claude` from the dependency does not remove it from the global active-target list.

## Closest existing command

The closest existing command is:

```console
apm install --global \
  /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle \
  --skill accessibility-guide \
  --skill python-style-guide \
  --target cursor,kiro
```

The relevant actual output was:

```text
[*] Validating 1 package...
[+] /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle (updated ref in apm.yml)
[*] Updated apm.yml dependency entries
[>] Installing 1 new package...
  [+] /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle (local)
  |-- 3 skill(s) integrated -> .agents/skills/, .kiro/skills/
[*] Installed 1 APM dependency
```

The resulting global manifest was:

```yaml
name: isolated-global-consumer
version: 1.0.0

targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro

dependencies:
  apm:
    - path: /tmp/apm-exact-reconcile/skill-bundle
      skills:
        - accessibility-guide
        - legacy-reviewer
        - python-style-guide
```

This is not state B:

- `--skill` unions the requested skills with the existing subset.
- `legacy-reviewer` remains selected.
- The positional rewrite removes the dependency-level target restriction.
- `--target cursor,kiro` applies only to this invocation.
- `cursor` is not added to the top-level active targets.
- The exact dependency-target restriction is not persisted.

In this reproduced package, no producer restriction, policy rule, or collision blocked deployment.

APM therefore deployed the unioned three skills to the invocation’s `cursor` and `kiro` targets.

A later bare global install cannot reproduce the requested selection from the resulting manifest.

The current additive `--skill` behavior is useful and should remain the default.

## Current workaround

The script can edit `~/.apm/apm.yml` directly and then run:

```console
apm install --global
```

This works because the manifest contains the desired state before APM starts.

However, the script must implement behavior that belongs to APM:

- Dependency identity matching
- Exact dependency replacement
- Top-level target activation
- YAML round-trip preservation
- Atomic file replacement
- Failure recovery

The manifest mutation and installation are also separate operations.

## Requested capability

Please provide one APM operation that accepts the complete desired state for one global direct Git dependency.

The existing dependency selector must be separate from the desired Git source. This permits APM to locate the old declaration before it writes the replacement.

The final CLI design is open. One illustrative shape is:

```console
apm install --global example-org/skill-bundle#v1.2.3 \
  --replace-dependency example-org/skill-bundle \
  --exact-skills accessibility-guide,python-style-guide \
  --exact-package-targets cursor,kiro \
  --ensure-package-targets-active
```

In this example:

- `--replace-dependency` identifies the existing canonical dependency.
- The positional package reference supplies the desired Git source and ref.
- `--exact-skills` supplies the complete skill subset.
- `--exact-package-targets` supplies the complete dependency-target restriction.
- `--ensure-package-targets-active` adds missing dependency targets to the top-level list.

The option names are illustrative. The required behavior is more important than the final syntax.

Existing `--skill` behavior must remain additive when exact replacement is not requested.

## Exact replacement behavior

For this use case, the operation applies to direct Git dependencies under `dependencies.apm`.

The desired managed declaration consists of:

- Git source
- Ref
- Skill subset
- Dependency-target subset

The operation must not union existing skills or dependency targets into those requested values.

It should behave as an exact upsert:

- If the selector exists in neither dependency section, add the desired declaration under `dependencies.apm`.
- If exactly one declaration matches under `dependencies.apm`, replace it with the complete desired declaration.
- If duplicate declarations with the same selected identity exist under `dependencies.apm`, consolidate them into one normalized desired declaration.
- If the selector is ambiguous, fail before mutation.
- If the selected identity appears under `devDependencies.apm`, fail instead of adding or changing a production declaration.
- If the declaration already matches, retain it and perform normal installation reconciliation.

The same desired-state command should handle every valid starting state.

## Global target behavior

The operation must ensure that every desired dependency target is active at the top level.

It must add missing targets without removing or replacing existing top-level targets.

For the state A to state B transition, it adds only `cursor`:

```yaml
targets:
  - agent-skills
  - claude
  - kiro
  - cursor
```

Adding `cursor` changes the global active-target universe. An unrelated dependency without its own target restriction can become eligible for Cursor deployment during a later global install.

This effect is intentional in state B and must appear in the operation’s plan.

The operation must preserve unrelated dependency declarations. It must not silently rewrite them.

## Transaction and validation behavior

The operation should use the normal APM policy, source-validation, integrity, lockfile, target-filtering, deployment, and cleanup paths.

It should apply one durable APM transaction containing:

1. The additive top-level active-target change.
2. The exact selected dependency declaration.
3. The normal lockfile update.
4. The normal installation reconciliation for the selected dependency.

Validation, resolution, or activation failure must retain the previous manifest and lockfile state.

Deployment and cleanup should retain APM’s existing ownership, hash, and recovery protections.

Package resolution and deployment should remain scoped to the selected dependency and its required transitive graph.

`--dry-run` should show:

- The existing dependency selector
- The complete replacement declaration
- The top-level targets that will be added
- The selected package’s deployment changes
- Global eligibility changes caused by activating a target

## Idempotence and determinism

The user should not have to reconstruct the dependency’s current state before invoking the command.

Different valid starting declarations should converge to the same desired declaration.

Repeating the command after a successful and consistent installation should produce no additional managed-state change.

This guarantee covers:

- `~/.apm/apm.yml`
- `~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml`
- Managed files for the selected package

Mutable Git refs can resolve differently over time. Reproducible source resolution still requires an immutable ref, lockfile, or frozen workflow.

## OpenAPM alignment

[OpenAPM v0.1](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/specs/openapm-v01/) already defines:

- Top-level active targets
- Consumer-authorized dependency-target subsets
- Producer target restrictions
- Per-dependency skill subsets

This request does not require a new manifest field.

It requests one APM-owned operation across two existing consumer-manifest surfaces:

1. Exact replacement of one direct dependency declaration.
2. Additive activation of missing top-level targets.

APM already owns dependency identity, subset validation, target intersection, lock state, deployment, cleanup, and recovery.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One global APM operation transforms state A into state B.
2. Existing dependency skills and targets do not affect the exact replacement.
3. The desired Git source, ref, skills, and dependency targets form the replacement declaration.
4. `cursor` is added to both the dependency restriction and top-level targets.
5. `claude` is removed only from the dependency restriction.
6. Every existing top-level target remains present.
7. Unrelated dependency declarations and manifest fields remain unchanged.
8. An absent direct dependency is added with the exact requested state.
9. Same-identity duplicates under `dependencies.apm` become one desired declaration.
10. A conflicting development dependency or ambiguous selector fails before mutation.
11. An already-correct declaration produces no additional managed-state change.
12. Validation, resolution, or activation failure retains the prior manifest and lockfile state.
13. Existing deployment ownership and cleanup protections remain active.
14. Existing additive `--skill` behavior remains unchanged.
15. `--dry-run` reports dependency, deployment, and global-target effects.

issues.title: [BUG] skills: subset install fails on 0.29+/0.30 with "no apm.yml or SKILL.md" (worked on 0.28)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

On APM 0.29.1 and 0.30.0, installing a Git skill-collection dependency with a `skills:` subset fails during resolve. APM materializes the **entire** upstream repo into `.apm-resolution-staging/.../replacements/<hash>`, then rejects the candidate because the package **root** has neither `apm.yml` nor `SKILL.md`.

The nested skill exists (e.g. `skills/find-skills/SKILL.md`). The same `apm.yml` shape succeeds on **0.28.0**. Using `path: skills/<name>` instead of `skills: [<name>]` also succeeds on 0.30.0 (sparse checkout).

This is distinct from closed issues like #2794 (`--frozen` cold install), #1707 (subset ignored / installs all), and #1999 (`apm pack` ignoring subset).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a minimal project:

```yaml
# apm.yml
name: repro
version: 0.0.1
author: test
description: repro
targets:
  - cursor
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills
      ref: v1.5.23
      skills:
        - find-skills
```

2. Run:

```bash
apm install --verbose --only apm
```

3. See error (0.29.1 / 0.30.0):

```text
[x] Failed to install APM dependencies: Downloaded dependency
'vercel-labs/skills' is invalid: Downloaded package has no apm.yml or
SKILL.md: .../apm_modules/.apm-resolution-staging/.../replacements/<hash>.
The downloaded candidate was not activated; fix the cause and retry the install.
```

4. Same failure with `github/awesome-copilot` + `skills: [git-commit]`.

5. Contrast:
   - APM **0.28.0** with the same manifest → install succeeds.
   - APM **0.30.0** with `path: skills/find-skills` (instead of `skills:`) → install succeeds.

**Expected behavior**

`skills: [find-skills]` should materialize a skill_bundle whose installable root contains `SKILL.md` (or otherwise validate nested skill markers), and install only that skill — as on 0.28.0.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Fedora Linux 44 (kernel 7.1.13-200.fc44.x86_64)
 - Python Version: 3.14.7 (also reproduced with standalone APM binaries)
 - APM Version: fails on 0.29.1 (`1b3d80a`) and 0.30.0 (`8c2e0d9`); works on 0.28.0 (`e041462`)
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**

Verbose failure (0.30.0):

```text
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
Parsed apm.yml: 1 APM deps, 0 MCP deps
[>] Resolving vercel-labs/skills...
Phase: resolve -> 0.162s
[x] Failed to install APM dependencies: Downloaded dependency
'vercel-labs/skills' is invalid: Downloaded package has no apm.yml or SKILL.md:
.../replacements/ac98481e7252896ca951b4ed195fe68e5cdc544d297754ac118d401a96f5bfed.
The downloaded candidate was not activated; fix the cause and retry the install.
```

strace during the failed 0.30.0 run shows the replacement candidate getting the **full** repo tree (`bin/`, `src/`, `skills/`, `.github/`, …), not a skill-root slice. Validation then looks only at that candidate root for `apm.yml` / `SKILL.md`.

Working workaround on 0.30.0:

```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - git: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills
      ref: v1.5.24
      path: skills/find-skills
```

```text
[i] perf: subdir .../skills/find-skills#v1.5.24 sparse=skills/find-skills
[+] github.com/vercel-labs/skills/skills/find-skills#v1.5.24
|-- Skill integrated -> .agents/skills/
```

**Additional context**

- Upstream layout for `vercel-labs/skills`: npm CLI package; skill marker only at `skills/find-skills/SKILL.md` (no root `apm.yml` / `SKILL.md`). Same class of repo as other skill collections.
- Lockfiles previously recorded this as `package_type: skill_bundle` with `skill_subset: [find-skills]` under APM 0.29.0-era installs; fresh resolve on 0.29.1/0.30.0 now hard-fails before activation.
- `--skill find-skills` alone (without a persisted subset that materializes correctly) did not fix the failure in our checks; `path:` did.
- Related but not duplicates: #2794, #1707, #1999, #2530, #2796, #2491.

---

*Disclosure: drafted with AI assistance; the failure was reproduced and verified manually on APM 0.28.0 / 0.29.1 / 0.30.0.*

```txt
Co-authored-by: Composer via Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
```

issues.title: Install fails on Windows with WinError 206 (path too long) / WinError 3 due to double-hashed staging paths
issues.body:
Install fails on Windows with WinError 206 (path too long) / WinError 3 due to double-hashed staging paths

**Environment:**
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26100)
- Shell: PowerShell
- Command: `apm install <my-package-source> --target claude`
- Project root: `C:\<my-path-30-chars>`

**Description:**

Installing the `<my-packages>` dependency fails on Windows because the resolver stages replacement files under a path that exceeds the Windows `MAX_PATH` (260 character) limit. Every failing file follows the same pattern — a `.apm-resolution-staging\<32-char hash>\replacements\<64-char hash>\...` structure appended on top of the already-long checkout path and the package's own nested folder names (e.g. `backlog\release-notes\.apm\skills\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes-skill`).

**Command run:**
```
apm install <my-package-source> --target claude
```

**Observed output (excerpt):**
```
[x] 1 package failed:
  +- <my-package-source> -- Failed to download dependency <my-package-dependency>:
[('...checkouts_v1\...\sparse-...\profiles\shared\packages\backlog\release-notes\.apm\prompts\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes.prompt.md',
'...apm_modules\.apm-resolution-staging\5eeb88cb...\replacements\93d0a232...\backlog\release-notes\.apm\prompts\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes.prompt.md',
'[WinError 3] The system cannot find the path specified'),
...
'[WinError 206] The filename or extension is too long: ...\backlog\release-notes\.apm\skills\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes-skill'"),
...
```

**Root cause (my analysis):**

The destination path built by the resolver is something like:
```
C:\<my-path-30-chars>\apm_modules\.apm-resolution-staging\5eeb88cb5cf84db5b6df5fccc2f33cfc\replacements\93d0a232a5d070466326b08efbb0bd5ebc195148afa09606a8e8e727999fb6fc\backlog\release-notes\.apm\skills\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes-skill
```
This is well over 260 characters. On Windows, without long-path support explicitly enabled and used by every layer in the chain (OS, git, and the Python runtime `apm` is built on), file/directory operations at this depth fail with `WinError 206` (path too long) or the related `WinError 3` (parent directory silently failed to be created, so it "can't find" it later).

This reproduces consistently for every package in this dependency that has moderately deep nested folder names (`sprint-planning`, `sprint-review`, `status-report`, `release-notes`), since the two long hex-hash segments (`.apm-resolution-staging\<hash>\replacements\<hash>\`) added by the resolver push otherwise-reasonable paths over the Windows limit.

**Expected behavior:**

The install should succeed on Windows, or `apm` should proactively detect/avoid excessively long staging paths (e.g., by using shorter hash prefixes, flattening the staging structure, or opting into Windows extended-length path syntax `\\?\` internally).

**Suggested fix:**
Shorten the staging directory naming scheme (e.g., truncate hashes, or avoid nesting `.apm-resolution-staging\<hash>\replacements\<hash>\` under the project's own `apm_modules` path).

**Workarounds attempted:**
- Enabling `LongPathsEnabled` in the registry and `git config --global core.longpaths true` (not authorized by company policy)
- Moving the project to a shorter root path (huge impact on other projects).

Thank you.

issues.title: [BUG] insteadOf rewrite matching the fetched URL blocks private installs since 0.30.0
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Since 0.30.0, `apm install` cannot download a **private** git dependency when the user's git config holds an `insteadOf` rewrite rule that matches the URL apm fetches:

```
Failed to download dependency OWNER/REPO: Unable to verify Git URL rewrite safety
(Git URL-match probe failed); check Git configuration and retry; inspect matching
rules with 'git config --show-origin --get-regexp ^url\..*\.insteadOf$' and remove
the unsafe rule
```

The rule is the most common SSH-preferring setup there is:

```
url."git@github.com:".insteadOf = https://github.com/
```

0.29.0 installs the same dependency in the same conditions without error, so this is a 0.30.0 regression.

**To Reproduce**

1. `git config --global url."git@github.com:".insteadOf https://github.com/`
2. In an empty directory, write an `apm.yml` declaring one **private** git dependency
3. `apm install`

Result: fails as above on 0.30.0, succeeds on 0.29.0.

Three observations that narrow the trigger:

- **Only the authenticated retry path.** The debug log shows `Unauthenticated access failed for github.com; will retry with [REDACTED]` immediately before the failure, so a public dependency never reaches the probe.
- **Only a rule that matches the fetched URL.** With `url."git@example.com:".insteadOf = https://example.com/` — same rule shape, different host — the install succeeds. Neither SSH nor the mere existence of a rewrite is the trigger.
- **Only when something must actually be downloaded.** In a project whose lockfile and `apm_modules/` are already populated, both `apm install` and `apm update --dry-run` succeed on 0.30.0.

**Expected behavior**

A standard `insteadOf` rule redirecting GitHub HTTPS to SSH should not prevent installing a private dependency. If a rewrite genuinely cannot be validated, the message should state what was probed and why it failed, rather than asking the user to remove a legitimate and widespread configuration.

**Environment**

- OS: Windows 11 Pro (26200)
- Python: 3.12 (bundled in the release binary)
- APM: 0.30.0 — works on 0.29.0
- git: 2.55.0.windows.5

**Logs**

```
[>] Resolving PKG...
DEBUG apm_cli.core.auth Unauthenticated access failed for github.com; will retry with [REDACTED]
  [x] 1 package failed:
    +- PKG -- Failed to download dependency OWNER/REPO: Unable to verify Git URL
       rewrite safety (Git URL-match probe failed); ...
[x] Installation failed with 1 error(s) in 0.3s. No install transaction changes were committed.
```

**Additional context**

`src/apm_cli/utils/git_env.py` grows from 113 lines in v0.29.0 to 1524 in v0.30.0, and neither `GitUrlRewriteProbeError` nor `--get-urlmatch` appears anywhere in the v0.29.0 tree. The commits in range that introduce the mechanism are `7da6ebe9` (`fix: bind Git execution to validated policy`), `b33b313c` (`fix: close Git transport policy gaps`) and `129b6bc2` (`fix: close final Git transport gaps`).

The raised error is the `Git URL-match probe failed` branch of `_urlmatched_header_group`, i.e. `git config --null --get-urlmatch http.extraHeader <url>` returning something other than 0 or 1. We could not reproduce a non-zero exit by hand: run from the git executable's directory, with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` / `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` pointed at devnull and an injected `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0` header, that command exits 0 — with both `/dev/null` and `nul` as the devnull path. So the failing input is something in apm's own probe environment that is not observable from outside.

Worth noting: the machine's git config declares no `http.extraHeader` of its own, so the header group the probe inspects can only come from the credential apm injects on the authenticated retry.

issues.title: [BUG] Installer declares glibc 2.35 floor but prebuilt Linux binary requires 2.38 (fails at dynamic-link time on glibc 2.36/2.37)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The Unix installer (`https://aka.ms/apm-unix`) gates on `REQUIRED_GLIBC="2.35"`, but the prebuilt Linux binary's bundled `libpython3.12.so.1.0` requires **`GLIBC_2.38`**. Systems with glibc **2.36 or 2.37 pass the installer's version check and then fail at dynamic-link time**, which is a much more confusing failure than an upfront rejection.

Affects `linux-x86_64` and `linux-arm64`, and is still present in **v0.30.0** (latest) and the currently-served installer.

**Evidence**

The binary's own symbol versions, from the v0.29.0 release asset:

```console
$ readelf -V apm-linux-x86_64/_internal/libpython3.12.so.1.0 | grep -oE 'GLIBC_[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | sort -uV | tail -3
GLIBC_2.34
GLIBC_2.35
GLIBC_2.38
```

The four symbols responsible:

```console
$ readelf -sW .../libpython3.12.so.1.0 | grep GLIBC_2.38 | awk '{print $8}' | sort -u
__isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38
__isoc23_strtoul@GLIBC_2.38
__isoc23_wcstol@GLIBC_2.38
fmod@GLIBC_2.38
```

The `__isoc23_*` symbols are the C23 variants glibc introduced in **2.38**; GCC emits them automatically when building against a 2.38+ system. This suggests the release is **built on a host with glibc ≥ 2.38**, silently raising the runtime floor above the declared 2.35 — rather than being a deliberate floor choice.

**To Reproduce**

As root in Docker on `linux/amd64`:

```console
$ docker run --rm node:22-bookworm sh -c \
    'curl -fsSL https://aka.ms/apm-unix | sh -s -- "@v0.29.0" --prefix /usr/local'
[PYI-68:ERROR] Failed to load Python shared library '.../libpython3.12.so.1.0':
  /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
[!] glibc version incompatibility detected
Your system has glibc 2.36 but the binary requires glibc 2.35+
```

Note the final line reports 2.36 ≥ 2.35 while simultaneously failing.

| Image | glibc | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `node:22-bullseye` (Debian 11) | 2.31 | rejected by the version check (correct) |
| `node:22-bookworm` (Debian 12) | 2.36 | **passes the check, then fails linking** |
| `node:22-trixie` (Debian 13) | 2.41 | works |

**Three places state 2.35**

A fix that changes only the constant leaves two user-facing messages wrong:

- `REQUIRED_GLIBC="2.35"` — the gate itself
- `"Use a system with glibc 2.35+ for the prebuilt binary"` — recovery guidance; **this actively sends users to the broken 2.36/2.37 case**
- `"Your system has glibc $GLIBC_VERSION but the binary requires glibc 2.35+"` — the post-failure message above

**Expected behavior / suggested fix**

Either would resolve it, and they have different trade-offs:

1. **Bump the declared floor to 2.38** in all three places. Simple, but narrows supported platforms — notably it drops Debian 12, which is still current stable.
2. **Build the release against an older glibc** (e.g. a `manylinux_2_34`/`2_35` image), so the artifact actually honours the advertised 2.35 floor.

Option 2 preserves the existing promise; option 1 just makes it accurate.

**Environment**

- OS: Linux — Debian 11 / 12 / 13 (tested in the official `node:22-*` images)
- Python Version: n/a (the bundled `libpython3.12.so.1.0` in the prebuilt binary)
- APM Version: v0.29.0 and v0.30.0 (latest)
- Installer: `https://aka.ms/apm-unix` as served today
- Arches: `linux-x86_64` and `linux-arm64` (both affected)

issues.title: [BUG] Aliases containing ".." escape apm_modules, poisoning the lockfile identity
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
A traversal alias (e.g., `..`) in a transitive dependency escapes the `apm_modules` directory, causing `apm install` to treat the consumer's project root as the dependency. This poisons the lockfile with the consumer's identity and breaks integrity tracking.

The consumer never types an alias: the declaring package's manifest is the only source. The same unguarded alias join exists at two sites: the integrate phase install path and the pre-download path.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a package `poisoned-pkg` whose `apm.yml` declares a child dependency with a traversal alias:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: github/some-public/some-agent.agent.md
         alias: ".."
   ```
2. In a consumer project `victim`, declare only `poisoned-pkg` with no alias:
   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: <host>/<owner>/poisoned-pkg
   ```
3. Run `apm install` in `victim/`.
4. Inspect `victim/apm.lock.yaml`. The entry for the public child dependency shows the consumer project's own `name` and `version`, has a `content_hash` equal to the hash of the consumer's whole project tree, and has no `deployed_files` / `deployed_file_hashes` entries.


**Expected behavior**
- Aliases containing `..`, leading/trailing dots, or similar traversal patterns should be rejected by the alias validator before reaching the install path.
- As defense-in-depth, the `install_path = apm_modules_dir / dep_ref.alias` join at both sites should be contained within `apm_modules/`, so a dependency can never resolve to the consumer's project root.
- The lockfile `name`/`version`/`content_hash` should always reflect the dependency's own manifest, never the consumer's.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Python Version: 3.12.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0

**Logs**
If applicable, add any error logs or screenshots.

**Additional context**

### **Root cause**

- `_ALIAS_PATTERN = ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$` (`models/dependency/object_fields.py:11`) accepts `.` and `..`.
- `install/phases/integrate.py:617-622`: `install_path = apm_modules_dir / dep_ref.alias` — no containment check.
- `install/phases/download.py:57-61`: same unguarded join for the pre-download path.
- Child deps keep the alias declared by their declaring package (`apm_resolver.py:302`).
- `CachedDependencySource.acquire()` (`install/sources.py:517-523`) parses `install_path / apm.yml` as the package identity and hashes `install_path` (`sources.py:618-619`). With `alias: ".."`, `install_path` resolves to the project root.

### **Observed effects**

- **Wrong identity:** the lockfile binds a real OSS repo to the consumer's project name. `apm ls`, `apm status`, `apm audit`, `apm policy`, and `apm uninstall` all see the wrong identity; audits cannot tell which package the record belongs to.
- **Broken integrity:** the dep's `content_hash` fingerprints the consumer's tree. Any consumer-side change moves the "dependency's" hash, producing spurious mismatch errors or silent re-recording.
- **Missing deployment tracking:** the aliased dep's `deployed_files` is absent, so `apm status`, `apm audit`, and cleanup logic cannot verify what was deployed.

### **Suggested fix**

1. **Reject traversal aliases** in the shared `_ALIAS_PATTERN` / `parse_alias_override`: forbid `.` / `..` and any alias containing a `..` segment, leading/trailing dots, or similar traversal patterns.
2. **Defense-in-depth containment** at both join sites — `integrate.py:619` and `download.py:58`:
   ```python
   from apm_cli.utils.path_security import ensure_path_within

   install_path = apm_modules_dir / dep_ref.alias
   ensure_path_within(install_path, apm_modules_dir)
   ```
3. **Regression test:** install a package whose child declares `alias: ".."` → assert the install either fails with a clear "alias escapes apm_modules" error, or that the lockfile `name` matches the dependency's own manifest name (never the consumer's).

issues.title: [BUG] apm update  writes  target: legacy  instead of  copilot  in v0.29.1 (regression from #2795 fix)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
In v0.29.1, `apm update` no longer mis-writes `target: agents` for virtual/`claude_skill` packages (the bug reported in #2795 is fixed for that case). However, it now writes `target: legacy` instead of `target: copilot` for most deployment entries in `apm.lock.yaml`, even though `apm.yml` declares `targets: [copilot]` for those packages. Running `apm install` afterward (with no other changes) correctly re-resolves every affected entry back to `target: copilot`, confirming `apm update`'s target-resolution logic is still not reading `apm.yml`'s `targets:` field correctly — it has just moved from one wrong heuristic value (`agents`) to another (`legacy`).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use a repo with an `apm.yml` declaring `targets: [copilot]` on multiple packages (including virtual/`claude_skill` packages), previously locked with a correct `apm.lock.yaml` (all `target: copilot`).
2. Run `apm update --yes` with apm-cli `0.29.1`.
3. Inspect `apm.lock.yaml` — most deployment entries now show `target: legacy` instead of `target: copilot`.
4. Run `apm install` immediately after (no manifest/version changes) — it corrects all entries back to `target: copilot`.

**Expected behavior**
`apm update` should resolve deployment targets the same way `apm install` does — from `apm.yml`'s `targets:` field — and should not need a follow-up `apm install` to fix them. `apm.lock.yaml` should never contain `target: legacy` for packages explicitly declaring `targets: [copilot]`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux (GitHub Actions runner, self-hosted, Ubuntu 24.04 ARM)
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.29.1 (regression; 0.29.0 had the related but different `target: agents` bug, see #2795)
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A (CI-only reproduction)

**Logs**

Before apm update (correct, from prior lock state):
`target: copilot`

After  apm update --yes  on v0.29.1:
`target: legacy`

After subsequent  apm install  (no other changes):
`target: copilot`

**Additional context**
This is a regression/incomplete fix following up on #2795 (PR #2774, released in v0.29.1), which fixed the `target: agents` mis-resolution but appears to have introduced `target: legacy` as a new incorrect default in the `apm update` code path specifically, while `apm install`'s target-resolution path remains correct. As a workaround, we now always run `apm install` immediately after `apm update` in our automation to force correct re-resolution before committing `apm.lock.yaml`.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Persist marketplace object-form deps; accept SHA catalog pins
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
On apm-cli 0.30.0, operating a registry-only marketplace (immutable commit-SHA pins, nested deps that must resolve through the catalog) hits several CLI mismatches:

1. `apm install plugin@<catalog>` validates through the marketplace, then writes `owner/repo#sha` git shorthands into consumer `apm.yml`. Durable marketplace identity requires hand-editing object form (`name` + `marketplace`) and reinstalling.
2. `plugin@marketplace` is the advertised install identity, but the same string is **rejected** inside `apm.yml`. Only object form persists.
3. `apm marketplace check` fails raw commit-SHA catalog pins even when `apm pack` and CI drift checks succeed.
4. The same marketplace Git URL can be registered under two names (e.g. a local alias and the published catalog name) with no warning; `@marketplace` suffixes and audit then disagree.
5. `apm deps list` Source stays `github` even when the lockfile has `discovered_via` / `marketplace_plugin_name`.
6. After `apm install -g`, parked executables require `apm approve` from `~/.apm` because approve has no `--global` and follows cwd.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Persist `name` + `marketplace` (optional `version`) in consumer `apm.yml` on `apm install plugin@<catalog>`. Keep resolved git coordinates in the lockfile.
- Accept commit-SHA refs in `apm marketplace check` for registry-only catalogs, or document that pack+CI is the SHA-pin gate.
- Align CLI shorthand with manifest grammar (accept `plugin@marketplace` in `apm.yml`, or stop advertising that string as the persisted identity).
- Warn in `apm doctor` / `apm marketplace list` when one source URL is registered under multiple names.
- Surface catalog provenance in `apm deps list` from lockfile `discovered_via`.
- Let `apm approve` target user scope after `-g` installs without `cd ~/.apm`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Keep expanding marketplace installs to git shorthands and document a manual rewrite step (what operators do today; easy to regress).
- Treat `apm marketplace check` failures on SHA pins as expected and ignore them (confusing for CI authors).
- Continue using lockfile fields only for provenance (works, but `deps list` misleads agents and humans).

**Additional context**
`apm marketplace audit` is already the right consumer check for nested catalog resolution. Nested package `dependencies.apm` must use object form on 0.30.0; git owner/repo shorthands install but audit as bypasses. Happy to split this into separate issues if maintainers prefer.

issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-08
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.30.0 (f8df1b7)
**Commands Inspected**: 22 (`apm --help` plus all core/deps/mcp/config/runtime commands and subcommands listed in the task; `apm deps why` was also inspected as an existing subcommand not in the original checklist)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps why --help` loses paragraph/example formatting present in equivalent commands

- **Command**: `apm deps why --help`
- **Problem**: The help text embeds a `\n\n` separated "Examples:" block in the docstring/`_HELP` string (see `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/why.py` lines 168-175), but Click's default help formatter collapses multiple embedded newlines into a single wrapped paragraph unless a `\b` (no-rewrap) marker precedes the block. As a result, the three example invocations run together on one line instead of one-per-line. Compare with `apm mcp install --help`, which uses the correct pattern (`"\b\n"` before the "Forwarded install options" block in `src/apm_cli/commands/mcp.py` line 104) and renders its example/option list correctly, one item per line.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps why --help
  Usage: apm deps why [OPTIONS] PACKAGE

    Explain why a package is installed by walking the lockfile back to one or
    more direct dependencies that pulled it in.

    Examples:   apm deps why shared-utils   apm deps why acme-org/shared-utils
    --json   apm deps why shared-utils --global

  Options:
    -g, --global  Resolve against the user-scope lockfile
                  (~/.apm/apm.lock.yaml).
    --json        Emit machine-readable JSON to stdout.
    --help        Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Compare to the correctly-rendered `apm mcp install --help`:
  ```
    Examples:

      apm mcp install fetch -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch

      apm mcp install api --transport http --url (example.com/redacted)

  Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list):
    --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
    ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: In `src/apm_cli/commands/deps/why.py`, insert a `"\b\n"` marker before the "Examples:" line (mirroring the pattern already used in `src/apm_cli/commands/mcp.py`) so Click preserves the one-example-per-line formatting instead of rewrapping it into a run-on sentence.

---

### Low Severity

#### `--yes`/`-y` flag description wording is inconsistent across commands

- **Command**: `apm init`, `apm update`, `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The `-y/--yes` flag exists on multiple commands but is worded differently each time with no shared convention:
  - `apm init --help`: `-y, --yes  Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults`
  - `apm update --help`: `-y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`
  - `apm deps clean --help`: `-y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt`
  None of these three descriptions use identical wording, even though they describe the same underlying behavior (auto-confirm / skip interactive prompt).
- **Evidence**: Text captured directly from `apm init --help`, `apm update --help`, and `apm deps clean --help` as quoted above.
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize on one short phrasing for `-y/--yes` across all commands, e.g. "Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI/automation)", reusing it verbatim wherever the flag appears.

#### `--verbose`/`-v` flag description wording is inconsistent across commands

- **Command**: multiple (`apm --help`, `apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`, `apm deps update`)
- **Problem**: The `-v/--verbose` flag has at least five distinct description strings across commands that all mean roughly "show more diagnostic detail":
  - Top-level `apm --help`: "Enable debug-level logging (equivalent to APM_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG)."
  - `apm init`, `apm run`, `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`: "Show detailed output"
  - `apm install`: "Show detailed installation information"
  - `apm uninstall`: "Show detailed removal information"
  - `apm update`: "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"
  - `apm compile`: "Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"
  - `apm deps update`: "Show detailed update information"
  This variance is expected to some extent since verbose output differs per command, but several of these (init/run/mcp search/mcp show vs. install/uninstall/deps update) describe functionally identical "show more detail" behavior with needlessly different wording, and the top-level flag's semantics (debug-level logging) are not clearly connected to the per-command "show detailed X information" phrasing, which could read as two unrelated features.
- **Evidence**: Per-command text captured above from the full `--help` transcripts.
- **Suggested Fix**: Where `-v/--verbose` genuinely shows the same category of information (e.g. init/run/mcp search/mcp show), use one shared phrase like "Show detailed output" consistently (already true for those four). For commands with genuinely different verbose behavior (install, uninstall, update, compile), keep command-specific wording but consider a short shared clause, e.g. "Show detailed (X) information", to signal these all map to the same `-v` semantics rooted in the top-level debug-logging description.

---

### Clean Areas

- Installation and `apm --version` / `apm --help` work correctly and match the documented commands.
- `apm deps`, `apm mcp`, `apm config`, and `apm runtime` command groups and all their subcommands exist as documented in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/{deps,mcp,config,runtime}.md`; flag names, defaults (e.g. `apm mcp search --limit` default 10, `apm mcp list --limit` default 20, `apm install --parallel-downloads` default 4), and behavior descriptions match between CLI `--help` output and the docs.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Add Pi coding agent as an APM target
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The [Pi coding agent](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`) is an actively-used harness that APM currently has no target for. Pi users therefore have no manifest/lockfile/upgrade story for their agent context (skills, prompt templates) — the exact gap APM exists to close for every other harness (Copilot, Claude, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, Windsurf, Kiro, Grok, Antigravity).

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add `pi` as a first-class APM target, following the existing opencode/kiro/codex pattern — one `TARGET_CAPABILITIES` entry plus one `KNOWN_TARGETS` profile, no new classes.

Pi's loadable project resources (verified against the shipped `dist/core/resource-loader.js` and `dist/config.js`):
- **skills** → converge on the cross-tool `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Pi natively reads both `.pi/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`); user scope `~/.pi/agent/skills/`.
- **commands** → Pi *prompt templates* (`/name` slash commands) → `.pi/prompts/<name>.md`, reusing the shared `claude_command` transformer (Pi's `description`/`argument-hint` frontmatter and `$1`/`$@`/`$ARGUMENTS` substitution match Claude commands).
- **instructions** → compile-only (Pi reads `AGENTS.md` → `compile_family="agents"`).
- **No `agents` primitive** — Pi has no native agent-definition directory (sub-agents are an extension capability), so no frontmatter transform is required.
- **No `hooks`**. MCP wiring deferred to a follow-up.

Project root `.pi/`, user scope `~/.pi/agent/`, auto-detected on a `.pi/` directory, included in `--target all`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Explicit-only target (like `antigravity`/`grok-cloud`): rejected — Pi is a mainstream harness with a stable `.pi/` config dir, so first-class auto-detection is appropriate.
- A dedicated Pi agent-frontmatter transformer (like OpenCode's): unnecessary, because Pi deploys no agent files.

**Additional context**

Implementation is ready and opened as PR #2907 (skills + prompt-templates target, tests mirroring kiro/opencode, docs updated, all unit + integration tests green). This issue tracks the feature request that PR resolves.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-09-09 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-09-09

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
1 finding identified.

### Findings

#### [F] Sequential registry lookups where parallel lookups already exist as a pattern -- src/apm_cli/registry/operations.py:292-310

- Current: O(n) sequential network round-trips. `batch_fetch_server_info()` loops over `server_references` and calls `self.registry_client.find_server_by_reference(server_ref)` once per server, in series, despite each call being an independent HTTP request (registry search + get_server, see `src/apm_cli/registry/client.py:704-737`).
- Proposed: O(n / max_workers) wall-clock via bounded parallelism. The sibling method `check_servers_needing_installation()` in the same file (lines 40-108) already solves this exact problem with a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)` and `executor.map()`; `batch_fetch_server_info` should follow the same pattern.
- Fix: Wrap the loop body of `batch_fetch_server_info` in a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor` (reuse the `max_workers=4` convention from `check_servers_needing_installation`) so per-server registry lookups run concurrently instead of sequentially.
- Impact: `batch_fetch_server_info` is called from `collect_runtime_variables` (line 333) and `collect_environment_variables` (line 411) in the same file, both invoked during MCP install flows with potentially many server references -- each currently pays full sequential network latency.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (477 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

Other candidates reviewed (nested loops in uninstall/engine.py, mcp_integrator.py,
deployment_ledger.py, script_runner.py, target_filter.py) were confirmed to already
