issues.title: Specification: preserve GitLab sparse-fetch transport
issues.body:
# #2929: Preserve GitLab sparse-fetch transport

**Status:** proposed engineering specification; this phase does not implement the fix.  
**Outcome:** GitLab `path:` dependencies honor the selected Git transport and cannot reach REST through an unauthorized protocol change.

## 1. Evidence and scope

| Input | Established fact |
| --- | --- |
| [Posted reproduction and original artifacts](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2929#issuecomment-5616563551) | Same observations on v0.30.0 `8c2e0d9c352e2ed0e8c56b40063a63e1dd4a1937` and main `e38261c5db4d893d6ddebc3925742e4e3bd2ba74`. All source references below use that main baseline. |
| [`reproduce_2929.py`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2929#issuecomment-5616563551) | Real manifest parsing, downloader routing, URL builders, sparse transport, and local Git setup; network fetch and HTTP boundaries intercepted. |
| [`repro-head.json`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2929#issuecomment-5616563551), [`repro-release.json`](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/issues/2929#issuecomment-5616563551) | Four SSH variants become HTTPS; HTTPS control stays HTTPS; forced Git failure reaches HTTPS REST with fallback both disabled and enabled. Seven observations per revision. |
| Root cause | `_download_gitlab_file_via_git` never requests SSH when building the remote or its injected callback. `build_repo_url` therefore takes its HTTPS default. |
| Important distinction | Parsing preserves SSH, username, and port. The observed wrong remote retains `:2222`; the report's abbreviated Git trace omits it. No private-server TLS failure was reproduced. |

**In scope:** GitLab single-file sparse fetch, protocol-plan consumption, per-attempt credentials, REST eligibility, same-run transport reuse, regression proof, and directly affected documentation.

**Out of scope:** new flags or manifest fields; SSH-to-web hostname mapping; changing parser or URL-builder defaults; lockfile/package identity changes; persistent-cache migration; new retry/backoff behavior; a general clone-engine rewrite; GitHub/ADO/generic download-policy changes; live GitLab infrastructure.

## 2. Required behavior

The [existing transport contract](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/e38261c5db4d893d6ddebc3925742e4e3bd2ba74/docs/src/content/docs/consumer/manage-dependencies.md#L210-L239) applies to GitLab file fetches, not only clones.

| Input/policy | Git behavior | REST after Git failure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit `ssh://` or SCP; fallback off | SSH only; preserve user, host, repository, non-default port, and ref | **Forbidden**, even when a GitLab PAT is available |
| Shorthand with SSH preference; fallback off | SSH only | **Forbidden** |
| Explicit HTTPS or default HTTPS shorthand; fallback off | Selected HTTPS attempt | Same-origin HTTPS REST remains available |
| Protocol fallback explicitly enabled | Execute `TransportSelector` attempts in order; stop at first success | Only after Git-plan exhaustion, and only for an eligible HTTPS attempt from that plan |
| Explicit HTTP | HTTP without managed credentials; any opt-in Git retry follows the selector | No automatic HTTPS REST upgrade |
| Safe Git rewrite to SSH/local mirror | Give Git the requested URL; use the effective URL for credential policy; apply rewrite once | A rewritten non-HTTPS attempt does **not** authorize REST |
| Traversal, symlink escape, unsafe rewrite, or invalid input | Terminal failure | **Forbidden**, regardless of fallback setting |

**REST eligibility is explicit:** at least one executed, plan-admitted attempt must have effective scheme HTTPS and the same normalized scheme/host/port as the GitLab API origin. Do not infer eligibility from a token, the original hostname alone, an exception string, or merely `_allow_fallback=True`.

**Custom ports:** retain the existing opt-in behavior from `CloneEngine` (#786): cross-protocol attempts reuse the declared port and warn once per dependency. Do not silently replace `2222` with `443`. With fallback off, the reported SSH-only alias never receives HTTP. With fallback on, the user has authorized the same-host/same-port HTTPS attempt; this does not discover the separate web endpoint. The documented workaround remains an explicitly declared HTTPS web URL.

**Compatibility:** same-origin GitLab HTTPS REST handling, its existing `main`/`master` fallback, PAT precedence, and successful sparse-file bytes remain unchanged. Existing SSH-to-REST behavior without opt-in is intentionally removed as the bug fix.

## 3. Architecture and code changes

### Ownership

| Decision | Authority | Required change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial scheme and ordered Git attempts | `deps/transport_selection.py` | Reuse `TransportSelector`; extract the existing initial-scheme rule into `initial_transport_scheme(dep_ref, cli_pref)`. Have `select` and candidate-URL consumers use it. Do not reproduce the rule in the file downloader. |
| Existing candidate consumers | `deps/clone_engine.py`, `deps/git_reference_resolver.py`, `install/validation.py` | Replace only duplicated initial-scheme expressions with the helper. Preserve current public-GitHub lazy auth, ADO behavior, and per-consumer fallback settings. |
| GitLab file orchestration | `deps/download_strategies.py` | `download_gitlab_file` owns plan execution and the REST gate. `_download_gitlab_file_via_git` executes **one prepared attempt**, not a second transport decision. |
| Repository URL syntax | `DownloadDelegate.build_repo_url`, `deps/host_backends.py` | Reuse existing builders with explicit attempt selection and `token=""`. Leave their defaults and parser unchanged. |
| Auth and effective-remote environment | `core/auth.py`, `core/host_providers.py` | Use existing `resolve_for_remote`, `git_env_for_remote`, and native credential environment APIs. No new token lookup or host-policy branch in the downloader. |
| Sparse checkout and containment | `deps/git_file_transport.py` | Keep current execution, path checks, locking, and cleanup. Inject a callback bound to the already prepared URL; do not reconstruct the URL inside it. |
| Same-run live transport identity | `DownloadDelegate._git_file_transport_key` | Key on provider, ref, normalized requested/effective URL, and attempt auth mode. Reuse `cache/url_normalize.py`; update the shared GitHub caller mechanically. |
| Static ownership boundary | `.apm/architecture/owners/transport-auth-platform.json` and `scripts/architecture_linter/` | Register the existing transport-selection authority and the new sparse consumer; add a guard proving the consumer routes through it. |

`download_strategies.py` remains the GitLab orchestration owner; do not create a general-purpose transport framework for this fix.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M["Parsed dependency + user policy"] --> S["TransportSelector"]
    S --> A["Prepare tokenless URL + AuthResolver environment"]
    A --> G["GitSparseFileTransport"]
    G -->|success| B["Return file bytes"]
    G -->|typed Git failure| N{"More admitted attempts?"}
    N -->|yes| A
    N -->|no| R{"Eligible HTTPS origin?"}
    R -->|yes| H["Existing GitLab REST reader"]
    R -->|no| E["Contextual failure"]
    G -->|security or local I/O failure| E
```

### Execution algorithm

1. Read the downloader's resolved `_protocol_pref` and `_allow_fallback`; do not reread environment variables. Build the initial tokenless candidate with the shared initial-scheme helper.
2. Ask `TransportSelector` for the candidate's effective transport. Resolve its auth context through `AuthResolver.resolve_for_remote`; select the final plan with actual token availability. An SSH/local candidate must not trigger native HTTPS credential lookup.
3. For each admitted attempt, prepare `requested_url`, `effective_url`, and `git_env`. Honor `attempt.requested_url` when present; otherwise use the backend builder. Managed-token attempts use `git_env_for_remote` for the effective URL. Credential-free/native attempts use the existing native environment API; HTTP suppresses credentials. Never embed a token in a URL.
4. Validate rewrite/credential policy before cache lookup. Obtain or create the per-attempt sparse transport under the existing cache lock. Its URL callback returns the prepared requested URL unchanged. Return immediately on success.
5. On `GitFileTransportError`, discard/close that attempt's failed transport, retain sanitized failure context, and advance only within the selected plan. Do not catch arbitrary `RuntimeError`/`OSError` as reasons to try REST. Security/validation errors propagate; local filesystem failures remain failures.
6. After plan exhaustion, invoke the extracted existing REST reader only if the eligibility predicate in section 2 holds. Resolve REST credentials only at this point. Otherwise raise a contextual file-download failure chained from the Git error.

Private helper names beyond `initial_transport_scheme` may follow local conventions. Public downloader signatures and `GitSparseFileTransport`'s constructor remain compatible.

### Cache, cleanup, and error requirements

| Concern | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Key | `(provider_kind, ref, normalize_repo_url(requested_url), normalize_repo_url(effective_url), auth_mode)`; `auth_mode` distinguishes managed versus native/credential-free attempts. No token value or token digest. |
| Identity distinction | Different protocols, SSH users, ports, effective mirrors, or refs cannot share a live checkout. Equivalent SCP/SSH URL forms may share through the existing normalizer. Persistent repository identity is unchanged. |
| Reuse | Same identity and ref, multiple paths: one initial fetch, then sparse expansion. Keep existing condition/lock semantics; no sleeps or new unbounded retries. |
| Failed entry | Discard the exact attempted key before retry. Concurrent eviction must not remove a replacement instance; make discard conditional on the failed transport identity if needed. |
| Shared caller | `_download_github_file_via_git` supplies its actual requested/effective URLs to the revised key. Preserve its throttle fallback, anonymous-first flow, and commit metadata. |
| Credentials | Reused transport is scoped to the delegate's stable run-time auth policy. Do not make it a persistent credential cache. Run rewrite/policy validation before a cache hit can bypass it. |
| Diagnostics | Name file/ref and failed transport; redact stderr. Strict SSH failure must not suggest that a PAT alone fixes SSH. Point to SSH access or an explicitly configured HTTPS dependency. |
| Port warning | Reuse the existing warning decision/text and shared host-level dedup state. Extract that decision into a pure helper alongside transport policy if necessary; no raw terminal output or repeated per-file warnings. |
| No silent recovery | A successful Git fetch never invokes REST; rejected paths/rewrites never reach another transport. Retain causal errors without raw tokens or credentials. |

### Static guard and documentation

Add `transport-platform-gitlab-sparse-plan` using the existing `FactsProvider` and rule registry. Inspect executable AST/calls in the bounded consumer methods: selector usage, prepared URL callback, AuthResolver routing, and gated REST call. A comment containing an owner name is not evidence of compliance. Include a mutation that bypasses each enforced edge. Register the transport owner rather than leaving an unreferenced linter rule.

Update existing sections only:

| File | Edit |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/src/content/docs/consumer/authentication.md` | SSH `path:` behavior, strict failure, and HTTPS REST eligibility |
| `docs/src/content/docs/consumer/manage-dependencies.md` | State that the existing transport policy includes GitLab file fetches |
| `packages/apm-guide/.apm/skills/apm-usage/authentication.md` | Mirror the same behavior for agents |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | One user-facing bug-fix entry following the repository release conventions |

No README, CLI flag, manifest schema, or new documentation page is required.

## 4. Teamwork and dispatch plan

**Before dispatch:** coordinate with `mahekara28`, who already volunteered on the issue. One integration owner controls the PR; avoid a competing fix. Freeze section 2, the helper signature, and file ownership before parallel edits. These are task briefs, not agents launched by this specification.

| Task | Agent role | Exclusive write scope | Deliverable / dependency |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T1: shared policy wiring | Python architecture engineer | `transport_selection.py`, initial-scheme call sites in `clone_engine.py`, `git_reference_resolver.py`, `install/validation.py`; existing selector tests and new `tests/unit/deps/test_initial_transport_scheme.py` | Shared helper, pure unit proof, and compatible call sites. Starts immediately. Own any shared port-notice extraction. |
| T2: GitLab execution | Auth/transport engineer | `download_strategies.py`; `git_file_transport.py` only if required for a demonstrated cleanup defect | Prepared attempts, REST gate, transport key, conditional eviction, contextual errors. Starts against frozen T1 interface; final integration waits for T1. |
| T3: contract regression | Test-coverage engineer | New `tests/unit/deps/test_gitlab_sparse_transport_contract.py`; adaptations to `tests/test_gitlab_git_transport.py` | Regression assertions from the original probe, protocol/auth/error/cache matrix. Starts immediately; no production edits. |
| T4: real-Git proof | Integration-test engineer | New `tests/integration/test_gitlab_sparse_transport_contract.py` | Deterministic materialization, ref, reuse, and cleanup checks with local Git. Starts immediately; no T3 fixture-file edits. |
| T5: structural and mutation proof | Architecture-test engineer | Owner registry, new `scripts/architecture_linter/checks/transport_gitlab_sparse.py`, catalog registration, new architecture and behavioral mutation test files | Registered guard plus bounded mutations in section 5. Designs against frozen interfaces in parallel; final mutations run after T1-T4. |
| T6: user documentation | Documentation engineer | The four documentation/changelog files above | Short behavioral update, no new product concepts. Drafts from section 2 in parallel; reconciles against integrated behavior. |
| T7: integrate and release | Integration owner | Merge/conflict resolution and evidence only; source corrections returned to their owner | Integrate T1/T2 with T3/T4; add T5/T6; run all gates on the same candidate. Preserve contributor authorship. Publish PR; no automatic merge/tag. |

**Dependency graph:** interface freeze -> T1/T2/T3/T4/T5/T6 in parallel -> T1-T4 integrated candidate -> final T5 mutation pass and T6 reconciliation -> T7 release gates.

**Handoff format:** commit SHA, owned paths, requirement IDs covered, exact command/result, and remaining blockers. T3/T4 must first show the applicable new regression failing on the unfixed baseline. Agents do not silently repair another owner's files.

**Critical path:** shared interface + executor integration -> deterministic proof -> final integrated gates. Use separate workspaces for mutation runs; never mutate another agent's active checkout.

## 5. Deterministic proof and release gate

This is the acceptance contract, not a claim that the proposed fix has been implemented or passed. The original probe exits successfully while recording the bug; its exit code is **not** a regression gate.

### Isolation and fixture rules

Use the existing pytest runner and fixtures, including `tests/utils/isolated_apm_environment.py` and `tests/utils/local_git_repository.py`. Isolate HOME/XDG and Git configuration; disable system/global user configuration unless the test deliberately supplies a local rewrite fixture. No real tokens, SSH agent, DNS, remote GitLab, Docker image pulls, external API, or timing-sensitive assertions. Pin local Git author/committer timestamps and fixture refs. Block unexpected HTTP/socket calls and network-capable subprocesses.

For successful materialization, intercept only the external `git fetch` boundary: first assert the real prepared remote and argv, then execute that fetch against a local fixture repository. Keep real Git init, remote setup, sparse-checkout, checkout, file reads, and containment. Do not fake returned file bytes or replace the URL builder/whole transport. This proves production materialization and selected URL separately; it is not a live SSH-authentication test.

Use module-level `component` classification for real filesystem/subprocess tests, regardless of directory name. Pure selector tests remain unit tests. Synchronize concurrency with barriers/events and bounded joins, not sleeps.

**Existing coverage to preserve:** the PAT REST test at `tests/test_gitlab_git_transport.py:749` uses default HTTPS shorthand, not explicit SSH; keep its same-protocol REST expectation and replace the fake generic `RuntimeError` with `GitFileTransportError`. Add separate strict-SSH negatives. Existing constructor-only transport mocks and the REST-only `test_gitlab_install_e2e.py` are not the new remote-fidelity proof. Do not use the network-dependent `test_transport_selection_integration.py` as an acceptance gate.

### Requirement-to-check matrix

| ID | Deterministic assertion | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | Exact reported manifest -> actual Git remote has scheme SSH, username `git`, alias hostname, port `2222`, correct repository; no HTTP/native HTTPS credential lookup. New assertion fails on both recorded baselines. | T3 |
| P2 | Parameterize SCP, SSH default/custom ports, non-default username, subgroup, explicit HTTPS/HTTP, shorthand preferences, and explicit-scheme precedence. Compare parsed URL components, not substrings. | T1/T3 |
| P3 | Strict SSH Git failure, with and without dummy PAT -> no later Git protocol and zero REST requests; failure retains file/ref/cause and is redacted. | T3 |
| P4 | Opt-in failure -> selector order, same custom port, one warning; success short-circuits. REST occurs only after exhaustion of an admitted HTTPS path. No guessed web alias. | T3 |
| P5 | Explicit HTTPS failure -> existing REST endpoint/headers/ref handling; successful Git -> zero REST. HTTP strict -> no HTTPS REST and no managed credentials. | T3 |
| P6 | Traversal, symlink escape, unsafe rewrite/probe error, and local filesystem failure -> terminal failure with no fallback, including opt-in mode. Ordinary typed Git failure alone is retryable by the plan. | T3/T4 |
| P7 | Dummy PAT is absent from SSH/HTTP argv, stored remote, child token variables, applicable auth headers, and error output. Authorized HTTPS retains its expected scoped auth channel. | T3 |
| P8 | Safe HTTPS-to-SSH/local rewrite applies once; policy sees effective URL; no REST from a non-HTTPS effective attempt. Unsafe rewrite cannot be bypassed by a cache hit. | T3/T4 |
| P9 | Local Git fixture yields exact bytes at the requested branch/tag/SHA. Missing custom ref does not silently select another ref. Two paths at the same identity/ref require one fetch. | T4 |
| P10 | Same identity reuses; differing user/protocol/port/ref/mirror/auth mode separates. Barrier-based concurrent access retains one reusable initial checkout; failed-entry eviction does not remove a replacement. | T3/T4 |
| P11 | Existing GitHub throttle fallback retains content and resolved SHA; public-GitHub anonymous-first, ADO, validation, and semver discovery contracts remain unchanged after shared-helper wiring. | T1/T7 |
| P12 | Static rule fails when a consumer bypasses the selector, prepared URL, auth owner, or REST gate; recognizes actual call structure rather than comment/string presence. | T5 |

### Bounded mutations: every mutant must be killed

Apply one deliberate mutation at a time to a disposable copy of the integrated candidate. Use pytest subprocess execution and its JUnit result to require a failure of the named behavioral assertion; import errors, syntax errors, collection errors, missing dependencies, and timeouts do **not** count as killed mutants. Baseline must pass first. Keep mutations out of the shipping tree.

| Mutant | Required failing proof |
| --- | --- |
| M1: force HTTPS at the sparse URL selection seam | P1/P2 |
| M2a / M2b: discard custom port / SSH username | P1/P2 |
| M3: restore unconditional REST after a strict SSH Git failure | P3 |
| M4: authorize REST for an HTTPS candidate rewritten to SSH/local | P8 |
| M5: pass managed HTTPS auth into the SSH child | P7 |
| M6a / M6b / M6c: restore old reuse key / omit effective URL / omit auth mode | P10 |
| M7a / M7b: make security failures / local-I/O failures eligible for fallback | P6 |
| M8a / M8b: return before real materialization / ignore the requested ref | P9 |
| M9: bypass the registered ownership edge while leaving its name in a comment | P12 |

Each lettered variant is a separate mutation: **14 mutants total**. Implement the driver in proposed `tests/integration/test_gitlab_sparse_transport_mutations.py`; static-rule mutants belong in proposed `tests/integration/test_architecture_gitlab_sparse_transport.py`. Reuse existing mutation-fixture conventions. No new mutation platform or full-repository mutation campaign is required.

### Commands and completion criteria

After implementation, run the new contracts and related existing regressions together:

```sh
uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/unit/deps/test_initial_transport_scheme.py \
  tests/unit/deps/test_gitlab_sparse_transport_contract.py \
  tests/integration/test_gitlab_sparse_transport_contract.py \
  tests/test_gitlab_git_transport.py \
  tests/unit/deps/test_github_downloader_gitlab_routing.py \
  tests/unit/deps/test_github_throttle_fallback.py \
  tests/unit/deps/test_download_strategies_selection.py \
  tests/unit/deps/test_git_reference_resolver.py \
  tests/unit/deps/test_clone_engine_bearer_env.py \
  tests/unit/test_transport_selection.py \
  tests/unit/cache/test_git_env.py \
  tests/unit/core/test_public_github_anonymous_first.py \
  tests/unit/core/test_git_transport_policy.py \
  tests/unit/install/test_validation_gitlab_ssh.py \
  tests/unit/install/test_validation_strict_transport.py

uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/integration/test_architecture_gitlab_sparse_transport.py \
  tests/integration/test_gitlab_sparse_transport_mutations.py
```

The existing SSH semver lifecycle contract is also deterministic but requires a candidate binary. Run it separately in an isolated Linux x86-64 build checkout, using the repository's existing build script, not an installed release:

```sh
uv sync --frozen --extra dev --extra build
UV_FROZEN=true uv run --extra dev --extra build bash scripts/build-binary.sh
test -x "$PWD/dist/apm-linux-x86_64/apm"
APM_BINARY_PATH="$PWD/dist/apm-linux-x86_64/apm" \
  uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/integration/test_ssh_semver_transport_contract.py
```

This suite redirects Git to local repositories and permits only file transport. Require execution, not a missing-binary skip.

On the final candidate integrated with current `main`, run the repository's canonical CI lint contract:

```sh
uv run --frozen --extra dev ruff check src/ tests/ \
  scripts/lint_architecture_boundaries.py scripts/architecture_linter/ \
&& uv run --frozen --extra dev ruff format --check src/ tests/ \
  scripts/lint_architecture_boundaries.py scripts/architecture_linter/ \
&& uv run --frozen --extra dev python -m pylint --disable=all --enable=R0801 \
  --min-similarity-lines=10 --fail-on=R0801 src/apm_cli/ \
  scripts/lint_architecture_boundaries.py scripts/architecture_linter/ \
&& bash scripts/lint-auth-signals.sh \
&& bash scripts/lint-architecture-boundaries.sh
```

Also execute the **unchanged** YAML-I/O, 2100-line, and raw `str(relative_to)` guards from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `Lint` job in its GNU/Linux environment. Do not rewrite or silently skip the GNU-grep guards on macOS. Run existing test-quality gates for the new modules:

```sh
uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/quality
uv run --frozen python scripts/check_test_assertions.py
uv run --frozen python scripts/check_exact_test_duplicates.py
```

Ship only when P1-P12 hold, M1-M9 fail for the intended reason, all lint/quality gates pass, and required CI checks pass on the actual PR candidate. Every new proof case must collect and execute without skips; pre-existing opt-in/live skips are not evidence for this fix. Record candidate/base SHAs, commands, assertions, mutation outcomes, and resulting source-tree identity. No gate may be replaced by an agent's opinion, a live-service smoke test, or a permissive baseline update. Any source change after evidence collection invalidates the affected evidence.

**Confidence boundary:** these checks prove APM's parsing-to-transport contract, local materialization, fallback authorization, credential isolation, and regression boundaries. They cannot certify a customer's SSH daemon, keys, DNS, proxy, or GitLab availability. Those are not prerequisites for accepting this source fix.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report - 2026-09-10
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-10
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.30.0 (e38261c)
**Commands Inspected**: 31 top-level commands + 22 `--help` invocations explicitly required by the audit script (init, install, uninstall, update, compile, run, deps [+list/tree/info/clean/update], mcp [+search/show/install], config [+set/get/list], runtime [+setup]), plus targeted follow-ups (deps why, view, search, marketplace, lock export) to verify cross-references.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm deps update --target` help text lists a different (and doc-inconsistent) target set than `apm update --target`

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help` vs `apm update --help`
- **Problem**: Both flags are documented as accepting the same target vocabulary (`apm deps update` is described everywhere, including its own help text, as a "strict superset" alias replaced by `apm update`), but the live `--help` output for `apm deps update --target` omits `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, and `openclaw` from its Values list, while `apm update --target` includes them. The published doc page (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`) documents yet a third variant that also drops `copilot-app`/`copilot-cowork`/`grok-cloud`/`openclaw`, so the doc happens to match `deps update`'s CLI output but not `apm update`'s.
- **Evidence**:
  `apm update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET   Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                         skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                         codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                         cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, ...
  ```
  `apm deps update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET   Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                         agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity,
                         claude, codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-
                         cowork, cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-
                         cloud, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw,
                         opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```
  (Both actually list the same full set on closer read -- but the docs page `deps.md` explicitly enumerates only: `agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, grok-build, hermes, intellij, kiro, opencode, vscode, windsurf` -- omitting `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, and `openclaw` without noting them as experimental-flag-gated, even though the CLI's live help text for the same flag lists them unconditionally.)
- **Suggested Fix**: Update `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`'s `apm deps update --target` table to either include the experimental targets with a footnote (as `runtime.md`-style docs do elsewhere) or explicitly state "experimental targets `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, `openclaw` also accepted when their feature flags are enabled" to match the live CLI output and avoid confusing users who diff CLI help against docs.

#### Top-level command list mixes trailing-period and no-trailing-period one-line descriptions

- **Command**: `apm --help`
- **Problem**: The `Commands:` section in `apm --help` is inconsistent in whether the one-line summary ends with a period. Roughly a third of the entries end with `.` and the rest do not, with no discernible pattern (it is not tied to truncation, since several full, untruncated lines still differ).
- **Evidence** (from live `apm --help` output):
  ```
  config        Configure APM CLI.
  pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
  publish       Publish a package to a registry.
  self-update   Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.
  targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
  ```
  versus, with no trailing period:
  ```
  compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  init          Initialize a new APM project
  mcp           Discover, inspect, and install MCP servers
  run           Run a script with parameters (experimental)
  runtime       Manage AI runtimes (experimental)
  search        Search plugins in a marketplace (QUERY@MARKETPLACE)
  update        Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
  view          View package metadata or list remote versions
  cache         Manage the local package cache
  marketplace   Manage marketplaces for discovery and governance
  outdated      Show outdated locked dependencies
  list          List available scripts in the current project
  experimental  Manage experimental feature flags
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention (no trailing period is more common across the list, ~19 of 31 commands) and normalize the `help=` string for the ~12 outlier Click commands (`config`, `pack`, `publish`, `self-update`, `targets`, `unpack`, `lifecycle`, `plugin`, `policy`, `preview`, `lock`, `doctor`, `deny`, `approve`, `audit`) to drop the trailing period, matching the majority style used by `compile`, `deps`, `init`, `mcp`, etc.

---

### Low Severity

#### `apm search`'s one-line summary embeds its own usage syntax while sibling commands describe behavior in prose

- **Command**: `apm search --help` (top-level summary: `Search plugins in a marketplace (QUERY@MARKETPLACE)`)
- **Problem**: Most top-level one-liners describe behavior only (e.g., "Manage APM package dependencies", "Show outdated locked dependencies"). `apm search` and `apm run` are outliers: `search` appends its own argument syntax `(QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` in parentheses, and `run`/`runtime` append parenthetical `(experimental)` status tags. This is a minor stylistic inconsistency, not a functional bug -- the `(experimental)` tags on `run`/`runtime` are meaningful signals so are reasonable to keep, but `(QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` on `search` duplicates information already shown in its `Usage:` line one level down and reads oddly next to peers.
- **Evidence**: `apm --help` line: `search        Search plugins in a marketplace (QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` vs. peer `outdated      Show outdated locked dependencies`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Drop the `(QUERY@MARKETPLACE)` suffix from the top-level summary (it is already documented in `apm search --help`'s own `Usage:` line and in `docs/cli/search.md`), leaving `Search plugins in a marketplace` for consistency with sibling one-liners.

#### `apm view`'s long-form help text is one of only a few commands using `\b` example blocks without a blank-line-separated "Options" lead-in style seen elsewhere

- **Command**: `apm view --help`
- **Problem**: `apm view --help` renders a distinct multi-section long-form layout (`Fields:` then `Examples:` blocks before `Options:`), while most other multi-option commands (e.g. `apm install`, `apm compile`) put all prose directly under the one-line summary with no `Fields:`/`Examples:` sub-headers, and `apm mcp install --help` uses an `Examples:` block but no `Fields:` equivalent. This isn't wrong, but it means the help-text structure is not standardized across commands with rich long-form docs, which could read as inconsistent to users comparing `--help` output across commands.
- **Evidence**: `apm view --help` output includes:
  ```
  Fields:
      versions    List available remote tags and branches

  Examples:
      apm view org/repo                       # Local metadata
  ```
  while `apm mcp install --help` uses only:
  ```
  Examples:

    apm mcp install fetch -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-fetch
  ```
  and `apm compile --help` / `apm install --help` include no structured `Examples:` section in `--help` output at all (examples live only in the docs site).
- **Suggested Fix**: No code change strictly required; consider (in a future pass) standardizing whether commands with non-trivial usage patterns (`view`, `mcp install`, `deps why`) all get an `Examples:` block in `--help`, versus commands like `install`/`compile` that rely solely on the docs site. Low priority, cosmetic only.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & version reporting**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly on a fresh `uv sync` install; version string is well-formed.
- **All 22 explicitly required `--help` invocations** (top-level, core commands, `deps` subcommands, `mcp` subcommands, `config` subcommands, `runtime` subcommands) ran successfully with well-formed `Usage:`/`Options:` sections and no crashes.
- **Error handling / exit codes**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), `apm config set` (missing args), `apm mcp show` (missing arg), and `apm runtime setup badruntime` (invalid choice) all exit with code `2` and print clean, Click-standard `Usage:` + `Error:` messages -- no stack traces or tracebacks observed.
- **`-v/--verbose` flag**: present and spelled consistently (`-v, --verbose`) across every command that supports it (`init`, `install`, `update`, `deps update`, `uninstall`, `mcp search/show`, `run`, `compile`, `lock`).
- **`--dry-run` flag**: spelled identically (no `--dryrun` variants found) across `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `deps clean`, `compile`.
- **`-y/--yes` flag**: consistent across `deps clean`, `update`, `runtime remove`.
- **`-g/--global` flag**: consistent naming and description pattern ("... user scope (`~/.apm/`) ...") across `install`, `deps list/tree/info`, `uninstall`, `compile`, `view`, `lock`, `deps why`.
- **Documentation cross-reference**: every command name checked against `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/*.md` (no separate `docs/cli-reference.md` file exists in this repo -- the doc set lives under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`) matches an existing CLI command; `README.md`'s CLI examples (`apm install`, `apm compile -t copilot`, `apm marketplace add`, `apm install --mcp ... --transport http`, `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx`) all correspond to real, working flags and subcommands.
- **`apm mcp`, `apm config`, `apm runtime`, `apm deps` subcommand groups**: all match their respective doc pages' documented subcommand tables exactly (list/search/show/install for mcp; get/set/list/unset for config; setup/list/status/remove for runtime; list/tree/info/why/update/clean for deps).

issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-09-11

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [E] Heavy Top-Level Imports on CLI Startup -- src/apm_cli/commands/view.py:15-17

- Current: `AuthResolver` (src/apm_cli/core/auth.py) and `GitHubPackageDownloader`
  (src/apm_cli/deps/github_downloader.py) are imported at module top level in
  `view.py`. `github_downloader.py` itself imports `git` (GitPython) and
  `requests` at its own top level. Since `apm_cli/cli.py` imports
  `apm_cli.commands.view` unconditionally to register the `view` command,
  every `apm` CLI invocation (any subcommand: `apm install`, `apm list`, `apm
  --help`, etc.) pays this import cost, even though both names are used only
  inside the single function `display_versions` (line 601), which itself only
  runs on the `apm view <pkg>` no-lockfile-match path. Measured locally:
  `import git; import requests` costs ~0.50s wall time.
- Proposed: Defer to a local import inside `display_versions`, so the cost is
  paid only by the command path that needs it.
- Fix: Move `from ..core.auth import AuthResolver` and
  `from ..deps.github_downloader import GitHubPackageDownloader` from
  view.py's module level (lines 15, 17) into the body of `display_versions`
  right before their use at line 601.

#### [A] Quadratic Loop Nesting -- src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py:1225-1244

- Current: `_calculate_hierarchical_coverage(placements, target_directories)`
  does `for target in target_directories: for placement in placements: ...`
  (O(len(target_directories) * len(placements)) `Path.resolve()` +
  `relative_to()` calls per invocation via `_is_hierarchically_covered`).
  It is called from `_optimize_low_distribution_pattern` (line 1016) **inside
  a loop over every placement candidate** (line 1014: `for candidate in
  candidates: ... self._calculate_hierarchical_coverage([candidate.directory],
  matching_directories)`), making the total cost
  O(len(candidates) * len(matching_directories)) filesystem-resolving
  operations for a single compile pass over one instruction pattern.
- Proposed: Precompute a resolved-ancestor-chain index for
  `matching_directories` once (e.g. a dict mapping each resolved target to
  its set of resolved ancestor paths, or a trie/prefix-set built once), then
  test membership for each candidate directory in O(1) amortised instead of
  re-resolving and re-walking every target directory per candidate.
- Fix: Precompute `{target: frozenset(target.resolve().parents) | {target.resolve()}}`
  once per `matching_directories` set before the `for candidate in candidates`
  loop at line 1014, and replace the nested-loop coverage check with a set
  membership test against each candidate's resolved directory.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (477 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-09-11
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-11
**APM Version**: 0.30.0 (e38261c)
**Commands Inspected**: 23 (`apm --help` plus every subcommand listed in the audit scope, including `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, and `runtime` subcommand groups)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 1 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing-period style in top-level command summaries (`apm --help`)

- **Command**: `apm --help`
- **Problem**: The one-line command summaries shown in the top-level `Commands:` table mix sentences that end with a period and sentences that do not, with no discernible rule (it is not simply "short vs. long" — some short ones have periods and some long ones don't).
- **Evidence** (exact output from `apm --help`, full untruncated text via `click.testing.CliRunner`):
  ```
  approve       Approve executable primitives (hooks, MCP, LSP, bin, canvas) for packages.
  audit         Scan installed primitives for hidden Unicode, drift, and lockfile/policy violations
  cache         Manage the local package cache
  compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  config        Configure APM CLI.
  deny          Deny executable primitives for packages (a narrowing override).
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  doctor        Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, marketplace config).
  find          Trace a materialized file back to its contributing package(s).
  init          Initialize a new APM project
  lifecycle     Inspect, test, and scaffold lifecycle scripts.
  list          List available scripts in the current project
  lock          Resolve dependencies and write apm.lock.yaml without deploying or deleting files
  pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
  publish       Publish a package to a registry.
  targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
  update        Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs
  view          View package metadata or list remote versions
  ```
  Compare `config` ("Configure APM CLI.") and `deny` ("...a narrowing override).") which both end with a period, against `cache`, `compile`, `deps`, `doctor`, `find`, `lock`, `targets`, `update`, `view`, which are equally short/complete sentences but have no trailing period.
- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention (Click's own doc style favors no trailing period on short summaries) and apply it uniformly across all `@click.command(help=...)` / docstring-derived summaries in `src/apm_cli/cli.py` and the command modules under `src/apm_cli/commands/`.

#### Subcommand group help text mixes deprecation notice into the description inconsistently (`apm deps update` / `apm deps --help`)

- **Command**: `apm deps --help`, `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update`'s one-line summary in the parent `apm deps` command table is written as a deprecation notice only ("DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset)."), while its own `--help` output states the deprecation notice *and then* still describes what it does ("...Update APM dependencies to latest refs"). No other deprecated command uses this exact two-part pattern in its parent-listing row — `unpack` instead prefixes with `[Deprecated]` in brackets, a different, non-uniform convention for the same concept (deprecation) used only two places in the whole CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps --help
  Commands:
    ...
    update  DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).
    ...

  $ apm unpack --help  (as it appears in apm --help)
    unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.

  $ apm deps update --help
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset). Update APM
    dependencies to latest refs
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize how deprecated commands announce themselves in both the parent listing and their own `--help` header — pick either the `[Deprecated] <description>` prefix style (used by `unpack`) or the `DEPRECATED: <reason>. <description>` style (used by `deps update`), and apply it to both commands identically.

---

### Low Severity

#### `--target` value list presentation differs between CLI help and `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help` vs. `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md`
- **Problem**: The CLI's `-t, --target` help text for `apm deps update` lists all target tokens (including experimental ones `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, `openclaw`) inline in one flat comma list. The docs page instead splits the same option into a "stable" list and a separate parenthetical "Experimental targets (...)" callout. Functionally equivalent, but the two presentations don't match token-for-token, so a reader diffing CLI output against docs may think a token is missing.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # CLI (apm deps update --help):
  Values: agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot,
  copilot-app, copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini, grok-build, grok-cloud, hermes,
  intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.

  # docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md:
  Values: `agent-skills`, `agents`, `agy`, `all`, `antigravity`, `claude`,
  `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `gemini`, `grok-build`, `hermes`, `intellij`,
  `kiro`, `opencode`, `vscode`, `windsurf`. Experimental targets
  (`copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `grok-cloud`, `openclaw`) are also
  accepted when their feature flags are enabled.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: No functional bug — purely a cosmetic/readability nit. Optionally add a short note in the docs page next to the CLI-help comparison clarifying that the CLI's flat list intentionally does not visually separate experimental tokens, to preempt confusion during doc-vs-CLI diffing.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & version check**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly from a fresh `uv sync` install.
- **Top-level command inventory**: Every command in `apm --help` (`approve`, `audit`, `cache`, `compile`, `config`, `deny`, `deps`, `doctor`, `experimental`, `find`, `init`, `install`, `lifecycle`, `list`, `lock`, `marketplace`, `mcp`, `outdated`, `pack`, `plugin`, `policy`, `preview`, `prune`, `publish`, `run`, `runtime`, `search`, `self-update`, `targets`, `uninstall`, `unpack`, `update`, `view`) is documented under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` and cross-referenced from `docs/src/content/docs/reference/index.md`. The README's `CLI Reference` link (`/reference/cli-commands/`) correctly redirects via `docs/astro.config.mjs` to `/reference/cli/install/`.
- **`deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime` subcommand groups**: All subcommands (`deps list/tree/info/clean/update/why`, `mcp list/search/show/install`, `config get/set/list/unset`, `runtime list/setup/status/remove`) run `--help` successfully and match their respective docs pages in required arguments, flags, and defaults (e.g., `mcp search --limit` default `10`, `mcp list --limit` default `20`, both matching `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/mcp.md`).
- **Flag naming consistency**: `--verbose`/`-v`, `--dry-run`, `-y`/`--yes`, and `-g`/`--global` are spelled identically everywhere they appear across all inspected commands — no `--dryrun` or other naming drift found.
- **Exit behavior on invalid input**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), `apm config set` (missing args), `apm mcp show` (missing arg), and `apm runtime setup badruntime` (invalid choice) all produce Click's standard `Usage:` + `Error:` messages with exit code `2`, no stack traces. `apm install --frozen` combined with `--mcp` or positional packages produces a clear, documented error (exit code `1`) matching the CLI help text's stated mutual-exclusivity behavior.
- **Documentation accuracy spot-checks**: `apm config` resolution-order documentation, `APM_POLICY_DISABLE` escape hatch (verified present in `src/apm_cli/install/phases/policy_gate.py` and `src/apm_cli/policy/discovery.py`), and `apm runtime` supported runtime list (`copilot`, `codex`, `llm`, `gemini`) all matched actual CLI behavior and output.

issues.title: [BUG] MCP-only package uninstall deletes unmanaged Claude and Kiro skills
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

On APM 0.30.0, uninstalling a local MCP-only package deletes unrelated, manually created skill directories under `.claude/skills/` and `.kiro/skills/`. These skills were never installed or owned by APM. Installation preserves them; uninstall reports success and “Cleaned up 2 integrated skills”. An equivalent unmanaged skill under `.agents/skills/` survives.

**To Reproduce**

Run the following Python script with APM 0.30.0 on PATH. It creates an isolated temporary HOME and project, uses a non-routable example MCP endpoint, asserts the observed deletion, and cleans up its temporary directory. No real agent configuration is used.

```python
import os, pathlib, subprocess, tempfile, shutil
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='apm-mcp-removal-') as tmp:
    root=pathlib.Path(tmp); home=root/'home'; project=root/'project'; package=root/'mcp-only'
    for p in (home,project,package): p.mkdir()
    (package/'apm.yml').write_text('name: mcp-only\nversion: 0.1.0\ndescription: Minimal MCP-only reproduction\ndependencies:\n  mcp:\n    - name: example\n      registry: false\n      transport: streamable-http\n      url: https://example.invalid/mcp\n')
    sentinels=[]
    for target in ('.claude','.kiro','.agents'):
        p=project/target/'skills'/'personal'/'SKILL.md'; p.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
        p.write_text('---\nname: personal\ndescription: Personal unmanaged skill.\n---\nPreserve this file.\n'); sentinels.append(p)
    env={'PATH':os.environ['PATH'],'HOME':str(home),'XDG_CONFIG_HOME':str(home/'.config'),'XDG_CACHE_HOME':str(home/'.cache'),'APM_HOME':str(home/'.apm'),'GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM':'1','GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL':os.devnull,'GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT':'0','NO_COLOR':'1','TERM':'dumb'}
    def run(*args):
        p=subprocess.run([shutil.which('apm'),*args],cwd=project,env=env,text=True,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        print(p.stdout.replace(tmp,'<temp>')); print('exit:',p.returncode); assert p.returncode==0
    run('--version'); run('install',str(package),'--target','claude,kiro,codex')
    print('after install:',{str(p.relative_to(project)):p.exists() for p in sentinels})
    print('lock:',(project/'apm.lock.yaml').read_text().replace(tmp,'<temp>'))
    assert all(p.exists() for p in sentinels)
    run('uninstall',str(package))
    print('after uninstall:',{str(p.relative_to(project)):p.exists() for p in sentinels})
    assert not sentinels[0].exists() and not sentinels[1].exists() and sentinels[2].exists()
    print('CONFIRMED: unmanaged Claude and Kiro skills deleted; agents skill preserved.')
print('Disposable environment removed.')

```

**Expected behavior**

Removing a package with no deployed skill files must preserve all unmanaged skills. Only the removed package's owned resources and MCP configuration should be removed.

**Environment**

- OS: macOS, Apple Silicon
- APM: Homebrew binary, `Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.30.0 (08e85c4e42)`
- Python: the reproduction harness uses Python 3; APM runs its packaged runtime
- Scope: project
- Targets: `claude,kiro,codex`
- VSCode: not involved

**Logs**

```text
After install:
.claude/skills/personal/SKILL.md: present
.kiro/skills/personal/SKILL.md: present
.agents/skills/personal/SKILL.md: present

[+] Cleaned up 2 integrated skills
[*] Uninstall complete: Removed 1 package(s) from apm.yml, Removed 1 package(s) from apm_modules/
exit: 0

After uninstall:
.claude/skills/personal/SKILL.md: missing
.kiro/skills/personal/SKILL.md: missing
.agents/skills/personal/SKILL.md: present
```

**Additional context**

Reproduced again locally on 2026-09-11. The package's lock entry has no `deployed_files`, only MCP configuration/deployment records.

The apparent code path in v0.30.0 is `_sync_integrations_after_uninstall()` converting an empty `all_deployed_files` set to `None` (`commands/uninstall/engine.py`, `sync_managed = all_deployed_files if all_deployed_files else None`). Legacy `clean_orphaned_skills()` removes unrecognized directories; its lockfile ownership guard applies to `.agents`, but not `.claude` or `.kiro`.

Related: #2852 / #2858 cover surviving transitive **instructions** and were closed as addressed in 0.30.0. This reproduction instead concerns **unmanaged skills** removed by an MCP-only package uninstall on that released version. I found no existing issue for this exact case. This report does not claim reproduction on current main or other operating systems.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Interactive selection of installed plugins for removal
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Managing plugins currently requires browsing a static table, copying or typing a package identifier, and running a separate command. Removal is particularly awkward when installed identities include a host, repository, and package subpath. Users should be able to select installed plugins by their recognizable names without reconstructing those identifiers.

#2749 already proposes interactive package selection for installation/search. This request covers the complementary removal workflow so adding and removing plugins can share a consistent interaction.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Provide an opt-in interactive removal picker, for example `apm uninstall --interactive` and `apm uninstall --interactive --global` (exact command shape subject to maintainer preference).

- List installed plugins in the selected project or user scope, showing their name, source, and scope.
- Support filtering and selecting one or more plugins.
- Resolve selections directly to their installed dependency identities, including marketplace packages, rather than asking users to type aliases or full paths.
- Show the removal plan and ask for confirmation before applying it through the existing uninstall implementation. Cancellation must leave the installation unchanged.
- Keep scripted/non-interactive commands available; do not hang waiting for input in CI or without a suitable terminal.

Align the picker with the installation UX proposed in #2749. Reuse existing dependency ownership and removal rules rather than adding a separate cleanup mechanism.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Use `apm deps list`, then copy the installed dependency into `apm uninstall`. This works as a command-line workflow, but long identifiers and truncated terminal tables make it inconvenient. A shell wrapper with an external picker would duplicate scope and identity handling outside APM.

**Additional context**

Requested after exercising marketplace registration, global installation, updates, and removal with APM 0.30.0. The goal is a small, consistent interactive workflow for adding and removing plugins, not a full-screen package-management application.

Related installation proposal: #2749.

issues.title: [BUG] Claude hook bundles drop nested package.json module metadata
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a Claude hook package places a JavaScript hook and its module metadata in a nested directory, APM deploys the JavaScript file but drops the nested `package.json`. APM then generates a CommonJS sidecar at the higher hook root, so Node executes the nested `.js` file with the wrong module semantics.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a Claude hook package with this layout:

   ```text
   hooks/
     hooks.json
     esm/
       entry.js
       package.json
   ```

2. Set `hooks/hooks.json` to:

   ```json
   {
     "hooks": {
       "SessionStart": [
         {
           "hooks": [
             {
               "type": "command",
               "command": "node ./esm/entry.js"
             }
           ]
         }
       ]
     }
   }
   ```

3. Set `hooks/esm/entry.js` to an ES module, for example:

   ```js
   import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
   writeFileSync(process.argv[2], "ok\\n");
   ```

4. Set `hooks/esm/package.json` to:

   ```json
   { "type": "module" }
   ```

5. Install the package into a project with Claude hooks enabled by running `apm install`.
6. Inspect the deployed hook under `.claude/hooks/<package>/hooks/esm/`.
7. Observe that `entry.js` is present, but `esm/package.json` is missing. The generated `.claude/hooks/<package>/hooks/package.json` contains `{"type": "commonjs"}`.
8. Run the deployed hook with Node and observe an import syntax error because the file is treated as CommonJS.

**Expected behavior**

APM should preserve the nested `hooks/esm/package.json`, or generate equivalent module metadata at the deployed `esm` boundary. Running the deployed `entry.js` should use ES module semantics and complete successfully.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.12.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0

**Logs**

APM reports no installation error. Executing the deployed JavaScript file produces a Node module syntax error such as:

```text
SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
```

**Additional context**

`src/apm_cli/integration/hook_bundle.py` excludes every file named `package.json` in `iter_deployable_hook_bundle_files`, regardless of target. Claude passes `exclude_json_files=False`, but that option only controls the broader `.json` suffix filter and does not restore the skipped filename.

`_hook_module_type` searches the hook source root and its ancestors, not nested metadata directories. With no package-root or `hooks/package.json`, it therefore defaults to CommonJS and writes one sidecar at the deployed hook root.

This is distinct from #2824, which concerns missing `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and other files outside the selected hook script bundle. This defect concerns module metadata inside an otherwise selected bundle.

issues.title: [BUG] Claude compilation omits CLAUDE.md from three-level dependencies
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm compile --target claude` does not import dependency `CLAUDE.md` files when the dependency is materialized more than two directory levels below `apm_modules`.

Azure DevOps dependencies use paths such as `apm_modules/<org>/<project>/<repo>`, but Claude compilation only checks `apm_modules/<owner>/<package>/CLAUDE.md`.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install an Azure DevOps dependency that contains a root `CLAUDE.md`.
2. Confirm the dependency is materialized at `apm_modules/org/project/repo/CLAUDE.md`.
3. Run `apm compile --target claude`.
4. Inspect the generated root `CLAUDE.md`.
5. Observe that it does not contain `@apm_modules/org/project/repo/CLAUDE.md`.

A minimal filesystem probe containing both two-level and three-level dependencies returns only:

```text
['@apm_modules/owner/package/CLAUDE.md']
```

**Expected behavior**

The generated root `CLAUDE.md` should include an import for every installed dependency containing a root `CLAUDE.md`, including:

```text
@apm_modules/org/project/repo/CLAUDE.md
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.12.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0

**Logs**

No error is reported. The dependency import is silently omitted from the generated root `CLAUDE.md`.

**Additional context**

`src/apm_cli/compilation/claude_formatter.py` method `_collect_dependencies` scans exactly two directory levels below `apm_modules` and checks only `<owner>/<package>/CLAUDE.md`.

`src/apm_cli/models/dependency/materialization.py` materializes Azure DevOps dependencies at `<org>/<project>/<repo>` and supports deeper repository paths for other hosts.

Dependency imports should be derived from installed package roots or lockfile/materialization records instead of assuming exactly two path components.

issues.title: Establish issue-first contribution and governance policy
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
APM's contribution guide describes implementation before explaining whether the work is wanted. Automated acceptance labels and "silence is approval" messages can imply commitments no human has made. There is no project-level GOVERNANCE.md documenting decision authority or contributor progression. This creates wasted contributor effort and concentrates review/merge responsibilities.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Phase 1 of an interactively approved governance and roadmap reset. Scope approved by @danielmeppiel in the planning session on 2026-09-11:

- Rewrite the CONTRIBUTING.md entry path around a linked issue and explicit human approval before substantive implementation. Approval records bounded scope, acceptance criteria, exclusions, and a reviewing maintainer; accepted unclaimed work needs no second permission request.
- Allow standing preapproval for trivial documentation corrections, still with a linked issue. Reporting, investigation, and design discussion require no permission. Private security reports continue through SECURITY.md.
- Add GOVERNANCE.md with the approved responsibility model: @danielmeppiel as lead/core maintainer, @sergio-sisternes-epam as project-wide core maintainer, and @nadav-y as registry public API maintainer, with core-maintainer backup. Document progression, appointments/retirement, and succession; do not change GitHub access.
- Align issue/PR templates, the docs-site development guide, and PRINCIPLES.md. Agent tooling and recommendations are optional/advisory, not human approval.
- Preserve technical contribution guidance and existing CI/merge requirements. Explain fair treatment of existing contributions while the later migration is pending.

Acceptance criteria:
- A newcomer can determine whether to start work, find the human scope-approval record, and identify the responsible maintainer before implementing.
- Issue acceptance, PR approval, and release targeting are distinguished.
- The contribution entry paths and templates agree; existing technical guidance remains accessible.
- No live backlog cleanup, label migration, roadmap changes, workflow changes, new repository permissions, README edits, or product behavior changes occur in this phase.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Mandatory approval from the lead alone would preserve the bottleneck. Automatically treating an agent recommendation or any acceptance label as authorization would preserve the current ambiguity. Requiring agent-generated reports or elaborate RFCs for routine fixes would add burden without deciding whether the work is wanted.

**Additional context**
This is the first PR in a planned stack. Later phases, each requiring separate approval, cover advisory triage and labels, roadmap/milestone management, and lightweight eligibility automation. Full retrospective cleanup occurs last, after a consolidated migration review. This issue tracks Phase 1 only; it does not authorize those later operations.

issues.title: Separate automated triage recommendations from human approval
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Phase 1 defines human contribution/governance authority, but the triage skill and workflow can still imply implementation approval, assign milestones, and conflate deferred work with accepted work. The automated write permissions must match the human policy rather than relying on prompt wording alone.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Phase 2 of the approved governance/roadmap stack, based on #2954 (corrected head 43391a54c8; full Deploy Docs CI passed). @danielmeppiel explicitly approved this phase in the interactive planning session on 2026-09-11 after the docs regression was fixed.

Approved scope:
- Make the triage package recommend a decision and a short proposed scope/acceptance brief. Remove agent ratification, silence-as-approval, and defer-later-to-accepted semantics.
- Restrict workflow write operations to permitted classification and advisory-processing metadata. No automated human acceptance, contributor invitations, or release-milestone assignments. Preserve human edits.
- Define a canonical label contract separating human decision states (needs-triage, needs-design, accepted, deferred) from bot-processing metadata. Keep useful type/area labels without a mandatory five-axis taxonomy for contributors.
- Prepare legacy-label migration rules and update directly affected consumers and regression tests. Do not apply the live migration in this phase.
- Preserve the human maintainer roster and approval rules approved in Phase 1. Labels alone are not authorization; enforcement of the human approval record belongs to a later phase.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated recommendations cannot authorize implementation or make release commitments through the workflow's allowed operations.
- Deferred work is never emitted/applied as accepted.
- Human decision state and bot deduplication/processing state are distinct, with an explicit safe rollout/legacy-compatibility approach.
- Direct consumers and generated workflow/skill artifacts remain coherent; relevant tests and validation cover the new boundary.
- No changes to runtime product behavior, GitHub role grants, the live roadmap, existing labels/issues/PRs, or backlog cleanup.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keeping consequential write tools and only telling the agent not to use them leaves a weak boundary. Treating any acceptance label as proof of human approval is not safe because GitHub has no per-label role ACL. Replacing the existing process with more agent panels would add overhead without repairing decision authority.

**Additional context**
Depends on the policy in #2953 / #2954. This PR must be stacked on #2954, not independently based on main. Its body should be concise and custom, not follow the PR-description skill format. Roadmap management, eligibility checks, and full retrospective cleanup remain later phases with separate approval; cleanup is last.

issues.title: Define issue-backed roadmap and release planning
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
APM's existing roadmap was retired in favor of a stale release milestone. Contributors and maintainers need a usable planning model that distinguishes visibility, priority, implementation approval, and release targeting without maintaining duplicate lists.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Phase 3 of the governance/roadmap stack, explicitly approved by @danielmeppiel in the interactive planning session on 2026-09-11. Stack this PR on #2956, which depends on #2954.

Document ONE native GitHub Project with these views over actual issues:
- Intake: native auto-add of open microsoft/apm issues; visibility is not approval.
- Roadmap: selected issues grouped by one Horizon field (Now / Next / Later) and ordered by priority. Hide unselected intake items from the roadmap view.
- Ready to contribute: accepted, unclaimed help-wanted work, with contributors checking the human scope-approval record and review contact.
- Release: use the existing issue milestone, not a duplicate target-release field.

Document operating decisions:
- Now means active, reviewer-backed priorities; start with at most three strategic outcomes alongside necessary maintenance. Next is a ranked shortlist; Later is deferred consideration. Neither placement nor reactions authorize implementation or guarantee delivery.
- Anyone may propose outcomes through an issue. Area maintainers assess scope, risk, and maintenance cost; core maintainers shape the shortlist and the lead coordinates final ordering.
- Aim for a weekly asynchronous triage pass and monthly roadmap refresh, without turning these into response-time guarantees or a mandatory meeting bureaucracy.
- Milestones hold plausible release cohorts, not every accepted idea. Reconsider unfinished work explicitly at release time rather than automatically rolling everything forward.
- Larger outcomes use parent issues linking bounded implementation issues. Keep scope/approval on issues, horizon/order on the Project, and release targeting in milestones.

Acceptance criteria:
- GOVERNANCE.md owns the planning model and responsibilities; contributor entry points link to it without a second roadmap document or duplicated roster.
- The intended Project settings and final rollout steps are actionable using native GitHub capabilities, not a new planning platform.
- Existing approval rules, technical recipes, and maintainer roster remain unchanged.
- No Project creation/reopening, automation activation, live settings/labels/milestones, priority selection, or backlog population/cleanup occurs in this PR. Those actions remain in the final approved rollout.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A pinned issue alone is insufficient as the maintainer's working planning surface. A custom planning system adds maintenance burden. Using milestones as the entire roadmap conflates product direction with delivery targets; manually copied roadmap lists will drift.

**Additional context**
Depends on #2955 / #2956. This is a small documentation-only layer unless a genuine implementation need is separately raised. Use a concise custom PR body, not the PR-description skill format. Phase 4 eligibility checks and final retrospective cleanup remain separate approval gates. Do not add fake live Project links or invent actual roadmap priorities.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Complete governance rollout and issue-backed contribution eligibility
issues.body:
Proposals are welcome before implementation. For substantive changes, wait
for a responsible human maintainer to approve the scope and identify a review
contact. An automated recommendation, label alone, or silence is not approval.
See [Contributing](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The governance and roadmap policy landed in #2954, #2956 and #2959, but live metadata and remaining automation still contradict it. The audited backlog contained 144 issues and 81 PRs; the lead has since withdrawn existing acceptance and closed 18 PRs lacking matching tracking. Remaining work needs a usable roadmap, truthful labels and a small deterministic eligibility check, without turning bot recommendations into approval.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Maintainer authorization: on 2026-09-12, @danielmeppiel explicitly requested planning and execution of the remaining cleanup below. This records that bounded scope, not renewed approval of unrelated backlog work. Scope/rollout contact: @danielmeppiel; independent code-review and merge requirements remain unchanged.

- Apply the audited description-only label corrections, evidenced completed/recovered issue closures, stale 0.29.0 milestone cleanup and seven child-link corrections in #2112; skip concurrent or already-completed actions.
- Restore public Project 2304 with Intake, Roadmap, Ready to contribute and Release views, a new empty Horizon, issue-only intake and native auto-add. Preserve history. Publish verified links after actual setup; do not invent other maintainers' availability or restore old acceptance wholesale.
- Remove Daily Docs Updater auto-merge; align remaining manual automation with explicit responsible-human issue-scope approval; fix legacy-only bug discovery and canonical classification aliases.
- Provision canonical processing/decision label definitions safely. Switch the active triage writer and compiled allowlists together in the code PR, retain compatible reads and deduplication, and do not retire legacy markers before deployment and migration verification.
- Add a deterministic, initially advisory PR-eligibility check for real scope-tracking issues and an explicit authorized-maintainer approval record. Cover ordinary/partial/stacked references, trivial documentation standing preapproval, confidential security tracking, forks, changes to approvals/references, and merge queues. Read trusted base configuration and never execute untrusted PR code with write credentials.
- Keep affected documentation and generated runtime artifacts consistent; use existing validation and exact-head CI/docs evidence.

Done when: live operations have before/after evidence; supported Project settings are verified or any required UI step is explicitly reported; source changes have focused regression coverage and a reviewable PR; label retirement is held until its deployed-code prerequisite is satisfied. Existing acceptance withdrawal and contribution authorship/history remain intact.

Out of scope: automatic PR merges, new required branch-protection checks, sweeping permission changes, new agent panels, mass reapproval/deferral, confidential public disclosures, destructive Project-history deletion, unrelated product fixes, and README changes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keeping labels as authority, deleting aliases before their writers change, auto-accepting roadmap items, or implementing an autonomous merge gate would recreate the original problems. A second planning platform and a five-axis labeling requirement add maintenance burden without resolving review capacity.

**Additional context**
Public policy: [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Roadmap target: https://github.com/orgs/microsoft/projects/2304. The exact audited migration records and operation journal are retained in the maintainer's session artifacts. Public communication must explain the bandwidth constraint empathetically and preserve an issue-linked path to reopening closed contributions.

issues.title: [BUG] audit --ci walks the whole target root (session transcripts under ~/.claude, ~/.codex): minutes of CPU and false content-integrity findings
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm audit --ci` walks the *entire* root of every dedicated target (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, ...) for the hidden-Unicode signal of `content-integrity`. At user scope those roots are not deploy trees: `~/.claude/` holds `projects/**/*.jsonl` session transcripts and `history.jsonl`, `~/.codex/` holds session logs. APM never deploys anything there, yet the audit regex-scans every byte of it on every run.

Two consequences on a normal developer machine (783 MB under `~/.claude`, 4.9 GB under `~/.codex`):

1. **Time.** The audit takes ~2m30s of CPU (`sre_search` over `TextIOWrapper.read`, sampled). Anything that runs `apm audit --ci` with a bounded deadline times out.
2. **False positives.** `content-integrity` failed with 22 "critical" findings, all in `.claude/history.jsonl` and `.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`. None of those files is deployed, none is in the lockfile, and `apm audit --strip` is not a sane remedy for a session transcript. `--ci` exits non-zero for content the audit cannot own.

Cause: `_scan_deployed_trees` (`src/apm_cli/security/file_scanner.py`) derives its walk roots from `install_governance()`, which by design returns the whole root for dedicated targets ("Dedicated target roots govern their full subtree") and only partitions the shared `.agents/` root by primitive subdirectory. That is the right scope for ownership tests, but `SecurityGate.scan_files` then `os.walk`s the whole root with no pruning, no size cap, and no extension filter. Introduced by #2381 (fix for #2379), which widened the scan from `deployed_files` to the governed tree so that unrecorded deployed files are covered. The widening is correct; the boundary it picked is one level too coarse.

Still present on `main` (`4aaa73cd`): `file_scanner.py` and `_check_content_integrity` are unchanged since #2381; `gate.py` only gained `__pycache__` exclusions. No open issue or PR covers this.

**To Reproduce**

1. Have a global APM workspace (`~/.apm/apm.yml` + lockfile) with the `claude` target and a few skills installed.
2. Use Claude Code or Codex for a while so `~/.claude/projects/` and `~/.codex/` hold transcripts (or seed them: `mkdir -p ~/.claude/projects/x && head -c 500M /dev/urandom | base64 > ~/.claude/projects/x/s.jsonl`).
3. `cd ~/.apm && time apm audit --ci --format json`

Observed: minutes of wall time; `content-integrity` reports findings under `.claude/projects/...` and `.claude/history.jsonl`.

**Expected behavior**

The hidden-Unicode walk covers each target's *primitive deploy directories and generated files* (`.claude/skills/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/`, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/rules/`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.agents/skills/`, ...), exactly the way `.agents/` is already partitioned. That keeps the #2379 guarantee (an unrecorded file under a deploy directory is still scanned) while leaving session data alone. Lockfile-claimed paths outside those directories (for example `.claude/settings.json`) stay covered by the lockfile-scoped scan, which is unioned with the tree walk today.

With that change on the same machine: 5s CPU, `content-integrity` passes, drift results identical.

**Environment**

 - OS: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
 - Python Version: 3.12
 - APM Version: 0.29.0 (`656f3d6`), also verified against `main` `4aaa73cd`

**Logs**

```
$ cd ~/.apm && time apm audit --ci --format json
...
138.26s user 6.41s system 92% cpu 2:37.16 total

$ ps -o etime,%cpu,command -p <pid>
01:52  98.8  .../apm audit --ci --format json

# sampled: sre_search <- _io_TextIOWrapper_read, no open FDs besides transcripts
```

Before/after on the same workspace, `apm audit --ci --format json`:

| | wall | CPU | content-integrity |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 2m37s | 138s | 22 findings, all `.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` + `.claude/history.jsonl` |
| bounded walk | 25s (5s idle machine) | 5s | 0 findings |

**Additional context**

I have the fix ready (small: a `bounded=` keyword on `install_governance()` that applies the existing `.agents/` partitioning to every root, used only by `_scan_deployed_trees`; ownership/prune callers unchanged; tests + docs). Will open the PR against this issue. Happy to adjust the boundary if maintainers prefer a different one (for example an explicit skip list per target instead of primitive partitioning).
